title: docs: 205 list markers corpus-wide render as literal text (same class as rf2-n5as)
description:
205 LIST MARKERS ACROSS 29 FILES RENDER AS LITERAL TEXT, corpus-wide. Same class as rf2-n5as (a marker sitting directly beneath a paragraph line with no blank line is a LAZY CONTINUATION, so python-markdown folds it into that paragraph and ships the marker as text). rf2-n5as scoped itself to `docs/the-mayor-method/` and rf2-v44k to `docs/EP/EP-template.md`; neither knew the class was this big, and nothing grades it. MEASURED AT THE RENDERER at trunk 806c4f12af over the gate's OWN 291-file corpus (`scripts/check_flattened_lists.py`'s `corpus(cfg, DEFAULT_ROOTS)` -- git-tracked markdown under docs/, spec/ and migration/, minus `exclude_docs`). python-markdown under the ELEVEN extensions mkdocs' own config loader produces, a unique sentinel injected into every source marker, and each sentinel asked which `
  • ` INSTANCE it landed in. Corpus-wide 210 before PR #9637, 205 after it repaired the five in `docs/the-mayor-method/`: spec/Cross-Cutting-Designs.md 27 of 30 markers spec/012-Routing.md 26 spec/Runtime-Architecture.md 20 spec/009-Instrumentation.md 15 spec/AI-Audit.md 15 migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md 14 spec/005-StateMachines.md 12 docs/api/re-frame.core.md 10 spec/014-HTTPRequests.md 9 docs/api/re-frame.ssr.ring.md 6 spec/Tool-Pair.md 6 docs/api/re-frame.routing.md 5 docs/EP/EP-0012-path-optics-and-canonical-forms.md 5 spec/002-Frames.md 5 docs/api/re-frame.test-support.md 4 docs/EP/EP-0017-recordable-coeffects.md 4 spec/Design-TransducerRouter.md 4 docs/api/re-frame.ssr.md 3 docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md 2 docs/machines/actors.md 2 spec/Cross-Spec-Interactions.md 2 docs/EP/EP-template.md 2 <- SEE BELOW, not a defect and 7 files with 1 each: docs/api/re-frame.ssr.head.md, docs/EP/EP-0032, docs/EP/EP-0033, docs/EP/EP-0038, docs/resources/tutorial/01-pages-and-state.md, spec/011-SSR.md, spec/Pattern-AsyncEffect.md SPOT-CHECKED AT SOURCE, not taken on the probe's word. `spec/Cross-Cutting-Designs.md` is the shape: a bold lead-in paragraph (`**Consumers.**`) with the bullet list opening on the very next line, so the whole list ships as one run-on paragraph. 27 of that file's 30 markers are affected. TWO OF THE 205 ARE NOT A DEFECT and should be subtracted before anyone counts a repair complete: `docs/EP/EP-template.md`'s two sit inside the HTML comment spanning source lines 7-92, so they render as nothing at all rather than as literal text. Verified in the BUILT page. That is the whole of rf2-v44k's Finding 2, and it is refuted there. THE INSTRUMENT, AND WHY THE OBVIOUS FORM OF IT IS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Giving a list item a continuation block makes its list LOOSE, so python-markdown wraps EVERY item's own text in a `

    ` -- and a marker swallowed into item 1 is still inside item 1's `

  • `. So asking "does its text land in an `
  • ` or a `

    `?" reports healthy loose items as BROKEN, and asking "does it have any `

  • ` ancestor?" reports swallowed ones as FINE. Measured on `docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md`: the first reading produced four false positives (:43, :949, :959, and loops.md :1112, :1139) and the second produced five false negatives. Asking which `
  • ` INSTANCE each marker landed in separates them and agrees with a direct `
      `/`
    1. ` count on every site. Keep a non-vacuity control in the same run. SCOPE AND SEQUENCING, which is why this is filed rather than swept. Six of the largest carriers are hot-zone files (`spec/009-Instrumentation.md`, `spec/012-Routing.md`, `spec/005-StateMachines.md`, `spec/002-Frames.md`, `spec/Tool-Pair.md`, `migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md`), so this wants sequencing against whoever else holds them rather than one corpus-wide pass. The non-hot-zone carriers (`spec/Cross-Cutting-Designs.md`, `spec/Runtime-Architecture.md`, `spec/AI-Audit.md`, `docs/api/*`, `docs/EP/*`) are ~110 of the 205 and are separable. RELATED, NOT THE SAME: rf2-jzv2 half 2 is whether to GATE the escaped-continuation class (a different class -- reindentation, not blank lines). Nothing grades EITHER class today. Do not settle that question by committing a probe for this one.
notes:
== NON-HOT-ZONE SLICE DONE, PR #9639 (2026-09-10). BEAD STAYS OPEN for the hot-zone half. == 115 markers repaired across 20 files, 67 inserted blank lines, diff is pure insertions (67 added / 0 removed). Corpus-wide the renderer count goes 208 -> 88 measured at the same base; re-measured after rebasing onto a main that had taken PR #9637, 88 -> 88 with the mayor-method five already gone. WHAT IS LEFT, and it is 88 rather than the 90 a subtraction suggests: spec/012-Routing.md 26 hot-zone, sequence spec/009-Instrumentation.md 15 hot-zone, sequence migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md 14 hot-zone, sequence spec/005-StateMachines.md 12 hot-zone, sequence spec/Tool-Pair.md 6 hot-zone, sequence spec/002-Frames.md 5 hot-zone, sequence spec/014-HTTPRequests.md 9 NOT HOT-ZONE AND NOT ASSIGNED -- see below docs/EP/EP-0033-...-view-evidence.md 1 NOT A DEFECT -- see below docs/EP/EP-template.md 2 NOT A DEFECT (in-comment), already known CORRECTION 1 -- spec/014-HTTPRequests.md IS A NINE-MARKER CARRIER THAT FELL BETWEEN THE TWO LISTS. The bead's own scope paragraph names the non-hot-zone carriers as Cross-Cutting-Designs, Runtime-Architecture, AI-Audit, docs/api/* and docs/EP/*, and 014 is in none of those; it is also not one of the six hot-zone files, and CLAUDE.md's hot-zone roster does not carry it either. So nobody was dispatched to it. It is a clean three-insertion repair of exactly this class -- three lead-in lines ending in a colon ("The fx:" at 235, "Sniff the response Content-Type header:" at 267, "Returns either:" at 334) with their lists jammed underneath. Dry-run measured, NOT applied: swallowed 9 -> 0, ul 20 -> 22, ol 10 -> 11, li 112 -> 121, rendered words 23394 -> 23385 with the nine marker tokens the only change and nothing added. Left untouched deliberately because it was outside the dispatched slice; it wants one more worker or a line in the hot-zone brief. CORRECTION 2 -- ONE OF THE 205 IS A FALSE POSITIVE OF THE CENSUS, so the class is 203 real defects. docs/EP/EP-0033-re-frame-ui-view-evidence.md:235 reads "+ generation, released/remounted on ambiguity." and is the WRAPPED TAIL of the sentence "identity under HMR is source anchor + structural path + generation" that begins on 234. The lazy continuation is what the author wanted: the page is CORRECT as it stands, the "+" is a plus sign in a sentence and not a bullet marker. Measured on the FULL file both ways (a fragment render lies here, because slicing lines out of a document changes what indentation means). As authored it renders as one clean paragraph; with a blank line inserted it renders as a paragraph truncated at "structural path" followed by a one-item bullet list holding half a sentence. A repair here would MANUFACTURE the defect it is meant to remove. Same family as EP-template's two, though by a different mechanism: the probe finds a line that starts with a marker character, and cannot know whether the author meant a marker. INSTRUMENT NOTE. The li-INSTANCE reading in the bead's own description is right and was used unchanged: sentinel per source marker, then ask WHICH li instance each landed in; swallowed means either no li ancestor at all, or sharing an innermost li instance with an earlier item. Non-vacuity control carried in the same run and passing on every invocation: healthy tight list 3 ok / 0 swallowed, healthy LOOSE list 3 / 0 (this is the one that refutes the "li or p?" reading), lazy-continuation list 0 / 3. THE CHECK THAT EARNED ITS KEEP was not the swallowed count but the BLAST RADIUS, because a blank line can fragment a list as readily as repair one. Per file: every swallowed marker must become EXACTLY ONE new li, and the rendered word stream must lose exactly those marker tokens and gain NOTHING. Both held on all 20 files. It also caught the one file where a frozen element count moved -- docs/api/re-frame.test-support.md, tr 10 -> 8 and td 18 -> 14 -- which turned out to be a BONUS REPAIR rather than damage: the swallowed "- **Example**:" was being absorbed by the opts table above it, so that table shipped with two garbage rows (one reading "- Example:", one holding the first two lines of the Clojure sample) while the rest of the sample opened a code block halfway through itself. Worth knowing for the hot-zone half: a swallowed marker sitting under a TABLE does more damage than one sitting under a paragraph, and the swallowed-count probe alone does not see it. Gates, each read from its own runner's exit status: python -m mkdocs build --strict 0, scripts/check_doc_slugs.py 0, scripts/check_flattened_lists.py 0 (291 files, 0 flattened, 0 unmeasurable) and its --self-test 29/29, scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci 0. No insertion lands inside a fenced block, so the fence-stripping blind spot both link gates share does not bound this result -- the item enumerator reads fence-stripped source, so a line inside a fence was never a candidate. All 20 files stayed CRLF-consistent. No probe committed; it lives in the worker scratchpad only, so rf2-jzv2's undecided half is not settled by the back door. == MAYOR NOTE, 2026-09-10: THREE CORRECTIONS FROM listcorpus-a, ONE OF THEM TO THIS BEAD'S TITLE == The non-hot-zone slice landed as PR #9639 (67 insertions across 20 files). The hot-zone slice is still in flight with listhot-a. Three things the worker measured that the bead did not know. (1) THE CLASS IS 203 REAL DEFECTS, NOT 205. THIS BEAD'S TITLE CARRIES THE SUPERSEDED NUMBER. `docs/EP/EP-0033.md:235` is a FALSE POSITIVE: the marker there already renders correctly, and inserting a blank line would have MANUFACTURED the very defect the repair exists to remove. The title is left as filed so briefs quoting it still resolve; read 203. WHERE THE 205 CAME FROM, since that is the reusable part and the error is the mayor's: the probe asked "does the marker's text land in an `
  • ` or a `

    `?". That reading reports healthy LOOSE list items as BROKEN — a continuation block makes a list loose, and python-markdown then wraps EVERY item's text in a `

    `. It is wrong in the other direction too: "does it have any `

  • ` ancestor?" reports genuinely swallowed markers as fine. The reading that works is to inject a SENTINEL per marker and ask which `
  • ` INSTANCE it landed in, rendered with the eleven extensions mkdocs' own config loader produces rather than `extensions=['extra']`. (2) `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md` WAS ON NEITHER SLICE LIST, so no worker was assigned it. 9 markers. listcorpus-a dry-ran the repair before finishing: 9 -> 0, `
  • ` 112 -> 121, words -9, 3 insertions — a clean lazy-continuation repair of exactly this class. It is a HOT-ZONE file, so it belongs to listhot-a and to nobody else; relayed to that worker mid-flight rather than dispatching a second one at a held file. Its own classification of the file wins over the dry run, which was taken on a tree that has since moved. (3) `spec/012-Routing.md` IS NOT ON CLAUDE.md's HOT-ZONE ROSTER. I called it hot-zone when slicing this bead. I took a BEAD'S GROUPING as the authority instead of the file that IS the authority — CLAUDE.md's Workflow section names the roster explicitly, and 012 is not on it. The cost was small here (a file sequenced that did not need to be), but the shape is the expensive one: a fence invented from prose reads exactly like a fence that exists. THE DEFECT CLASS ITSELF, restated once so it survives this bead: a list marker sitting directly beneath a paragraph line with NO BLANK LINE between them is folded into that paragraph as a LAZY CONTINUATION and ships as literal text. The fix is an inserted blank line and nothing else.
close_reason:
Delivered in two slices and CLOSED. PR #9639 (listcorpus-a, non-hot-zone, 115 markers across 20 files) and PR #9640 (listhot-a, hot-zone, 87 markers across 7 files), rebased onto main at 1f8e462163. 115 + 87 = 202, and the class measures ZERO real defects corpus-wide. THE DEFECT CLASS, stated once so it survives this bead: a list marker sitting directly beneath a paragraph line with NO BLANK LINE between them is folded into that paragraph as a LAZY CONTINUATION and ships as literal text in the rendered page. The repair is an inserted blank line and nothing else. === THE CLASS IS 202. THIS BEAD'S TITLE SAYS 205 AND MY OWN CORRECTION SAID 203. BOTH WRONG. === There are THREE false positives, not one and not two: docs/EP/EP-template.md 2 markers inside an HTML comment (source lines 7-92 are ONE comment, so they render as nothing at all). Refuted under rf2-v44k. docs/EP/EP-0033.md:235 1 a plus SIGN read as a list marker. Mechanism below. 205 - 3 = 202 = 115 + 87. It closes exactly, which is the only reason the number can be trusted. My "203" earlier today subtracted one of those sets and forgot the other. That is the FIFTH count error I have made on this class in one session against sound judgement about whether the work mattered every time -- the pattern recorded under the mayor-judgement memory, arriving again. === EP-0033 IS A FALSE POSITIVE, AND NOT FOR THE REASON I GAVE. THIS IS THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING. === I told listhot-a mid-flight that EP-0033:235 was the loose-list trap -- a healthy item misread because a continuation block makes the list loose and python-markdown then wraps every item's text in a `

`. THAT IS WRONG. listhot-a measured the real mechanism and it is a different class again. Line 235 reads `+ generation, released/remounted on ambiguity.` It is the CONTINUATION of a hard-wrapped sentence whose previous line ends `...source anchor + structural path`. The `+` is a PLUS SIGN in ordinary prose. The marker regex -- the same one `check_flattened_lists.py` uses -- matches it, so the probe enumerates a line of prose AS a list item and then CORRECTLY reports that it did not land in an `

  • `. The probe is not malfunctioning; it is answering truthfully about a thing that was never a list marker. MEASURED, both directions: inserting the blank line yields `

    ...structural path

    • generation, ...
    ` -- a MANUFACTURED list and a TRUNCATED sentence. The repair creates the defect. THIS IS A THIRD FAILURE MODE, IT IS SOURCE-SIDE, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE THAT FAILS DANGEROUSLY. The two already recorded are both RENDER-side readings that fail safe-ish (they mis-grade a real marker): "does the text land in an `
  • ` or a `

    `?" flags healthy loose items, and "does it have any `

  • ` ANCESTOR?" clears genuinely swallowed ones. NO RENDER-SIDE READING CATCHES THIS ONE, because the render is correct -- the error is upstream, in deciding that the line was a marker. THE STRUCTURAL TELL, which is what makes it screenable rather than a matter of reading every hit: a wrapped-prose false positive is a SINGLETON. No colon lead-in above it, no sibling markers around it. A genuine swallowed marker travels in company. listhot-a built a source-side screen on exactly that, controlled it on EP-0033 (it flags it), and ran it over all 87 of its own sites: 4 loose flags, all 4 verified GENUINE -- tails inside 3-to-4-marker runs under colon lead-ins, e.g. 005-StateMachines.md:2924 following "when ANY of the following holds:". So the screen has a measured false-positive rate of 4 flagged / 0 spurious on this corpus. === TWO MORE CORRECTIONS TO MY BRIEF, BOTH MINE === MY "~95 SITES" FOR THE HOT-ZONE SLICE WAS 78. My own six per-file numbers sum to 78. An arithmetic slip on figures I had already measured correctly, not a measurement error -- which is the same shape as the 203 above. `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md` AND `spec/012-Routing.md` ARE NOT HOT-ZONE. Five of the seven files in #9640 qualify; those two do not. It changed nothing here (one commit per file either way), but a dispatch filter keyed on the REAL roster would have parallelised those two out of the sequential lane. I had already caught 012 via listcorpus-a and still shipped 014 into the hot-zone brief, so this is the same error twice. === VERIFIED BY THE MAYOR RATHER THAN RELAYED === THE TRANSFORM IS BLANK LINES ONLY. Read line by line off the PR's own range (f388425bc9..1f8e462163): 30 added lines, EVERY ONE BLANK, 0 removed, 0 non-blank on either side. AND THE INSTRUMENT I REACHED FOR FIRST WAS WRONG, which is worth recording because rf2-6ml6's close reason makes `git diff -w` look like the standard check for this family. It is not, for THIS transform: `-w` ignores whitespace WITHIN a line, so a wholly new BLANK LINE is still a real addition and `diff -w` reports it. It read 265 lines here and that is correct behaviour, not a finding. rf2-6ml6 was a REINDENT -- leading whitespace changed on existing lines -- where `-w` IS the right instrument and empty IS the expected answer. Same family, opposite transform, opposite instrument. Read the added lines instead. title: xray: ManagedFxList handed records-list the whole sub map, so the managed-fx panel threw before painting
description:
Found while wiring the managed-fx section disclosure (rf2-s6m6), at base 58399caf58.

`panels/ManagedFxList` (panels.cljs) read the composite sub and handed the WHOLE
RESULT MAP to `managed-fx-template/records-list`, which takes a RECORDS VECTOR:

    (let [records @(rf/subscribe [:rf.xray/managed-fx-for-focused-event])]
      (managed-fx/records-list dispatch records))

`:rf.xray/managed-fx-for-focused-event` answers
`{:dispatch-id <id> :frame <f> :records [<record> ...]}` -- pinned by its own test,
`managed_fx_subs_cljs_test.cljs`, which reads `(:records out)` throughout.

So `records-list` received a 3-entry MAP. `(seq records)` is truthy, `(count records)`
reads 3 -- the caption would have said "3 managed-fx records in this event-bundle"
regardless of the real count -- and `(for [rec records] ...)` walks MAP ENTRIES.
`record-panel` then evaluates `(name (:status record))` on a MapEntry, where
`(:status ...)` is nil, and `(name nil)` throws in CLJS.

The panel therefore threw before painting whenever the focused event-bundle had any
managed-fx records at all. It is the same presentation as the rf2-qhoj incident --
a panel that never appears rather than a visible error -- because there is no error
boundary above this render path.

NOT A REGRESSION FROM RECENT WORK. `git log -L` on those lines shows the binding has
passed the whole map since before the Causa -> Xray rename (731188b1fb); rf2-nesy9
(ea5b702b05) added the `dispatch` argument in front of it and rf2-kimk1q (e9a7d4cec0)
only rewrote the comment above it. Neither touched the value.

FIXED IN PASSING under rf2-s6m6, because that bead's deliverable is the record
payloads being REACHABLE IN THE UI, and they are not reachable through a panel that
throws on mount. The fix is `(:records focused)`. Recorded here as its own bead
because it is a distinct defect with its own cause and its own blast radius.

WHAT IS STILL OWED, and why this bead stays open rather than closing with that PR:
nothing grades the `ManagedFxList` reg-view's own render. `panels_mount_cljs_test.cljs`'s
`mount-managed-fx-wraps-ManagedFxList` asserts only the frame-provider wrap, and the
template tests exercise `records-list` / `record-panel` directly with a vector, so
every tier was blind to the one call site that composes them. A row that mounts the
reg-view against a seeded buffer and asserts a record panel appears is what would
have caught it -- and would catch the next caller that hands the composite's map to
a vector-shaped renderer.
notes:
== MAYOR, 2026-09-10: HELD, NOT DISPATCHED — the fix is already in flight ==

DO NOT DISPATCH THIS BEAD. The fix rides in worker `disclose-a`'s commit
`10dd6f3320` ("fix(xray): wire the managed-fx record panel's section
disclosure (rf2-s6m6)"), on branch `worker/disclose-a`, which at the time of
writing is COMMITTED BUT NOT PUSHED — so there is no PR to read yet and
nothing has landed on trunk.

WHY IT LANDED THERE: rf2-s6m6's disclosure wiring had to touch the very
binding this bead is about. `ManagedFxList` now reads the sub into `focused`
and passes `(:records focused)`, and the commit's own comment cites rf2-90kv
by id.

PREMISE CONFIRMED AT SOURCE BEFORE READING THAT COMMIT — the order matters,
so this is a corroboration and not a relay. Measured on trunk at the time:

  - `panels.cljs:443` bound the WHOLE sub result to `records`, and `:447`
    handed it to `managed-fx/records-list`.
  - `panels/managed_fx_subs.cljs:55` builds `{:dispatch-id … :frame …
    :records […]}`, and its `:9` docstring documents that shape.
  - `panels/managed_fx_template.cljs:420` `records-list` is documented
    "Pure fn over the records vector", arities `([records])` and
    `([dispatch records])`.
  - `panels.cljs`'s OWN docstring at `:433-434` already said `records-list`
    "is a pure fn over a records vector" — so the file contradicted itself,
    caller against docstring, which is the cheapest tell here.

FOLLOW-ON, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN: the fix carries NO
REGRESSION TEST. `10dd6f3320` adds twelve deftests and every one of them is
about disclosure (rf2-s6m6); none asserts the caller contract. The existing
`panels_mount_cljs_test.cljs:190 mount-managed-fx-wraps-ManagedFxList`
CANNOT cover it — it redefines `rf.substrate.adapter/render` to a stub and
asserts only that a `frame-provider` wraps `ManagedFxList`, so the view's
BODY never executes and nothing observes what reaches `records-list`.
Verified by reading that test, not inferred from the absence of a name.

DISPOSITION: keep OPEN until `worker/disclose-a`'s PR MERGES, then verify the
fix at trunk and decide the test question. Do not close this on the strength
of an unpushed commit — the change is still open, and a bead closed against
an unlanded branch is a bead that quietly reopens.

A request to add the regression test inside that same PR has been sent to
`disclose-a` while its branch is still unpushed, so the test can ride along
rather than cost a follow-on dispatch. If that request is declined or the PR
lands without it, this bead's remaining scope is exactly that one test.
close_reason:
Fixed and merged inside PR #9630 (rf2-s6m6's change), rebased onto main at 8120c21de7.

THE DEFECT, which I verified at source myself before reading any worker's account of it:
`ManagedFxList` bound the WHOLE result of `:rf.xray/managed-fx-for-focused-event` and handed it
to `managed-fx-template/records-list`. The sub answers `{:dispatch-id .. :frame .. :records [..]}`
while `records-list` takes a records VECTOR -- so `(for [rec records] ...)` walked MAP ENTRIES and
`(name (:status rec))` threw before the panel could paint. The rf2-qhoj "panel that never appears"
shape. The file contradicted itself: `panels.cljs`'s own docstring already said `records-list` "is
a pure fn over a records vector".

NOT A REGRESSION: the binding predates the Causa->Xray rename (worker's `git log -L`, relayed).

WHY IT LANDED IN SOMEONE ELSE'S PR, and why that was right. rf2-s6m6's disclosure wiring had to
edit those exact two lines, so the fix was free there and would have collided with anything I
dispatched separately. I held this bead rather than dispatching it, and closed it only when the
PR merged -- not when the branch carried the fix, because a bead closed against an unlanded
branch is a bead that quietly reopens.

THE REGRESSION TEST, which is the part worth keeping. When I found the fix riding in that commit
I also measured that NOTHING pinned it: all twelve tests the commit added were disclosure tests,
and the pre-existing `mount-managed-fx-wraps-ManagedFxList` stubs `rf.substrate.adapter/render`
to a stub, so the view's BODY never executes and no test could observe what reached `records-list`.
I asked the worker mid-flight to add one before pushing, with permission to decline if the render
seam fought it.

It added one, and it is not hollow. It invokes the reg-view body via `((rf/view id))` against a
cascade seeded with two managed-fx invocations, and under the old binding it goes red BY ERRORING
-- `Doesn't support name:`, i.e. CLJS `(name nil)` inside `record-panel` -- at 27 assertions and
exit 1, against 28 and exit 0 restored. Its control (that the composite really answers two
records) PASSES IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is what isolates the fault to the composition rather
than to the seeding; a control that failed alongside would have proved only that the fixture was
broken. Restore verified by effect: `git diff --quiet` exit 0 and the default `git hash-object`
form matching the committed blob.

A PROCESS NOTE WORTH THE LINE. This bead was filed by the merged-PR audit harness, and the fix was
already in flight when I read it. The useful act was therefore not dispatching a worker -- it was
reading the live tree, finding the fix already there, and noticing the test that was missing. Had
I dispatched on the bead as filed, two workers would have edited the same two lines.

title: fix(xray): the edn-inspector's type-change suffix uses a plain fn as a hiccup head, which is a loud Fresco refusal (HD-016)
description:
THE APP-DB PANEL THROWS AND TAKES THE WHOLE XRAY ROOT DOWN WHENEVER THE FOCUSED
EPOCH CONTAINS A LEAF TYPE CHANGE. One token is wrong: a hiccup vector whose head
is a plain function, in the ONE branch of the shared edn-inspector that only a
type-changing diff reaches.

=== THE SITE ===

title: ssr: the pure-CLJS emitter dumps a fragment's attribute map into the markup as escaped EDN
description:
The pure-CLJS SSR emitter dumps a fragment's ATTRIBUTE MAP into the markup as escaped EDN, so a keyed fragment puts garbage in the server bytes. `re-frame.ssr.emit`'s `:<>` branch calls `(emit-children-threading-root-attrs (rest el) root-attrs)`. `(rest el)` does not skip a props map at position 1, so the map itself is emitted as a CHILD. Measured on the JVM at trunk a3739d00a1: [:<> {:key "k"} [:div "x"]] => "{:key "k"}
x
" [:<> {} [:div "x"]] => "{}
x
" [:<> [:div "x"]] => "
x
" (correct — no map) WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: `[:<> {:key i} ...]` inside a `for` is the canonical fragment idiom, so this is reachable from ordinary application markup, not a corner. The output is garbage text in the response and a guaranteed hydration mismatch against a client render that emits no such text. It is also exactly the failure the SIBLING `:>` branch's own comment says it refuses to commit — that splicing `(rest el)` through `emit-children` "would stringify the component ref and dump the props map as raw EDN into the markup (garbage output, not a rendered component)". The `:<>` branch does precisely that. LIKELY SHAPE OF THE FIX: skip a leading props map the way the React-side codec does (`props-map?` at position 1), keeping `root-attrs` threading onto the first CHILD unchanged (rf2-58zvy1 finding 2 — do not regress that). Whether a non-`:key` fragment attr should then be refused or silently dropped is a separate question; the React-side codec currently drops. A LESSER SIBLING OF THE SAME CAUSE, worth folding in only if it is cheap: the same emitter passes STRUCTURAL SLOTS through as DOM attributes on native tags — `[:div {:key "k"}]` emits `key="k"`, and a string-valued `:ref` emits `ref="R"`. React's own serialiser emits neither. A function-valued ref is already correctly dropped, and a string ref is illegal in React, so the reachable case is `:key`. Found by rf2-26hs (fragment ref forwarding) while checking its SSR/hydration verification row. Not fixed there: `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc` was outside that dispatch's write surface, and the `:key` case dominates the `:ref` one, so it is its own bead rather than a passenger.

x
CORRECT, and only because no map BUT THE WORSE HALF WAS NOT ON THE BEAD, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS WAS A P1 RATHER THAN A COSMETIC BUG. Because the props map became the FIRST CHILD, `emit-children-threading-root-attrs` threaded root-attrs onto a value that cannot carry an attribute — and the `data-rf-render-hash` MARKER VANISHED ENTIRELY: [:<> {:key "k"} [:div "a"] [:div "b"]] with {:render-hash "deadbeef"} before => "{:key "k"}

title: machines: preserve the machine DEFINITION through every actor teardown (RULED — 3 sites, delete *definition-preserved-at*, Spec 005 D4/D5/D7)
description:
**RULED 2026-09-09. This is an implementation bead — the decision is made, do NOT re-investigate.** Full reasoning, the weighed alternatives and the measured evidence are in the notes; read them before starting.

## The ruling

A `reg-machine` DEFINITION survives every actor teardown — explicit `[:rf.machine/destroy <id>]`, the D7 `:final?` singleton auto-destroy, and frame destroy alike. Inseparably, `actor-live?` stops treating a definition-bearing registrar entry as a liveness signal.

The registration is a load-time PROGRAM that makes an address creatable; the snapshot is the INSTANCE. Teardown ends the instance and never the program. `rf/clear` remains the public spelling for permanent removal, unchanged.

## Why it matters

`reg-machine` writes ONE registrar entry playing TWO roles — the singleton actor's ADDRESS and the shared TYPE DEFINITION every spawn resolves through. Teardown targets the address and the definition goes with it, so every later `[:rf.machine/spawn {:machine-id X}]` anywhere in the app fails `:rf.error/machine-spawn-unregistered-type`.

Reachable with NO teardown code written by the author: a root-level `:final?` leaf fires the D7 auto-destroy. Masked in dev by hot reload re-running `reg-machine` from the same source coords; live only in production. A shipped example is broken today — `examples/capabilities/resources/resources/core.cljs` starts `:resources.app/reader` (`:334`), destroys it (`:341`), and offers "Open in reader" again (`:478`).

## Scope — ONE PR, all of it

1. **Three sites, one predicate** (`resolver/spec-from-registry`, `resolver.cljc:50`): gate `destroy.cljc:316-318` (teardown step 8) and `finalize.cljc:702` on the address NOT carrying a definition; amend `actor-live?` (`destroy.cljc:118`, body `:162-166`) so a definition-bearing entry alone is not liveness while a non-machine entry still is.
2. **Delete `*definition-preserved-at*`** (`destroy.cljc:168-192`, `:317`, `:869`, `:885-887`) — dead once step 8 protects every definition. The change is net-negative code; no API grows.
3. **Spec 005 (HOT-ZONE one-toucher, sequence never parallel)**: §Liveness is derived from runtime-db, §Destroy is silent-idempotent, and D4/D5/D7 together. **D5 is deliberately revised** — lazy re-creation by an ordinary event is accepted.
4. **Fix the phantom `§Spawning §v1-partial` citation** at its three tracked sites (`frame_destroy.cljc:159`, `:215`, `frame_destroy_cascade_test.clj:215`) — that section does not exist anywhere in `spec/`.
5. Test churn and new coverage as enumerated in the notes.

Consistent with rf2-dokz: same predicate, applied generally instead of at one address, deleting the narrow dynamic var it introduced.

**All line numbers measured at trunk `ff9f7a833f`; `destroy.cljc` is hot — re-measure before editing, and sequence behind anything live on it or on `spec/005-StateMachines.md`.**
notes:
--- MAYOR 2026-09-09 AUSEST — §2 REREAD: STILL TRUE OF TRUNK. THE RULING IS STILL OWED. ---

    d83ee76d27  fix(machines): a registered TYPE is not a live occupant at a fixed address

Both are about ADDRESS OCCUPANCY on the spawn side; neither touches singleton re-wake. So this bead
is **not** quietly fixed in the tree, and the ruling it asks for is still owed.

**NOT DISPATCHABLE, and the bead itself says why** — "Do not implement either without that ruling.
The stance says record a decision rather than build machinery." Agreed; I am not dispatching it and

---

## RULING 2026-09-09 (decision closeout, trunk ff9f7a833f)

**RULED: a `reg-machine` DEFINITION survives every actor teardown — explicit destroy, `:final?` auto-destroy, and frame destroy alike. AND, inseparably, `actor-live?` stops treating a definition-bearing registrar entry as liveness.** The registration is a load-time PROGRAM that makes an address creatable; the snapshot is the INSTANCE. Teardown ends the instance and never the program. Permanent removal keeps its existing public spelling, `rf/clear`.

This is the dossier's Option A **amended by the Codex review's third correction, which is load-bearing and without which Option A is broken.** Options B, C and D are refused.

### Who won the conflicts: Codex, on all four corrections. Every one verified at source here.

1. **DECISIVE — Option A as the dossier wrote it breaks silent idempotence.** `actor-live?` (`destroy.cljc:118`, body `:162-166`) has the registrar lookup as its FIRST liveness disjunct: `(or (some? (rf.registrar/lookup :event actor-id)) (snapshot-present? runtime-db actor-id) ...)`. Preserve the definition and a destroyed singleton STILL reads live, so a second `[:rf.machine/destroy id]` re-runs the whole teardown: phantom `:rf.machine/destroyed` trace plus re-fired resource release. Codex's JVM probe measured exactly two destroyed traces for both explicit-then-destroy and final-then-destroy. That violates Spec 005 §Destroy is silent-idempotent, and the tree already names this precise failure mode for the sibling spawn-order channel in the comment at `finalize.cljc:690-698` (a later stale destroy "sees it live -> `teardown-live-actor!` RE-RUNS (phantom destroyed trace + re-fired resource release, violating silent-idempotent destroy)"). The dossier missed it entirely. **So the ruling is THREE sites, not two.**

2. **The dossier's §7.5 "never tested in either direction" is FALSE.** `final_state_cljs_test.cljc:236` is `dispatch-to-done-actor-reuses-no-such-handler` — a deliberately named D5 pin that finishes a singleton, dispatches again to the same id, and asserts `:rf.error/no-such-handler`, with an inline comment saying it must NOT become a new half-state. That is a behavioural pin, not an incidental `nil?` assertion, and it is **deliberately revised** by this ruling (see D5 below).

3. **"Nothing that worked stops working" overstates compatibility.** `registration.cljc` synthesises a fresh initial snapshot for ANY event when none exists (`(nil? existing-snap)` -> `(assoc @base-initial :rf/bootstrap-pending? true)`, ~`:476`, re-measure). So preservation means a late ORDINARY event — not only `[:rf.machine/start]` — births a new instance at a torn-down singleton's address. **Accepted deliberately, not overlooked** (see below).

4. **Definition-bearing address is NOT equivalent to singleton, and the "three paths" table understates the damage.** A spawned actor may sit at a `:fixed-actor-id` equal to its own registered machine type — the supported shape pinned by `fixed_actor_id_addressing_test.clj:484` — and its snapshot then DOES carry `:rf/machine-type`. So Option B's snapshot discriminator would miss real damage, and frame-destroy's **spawned** branch (`frame_destroy.cljc:~260`, which routes to `destroy-single-actor!`) reaches the very same unregister site. Only frame-destroy's SINGLETON branch preserves. **The rule protects DEFINITIONS regardless of what kind of actor occupied their keyword.**

Where the dossier won: its recommended DIRECTION, its predicate choice (`spec-from-registry`, not the snapshot discriminator), and its reading that the tree has no contract here — only three independent guesses. Codex reached the same direction independently.

### Why this ruling

- **Silent footgun in public API, and the worst-visibility kind.** Reachable with NO teardown code written by the author: a root-level `:final?` leaf triggers the D7 singleton auto-destroy and deletes the definition — a path the original bead never mentions. Dev hot reload re-runs `reg-machine` from the same source coords and `collision?` re-installs it silently, so the definition quietly comes back on every save and stays gone in production.
- **The harm is not confined to the actor destroyed.** `reg-machine` writes ONE registrar entry playing TWO roles — the singleton's ADDRESS and the shared TYPE DEFINITION every spawn resolves through. So after any repro, every later `[:rf.machine/spawn {:machine-id X}]` anywhere in the app fails `:rf.error/machine-spawn-unregistered-type`. `destroy.cljc:865-868` already names this exact harm ("stranding the replacement ... and every sibling actor of that type with it") for the replacement case; it applies identically here.
- **A shipped consumer is broken today.** `examples/capabilities/resources/resources/core.cljs` registers one `:resources.app/reader`, starts it at `:334`, stops it with `[:rf.machine/destroy :resources.app/reader]` at `:341`, and offers "Open in reader" again at `:478`. The second open has no definition to resolve. Stronger evidence than any hypothetical sign-in sequence.
- **A runtime actor teardown must not delete a load-time authoring artefact the author never asked it to touch.** Trust-the-programmer is a reason not to nag an author about something they chose; it is not a reason for destroy to reach past its own object.
- **The change is net-negative code and grows no API.** No new key, no new error, no new `:reason` member, no warning taxonomy, no second registry.

### Consistency with rf2-dokz (ruled 2026-09-08): exact, and this subsumes it

rf2-dokz routed a spawn at an occupied `:fixed-actor-id` through the ORDINARY destroy path under the EXISTING `:reason :explicit`, adding no key and no enum member, and wrote `*definition-preserved-at*` as a narrow one-address exception whose general argument was already stated in full at `destroy.cljc:865-868`. This ruling applies that same predicate generally and **deletes the var** — same principle, one level up, less code.

**Stated so the claim is not overstated:** rf2-dokz *had* to preserve (the replacement resolves its handler through that key microseconds later, so deleting it broke the operation in flight). Here nothing needs the definition immediately; the question is whether it is there LATER. rf2-dokz supplies the mechanism, the predicate and the argument — not the verdict. The verdict rests on the footgun and the shipped consumer.

### D5 is deliberately revised: lazy re-creation is ACCEPTED

After teardown a singleton address behaves EXACTLY as it did before its first start — an event arrives, no snapshot exists, the initial snapshot is synthesised. That is the elegant invariant and it needs no new state.

The alternative (preserve the definition but require an explicit restart) was considered and refused: an absent snapshot currently also means "never started", so distinguishing "finished" from "never started" requires a durable tombstone or a broader redesign of singleton birth. That is a larger design than the problem warrants and is exactly the ceremony the posture forbids.

`:rf.error/no-such-handler` remains the honest answer for an address carrying NO definition — a destroyed spawned actor, a never-registered id — and that coverage is retained.

**All line numbers measured at trunk `ff9f7a833f`. `destroy.cljc` is HOT — re-measure before touching.**

Replace the `not=` clause with `(nil? (resolver/spec-from-registry actor-id))`, keeping `db-swapped?` and the `owner-gone?` recheck in their present order (that recheck is the rf2-rbxdxa terminal-fence law — do not disturb it).

2. **`finalize.cljc:702`** (the D7 `:final?` singleton auto-destroy — `(rf.registrar/unregister! :event machine-id)`), same gate, likewise inside the existing `(when-not (owner-gone?))`.

3. **`destroy.cljc:118` `actor-live?`, body `:162-166` — THE AMENDMENT.** The registrar disjunct must no longer answer "live" for a definition-bearing entry. Keep registrar-only liveness for a **non-machine** entry (that is the stale/externally-installed per-instance case step 8 exists for); for a definition-bearing address require the snapshot. Preserve the snapshot disjunct and the guarded spawn-order/live-snapshot fallback untouched. **Do not** substitute `occupant-actor-live?` here — it deliberately ignores stale plain handlers and would change the other half of the behaviour.

No test names it (it is `^:private ^:dynamic`; the string appears only at `destroy.cljc:168,312,317,869,885` plus `.beads/issues.jsonl`).

HTML/React attributes do not share one boolean class. In particular, aria-* and data-* boolean values stringify, and booleanish attributes such as contentEditable, draggable, and spellCheck stringify both true and false. The current path therefore turns aria-expanded=true into a present attribute with the empty string, drops aria-expanded=false entirely, turns contentEditable=true into a bare attribute, and drops contentEditable=false. This is not a theoretical edge. Boolean ARIA state is ordinary SPA authoring, and contentEditable=false is the way a child opts out of an editable ancestor. Omitting that false marker changes the server DOM's semantics. Spec 011 also records that React attribute-only hydration mismatches are not guaranteed to be patched and do not reach onRecoverableError, so the wrong server attribute can survive hydration without the framework's mismatch signal. The separate structural-tree serializer already models the needed categories in implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/ui_tree.cljc. This is drift in the stock-Reagent-compatible hiccup emitter, not a missing design. ## Verified evidence Verified at source tip 52283022e9; the relevant html_helpers.cljc, ui_tree.cljc, and ssr_emit_test.clj blobs are byte-identical to origin/main at 82c112928c. - implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc:563-626 — attr-string branches on the value alone. Lines 595-597 emit every true bare and omit every false/nil before considering the attribute name. - implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc:778-794 — the standard renderer sends DOM attrs through attr-string. - implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/streaming.cljc:391-404 — the streaming shell uses the same helper, so both hiccup SSR modes are affected. - implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr.cljc:48 and implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/emit.cljc:883-920 — this is the public render-to-string implementation installed into the headless/Reagent-compatible adapter path. - Focused JVM probe of the current emitter: aria-expanded true -> aria-expanded false -> contentEditable true ->
...
nested contentEditable false -> the child has no attribute - Focused probe against the repository's installed react-dom 19.2.0: aria-expanded true -> aria-expanded="true" aria-expanded false -> aria-expanded="false" contentEditable true -> contentEditable="true" contentEditable false -> contentEditable="false" For the nested editable-parent case, React emits the child's explicit false marker; the current SSR emitter emits
locked
, so the section inherits editability. - implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/ui_tree.cljc:598-650 already distinguishes aria/data, booleanish, overloaded-boolean, true boolean, and ordinary boolean-valued attributes. - implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr/emit_ui_tree_cljs_test.cljc:238-256 pins contentEditable="false" and aria-hidden="false" on that serializer. - implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_emit_test.clj:716-735 covers only the true-presence class (disabled/required) and therefore stays green while the other classes are wrong. - spec/004B-UI-Tree-and-Conversion.md:552 and 565-567 records the React 19.2 attribute classes; spec/011-SSR.md:842 records the consequence of attribute-only hydration drift. ## Recommended minimal fix Make html-helpers/attr-string classify boolean values by attribute name before emitting them, using the already-shipped ui_tree classification as the local reference. Prefer one small shared classifier/roster if that reduces drift cleanly; a faithful local reuse is also acceptable if sharing would distort the two deliberately separate emitters. Preserve the existing public API and the current escape, security-strip, and attribute-name-validation order. At minimum, aria-* and data-* booleans and the booleanish contentEditable/draggable/spellCheck family must stringify true and false; true boolean and overloaded-boolean attributes must retain presence semantics; booleans on ordinary non-boolean attributes must not become arbitrary bare attributes. The implementation should remain a small serialization correction, not a renderer redesign. ## Posture rationale Excellent SSR ergonomics means authors can write the same natural SPA hiccup they use on the client, especially normal accessibility state such as aria-expanded open?, without hand-stringifying booleans to compensate for the server. The fix is compact and already has a correct sibling implementation to follow. It adds no abstraction users must learn and avoids a broad compatibility project. ## Non-goals - No new public API, protocol, renderer option, or hydration detector. - No rewrite of the structural-tree serializer, component resolution, style serialization, attribute ordering, or DOM-property alias system. - No emulation of React development warnings. - No attempt to exhaustively clone every React DOM implementation detail beyond the boolean attribute classes needed for server/client semantic parity. - No unrelated security-filter or escaping changes. ## Related and duplicate search Searched every bead status and full issue text for ARIA, aria-*, contentEditable, booleanish, overloaded boolean, attr-string, generic boolean, false attribute, attribute semantics, and render-to-string. No issue owns this defect. rf2-51tgp is the closed oncommand security-filter gap and does not concern value classification; the Hicasso contenteditable beads concern controlled-input documentation and are unrelated. Git history across all local and remote refs found the generic value-only branch introduced by 9cfc27065c (2026-05-14), the focused presence-only coverage, and the later richer structural-tree serializer (260fe87d57). It found no commit that adds name-aware boolean classification to html-helpers/attr-string. The latest relevant source blobs match origin/main. ## Uncertainty The exact internal sharing shape is intentionally left to the implementer because render-to-string and emit-ui-tree consume different tree representations and Spec 004B says not to conflate their pipelines. The behavioral requirement is certain from direct output comparison. A browser may canonicalize bare true attributes differently by element, but that does not rescue false ARIA/booleanish values: the emitted marker is absent, while React explicitly emits "false".

title: implementor skill: foundation gate can pass a reference-keyed live sub-cache
description:
## Scope

Correct the completion and EP-006 verification workflow in `skills/re-frame2-implementor/**` so a non-CLJS port cannot be declared foundation-complete while its live subscription cache is keyed by host reference identity. Keep the corpus score as an honest corpus score; add only the one port-owned live witness needed for the observability gap already acknowledged by the pinned Spec. Limit supporting checks/evals to this outcome.

## Correctness finding

The skill makes the conformance corpus the acceptance test and its Done gate accepts a green `:core/* + :identity/* + :data-classification/*` run as foundation completion. Its EP-006 row specifically calls the two `:identity/cedn1` Mode-B fixtures "sub-cache fixtures." Those fixtures never touch a frame, `subscribe`, a cache slot, ref-counting, or disposal: they call the canonical-identity primitive directly. The owning Spec explicitly says the missing live assertion would subscribe one query through two distinct host allocations and observe one cache-slot creation.

A TypeScript port can therefore implement CEDN-1 correctly, use Immer for structural sharing, but store query arrays in a native reference-keyed `Map`. Every required fixture can pass and the skill can report v1 completion even though equal freshly allocated queries create separate derived containers forever. This is a false-green proof of a pattern-required runtime contract, not a request for broader coverage.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/SKILL.md:9-10,31,52,70-75` repeatedly says the corpus is the acceptance test and defines Done as the three required fixture families being green.
- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/phase-2-impl-order.md:35` describes `:identity/cedn1` as the EP-006 "sub-cache fixtures"; lines 40 and 68 make fixture-set greens acceptance gates, and line 78 permits completion after those discovered gates.
- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/conformance.md:78-90` requires a port-owned self-test only when a mandated surface has no fixture. It does not cover a fixture that exists but observes only a prerequisite, and line 90 equates `N / N` with conformance against the claim.
- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:793-820` requires `rf=`-keyed live lookup and explains that native JS `Map`/array identity breaks de-duplication, ref-count convergence, and disposal. It also notes that Immer supplies neither value equality nor a value-keyed map.
- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:824-829` says the two fixtures assert only canonical cache-key identity and explicitly leaves the deeper live-runtime assertion as follow-up because the current Mode-A DSL cannot subscribe two distinct host allocations.
- `spec/conformance/fixtures/sub-cache-dedupes-equal-query-v.edn:36-76` is a Mode-B `:fixture/calls` file containing only `:canonical-identical` and `:canonical-distinct` calls. Its companion `sub-cache-key-map-arg-order.edn` likewise tests canonical bytes/identity only.
- `implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_runner.cljc:1026-1039` executes those calls through `identity/identical-identity?`; no subscription-cache code is reached.
- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/evals/evals.json:4-25` is trigger-only, so no outcome regression prevents the skill from accepting this corpus-green/runtime-red port.
- The focused implementor guards are currently green, but they check EP order, required family names, partition vocabulary, and bead leakage; neither exercises this completion invariant (`python scripts/check_skill_implementor_order.py --self-test`, `python scripts/check_skill_implementor_order.py --verbose --ci`, `python scripts/check_skill_implementor_partition_drift.py --self-test`, and `python scripts/check_skill_implementor_partition_drift.py --verbose --ci`).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a minimum TypeScript-shaped port, implement the CEDN-1 canonical operations correctly and use a native `Map<QueryVector, CacheEntry>` for the live sub-cache.
2. Run all claimed required-family fixtures. The two named sub-cache fixtures pass because they invoke only the canonical identity functions, and the required-foundation score can reach `claimed-applicable / claimed-applicable`.
3. Allocate two separate arrays with equal contents, for example `q1 = ['editor/field-error', 'title']` and `q2 = ['editor/field-error', 'title']`, and subscribe both in one frame.
4. Observe two native-Map keys, two derived containers, and two first-run computations. Releasing the readers cannot converge on one slot's last-reader disposal even though the skill's current completion proof is green.

## Failure scenario / invariant

A React view constructs its query array afresh on every render. Under reference-keyed lookup, every render misses the cache, repeats the subscription computation, and leaves an independently referenced entry whose lifecycle cannot converge with the prior readers. The port is reported conformant despite violating the required invariant: two separately allocated query vectors that are `rf=` must resolve to one live cache entry, one shared computation, and one ref-count; that entry disposes exactly once after the last equal reader releases it. A non-equal query must remain a different entry.

## Recommended minimal fix

Add one explicit EP-006 completion proof to the skill: on a host whose ordinary map keys collections by reference (or whenever the selected cache mechanism does not intrinsically provide `rf=` keys), run a port-owned live test using two separately allocated but `rf=`-equal query values. Require the result at the EP-006 checkpoint and in the v1 Done gate alongside the corpus score. In `conformance.md`, name this as the pinned Spec's known observability gap: the existing identity fixtures prove the canonical-key prerequisite, not live cache wiring, so a port-owned self-test is required even though fixture files exist.

Keep the proof mechanism-agnostic. The port may use an `rf=`-keyed persistent map or an interned canonical key; the skill should require the observable one-slot/one-lifecycle result, not prescribe a library. Add a focused outcome regression for the skill so a corpus-green/live-red TypeScript-shaped port is diagnosed as incomplete.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The published EP-006 workflow and Done checklist explicitly distinguish canonical-identity fixture success from live sub-cache success. A non-CLJS/reference-keyed host cannot be called EP-006-, foundation-, or v1-complete until the live witness below has run green; the reported conformance fraction remains the fixture result rather than being silently inflated.
2. The required executable witness creates `q1` and `q2` through separate host allocations, first proves `rf=(q1,q2)`, subscribes both in the same frame through the public/runtime subscription path, and observes exactly one cache slot, one derived container/first-run computation, and a shared ref-count. Releasing one reader keeps the slot live; releasing the second removes it and invokes disposal exactly once.
3. Negative control: a third query with a different argument value is not `rf=` to `q1` and produces a second cache slot and second first-run computation. This prevents a degenerate implementation that interns or collapses every query from satisfying the positive witness.
4. Non-vacuity mutation control: temporarily replace the value-keyed lookup in the test port with the host's native reference-keyed `Map`. The existing `sub-cache-dedupes-equal-query-v.edn`, `sub-cache-key-map-arg-order.edn`, and required-foundation corpus run remain green, while the live witness exits nonzero on two slots/two first-runs. Restore the conforming lookup and record the same witness green.
5. A focused checked-in skill outcome eval presents that exact corpus-green/live-red TypeScript-shaped checkpoint. The expected result withholds EP-006/v1 completion, names reference-keyed live lookup as the port bug, and asks/runs the live witness; a paired one-slot control is accepted. The eval must execute through the skill's normal route, not merely search for a phrase in Markdown.
6. Existing implementor order/partition self-tests and CI modes remain green. Any focused guard added for this invariant has its own red control (remove the live-proof requirement and the guard/eval fails) and does not pin a copied fixture catalogue or implementation token.

## Non-goals

- No new Mode-A conformance operator, cross-host fixture protocol, generated fixture translation, or rewrite of the conformance corpus.
- No mandate for Immutable.js, CEDN interning, or any one cache implementation.
- No expansion into every subscription invalidation/performance law; this issue owns only equal-query live cache identity and its reader lifecycle.
- No change to CEDN-1, `rf=` semantics, capability tags, scoring arithmetic, or the CLJS reference implementation.
- No broad behavioral-eval platform, generic conformance hardening, compatibility layer, or documentation polish.

## Related / duplicate search

All-status census covered 1,133 beads. Exact title/description/notes searches for `sub-cache`, `value-keyed`, `reference-keyed`, `rf=`, `Immer`, `sub-cache-dedupes`, `live-runtime assertion`, `Mode-A harness primitive`, `cache key`, and implementor/conformance acceptance found no bead owning this false-green port-completion outcome.

- `rf2-nuy8x` (closed) reduced the implementor skill to the pinned-spec/fixture loop and added the current required-family gates; it did not require a live two-allocation sub-cache proof. This bug is a correctness residual of that completed workflow, not a duplicate of its ergonomic reduction.
- `rf2-rzeko` (open) owns exactly-once disposal of stock Reagent `Reaction`s in the CLJS adapter. It does not cover non-CLJS query-key equality, duplicate live cache slots, or implementor-skill completion evidence.
- `rf2-a9l6e` (open) owns the MCP conformance tool's compatibility-profile UX, not a port runtime or this skill's proof boundary.
- The owning Spec's line-829 follow-up note is prose, not a tracked bead, and it proposes a future corpus primitive; this task deliberately takes the smaller skill-level port-owned witness.

title: CLAUDE.md item (d): the MSYS ref:path mangling trigger is a slash in the REF plus a path STARTING WITH A DOT, not 'both contain a slash' — wrong in both directions, including one that marks origin/main:.gitignore safe
description:
CLAUDE.md instrument item (d) states the wrong trigger for the MSYS `<ref>:<path>` mangling, and it is
wrong in BOTH directions — including the one that marks a mangled form as safe.

## What item (d) says

> **(d) `git show <ref>:<path>` mangles when the REF AND THE PATH BOTH contain a slash** — MSYS reads
> `a/b:c/d` as a colon-separated POSIX path LIST and rewrites it to `a\b;c\d`. Measured across all four
> combinations: `HEAD:CLAUDE.md`, `HEAD:.github/workflows/test.yml` and `origin/main:CLAUDE.md` all exit
> 0; `origin/main:.github/workflows/test.yml` exits 128 ...

## Measured 2026-09-18 at trunk `d7160a5a63`, Git Bash, `git rev-parse "<ref>:<path>"`

Mangling told apart from an honest not-found by the ERROR TEXT, not the exit code (both exit 128): a
mangled argument is echoed back as `origin\main;...`, while a missing path reads
`fatal: path '...' does not exist in 'origin/main'`.

    origin/main:docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md     OK        both contain a slash
    origin/main:spec/API.md                        OK        both contain a slash
    origin/main:tools/xray/spec/API.md             OK        both contain a slash
    origin/main:implementation/.gitignore          OK        dot only in a LATER segment
    origin/main:CLAUDE.md                          OK
    origin/main:.beads/PRIME.md                    MANGLED   'origin\main;.beads\PRIME.md'
    origin/main:.github/workflows/test.yml         MANGLED
    origin/main:.clj-kondo/config.edn              MANGLED
    origin/main:.gitignore                         MANGLED   PATH HAS NO SLASH AT ALL
    main:.beads/PRIME.md                           OK        no slash in the REF
    HEAD:.beads/PRIME.md                           OK
    MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 origin/main:.beads/PRIME.md OK        the prescribed fix works

**The determinant is a slash in the REF plus a PATH WHOSE FIRST CHARACTER IS A DOT.** Whether the path
contains a slash does not matter: `origin/main:spec/API.md` (both slashed) is fine, and
`origin/main:.gitignore` (path unslashed) mangles.

## Why the wrong trigger was written down

Item (d)'s four combinations CONFOUND the two variables. Its slashed path, `.github/workflows/test.yml`,
also begins with a dot, and its unslashed path, `CLAUDE.md`, does not — so every case it measured fits
"the path has a slash" and "the path starts with a dot" equally well. The measurement was sound; the
generalisation picked the wrong one of two hypotheses the data could not separate.

## Why it matters, in both directions

- **Under-inclusive — the dangerous half.** Read literally, (d) marks `origin/main:.gitignore` safe. It
  fails loudly, so this is only silent where stderr is suppressed and stdout piped — which (d) itself
  says is exactly how it bites.
- **Over-inclusive — the half that discredits the guard.** A reader who tries (d) on
  `origin/main:spec/API.md`, sees exit 0, and concludes the item is stale drops `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1`
  altogether — and then meets `.github/workflows/`, the dot-leading directory the mayor's clause-5
  merge check reads every tick. An overbroad claim invites refutation by its first counterexample, and
  the refutation carries the TRUE half away with it.

## The fix

Correct the trigger sentence and the "four combinations" account in item (d) to the measured
determinant; keep both prescribed guards, which are right; and say that the original measurement was
confounded rather than wrong. **Re-measure at your own trunk before writing** — the table above is
evidence to reproduce, not text to paste.
notes:
---

## DISPATCHED — BUNDLED, DO NOT DISPATCH SEPARATELY (mayor, 2026-09-18, trunk d7160a5a63)

**This item is in flight as one of THREE beads carried by a single worker on branch
`worker/clmd-fixes-3`** (worktree `C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/clmd-fixes-3`): rf2-86g1q,
rf2-za56k and rf2-vwst8. All three are corrections to `CLAUDE.md`, and instrument items (a) through (z)
sit on one physical line of it, so a second worker on any of the three would conflict with the first
at merge.

**Clears when that branch's PR MERGES** — not on the worker's report. The mayor closes all three
beads after the merge.
Merged-PR audit #10054 (99d98c1b94370b2701780b32a3aab74e296e054a; merged 2026-09-18T07:09:10Z). Completeness: All three correction requests addressed plus the dependent item-(s) cross-reference; unchanged instrumentation guidance preserved. Correctness: Independent diff-word comparison confirms limited prose edits; reproduced slash-ref/dot-path mangling with clean path/ref controls, checked repaired macro source and positive/negative workflow-history diffs. Implementation quality: Self-derived history boundary avoids expiring offsets and keeps the repair in prose without adding gates. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.
close_reason:
Done — item (d)'s trigger corrected. PR #10054, merged at `99d98c1b94`.

**Before**: "mangles when the REF AND THE PATH BOTH contain a slash … Measured across all four
combinations". **After**: "mangles when the REF contains a slash AND the PATH BEGINS WITH A DOT —
whether the path itself contains a slash is irrelevant", with the re-measured cases, the rule for
telling mangling from not-found **by error text rather than exit code**, and a statement that the

**Re-measured by the worker at `origin/main` `b05f8b37c6`**, not transcribed from this bead:

  `CLAUDE.md`, and the unslashed refs `main:.gitignore`, `HEAD:.github/workflows/test.yml`.
- exit 128 MANGLED: `.gitignore`, `.beads/PRIME.md`, `.github/workflows/test.yml`,
  `.clj-kondo/config.edn`, and `refs/heads/main:.gitignore` — reading
  `fatal: ambiguous argument 'origin\main;.gitignore': unknown revision or path not in the working tree.`
- exit 128 honest not-found: `fatal: path 'spec/no-such-file.md' does not exist in 'origin/main'`.
- `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` exit 0 on all four mangled cases; `git show` behaves identically; the

**It sharpened the finding beyond this bead**: a leading `./` or `../` is NOT rewritten

**Named out of fence, not touched**: `tools/story/spec/findings/parity-2026-09/` (the `fable/report.md`

## Shared: one PR carried three beads

**Declared fence extension, accepted**: item (h) restated (d)'s OLD trigger ("there a ref and a path

**File health** (Python on bytes, worker): `cr=161 crlf=161 bare_lf=0` before and after, still

`i/lf w/crlf`, `cr=161 crlf=161 bare_lf=0`; **the stance block is intact at exactly `:7-11`, and
`ai/assemble-brief.sh` still extracts it 5/5 verbatim** — the dependency every future dispatch brief

**Gates — stated unfavourably**: `check_readme_links.py --ci` exit 0 but **vacuous for this diff** (23

demonstrating it does not cover repo-root markdown. Restore verified against `HEAD:CLAUDE.md`

**Nothing grades this file's prose**: the evidence for each correction is its measurement, below.

**Mayor's merge verification**: all five clauses at trunk `8e88c9b25f` — rollup **88** with the

branch AND full head `d151ead7c1c6e1561eec3bebd6f77225692dc418`, not a draft; clause 5 control **1**,
reading **0**. **Direction re-derived against the trunk as it stood after #10050 AND #10052 merged**

title: review(xray/epoch-panel): senior-developer findings, 8 ranked, 2 spec chapters drift, trunk 9555881fe3 (2026-09-17)
description:
# Senior review: xray-epoch-panel

Reviewer persona: a senior engineer who has built trace viewers and time-travel debuggers and knows that a projection over an event log is where every off-by-one, every stale cache and every "the badge says green but the row is red" bug lives.
Tree: xray-review-sep17 worktree, trunk 9555881fe3
Scope read: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/{view.cljs (6,370, in full), projection.cljc (4,241, in full), format.cljc (725), badge.cljc (544), icons.cljc (69)}, panels/epoch_panel.cljs (332), panels/event/{event_status_colour.cljc (318), icons.cljc (48)}, panels/l2_timeline.cljc (458), panels/reply_envelope.cljc (919), panels/issues_ribbon_helpers.cljc (411), plus panels/shared/focus_resolver.cljc, app_db_diff_subs.cljs:120-140 and spine.cljs:250-300/488-525 as the consumers' inputs — ~14,400 lines; tests under tools/xray/test/.../panels/epoch/ skimmed by grep for what they pin. Framework side read for the refusal arms: implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc (1795-1830, 2101-2150, 2229-2300, 2690-2730, 3160-3232, 4103-4177), router/diagnostics.cljc:31-73, fx.cljc:1512-1548, trace/projection.cljc:291-334, subs/memo.cljc.
Owning specs consulted: tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md (§9.1 epoch panel 1677-4030 in full; §1, §6, §8, §17.1.5 skimmed), 019-Cross-Cutting-Insight.md (in full), 002-Time-Travel.md (in full), DESIGN-RATIONALE.md (Locks #7, #11 and the supersession table).

## Findings, ranked

### 1. A refused dispatch (no handler) paints a red L2 row, and the Epoch panel silently shows a DIFFERENT epoch for it  [CONFIRMED] [severity: high] [kind: correctness] [size: M]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/shared/focus_resolver.cljc:64-73 and :84-92; tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/spine.cljs:254-280 and :513-521; tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch_panel.cljs:196-199
- What: `nil :epoch-id` means both "cold start, show the latest" and "this focus has no epoch at all", and the resolver cannot tell them apart, so a router refusal that settles no epoch focuses the HEAD epoch's cascade under a red row for another event.
- Evidence: `:rf.event/dispatched` is emitted at enqueue before the handler is resolved (router.cljc:4160-4171 — a nil handler-meta makes `no-emit?` false), and `handle-no-handler!` (diagnostics.cljc:31-73) emits `:rf.error/no-such-handler` inside `process-event!`'s handler scope (router.cljc:3194-3207), so the trace carries the dispatch-id and `group-by-event` (core trace/projection.cljc:291-334) forms an L2 bundle `{:dispatched … :other [no-such-handler]}`; `has-error?` (event_status_colour.cljc:230-234) paints it ✗. No run-start/run-end fires and no epoch record exists (router.cljc:3189-3192; Story's own fix commit 20038afb74 says the same: "settles no epoch for it"). Clicking the row: `epoch-id-for-event-bundle` returns nil (spine.cljs:275-280), the reducer stores `:epoch-id nil` + `:mode :retro` (spine.cljs:559-567), `compose-focus` passes nil through (spine.cljs:513-521), and `resolve-focus-status nil history` answers `:focused` with `(peek history)` (focus_resolver.cljc:68-69, 85-92). The Issues ribbon's focused-epoch scope resolves the same way. Xray source names `no-such-handler` nowhere (0 hits under tools/xray/src; control: `:rf.error/handler-exception` 6 hits in 2 files). PR #9878 is not findable in git history (`--all --grep='9878'` 0; control `--grep='no-such-handler'` 73).
- Action: decide: A — carry "focus resolved to no epoch" as a distinct focus status (e.g. the spine keeps `:dispatch-id` and marks `:epoch-id ::none`, or the resolver takes the bundle and answers `:no-epoch` when `:dispatch-id` is set but no record matches) and give the Epoch panel a one-line empty state naming the refusal ("refused before any handler ran — see the Issues feed"); or B — project a one-step DISPATCH-only cascade from the L2 bundle with the refusal card under it. A is a morning; B needs a spec sentence in 021 §9.1.3 (the "every epoch starts here" row) either way.

### 2. Every `:rf.error/*` outside a seven-op closed set leaves the panel `:ok` with no card while L2 and the ribbon go red; the effect-map-shape refusal is the vivid case  [CONFIRMED] [severity: high] [kind: correctness] [size: M]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc:3087-3137 (`cascade-exception-ops`), :3703-3723 (`epoch-outcome`), :1968-1982 and :2223-2251 (the "silently ignored / DROPPED" other-key model), :3007-3037 (`attach-violations` drop arms)
- What: `epoch-outcome` only sees exceptions from `cascade-exception-ops` and schema violations, so in-band refusals and other error traces in the epoch's `:trace-events` (`:rf.error/effect-map-shape`, `legacy-runtime-root`, `classification-effect-shape`, `sub-exception`, `cofx-value-invalid`, …; 139 emit-site hits across 19 core files) never reach a step, the outcome or a card — while `event-bundle-outcome` counts any error trace.
- Evidence: rf2-04tx's router (router.cljc:2101-2113, settle cond :2704-2712) REFUSES a foreign top-level effect key: `:error` outcome, no `:db`/`:rf.db/runtime` commit, no `:fx`. The t1 `:rf.event/db-pending` still fires earlier (router.cljc:1826-1827), so the projection renders a HANDLER `:db` diff of a value that was never committed, `db-commit?` (projection.cljc:2075-2079) is false so no `:db` row, no `:rf.fx/do-fx` fires so `other-effect-rows` is empty and `side-effects-step` returns nil (:2340-2350) — the cascade reads as a clean `{:db}` handler, `data-rf-xray-outcome="ok"`. The projection comments (:1974-1982, :2233-2237) and 021 §9.1.10.6 :3819-3821 still describe the pre-rf2-04tx runtime ("silently DROPPED — never executed, never traced"). Same class: `attach-violations` drops a `:fx-args` violation when no SIDE EFFECTS step projected (:3031-3033 `(if i … s)`), reachable for a handler whose only fx fails schema validation (fx.cljc:1520-1548 skips it; no per-fx op to build a row from — PLAUSIBLE for that last hop), whereas `attach-exceptions` has a HANDLER catch-all (:3646-3655). The docstring at :3707-3709 and 021 :3724-3727 claim parity with `event-bundle-outcome`; the code does not have it.
- Action: add one generic pass after `attach-exceptions`: every `:op-type :error` / `:rf.error/*` trace in the record not already attached lands on its best step (effect-map-shape → SIDE EFFECTS, synthesising the step; `sub-exception` → SUBSCRIPTIONS; else HANDLER) as the shared exception card, and `attach-violations` uses the same catch-all. Rewrite the two "silently dropped" paragraphs (projection.cljc:1968-1982, 2233-2237; 021 §9.1.10.6 :3811-3824) to say the runtime REFUSES the event. Pin with one fixture per refusal op.

### 3. The view re-decides which record is focused, and decides differently from the projection  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs:6278-6279 and :4159-4262; tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/app_db_diff_subs.cljs:128-136
- What: `Panel` reads `:rf.xray/selected-epoch-record` (no head-fallback: `(when selected-id …)`) beside the pipeline sub whose `:record` DOES head-fall-back, so whenever `:epoch-id` is nil the HANDLER `:db` block renders with `db-before nil`, `db-after` = the t1 value, and every inspector site/mount id keyed on `(:epoch-id record)` = nil.
- Evidence: view.cljs:4222-4229 takes `db-before` and `db-after` from the ctx record; :4243-4251 keys `:mount-id`/`:site-id` on `(:epoch-id record)`; the docstring at :4215-4217 admits "nil renders as db-before absent". nil focus with non-empty history is a designed state, not a corner: spine.cljs:504-512 returns nil on purpose for a multi-frame or evicted head ("Panels uniformly treat nil as 'no pin, use the head fallback'"), cold start does it, and finding 1 does it on every refused dispatch. The effect is a full post-handler tree with no diff annotations (reads as "handler changed nothing") and expansion/zoom state shared across every head-fallback epoch.
- Action: drop the second read; thread `(:record pipeline)` into ctx as `:selected-epoch-record` (the projection already chose it). Panel goes from three reads to two, and the rf2-k97c.3 docstring paragraph about hoisting it can shrink. One node-lane test: head-fallback focus renders `rf-xray-epoch-handler-db-full-with-diff` with a `:before`.

### 4. `:rf.xray/epoch-pipeline` re-projects and re-renders the whole panel on every host epoch, even pinned RETRO on an unchanged record  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: perf] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch_panel.cljs:192-233 (inputs :193, `:epoch-history` in the value :232); tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs:6260-6270
- What: the composite's inputs are `[:rf.xray/focus] [:rf.xray/epoch-history]`, so each settled epoch re-runs `find-epoch-record` (O(history) `some`) and `project-numbered` (O(trace-events), with `exception-rows` computed three times inside `project`), and because the value embeds the whole history vector it can never compare `=`, so the value-equality propagation gate (spec/006:962; memo.cljc:79) never cuts and the 6k-line Panel re-renders per settle.
- Evidence: read of the sub body; the comment at :225-231 says history is pinned on the value to avoid a second sub "in the per-row hot path", which trades one cheap sub for a per-settle re-render. There is no memoisation anywhere in projection.cljc (0 `memoize`/`atom`/`volatile!`; control: `long-step-threshold-ms` found at :4157), so nothing can serve a stale result — the cost is all recompute. 021 §9.1.9 :3169 lists the yield without `:epoch-history`.
- Action: layer it: a `:rf.xray/focused-epoch-record` sub (focus + history → record, `identical?` across settles when pinned) feeds `:rf.xray/epoch-pipeline` with inputs `[[:rf.xray/focused-epoch-record]]`; resolve the DISPATCH step's parent epoch from a tiny `:rf.xray/parent-epoch-id` sub keyed on the record's `:parent-dispatch-id` instead of shipping the history. Finding 3's fix falls out of the same sub.

### 5. The LOCKED badge inventory is neither complete nor enforced: `:INTERCEPTORS` is emitted but not in `badge-set`; `:SCHEMA-HOT-RELOAD` is in the set but never emitted  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: spec-drift] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/projection.cljc:4193-4223 (`badge-set`), :3478 and :3500 (`:badge :INTERCEPTORS`), :2981-2983 (`attach-violations` docstring citing `hot-reload-step`); tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md:1761-1765
- What: 021 says "The inventory is LOCKED — the projection's `badge-set` enforces that every emitted step's `:badge` is a member", but the set is stale in both directions and nothing in src enforces it.
- Evidence: `:badge :INTERCEPTORS` 2 emits vs 0 in `badge-set`; `:badge :SCHEMA-HOT-RELOAD` 0 emits (control `:badge :SIDE-EFFECTS` 1) while the tail step was retired (021 :3269-3272, rf2-7gf7v); `hot-reload-step` has 0 definitions (control `(side-effects-step ` 1 call); `valid-badge?` has 0 src callers (only tests); `badge-set-test` (projection_cljs_test.cljc:3419-3430) builds a record with no authored interceptors so the missing member is never exercised; `badge_cljs_test` iterates the set and so blesses the stale member. The view has its own `:INTERCEPTORS` colour (view.cljs:2932-2933), which is why nothing looks wrong.
- Action: `#{… :INTERCEPTORS …}` minus `:SCHEMA-HOT-RELOAD`; fix the two docstrings; have `project` assert `valid-badge?` in dev or have the test project a fixture with an authored interceptor. While there: 021 §9.1.3 :1720/:1723 name `:rf.flow/recomputed` and `:rf.view/render` as the driving traces; the code and 021's own §9.1.10.1 :3198/:3202 say `:rf.flow/computed` / `:rf.view/rendered`.

### 6. DESIGN-RATIONALE Lock #11 (handler-coord fallback with a `(?)` chip) is not honoured by the DISPATCH source label  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: spec-drift] [size: S]
- Where: tools/xray/spec/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md:425-472; tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/epoch/view.cljs:2151-2171; tools/xray/spec/021-Dynamic-Panel-Designs.md:3024 and :3028-3036
- What: the lock rules "Handler-coord fallback via `:rf.trace/trigger-handler`, inline `(?)` annotation when the dispatch coord is missing"; the code renders a plain span (`coord-link` no-coord branch) and 021 §9.1.6.3 documents `:machine-spawn` as "none" and vanilla sources as call-site-only.
- Evidence: view.cljs has 0 `trigger-handler` reads (control: projection.cljc 3, all in `exception-source-coord` :3177-3188 for the exception card); `dispatch-source-label` passes only the call-site coord. The lock is not in the supersession table (DESIGN-RATIONALE.md:941-945 lists #6, #8, #10 only).
- Action: decide: A — implement it (on nil call-site coord, resolve `(rf/handler-meta {:source :store :kind :event :id event-id})` and render `coord-link` with a `(?)` glyph + title "handler's coord, dispatch was synthesised") — S; or B — retire Lock #11 as superseded by 021 §9.1.6.3's per-source enrichment (parent-epoch chip, state-path link), adding it to the supersession table — S, spec-only. The `:machine-spawn` row is the one case where B leaves an inert label.
