description:
# Senior review: core-instrumentation-classification

Reviewer persona: senior observability/privacy engineer; burned by dev-only instrumentation leaking, redaction failing open, listener fan-out blocking the caller, and sentinel aliasing. Every "always-on" claim judged against what survives `goog.DEBUG=false` / `-Dre-frame.debug=false`.
Tree: review-sep16 worktree, trunk d89a41e057
Scope read: implementation/core/src/re_frame/{trace,error_emit,event_emit,emit_substrate,error,observability,elision,classification,projection,privacy,privacy/url,performance,path,recordable,test_support,test_helpers}.cljc and trace/{tooling,projection,cascade}.cljc (~12,000 lines; trace, trace/tooling, error_emit, elision, classification, observability, projection read in full). Grep/sed-scoped for the census: router.cljc emit-frame-destroyed! and capture-op sites, frame.cljc 955-1162, source_coords.cljc, subs.cljc 826-930, cofx.cljc raise-removed!, events.cljc 1350-1466, fx.cljc emit-fx-error!, schemas/validate.cljc, machines/{error_emit,lifecycle_fx/*}.cljc, ssr/{boot,egress,response,error_projector}.cljc, ssr-ring/streaming.clj, test/re_frame/error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj (938 lines).
Owning specs consulted: spec/009-Instrumentation.md (§Production builds 1082-1420, §Error contract / promotion criterion 1676-1945, §Error event catalogue preamble + rows incl. the `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` per-arm paragraph 1962-2004), spec/015-Data-Classification.md (full; §process default), spec/Security.md §Production gates (89-183), spec/Ownership.md (full).

## Findings, ranked

### 1. `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` source-coord fallback attributes a dead-frame DISPATCH to a same-named SUB, and `route-frame?` is derived from the same missing `:op`  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness]
- Where: implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc:431-448 (`error-source-coord`); implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:2311 (`emit-frame-destroyed!` 3-arity delegates with `nil` op), 2339-2353 (4-arity builds `(when op {:op op})` and passes `(nil? op)` as route-frame?); the `capture-op` call sites at 4385/4404/4455/4574/4591/4684 pass nil "for an ordinary address-directed dispatch".
- What: the ordinary dispatch path never stamps `:op`, so `error-source-coord` falls through `case op` to `(or (coords-for :sub id) (coords-for :event id))`, and a legal same-keyword sub/event pair (acknowledged in error_emit.cljc under rf2-xgkgx) stamps the DISPATCH failure with the SUBSCRIPTION's `:source-coord`; the same `(nil? op)` is also what decides whether the record is routed to the frame's own sink, conflating "realm known" with "op captured".
- Evidence: traced end to end: `case op :dispatch/:dispatch-sync -> [:event]`, `:subscribe -> [:sub]`, else the sub-first `or`. subs.cljc:1111-1112 stamps `:op :subscribe` at its `emit-error-both!`, so the SUB side is unambiguous and only the EVENT side falls through. `source_coords.cljc` `error-coords-for [kind id]` is keyed by kind, so the registry can answer correctly if asked. Control for the "never stamps" zero: `:op :subscribe` at subs.cljc:1112 and the six `capture-op` sites are the only `:op` producers reaching `emit-frame-destroyed!` (Grep `:op :dispatch` / `:op :subscribe` / `capture-op` in router.cljc + subs.cljc).
- Action: stamp `:op :dispatch` / `:op :dispatch-sync` at every router `emit-frame-destroyed!` site (the router always knows which it is), carry "captured op" as its own boolean for `route-frame?`, and delete the sub-first `or` fallback so an unknown realm is a nil coord rather than a guess.

### 2. The process-default sink (the ONLY door for frameless / dead-incarnation records) receives `:exception :rf/redacted` and `:tags :rf/redacted`, so the records that most need a shipper arrive with nothing to ship  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: ergonomics]
- Where: implementation/core/src/re_frame/projection.cljc:382-423 (`project-error-record` walk-slots `:exception` through `elide-wire-value` at 422-423 whenever the profile is not `:rf.egress/public-error`); implementation/core/src/re_frame/elision.cljc:1296-1314 (`live-frame?` false and no `:rf.egress/include-sensitive? true` -> the WHOLE value becomes `rf.privacy/redacted-sentinel`); implementation/core/src/re_frame/observability.cljc:572-588 (`route-error-record!` keeps `:exception` top-level and pushes every non-summary key into `:tags` before projecting).
- What: every record that reaches the process default BECAUSE it has no live frame (`:rf.error/no-frame-context`, `:rf.error/ambient-frame-refused`, `:rf.error/bad-frame-provider-arg`, `:rf.error/malformed-hydration-payload` frameless arm, `:rf.error/frame-teardown-failed` with `route-frame? false`, fresco compute-sub `:rf.error/sub-exception`) has its `:exception` and its entire `:tags` map (including the framework-composed `:reason` and `:hook-failures`) collapsed to the sentinel, while the identical record under a live frame carries the exception through (the walker acts on classified paths and marks; an exception object is an opaque leaf) — frame liveness has nothing to do with whether an exception message is sensitive, so this is inconsistency, not policy.
- Evidence: read the three code paths above. Spec 015 §process default pins only "tree slots project to `:rf/redacted` while the summary ids stay intact"; the conformance fixture spec/conformance/fixtures/data-classification-process-default-record-projection.edn pins `:tags :rf/redacted` (lines 82, 102) and mentions `:exception` zero times; implementation/core/test/re_frame/observability_process_default_cljs_test.cljc mentions `:exception` zero times (control: `:rf/redacted` / `:frame nil` hits exist, e.g. `frameless-record-reaches-the-default-fail-closed` at 304). Spec 009 §What IS available's own process-default example resorts to `:rf.egress/local-raw` (projection.cljc:150 is the only `include-sensitive? true` in src; Grep control: prose hits in elision/projection/tool_pair).
- Action: decide: A) treat `:exception` as an opaque summary slot in `project-error-record` (pass through unless `:rf.egress/public-error`, which already drops it) so a frameless record still carries the throwable a shipper exists for, and pin it in the fixture; or B) keep fail-closed and say in 015 §process default that frameless records ship `:exception :rf/redacted`, steering hosts to `:rf.egress/local-raw` for the process default. A is one `cond` arm plus a fixture line; B is a paragraph and leaves the default sink useless for exactly the three categories that can only reach it.

### 3. The channel-conformance gate cannot see the `verify-hydration!` class: it checks mechanism->catalogue only, and its always-on mechanism regex omits `dispatch-error-record!` / `dispatch-frame-teardown-report!`  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: test-gap]
- Where: implementation/core/test/re_frame/error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj:407 (`always-on-mechanism-re` = `emit-error-both!|dispatch-on-error!`), 784-812 (`always-on-mechanism-emits-are-catalogued-always-on`, the only channel-direction test), 630 (`parsed-always-on-set-equals-the-exercise-literal` drives `dispatch-on-error!` directly rather than the runtime emit site).
- What: nothing pins catalogue-always-on -> "at least one runtime site routes this literal through an always-on chokepoint", and the ~15 categories whose only always-on route is `dispatch-error-record!` (SSR family, safe-redirect-*, malformed-hydration-payload, machine-action-exception, machine-spawn-unregistered-type, root-boot-failed, frame-teardown-failed, the two rf2-xpd8 schema arms) are invisible to the mechanism check in BOTH directions, so a new `dispatch-error-record!` site under a `diagnostic` row, or an always-on row whose last always-on site is deleted, passes green.
- Evidence: Grep `dispatch-error-record|dispatch-frame-teardown-report` in the test file = 0 hits (control: `emit-error-both!` 10+ hits at 67/315/325/407/786/806). Census (scratchpad/always_on_census.py, output census_out.txt): catalogue parsed section-scoped exactly as the gate does = 476 rows, 47 always-on, 429 diagnostic; 324 src files scanned. Category level: 47/47 always-on categories have at least one always-on runtime route (38 by literal in a +/-6-line window; the 9 NO-CODE-HIT rows resolved by hand: the four `*-removed` stubs -> cofx.cljc:1236 `raise-removed!` -> `emit-error-both!` hook; the three safe-redirect-* -> response.cljc:1045 `dispatch-safe-redirect-record!` -> `:error-emit/dispatch-error-record` hook; the two sub-input-fn-* -> subs.cljc:833 `emit-sub-input-fn-error!` -> `emit-error-both!` hook with a variable category). Site level: 36 windows showed a dev emit with no always-on sibling; 35 resolve (11 docstring/comment lines; 17 paired with an always-on call 7-12 lines away — frame.cljc 964/1088/1147, router.cljc 3425, boot.cljc 103, machines error_emit + 3 sites, adapter.cljc 580, spawn.cljc 156, error_projector 371/441, lifecycle.clj 192, error_listener 312, streaming.clj 463 via `emit-always-on-error!`; 6 are `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` arms the catalogue row itself scopes as dev-only; tool_pair.cljc:1158 returns a structured `{:outcome :fail}` to its caller). Exactly ONE genuine member of the class remains: ssr/boot.cljc:144 (the sibling's `verify-hydration!` finding). So the class is small today and the gate would not notice it growing.
- Action: add `dispatch-error-record!` and `dispatch-frame-teardown-report!` to `always-on-mechanism-re` with the category read from the adjacent `:error` literal, and add the reverse leg — every `always-on` row must have >= 1 literal emit site through an always-on chokepoint in non-test src (allow-list the variable-category helpers `emit-sub-input-fn-error!`, `raise-removed!`, `emit-fx-error!`). The census script in the scratchpad is the prototype.

### 4. `dispatch-on-error!` / `emit-error-both!` are 7/8/9-arity positional, so call sites carry ladders of annotated `nil`s  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: ergonomics]
- Where: implementation/core/src/re_frame/error_emit.cljc:551-555 (`[error-kw event event-id frame-id exception elapsed-ms time attrs route-frame?]`), 724 (`emit-error-both!` 8/9-arity); worst sites frame.cljc:1147 and substrate/adapter.cljc:580 (four bare `nil`s each, every one with a `;;` explaining which slot it is), frame.cljc:964/1088, cofx.cljc:1252 (three).
- What: the always-on emit API that every feature artefact reaches through a late-bind hook is positional across nine slots, and 10 of the 31 non-test call sites pass >= 2 bare positional `nil`s (5 pass >= 3) — friction for the programmer and the AI adding the next emit site, and the reason finding 1's `route-frame?` rides as a trailing boolean nobody stamps.
- Evidence: scratchpad Python census over implementation/**/src (324 files): 31 call sites of `(emit-error-both!` / `(dispatch-on-error!` (excluding defns), nil counts per site listed in the run output; the frame.cljc sites annotate each nil with a comment (`;; no event vector`, `;; no frame — that is the whole point`).
- Action: one map-taking entry (`{:error :event :event-id :frame :exception :elapsed-ms :time :attrs :route-frame?}`) with the positional arities kept as thin wrappers until the 31 sites are swept; sized to a morning, not a redesign.

## Considered, left alone
- `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure` has 7 dev-only arms vs 3 always-on: the catalogue row (009:2002) and the rf2-xpd8 paragraph scope promotion per-arm on purpose, so the per-category Channel column is knowingly coarse, not drift.
- `trace/compute-sensitive?` uses `true?` while `privacy/sensitive?` uses `boolean`: every producer stamps a boolean (Grep `:sensitive\?\s+[^tfn\s)}\]]` = 0 non-boolean producers, control: many `true`/`false` hits), so the asymmetry is moot.
- `elision.cljc` `warned-unschema'd` process-global set is never pruned on frame destroy: dev-only, bounded by schema-id cardinality.
- Late-bind `when-let` hooks silently skip when `re-frame.error-emit` is not loaded: router.cljc:22 requires it statically, so any frame that can emit has the hooks bound.
- routing/navigate.cljc:463 emits `:where :event` for a `route-url` throw, the same `:where` as the always-on boundary arm: dev-only by the row; a naming collision for a consumer filtering on `:where`, nothing more.

## Instruments and controls
- scratchpad/always_on_census.py -> census_out.txt: section-scoped parse of 009's catalogue (476 rows / 47 always-on / 429 diagnostic) x literal scan of 324 src files; per-category verdict 38 OK-ALWAYS + 9 NO-CODE-HIT (all 9 hand-resolved to always-on helpers with variable category); per-site pass 36 dev-only windows, 35 resolved by wider reads, 1 genuine (boot.cljc:144). Run with `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` (cp1252 stdout crashed on a `->` in the catalogue).
- Grep tool (ripgrep) for every search per the brief; Bash `grep` never used. `defn-? walk-tree` in elision.cljc = 0 (the kernel is not named that; the elide-wire-value frameless branch at 1296-1314 is what finding 2 relies on).
- Grep `dispatch-error-record|dispatch-frame-teardown-report` in error_catalogue_channel_conformance_test.clj = 0; control `emit-error-both!|dispatch-on-error!` = 10+ hits (67, 315, 325, 407, 786, 806).
- Grep `:exception` in observability_process_default_cljs_test.cljc = 0; control `:rf/redacted` and `:frame nil` hit (line 304). Grep `:exception` in the process-default fixture .edn = 0; control `:tags :rf/redacted` at 82, 102.
- Grep `include-sensitive\?\s+true` across implementation/**/src = 1 code hit (projection.cljc:150, the `:rf.egress/local-raw` profile) + prose.
- Grep `\[re-frame\.error-emit\s+:as` in core/src = router.cljc:22, test_support.cljc:163.
- Python positional-nil census: 31 `(emit-error-both!`/`(dispatch-on-error!` call sites in src (first regex missed the 19 sites whose call name ends the line; fixed with `(?:\s|$)` and re-run).
- Ripgrep has no look-around: `(?!true|false)` rejected; replaced with a character class.
- No `clojure -M:test` run was needed; no git write, no `bd`, no build tool invoked.

title: review(core-frame-router): senior-developer findings, 5 ranked, trunk d89a41e057 (2026-09-16)
description:
# Senior review: core-frame-router

Reviewer persona: senior engineer who has maintained an event-loop dispatch runtime at scale (re-frame v1 / Redux-class); cares about run-to-completion, re-entrancy, interceptor chains, frame identity, teardown races, and what a programmer sees when a dispatch goes wrong.
Tree: review-sep16 worktree, trunk d89a41e057
Scope read: all 19 slice files under implementation/core/src/re_frame/ in full — frame.cljc (4943), router.cljc (4781), live_frame.cljc (1941), fx.cljc (2026), events.cljc (1533), cofx.cljc (1300), reply.cljc (797), interceptor_registry.cljc (554), router/diagnostics.cljc (475), identity.cljc (451), frame_classification.cljc (381), interceptor.cljc (340), std_interceptors.cljc (327), router_transducer.cljc (312), capture_frame.cljc (237), cofx/value_check.cljc (125), managed_timer.cljc (122), movement.cljc (122), disposable.cljs (53) ≈ 20.8K lines. Tests skimmed: core/test/re_frame/{drain_test,concurrency_stress_test,trace_listener_drain_deadlock_test,cross_frame_dispatch_sync_warn_test,events_test,fx_test}.clj, epoch/test/re_frame/epoch_silencing_emit_deadlock_test.clj, spec/conformance/fixtures/drain-depth-limit.edn.
Owning specs consulted: spec/002-Frames.md §Destroy (:696-827), §dispatch-sync inside a handler / cross-frame (:1798-1806), §Run-to-completion rules 1-3 (:1842-1854), §Single-drainer invariant (:1856-1860), §Drain-loop pseudocode (:1939-2038); spec/009-Instrumentation.md §Error event catalogue rows :2016-2018; spec/API.md :506 (`:dispatch-later` shape), :897 (interceptor context plumbing); spec/conformance/README.md :388, :579; spec/Ownership.md rows 25-37 (envelope, drain, overrides → 002).

## Findings, ranked

### 1. A drain of EXACTLY `:drain-depth` events is reported as a runaway  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness]
- Where: implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:3691-3702 (`run-one-pass!` loop order), :3370-3371 (`handle-depth-exceeded!` `last-event` fallback); spec/002-Frames.md:1998-2021 (pseudocode shares the boundary); frame.cljc:2396-2397 (`:story` preset = 16), router.cljc:3294-3300 (default 100)
- What: `run-one-pass!` tests `(>= depth drain-depth)` BEFORE looking at the queue, so a cascade that settles cleanly after exactly `drain-depth` events (queue already empty) still takes the halt branch — an always-on `:rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded` record fans out with `:queue-size 0`, and a `:halted-depth` epoch record is committed for a "halting event" that is the fallback `last-event`, i.e. an event that actually ran and settled `:ok`, with a nil `:committed-at`.
- Evidence: cond order at :3695 (depth) → :3722 (disposed) → :3733 (`take-event!`); `depth` starts at 0 and increments per processed event, so after N events the depth test fires before the empty queue is consulted. `handle-depth-exceeded!` :3370-3371 falls back to `last-event` and the comment calls the empty-queue case "defensive"; it is reachable by any exactly-N cascade. Spec rule 3 (:1846) says the halt "discards the remaining queued events (the next, halting event never runs)" and the `:halted-depth` record is "for the halting event" — with an empty queue there is none, so the record misattributes. Under `:story` (16) a legitimate 16-event init cascade is flagged; under the default (100) it is rarer but identical. Test-gap: drain_test.clj:264-308 pins the RUNAWAY case (exactly N handlers run, then halt); no test asserts that an N-event cascade which settles is NOT halted (a search of core/test for a negative assertion on `drain-depth-exceeded` returned 0; control: the positive assertions at drain_test.clj:135-308 were found by the same instrument).
- Action: peek first, then halt only when there IS a next event — `(if-let [envelope (take-event! …)] (if (>= depth drain-depth) halt process) settled)` (or `peek` before `>=`); drop the `last-event` fallback in `handle-depth-exceeded!` once the branch is unreachable with an empty queue; adjust the spec pseudocode comment at 002:1998-2006 in the same PR (one sentence); add the "exactly N, settles, no halt" pin beside drain_test.clj:264.

### 2. On the JVM, a concurrent `dispatch-sync` from another thread is silently DROPPED (and blamed on "inside a handler") whenever the frame is mid-SYNC-drain  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: spec-drift]
- Where: implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:4526-4540 (`nested-sync?` = `(or (:in-sync-drain? router-state) same-thread-drain?)`), :4593-4607 (rejection arm, dev-only `rf.trace/emit-error!`), :4644-4655 (flag set in the seed-push, cleared in `finally`); spec/002-Frames.md:1800, :1860
- What: the `:in-sync-drain?` arm makes ANY thread's `dispatch-sync` into a frame that another thread is currently sync-draining take the `:rf.error/dispatch-sync-in-handler` branch — the event is never enqueued, the diagnostic names the wrong cause ("called from inside a running drain"), and in production (the emit is dev-only per the 009 catalogue) nothing is reported at all — whereas the spec says a concurrent caller "spin-waits for the lock and performs its seed-push under the lock".
- Evidence: spec 002:1800 rejects only a call "from inside an event handler's interceptor pipeline" against its OWN frame; 002:1860 (§Single-drainer invariant) prescribes the spin-wait; conformance/README.md:388, :579 describe the guard as the `:in-drain?` (same-thread) guard. The code's own comment at :4529-4536 says "Only flag as nested when the current thread is the drainer — a different thread mid-drain is a concurrent caller, which `drain-block!` handles correctly", and `mark-drainer!` :3550-3556 stamps the drainer's Thread exactly so `same-thread-drain?` can make that distinction — but the `or` at :4540 then defeats it. The comment at :4631-4632 and three test docstrings (concurrency_stress_test.clj:192-196, trace_listener_drain_deadlock_test.clj:19-25, epoch_silencing_emit_deadlock_test.clj:32-36) describe the drop as "by-design (rf2-ynk7)"; none of them pins it as a behaviour, and the concurrency stress test explicitly avoids the case. The asymmetry is the tell: the same concurrent `dispatch-sync` during an ASYNC drain (`:in-sync-drain?` false, `:in-drain?` = executor thread) correctly spin-waits and runs. Worse, the router state is read without the lock at :4528, so whether the second caller's event runs or is dropped depends on whether it reads the flag before or after the first caller's seed-push — a race that decides between "runs" and "silently vanishes". Deadlock-freedom is not at stake: `drain-block!` (:3932-3988) is bracketed by `call-with-deferred-listener-delivery`, which is exactly what trace_listener_drain_deadlock_test.clj proves safe for the async-drain spin — the sync-drain spin is the same shape (reasoned, not run). CLJS is unaffected (`same-thread-drain?` already covers every case on a single thread).
- Action: delete the `(:in-sync-drain? router-state)` arm at :4540 (keep `same-thread-drain?`); fix the comment at :4631-4632 and the three test docstrings; leave the `:in-sync-drain?` flag itself in place — its other readers (router/diagnostics.cljc:97, epoch/tool_pair.cljc:346) are diagnostics that also read `:in-drain?`. Optionally add a JVM pin: two threads, same frame, sync drain in flight, both events settle exactly once. If rf2-ynk7 really ruled the drop intentional, the spec at 002:1860 must say so instead — decide which is right; the spec's version is the one the concurrency story (SSR, JVM tests) is built on.

### 3. Every production dispatch pays a registrar resolution for a trace that is elided  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: perf]
- Where: implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:4117-4126 (`emit-dispatched-trace!`), :4100-4101 (comment claiming DCE), :4162 (the only debug gate in the fn)
- What: the `handler-meta` binding (`rf.live-frame/call-with-frame-resolution` + `rf.registrar/lookup`) runs on every `dispatch!` / `dispatch-sync!` regardless of `rf.interop/debug-enabled?`, solely to compute `no-emit?` for an `rf.trace/emit!` whose body is a runtime-gated `defn` (trace.cljc:857), so production resolves the handler at enqueue AND again at process time.
- Evidence: `emit!` is a defn, not a macro, so the surrounding `let` is not folded away; the comment's "this whole emit DCEs under goog.DEBUG=false" is true only of the tag map at :4162. Control: `build-envelope` :234-246 gates its own dev-only reads with `(when rf.interop/debug-enabled? …)` — the idiom is next door. Hot path named: every dispatch.
- Action: wrap the `handler-meta` / `no-emit?` computation in `(when rf.interop/debug-enabled? …)` (two lines; `no-emit?` becomes false in prod, which is what prod already effectively gets).

title: fix(testbed-support): open-in-editor endpoint 403s every loopback caller on shadow-cljs 3.4.10 - shadow-http sets :remote-addr to SocketAddress.toString (/127.0.0.1:port), which loopback-peer? refuses
description:
Discovered by the rf2-78s0d worker while live-probing the open-in-editor :dev-http ports (2026-09-14, shadow-cljs 3.4.10, Windows). The mechanism is platform-independent Clojure. Dev tooling; S.

MEASURED, LIVE: probed against that worktree's own `npx shadow-cljs server` (listener PID confirmed through `.shadow-cljs/server.pid` and the parent process chain).
- `POST /__rf-open-in-editor` with no `file` answered 403 `{"ok":false,"error":"forbidden"}`, from localhost, 127.0.0.1 and [::1] alike.
- The OPTIONS preflight answered 403 too, and `handle` gates the preflight on `loopback-peer?` alone.
- A genuine loopback POST with no `file` should reach the 400 `missing-file` branch instead.

MECHANISM, READ AT SOURCE: shadow-cljs 3.4.10 serves :dev-http through shadow-http 0.1.8.
- Its `shadow.http.server.ring/build-request-map` (`shadow/http/server/ring.clj:51`) sets `:remote-addr (str (.getRemoteAddress request))`, which is a stringified `java.net.SocketAddress`.
- `re-frame.testbed.open-in-editor-server/loopback-peer?` accepts only a bare numeric literal (`[0-9A-Fa-f:.]+`) and fails closed on everything else.
- Its docstring's premise, "shadow-cljs fills `:remote-addr` from `InetAddress.getHostAddress`", no longer holds on this server. rf2-mpgs introduced the peer check.

MEASURED, JVM (tools/testbed-support src plus shadow-cljs 3.4.10 on the classpath):
- `(str (InetSocketAddress. (InetAddress/getByName "127.0.0.1") 54321))` is `"/127.0.0.1:54321"`, and `loopback-peer?` on it is false.
- The `::1` form is `"/[0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]:54321"`, and `loopback-peer?` on it is false.
- Control: the bare literal `"127.0.0.1"` is true.
- `handle` answers 403 to an OPTIONS preflight carrying the shadow-http shape.

EFFECT: on this shadow version the endpoint can never launch an editor.
- It fails SAFE. Every non-2xx sends the client to its `editor://` URI fallback, so nothing is exposed.
- What is lost is the endpoint's whole value: resolving relative classpath coordinates, which the URI fallback cannot do.
- The JVM suite cannot see this, because every test hand-types `:remote-addr` in the old bare shape.

FIX SHAPE, for the worker to settle:
- Take the host out of shadow-http's `/host:port` and `/[v6]:port` renderings before the numeric-literal check.
- Keep fail-closed for anything else, and keep the no-name-resolution rule, which is security-relevant.
- Pin the fix with a test whose `:remote-addr` is produced the way shadow-http produces it, e.g. `(str (java.net.InetSocketAddress. (java.net.InetAddress/getLoopbackAddress) 54321))`, rather than hand-typed.
- The file is `tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server.clj`. rf2-78s0d's PR #9813 edits only its `handler` fn and adds tests, so sequence after that PR merges to avoid a conflict.

FENCED (mayor, 2026-09-14): waits for PR #9813 (rf2-78s0d) to merge, because both change tools/testbed-support/src/re_frame/testbed/open_in_editor_server.clj. Clears when rf2-78s0d closes. The tracker edge was changed from discovered-from to blocks on rf2-78s0d so bd ready enforces the wait; the discovery provenance stays in the description.
== MAYOR PREMISE CHECK (2026-09-14, trunk 90b448f303, after PR #9813 merged; before dispatch to worker/loopbackpeer-a) ==
FENCE DISCHARGED: rf2-78s0d closed and PR #9813 merged.
VERIFIED AT SOURCE: `loopback-peer?` (:407) still carries the docstring premise that `:remote-addr` arrives as a bare numeric literal from InetAddress.getHostAddress, never addr:port. `loopback-host?` (:384) is the separate, client-written Host-header check.
NOT RE-VERIFIED BY THE MAYOR: shadow-http 0.1.8 ring.clj:51 stringifying the SocketAddress. The rf2-78s0d worker measured it; the next worker re-reads the jar.
ADDED TO THE BRIEF: InetSocketAddress renders as hostname/literal:port when a hostname is attached, so the fix must take only the literal, never trust or resolve the hostname half, and stay fail-closed on unrecognised shapes. Controls run in both directions: loopback renderings built from real InetSocketAddress objects must be accepted, and a deliberately too-permissive plant must turn a negative test red.
== WORKER VERDICT (worker/loopbackpeer-a, PR #9815, base 90b448f303, 2026-09-14) ==
PREMISES VERIFIED AT SOURCE, and all of the bead's claims held:
- tools/testbed-support's :test classpath resolves shadow-http 0.1.8. Its shadow/http/server/ring.clj line 51 reads ":remote-addr (str (.getRemoteAddress request))}". The chain is HttpRequest.getRemoteAddress -> SocketConnection.getRemoteAddress -> socket.getRemoteSocketAddress() on a ServerSocket.accept() socket. shadow-cljs 3.4.10 dev_http.clj wraps the :handler via http-server/ring-handler -> build-request-map.
- Renderings were measured on a live shadow.http.server/start (JDK 21.0.10, Windows) with raw HTTP clients:
  - An IPv4 client renders as "/127.0.0.1:<port>" whether the server binds 0.0.0.0, :: or 127.0.0.1. A dual-stack :: socket unmaps IPv4, so no ::ffff: form appears.
  - An IPv6 client renders as "/[0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]:<port>".
  - Windows reports 127.0.0.2 and 127.1.2.3 clients as 127.0.0.1.
  - The hostname half "<name>/<literal>:<port>" appears only once something calls getHostName on the socket's InetAddress, which caches the name. Measured: "kubernetes.docker.internal/127.0.0.1:<port>". shadow-http never calls getHostName.
  - Other toString shapes: "localhost/<unresolved>:<port>" and "/[fe80:0:0:0:0:0:0:1%1]:<port>".
  - shadow-http 0.1.8 needs JDK 21 (Thread/ofVirtual), so the pre-JDK-14 unbracketed IPv6 rendering cannot occur. It fails closed.
- Trunk loopback-peer? returned false for "/127.0.0.1:54321" and "/[0:0:0:0:0:0:0:1]:54321" (reproduced).

FINDING BEYOND THE BEAD: trunk loopback-peer?'s docstring said nothing could reach name resolution. That was false. InetAddress/getByName resolves any string it cannot parse as a literal, and the old filter let two shapes through: a dotted quad with an octet over 255, and a colon form starting with ".". With -Djdk.net.hosts.file mapping 127.0.0.999, 1.2.3.456 and .::1 to 127.0.0.1, trunk loopback-peer? returned TRUE for all three. On the branch it returns FALSE, while the same file still resolves them in that JVM. Leading-zero quads parse as literals with no lookup, and their handling is unchanged. The adapter produces :remote-addr, not the client, so this was latent rather than exploitable from a request, but the no-lookup rule is now actually true.

FIX: a new private peer-literal.
- It reads only the literal after the last "/": either "[v6]:port" with a colon inside the brackets, or "v4:port".
- It strips a scope id, requires IPv4 octets to be at most 255, and requires a colon form to start with a hex digit or ":".
- The hostname half is never read. The bare literal still passes. Every other shape returns nil.
- loopback-peer? applies the unchanged isLoopbackAddress rule to that literal and has a corrected docstring.
- handler, local-request?, loopback-host?, allow-origin and deps.edn are untouched. The existing tests are unchanged apart from the stale req docstring and one stale comment.

GATES (tools/testbed-support, RF2_REQUIRE_NODE_PROBES=1, every exit code captured from the runner):
- open-in-editor namespace at trunk: 48 tests, 348 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0.
- open-in-editor namespace on the branch: 51 tests, 401 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0.
- full clojure -M:test after both restores: 51 tests, 401 assertions, 0 failures, exit 0.
- clj-kondo: 0 errors, 0 warnings, exit 0. CI's kondo job does not lint this tree.
- require-alias ratchet: clean, exit 0.

CONTROLS:
(1) loopback-peer? body reverted to trunk, helper kept: exit 1 with 12 failures, all in loopback-peer?-accepts-shadow-http-socket-renderings. The POST and the preflight both answered 403, and every negative test stayed green.
(2) Too-permissive plant (a rendering containing "127." is accepted): exit 1 with 32 failures, including the new negatives 127.0.0.1/203.0.113.7:54321 and 127.0.0.1.attacker.example/192.168.1.1:54321.
Both restores were verified by blob hash: the default-form git hash-object equals the HEAD blob hash 3ea64d23082d25e6236d91161785bfeb60f1d604, and git diff --quiet exits 0.

title: fix(story-ui): upgrade-snippet (view_state.cljc:373) emits an unreadable body — the rung comment swallows the envelope's closing }) — and the compiled upgrade still keeps the parent's :sub-overrides, so the "upgrade fidelity in place" handoff does not work
description:
Found independently by all three Story-parity research passes (ai/findings/Story/{astra,grok,fable}/report.md, 2026-09-14) and reproduced on the JVM at trunk 98e8ffe9cb; the mayor verified the fn's location at source. Filed under rf2-rln91 (R0b in the fable report).

WHAT, two halves:
1. `re-frame.story.ui.view-state/upgrade-snippet` (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/ui/view_state.cljc:373) places the rung slot's `; real events ...` comment on the LAST map line, so `reg-variant-envelope`'s closing `})` sits inside the comment and `clojure.edn/read-string` (and `cljs.reader/read-string`) throws `EOF while reading`. The snippet the UI hands the author to paste does not parse.
2. Even after hand-completing the body with valid syntax, a child that `:extends` a `:sub-overrides` parent compiles to a plan whose `:fidelity` is `#{:real-setup :sub-overrides}` and still pins the subscription (`[:login/email]` -> "PINNED" in the probe). The "upgrade" adds a rung without dropping the pin, so the stronger case cannot detect a handler defect the pinned picture could not.

WHY IT MATTERS: the fidelity ladder (docs/story/03-fidelity-ladder.md; 018 section 3.1 "explicit args + honest fidelity rungs") is one of Story's claimed surpasses; the LABELS are honest (a pinned sub never satisfies `sub-equals`, the chips say so), but the UPGRADE is not yet a trustworthy handoff. Grok's and astra's reports both rank this immediately after the promotion defect.

FIX (S): emit the comment on its own line (or after the map), so the snippet round-trips through `read-string`; and generate an upgrade body that actually excludes the inherited pinned outputs while retaining the context the author needs (a readable scaffold that removes the pin, or a clear recipe for editing the original declaration). No new generalized deletion/merge API. Test the COMPLETED generated artifact, not merely the presence of `:setup` in the snippet.

ACCEPTANCE: `edn/read-string` of the emitted snippet succeeds; the compiled child plan's `:fidelity` no longer contains `:sub-overrides` unless the author deliberately kept the pin; a handler defect the pinned parent could not detect is detected by the upgraded child. GATES: tools/story UI cljs tests and JVM tests; not a hot zone.

description:
Complete the Fresco SSR example's client-asset serving composition. Show a concrete minimal Ring route/middleware or deployment URL mapping for the emitted browser build, align the shell's script URL with that mapping, and forward only page requests to the SSR handler. Include the development bundle's dependency URLs; no new general-purpose server framework is needed.

Ownership and revision

- Slice: examples_substrates. Own `examples/substrates/fresco/login/host.clj:88-112` (especially `:script-src "/js/main.js"` at 108 and the exported-handler instruction at 111) and `examples/substrates/fresco/login/README.md:233-254`.
- The producer contract is `implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:1709-1713`: `:examples/login-fresco` emits to `out/examples/login-fresco`, uses `:asset-path "."`, and boots `fresco.login.core/run`. Build metadata need not change if the example serves that output coherently.
- Reviewed baseline: `9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261`; observed HEAD: `9291090725fa3ebcad67ea81a74946fc3aac96a4`. All 21 owned files are unchanged between those revisions (`git diff --exit-code`, exit 0).
- SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).
- Remediation fence inherited from the second finding in `rf2-fzbj.36`: until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj. Review evidence only; no fixer is dispatched.

Concrete trigger and behavior

Compile the server/client bundles and start the sidecar per the README. Initialize the JVM adapter explicitly to get past the independent missing-startup defect, then serve exported `host/handler` through a Ring server adapter as instructed. GET / includes `<script src="/js/main.js">`, so the browser requests that URL from the same host.

Expected: the bootstrap URL serves compiled JavaScript and its generated dependency/runtime URLs are reachable, allowing `fresco.login.core/run` to read the payload and hydrate the SSR markup.

Actual: `host/handler` is only `ssr-handler`, with no static routing, and the recipe supplies none. The SSR handler renders a document for every request sent to it. GET /js/main.js therefore returns HTTP 200 with `content-type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and another complete login HTML document. Compiling `implementation/out/examples/login-fresco/main.js` creates no URL mapping in a Ring application, and a server adapter adds none. The script does not execute, leaving the server-rendered page inert; each asset fetch also performs unnecessary SSR work.

Fresh current-source witness: after explicit JVM initialization, the constructed host handler returns a 200 page containing `src="/js/main.js"`. Send GET /js/main.js to the SAME handler. It returns 200 text/html, includes the synthetic form body, begins with the HTML doctype, and increments the renderer call count from 1 to 2. The controlled renderer isolates the application's routing behavior; no browser or real sidecar is required to prove that the requested script receives an HTML response.

Suggested repair and acceptance

1. Supply a concrete example application composition that serves this client output and sends the page route to `host/handler`; align `:script-src` with the mapping.
2. Account for the dependency/runtime URLs emitted by the documented development `compile` build and its `:asset-path "."`, not merely a release `main.js` file. Serving the output tree coherently is sufficient.
3. Request the emitted script URL through the documented composed application and assert JavaScript content, not an SSR document. Check the emitted runtime dependencies at their actual requested URLs. An unknown asset must produce an asset miss rather than another login document.
4. Confirm the SSR login hydrates and sign-in interaction works through a focused browser/manual check once this application wiring and the independent JVM startup repair are applied. Keep regression coverage centrally owned, without per-example `spec.cjs` files.

The general-purpose `ssr-handler` should keep its existing contract: routing is the host application's responsibility. The library already demonstrates static middleware in front in `implementation/ssr-ring/src/re_frame/ssr/ring.clj:342-370`. This issue repairs the executable example recipe that currently tells the reader to serve its uncomposed handler directly.

Executed `ai/surface-review-20260913/examples_substrates/probe-examples_substrates-host-1.clj` through `java -cp ... clojure.main`, current source and existing cached dependencies only. Exit 0 is captured in the same-stem `.exit`, full evidence in `.log`. No CLJS compile, dependency installation, release build, live Ring/Node server, browser execution, or broad gate was run. The witness establishes the wrong MIME/body/dispatch at the bootstrap URL; it does not claim actual compiled-client hydration.

Deduplication and references

Revalidated and split from the two-finding aggregate `rf2-fzbj.36`, which stays OPEN and unchanged; read its current record and newest three history entries. Existing host tests exercise the HTML/script-tag shell, not this application's static route composition. title: Preserve sequence-valued Slim component output
description: Preserve sequence-valued component output in reagent-slim's runtime wrapper so ordinary untagged components render sibling elements instead of throwing. P2. This is the independently actionable split of rf2-fzbj.30 finding 1, revalidated on 2026-09-13. The inherited fence remains: remediation is held until Mike rules who remediates rf2-fzbj. This issue records review findings and does not authorize or dispatch implementation. Ownership and source Primary owner: adapter_reagent_slim, implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/component.cljs:353-375, especially line 372 `(seq? out) (vec out)`. The output travels through make-render-method at lines 606-618 to implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:1298-1304, where vectors mean a single Hiccup form and sequences mean sibling children. Baseline: 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261. Reviewed HEAD: 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879. `git diff --name-only BASELINE -- implementation/adapters/reagent-slim` returned no paths: owned source is unchanged. SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review). Concrete trigger ```clojure (defn rows [] (list ^{:key :a} [:span "a"] ^{:key :b} [:span "b"])) ;; Render [rows] through reagent2.dom.client/render. ``` Expected: two sibling spans with their keys, the same result as direct as-element, a tagged Form-1, or a Form-2 inner renderer returning the same sequence. IMPL-SPEC sections 5.1 and 7.1 explicitly preserve the untagged runtime path and sequence output contract. Actual: the wrapper turns the list into `[[:span "a"] [:span "b"]]`. The template vector arm treats the first span vector as a Hiccup head and throws :rf.error/template-bad-tag. An empty sequence instead becomes an invalid empty Hiccup vector; text siblings may be misinterpreted as a tag/children combination. The sequence-to-vector arm is confined to untagged classification, so behavior depends on classification metadata rather than output meaning. This affects plain reusable functions and reg-view* callers. Suggested repair Remove the sequence-to-Hiccup-vector coercion from wrap-render. Return the sequence unchanged, or eagerly realize it in a sequence-preserving form if realization is required. Keep actual Hiccup vectors unchanged and align untagged Form-1, tagged Form-1, Form-2 and Form-3 output handling. No new wrapper DOM node is needed. Acceptance criteria - Exercise actual generated-class render/as-element behavior for keyed element siblings, an empty sequence and text siblings. A wrap-render-only `=` assertion can miss this because sequence/vector equality does not prove the same dispatch. - Equivalent tagged Form-1 and Form-2 controls produce the same siblings without an extra DOM wrapper; keys survive and ordinary Hiccup vectors still render correctly. - Include a mounted sibling-output regression in the existing browser target when implementing the repair. Synthetic instances are unmounted in finally. title: mcp-conformance: inspect CLJS reader branches in trace-key lint
description:
Make the trace-catalogue linter inspect every relevant reader-conditional branch, including CLJS-only and splicing branches. Its JVM reader currently removes those forms before the duplicate-key detector can see them.

Ownership and review identity

- Surface tools_mcp_conformance; parent rf2-gwye; SOURCE_ROOT=C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2; WORKTREE_ROOT=(none; read-only review).
- Baseline 9e8ca973767f4ecff455421e48e1765d59783261; reviewed head 4df6a3303c68c77ced1f84ce92178bed1d7f7879; owned paths unchanged from baseline.
- Owned source: tools/mcp-conformance/wire-vocab/test/re_frame/mcp_conformance/trace_catalogue_lint_test.clj:60-72 (read-all-forms), :81-91 (duplicate-hits), :120-152 (sanity tests).

Trigger and fresh reproduction

Call the actual private read-all-forms followed by duplicate-hits, resolved with ns-resolve from a fresh Clojure 1.12.0 JVM. Input:

    #?(:clj {:rf.reply/work-id work-id}
       :cljs {:rf.reply/work-id work-id :work/id work-id})

The reader returns only the CLJ map; duplicate-hits reports zero. A standalone `#?(:cljs {:rf.reply/work-id work-id :work/id work-id})` returns no forms at all. `[#?@(:clj [] :cljs [{:rf.reply/work-id work-id :work/id work-id}])]` returns `[[]]` and zero hits. Unconditional and CLJ-only versions of the same duplicate each report one hit; a valid two-branch conditional reports zero.

Expected: the source gate reports the prohibited duplicate in CLJS as it does for CLJ. Its stated scope is production .cljc emitters read as data, covering their emitted reply-fact vocabulary. Actual: `{:read-cond :allow}` chooses the JVM arm. The comment mistakenly attributes preservation to :allow. The sanity test supplies an already-read unconditional literal, so it proves traversal without exercising the lossy read boundary.

Impact: a CLJS-specific emitter can reintroduce :work/id beside :rf.reply/work-id, or :completed-at beside :rf.reply/completed-at, without this cross-platform linter failing. This is a proven coverage defect; the review does not claim production emitters currently contain a hidden duplicate.

Suggested repair and acceptance

Preserve reader conditionals and explicitly traverse their forms, or use a reader strategy that demonstrably visits all relevant platform arms and reader-conditional splices. Changing :allow to :preserve alone is insufficient unless the walker handles ReaderConditional values. Add composed reader-to-detector tests: unconditional, CLJ-only, CLJS-only, nested #?, and #?@ duplicate branches must all produce the appropriate pair hits. Preserve acceptance of valid alternatives, lone :work/id and separately nested carried/current identity maps. The three disappearing-branch examples above must become detector-positive without mutating a production source file.

Validation and limits

Executed probe-tools_mcp_conformance-2.clj on the pinned Clojure 1.12.0 with only cached jars and the current absolute wire-vocab test classpath. Exit 0 confirms all six stated current results, including the two positive detection controls and valid conditional. Artifact pair: ai/surface-review-20260913/tools_mcp_conformance/probe-tools_mcp_conformance-2.log and .exit. No suite runner, source mutation, install, build or live process. This characterizes the parser/detector seam; it is not a claim that the whole JVM suite passed.

Known references and disposition

Fresh revalidation and independent split of rf2-fzbj.14 F3. Current/closed title searches for conformance/reader and description search for read-all-forms found only the existing aggregate carrying this defect, no dedicated actionable issue. Read rf2-fzbj.14 and rf2-fzbj newest-first histories with limit 3. The prior duplicate-name cleanup is not being reopened.

REMEDIATION FENCE: retain rf2-fzbj's hold until Mike rules who owns remediation. This bead records the review result and dispatches no fixer; existing statuses and notes remain unchanged.
notes:
VERDICT (mcpconf-a worker, 2026-09-13): FIXED in PR #9755, surface tools/mcp-conformance only. One finding set, five beads: rf2-fzbj.14 carries F1-F3, and rf2-gwye.36/.38/.40 are its per-finding splits. rf2-gwye.41 is the review's new finding on the same surface.

Every finding was re-verified before fixing, at tip e428126d87 (after #9752 merged), by re-running the review's own probes. All four reproduced. No tools/mcp-base change was needed: tools/mcp-base/spec/dedup.md already promises that encode-then-decode is the identity on the JSON projection.

- rf2-gwye.36, rf2-fzbj.14 F1 (own __proto__ keys). lib/dedup-envelope.cjs now creates each decoded key with Object.defineProperty instead of assigning it. An own "__proto__" key therefore survives expansion at the root and nested levels, and never becomes the rebuilt object's prototype. The regression is in test/dedup-envelope.test.cjs. Its fixture is transcribed from a real dedup-value plus Cheshire encode, re-run after #9752 merged; the wire is byte-identical.

Regressions: dedup-envelope.test.cjs covers a harmless sibling and a conflicting one; is-error-matches-ok.test.cjs runs the review's reproduction through structured and assertIsErrorMatchesOk. - rf2-gwye.40, F3 (every reader-conditional arm). trace_catalogue_lint_test.clj reads with :read-cond :preserve, and duplicate-hits replaces each preserved conditional with the vector of all its arms before walking. The new test every-reader-conditional-arm-is-inspected drives source text through read-all-forms and then duplicate-hits. Read the entry point, README/package/plugin metadata, all six catalogue leaves, maintainer index, design/inputs/reauthoring documents, all 33 JSON fixtures, harness guidance, and the storage-materializer structural test. Checked the one-pass review/edit-intent boundary, sibling routing and packaged normal-path dependencies; compared the principal worked API shapes with local Managed HTTP, RemoteData, cofx, schema and view contracts. No defect is inferred just from their legacy APIs, an intentionally elided machine, or an absence of example tests. No production files, existing beads, dependencies, compilation outputs, git refs, or services were changed. No broad gates were run. No installed Claude session, package installation, live HTTP request, browser rendering, SSR execution, or full behavioural benchmark was exercised; those remain outside this bounded static review.

## Finding F1 — P2: canonical validated HTTP reply never terminates :loading

Owned evidence:
- references/schemaless-events.md:65-74 registers :article/load and writes [:article :status] = :loading at line 69 before issuing the correctly addressed :rf.http/managed request with :decode Article.
- references/schemaless-events.md:76-78 registers :article/loaded; line 78 changes only [:article :data].
- references/schemaless-events.md:80-82 registers :article/load-failed; line 82 changes only [:article :error].
- evals/evals.json:88 repeats the loading start and data-only successful completion in behavioural fixture 20. Lines 89 and 95 state that the missing production validator is the "sole defect". The non-error addressing assertion is correct, but the exclusivity claim suppresses this independent lifecycle defect.

Trigger / reproducer:
1. Use the leaf's complete "After — schema-validated boundary with a production gate" declarations.
2. Start from an empty app-db and process [:article/load {:slug "alpha"}]. Its returned :db has {:article {:status :loading}}.
3. Feed the successful completion handler [:article/loaded {:status :ok :value {:slug "alpha" :title "Alpha" :body "Synthetic" :authors []}}].
4. Independently, from the same started db, feed [:article/load-failed {:status :error :error {:category :rf.http/http-5xx :message "Synthetic failure"}}].
5. Inspect [:article :status] in both returned dbs: it is :loading in both. The successful article and failure map have arrived correctly, so this is the completion transition itself, not transport addressing or decoding.

Expected: success stores the validated Article under [:article :data] and changes the lifecycle status to :loaded; failure stores the classified error beside the payload and changes status to :error (with cancellation policy stated if distinguished). No settled response should leave the sample's in-flight status active.
Actual: success and failure retain :loading indefinitely. There is no further completion handler or automatic status writer in this snippet.
Impact: a reader applying the skill's canonical fix to a status-driven page gets a permanent spinner after either outcome, despite valid data/error delivery. This is the same missing-terminator class the sibling manual-loading-flags.md exists to diagnose. A schema-only answer can satisfy eval 20 while preserving the bug; the fixture's "sole defect" language also discourages reporting it.

Supporting current contract: skills/re-frame2/patterns/remote-data.md:69-74 explicitly sets :loaded alongside :data, and :79-82 sets :error alongside the classified error. That pattern's opening defines load/loaded/load-failed/reset as lifecycle events; Managed HTTP reply addressing dispatches those events and does not independently own an application's :article status slot.

Precise repair recommendation:
- Make :article/loaded update :status :loaded together with :data, keeping the payload at [:article :data] so reg-app-schema still sees Article only. Clear stale :error on successful completion if retained across retries.
- Make :article/load-failed update :status :error together with :error, preserving the intended data policy. There is no need to migrate the sample to a machine or introduce another effect.
- In eval 20, either repair the unrelated lifecycle in the input fixture to preserve its schema-only focus, or explicitly permit/report the second finding and require a proposed full rewrite to settle status. Remove the false "sole defect" claim while preserving the useful assertion that current reply addressing is valid.
- Reuse the existing behavioural fixture; do not add a generic evaluator or a prose-presence test merely to lock the words.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Starting from the shown :article/load result, the shown :article/loaded handler returns :status :loaded and the exact validated Article at [:article :data].
2. Starting from the same :loading db, :article/load-failed returns a terminal non-loading status and the exact classified error under [:article :error].
3. :decode Article remains an always-on trust gate, the explicit reply targets remain valid, and lifecycle/error keys stay outside the schema-registered Article payload path.
4. Eval 20 no longer declares the current lifecycle-broken input's missing production validation its sole defect. Its input and grade agree on whether lifecycle completion is already fixed or part of the critique.
5. A negative control restoring either original data-only/error-only completion fails the corresponding status assertion. An in-memory correction of both handlers succeeds without changing payload/error contents. Report runtime-versus-pure-handler validation honestly.

## Executed witness and limits

A bounded Babashka probe extracted the actual fenced After block from the absolute owned path, required exactly one matching block, and evaluated its function bodies with process-local registration collectors. reg-app-schema was a no-op, and no framework runtime or network effect was invoked. This validates the exact pure :db transformations; it does not purport to validate HTTP or schema execution.

Observed original: start-status :loading; success-status :loading; success-data-correct true; failure-status :loading; failure-error-correct true.
Observed in-memory control, modifying only the two completion expressions: success-status :loaded; failure-status :error; success-data-correct true; failure-error-correct true.

Evidence artifacts (ignored, unique slice/attempt names):

- ai/surface-review-20260912/probe-skill-improver-article-status-3.log
- ai/surface-review-20260912/probe-skill-improver-article-status-3.exit
The completed probe's own exit was 0 and its root banner was C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2. Attempts 1 and 2 exited 1 before the witness: this installed bb does not treat '-' as a script, then the stdin probe collided with Babashka's existing user/source var. Attempt 3 used a dedicated namespace and absolute ignored script; no probe process remains. No earlier attempt's output or exit was reused as a success.

All-status title/description searches covered improver, schemaless, skills/re-frame2-improver, schemaless-events.md, article :status, and spinner. No existing bead found owns the HTTP completion-status miss.
- rf2-uhszv (closed) owns the completed one-pass/proportionate review reshape. Preserve that result; this is a specific unsafe suggested correction, not a request to redesign the reviewer.

- rf2-1lv3 (closed) fixed the same leaf's separate storage materializer for absent/corrupt storage. Its property-first, bounded decoding shape is present. This finding concerns the earlier HTTP After block.
- rf2-z65e (closed) wired tests/storage_materializer_test.clj into skills-structural. That fixture structurally checks storage materialization, not the article completion paths; lack of this specific runtime assertion does not mean the existing test job is absent.
- rf2-3i9ci (closed) completed status-slice guidance in the boolean/loading leaves and summaries. Its owner paths and repair do not include this HTTP schema sample's completion events.
- rf2-237ug and rf2-lzsrd (closed) corrected recommended view frame scope, routing/API references, packaging markers and severity enumeration. Those corrections are visible and are not duplicated.

No additional confirmed defect is claimed. Potential grading/tool-harness limitations were inspected but not run as an installed skill, so they are validation limits rather than extra findings. This is the slice's sole review bead under rf2-fzbj; root owns checkpoint/push.

Both settled replies left the status at `:loading`. The reply addressing and the `:decode` gate were correct throughout; what never happened was the lifecycle transition, which is the missing-terminator class the sibling `manual-loading-flags.md` exists to diagnose and which `:decode` cannot touch. `evals/evals.json` fixture 20 repeated the data-only success completion in its input and its grade called the missing production validator the "sole defect" twice (the expected_output prose and expectation 5), which suppressed reporting the second defect.

WHAT LANDED.

1. `references/schemaless-events.md` -- both reply handlers now settle the lifecycle, matching the four-state slice in `skills/re-frame2/patterns/remote-data.md` (which sets `:loaded` beside `:data` and `:error` beside the classified error) and the single-handler form in `skills/re-frame2/patterns/managed-http.md`:
   - `:article/loaded` writes `[:article :data]` (unchanged value), `[:article :status] :loaded`, and clears a stale `[:article :error]`;
   - `:article/load-failed` writes `[:article :error]` (unchanged classified map) and `[:article :status] :error`.
   Lifecycle keys stay off `[:article :data]`, so `reg-app-schema` still sees an `Article` and nothing else -- acceptance criterion 3. A short paragraph after the fence says why both branches settle and points at manual-loading-flags.md and the RemoteData pattern.

2. `evals/evals.json` fixture 20 -- the input's `:article/loaded` now settles status alongside `:data`, and the "sole defect" exclusivity is gone from BOTH the expected_output and expectation 5. The replacement says the defect it must report is the missing production validation, and that an agent additionally naming the absent `:on-failure` branch is not wrong and must not be marked down. That is acceptance criterion 4 read literally: the input and the grade now agree that lifecycle completion is already fixed. The useful assertion that the reply ADDRESSING is valid is preserved verbatim, as is the trailing clause about keeping a loading sentinel off the schema-registered payload path. Repo-wide count of "sole defect" across the improver corpus is now 0.

I did NOT add an `:on-failure` branch to the eval input. The fixture's whole subject is a request missing its always-on gate; giving it a failure branch would enlarge it without serving the finding, and softening the exclusivity already stops a correct extra observation from being graded as a miss.

REGRESSION TEST -- `skills/re-frame2-improver/tests/article_lifecycle_test.clj` (new, 5 tests / 17 assertions). It EVALUATES the shipped fenced block rather than grepping it: extracts the single block registering `:article/load-failed`, drops the `rf/` prefix so `reg-event` and `reg-app-schema` bind to process-local collectors in the test namespace, and runs the three pure `:db` transitions. No framework runtime, no HTTP, no schema execution -- it validates exactly the handler bodies a reader copies. It also pins the always-on gate itself (`:decode` present and carrying a schema value, both reply targets addressed), so a "fix" that settled the lifecycle by dropping the gate fails too.

Run by `.github/workflows/test.yml`'s `skills-structural` job, step "Run re-frame2-improver structural tests", which loops `tests/*_test.clj` -- so no workflow change was needed. `skills/re-frame2-improver/*` arms `skills_structural` in the classifier (confirmed by running `.github/scripts/report-changed-surfaces.sh` over the changed PATHS -- handed revisions instead it reports every surface unaffected, which is indistinguishable from an honest miss).

  success handler restored to the pre-fix data-only form   -> exit 1, 2 failures, both the success-status assertions; the payload and lifecycle-keys-off-the-payload-path assertions stayed green
  failure handler restored to the pre-fix error-only form  -> exit 1, 2 failures, both the failure-status assertions; the classified-error assertion stayed green
  restored, no plant                                       -> exit 0, 5 tests / 17 assertions, 0 failures
Anchor match counts were read before each plant (1 and 1, so no silent no-op). Restore verified against the committed blob 17b22357b900b91806cb0d3ee23208668d46d8fd -- the default `git hash-object` form matched it, and `git diff --quiet HEAD -- <path>` exited 0 as an independent second instrument.

  scripts/check_skill_eval_docs.py --verbose --ci       exit 0  (eval counts/names unchanged; only fixture 20's text moved)
  scripts/check_skill_eval_packaging.py --verbose --ci  exit 0

NOTHING SKIPPED on this bead. The review claims no second confirmed defect in the slice and re-reading at tip found none. The bead's own restraint clause -- "Reuse the existing behavioural fixture; do not add a generic evaluator or a prose-presence test merely to lock the words" -- was honoured: no evaluator, no scorer, and the new test asserts BEHAVIOUR of the evaluated block rather than the presence of words.
