title: story: reg-story* silently drops :variants for a non-literal body — the programmatic twin registers zero variants and returns success
description:
Discovered by the senior-developer review rf2-wd2t (2026-09-13, trunk 1c9ff9697b). Verified at source by the mayor; the probe is the reviewer's, re-measure at tip.

WHERE: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/registrar.cljc:476-484 ((dissoc :variants) before validation, comment "Form-B sugar is removed by the macro"); macros.clj:165-172 ("for non-literal metadata punt to runtime (helper drops :variants)").

EVIDENCE (JVM probe): (reg/reg-story* :story.probe-s {:doc "p" :variants {:v {:setup [[:probe/ok]]}}}) -> story registered? true, variant :story.probe-s/v registered? false, no error. spec/001 declares the * helpers public for programmatic registration.

WHY IT MATTERS: a story whose variants come from a def'd or merged map, the natural programmatic shape, registers zero variants with a success return. It is the one place a macro and its * twin behave differently.

SMALLEST CHANGE: in reg-story*, when (contains? body :variants) desugar at runtime (doseq -> reg-variant* via variant-id-for) or throw :rf.error/story-variants-not-literal.

GATE: jvm-tools-story.

ALREADY-COVERED CHECK: not in the closed story roster.
notes: Merged-PR audit #9719: follow-up rf2-g2k4 tracks the remaining computed-:variants macro expansion failure. The runtime helper is fixed, but a literal outer body with :variants vs or (merge ...) never reaches it. Public JVM reproducer and the minimal macro fallback correction are in rf2-g2k4. Existing closure and criteria preserved; no mayor notification or acknowledgment inferred.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #9719 (branch worker/storyreg-a, commit 0062ea7994, base 5b89378c45). Worker storyreg-a.

VERDICT: the defect was real and is fixed by RUNTIME DESUGAR, the first of the bead's two options, not the throw.

- Premise re-measured at base with a JVM probe run as clojure -M -i <probe> from tools/story: (reg-story* :story.probe-s {:doc "p" :variants vs}) with vs def'd returned the id. The story was registered, :story.probe-s/v was NOT, and nothing was thrown.
- Why desugar rather than throw: tools/story/spec/Conventions.md pairs reg-story* with "optional :variants desugaring (Form B)", and 001-Authoring.md makes the * helpers the public programmatic path. Making the twin behave like the macro is the ergonomic answer, and it needs no new error id.

CHANGE (tools/story/src/re_frame/story/registrar.cljc, reg-story*):
- It validates the body WITH :variants present, so the Story schema's existing [:map-of :keyword :map] entry is now live and a non-keyword variant name is :rf.error/story-shape.
- It stores the story without :variants.
- It registers each entry through reg-variant* under <story-id>/<variant-name>, inside the macro's bound *pending-coords*. A desugared variant therefore carries the same :source stamp as on the literal path.
- A (declare reg-variant*) precedes it. The schemas.cljc docstring and comment on :variants are updated to match.
- The reg-story macro (story.cljc) and macros.clj are UNTOUCHED. The macro's non-literal branch already calls reg-story* with the full body, so it is fixed by this change too; the dispatch fence's STOP condition did not arise.

AFTER THE FIX: the same probe registers the variant, confirmed true.

TESTS (story_authoring_validation_test.clj):
- reg-story*-desugars-programmatic-variants
- reg-story-macro-desugars-non-literal-variants, which checks that the desugared variant shares the parent's expansion line
- reg-story*-rejects-malformed-variants: a non-keyword name gives story-shape; a bad desugared body gives variant-shape with the nearest-key hint

GATE (jvm-tools-story, clojure -M:test from tools/story):
- Baseline at base: exit 0, 1914 tests / 7047 assertions.
- With the fix: exit 0, 1920 / 7080 (+6 deftests, +33 assertions, which is exactly the new tests).
- Sabotage: the reg-variant* call inside the desugar was replaced with nil, alongside the rf2-uys9 plant. Result: exit 1, 24 failures, all in the 6 new deftests, with totals unchanged at 1920/7080. This bead's three tests took 8 of those failures.
- Restore verified by blob hash against the committed object.
- Post-restore re-run: exit 0, 1920 / 7080.
- The CLJS node-test lane is relied on in CI. The new tests are in a .clj file (JVM only); the source change is .cljc using only core fns.

LEFTOVER, deliberately not fixed because it is outside the dispatch fence: tools/story/src/re_frame/story/macros.clj, in expand-reg-story's comment, still says the non-literal branch will "punt to runtime (helper drops :variants)". The punt is now correct; only the parenthetical is stale. It is a one-word edit for whoever next touches macros.clj.

No overlap with held finding rf2-fzbj.3, whose findings concern loaders and args resolution.

title: test: 15 files of never-executed rows remain after rf2-6ppy's census — plus one dead row hollowing a live assertion
description:
FOLLOW-ON TO rf2-6ppy, WHICH ITS CENSUS PRODUCED AND ITS PR (#9681) DELIBERATELY DID NOT ABSORB.

PR #9681 repaired exactly ONE of the affected files (recents) and censused the rest, because the
repair shape is a convention call and widening a bounded pass is how a bounded pass stops being
bounded. That was the right call. This bead owns the remainder.

=== THE MEASURED POSITION ===

16 files, 106 guarded assertions, executing in NEITHER lane. One is repaired by #9681; 15 remain.

The guard has TWO spellings and the second is the larger half -- eleven of the sixteen route the
check through a local (browser?) predicate, (and (exists? js/window) (.-localStorage js/window)),
which is invisible to a census keyed on `exists? js/document`. A census on the obvious spelling
reads 7 files; counting both reads 16. Several of those predicates carry docstrings asserting
"browser-test returns true" -- the author's intent, never realised.

Node has no jsdom or happy-dom in any dependency list; `document`, `window` and `localStorage` are
all undefined there. :node-test selects `cljs-test$`, :browser-test selects `.*-dom-cljs-test$`.

=== THE TWO THAT ARE WORSE THAN THE COUNT SUGGESTS ===

1. toolbar_persistence_cljs_test.cljs -- 20 of 20 rows guarded. An entire namespace, billed as a
   regression net for reload persistence, executes ZERO assertions anywhere.

2. xray_preset -- A DEAD ROW HOLLOWING A LIVE ONE, which is worse than a dead row. Its one guarded
   row is a PRECONDITION that calls attach!. It never runs, so the unguarded assertion two lines
   below -- (is (false? (attached?))) "wire-cross-host! removed the listener" -- PASSES VACUOUSLY.
   That is a false green standing in the tree right now, not merely absent coverage.

Also recorded: backgrounds_test.cljc and viewport_test.cljc are dead one level FURTHER out. Their
namespaces do not end `cljs-test` either, so node does not select them and browser does not match
them, and their storage rows sit in #?(:cljs ...) which the JVM lane never reads. Removing the guard
would not help them; they need a different answer.

=== THE CONVENTION, RULED SO THE NEXT WORKER IS NOT BLOCKED ON IT ===

Both shapes already exist in this repo, and the choice is per-property rather than global:

  * If the property is ABOUT real browser storage semantics -- write-through, cap-at-max,
    survives-reload, hydrate -- it needs a real host. Move it to a `-dom-cljs-test` namespace.
    That is the shape #9681 used.
  * If the storage touch is INCIDENTAL and the property is really about logic, install a host stub
    so it runs on node. url_state_cljs_test.cljs documents this exact defect in prose and fixes it
    that way, so the precedent is in the tree.

A worker that finds a file fitting neither should REPORT it rather than force-fit.

=== THE THING THAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT FROM ORDINARY TEST WORK ===

These assertions HAVE NEVER EXECUTED. Their first run is the first honest evidence about the code
they cover, so a red is EVIDENCE ARRIVING, not the worker's breakage. A worker must not quietly
adjust an assertion to make a newly-live row green -- that reproduces the defect one level up, and
it is exactly what the xray_preset case shows is already possible. Report a genuine red; do not
paper it.

Whether a lint rule should catch this class is an open question, flagged by the censusing worker and
deliberately not filed as work.
notes:
=== CORRECTION (mayor, same day): THE CONVENTION RULED IN THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION IS WRONG ===

The description's first bullet says a real-storage property should "Move it to a `-dom-cljs-test`
namespace", citing PR #9681 as the precedent. I ruled that WITHOUT checking what the two lane
selectors actually do, and it is wrong in a way that manufactures red.

THE MECHANISM, from implementation/shadow-cljs.edn:990-1004, which states it in terms:

    `:node-test`'s `cljs-test$` regex still matches both suffixes
    (`-cljs-test` AND `-dom-cljs-test`), so the DOM-tagged files run
    on BOTH targets and the cross-runtime asserts continue firing in Node.

`cljs-test$` is a SUFFIX match, and `-dom-cljs-test` ends in `cljs-test`. So moving a file to
`-dom-cljs-test` does not take it OUT of the node lane -- it ADDS the browser lane. Both lanes then
load the file.

THE PROOF IS THE CITED PRECEDENT ITSELF. PR #9681 moved recents' two round-trip rows into
recents_dom_cljs_test.cljs and dropped their guard on the way. CI:

    FAIL in (save-load-round-trip) (day8/re_frame2_xray/palette/recents_dom_cljs_test.cljs:31:7)
    expected: (= [:foo :bar] (recents/load))
      actual: (not (= [:foo :bar] []))

That is the node lane running the moved file where localStorage does not exist. #9681's shape is the
error, not the precedent.

THE CORRECTED RULE. The guard was never the problem -- the FILE LOCATION was. A `(when (browser?)
...)` row inside a `-dom-cljs-test` file is TRUE in the browser lane and FALSE in node, which loads
it and harmlessly skips the body. So:

  * KEEP THE GUARD and move the file. The row goes from executing NOWHERE to executing in the
    browser, which is the entire ask of this bead.
  * Strip a guard ONLY if the row is genuinely cross-runtime -- no localStorage, document or window.
  * The host-stub-on-node option (url_state_cljs_test.cljs precedent) is unaffected and still valid
    where the storage touch is incidental.

WHAT STANDS UNCHANGED. The census is sound. A guarded row in a plain `-cljs-test` file really does
execute in neither lane: node loads it with the guard false, and the browser never loads it at all.
Only the repair shape was wrong. The two-spelling finding, the 16-file count, the toolbar_persistence
20-of-20 case and the xray_preset hollowed-assertion case all stand.

The live worker on this bead was messaged with this correction and with the reasoning, not just the
replacement rule.
=== WORKER lanefix-a — PR #9685 (2 of the 15 files) ===

SCOPE DONE: toolbar_persistence and xray_preset. The other thirteen remain.
Both files are under tools/story/, NOT tools/xray/ as the dispatch brief framed
them: tools/story/test/re_frame/story/ui/toolbar_persistence_cljs_test.cljs and
tools/story/test/re_frame/story/xray_preset_cljs_test.cljs.

CENSUS PREMISES RE-VERIFIED AT TIP — both hold. No jsdom/happy-dom in
implementation/package.json devDependencies. keybinding/attach! and detach!
each open with (exists? js/document), so on node nothing attaches and
(is (false? (attached?))) read (false? false) and passed. The 20-of-20 figure
for toolbar_persistence is 11 deftests / 22 assertion sites; the count differs,
the finding does not.

THE REPAIR SHAPE IN THE DISPATCH BRIEF WAS WRONG, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE
MAIN DURABLE FINDING. "Move it to a -dom-cljs-test namespace" does NOT take a
file out of the node lane. :node-test's ns-regexp `cljs-test$` is a SUFFIX
match and `-dom-cljs-test` ends in `cljs-test`, so a -dom-cljs-test file is
loaded by BOTH targets. Moving a file there ADDS the browser lane; it removes
nothing. implementation/shadow-cljs.edn states this in terms in the
:browser-test build comment, and two existing dom-test docstrings in the tree
say the same ("under :node-test every DOM claim degrades to a stated skip").

CONSEQUENCE: THE GUARD MUST BE KEPT, NOT DROPPED. A (when (browser?) ...) row
inside a -dom-cljs-test file is true in the browser lane and false in node,
which is the whole repair. Dropping the guard on the way across leaves a
browser-only row running under node, where it fails. PR #9681 — the precedent
the brief named — did exactly that and is red in CI for it: recents/save!
no-ops without localStorage because day8.re-frame2-xray.local-storage/available?
returns false, so (recents/load) answers [] and (= [:foo :bar] []) fails. That
PR is a sibling holding and was not touched here.

MEASURED, not inferred: a focused `node out/node-test.js --test=` selection of
the three affected namespaces ran 29 tests (17 + 11 + 1 = all three, both
-dom-cljs-test files included) containing 33 assertions, every assertion from
the node-lane namespace. The two dom namespaces loaded and skipped.

WHAT LANDED
1. toolbar_persistence_cljs_test.cljs -> toolbar_persistence_dom_cljs_test.cljs,
   ns renamed to match, all (when (browser?) ...) guards kept. Added an :after
   storage clear: the slot is chrome-wide and the browser lane runs every
   namespace on one page, so a leftover Mode.persist.* id would be in storage
   when the next namespace hydrates.
2. xray_preset row SPLIT by what each lane can prove. The slot flip stays on
   node as wire-cross-host-flips-the-keybinding-slot, now with a real
   precondition that the slot starts true so it reads a transition rather than
   an already-false slot. The listener removal moved to the new
   re-frame.story.xray-preset-dom-cljs-test, guarded.
3. tools/story/spec/015-Test-Coverage.md — three stale path references followed
   the rename. Nothing in CI grades those paths; they are inline code spans and
   the slug gate masks inline code. Pre-existing unrelated staleness at line 139
   (cites xray_preset_test.clj; the file is .cljc) was left alone as sprawl.

THE VACUITY, MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED. With wire-cross-host! suppressed and
the row running in a real browser, the assertion reports
  expected: (false? (xray-keybinding/attached?))   actual: (not (false? true))
attached? is TRUE — a real listener genuinely installed, which is exactly what
could never happen on node. That is the proof the old unguarded assertion was
passing vacuously.

GATES — every number from the run's own captured .exit file
  compile node-test                  exit 0   1967 files, 0 warnings
  node out/node-test.js              exit 0   11739 tests / 58661 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors
  compile browser-test               exit 0
  browser lane (port 8167)           exit 0   1002 tests / 5601 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors
  focused --test= (3 ns)             exit 0   29 tests / 33 assertions
  check_retired_spellings.py         exit 0   4661 files, content and paths
  check_test_lane_bijection.py       exit 0   1639 files, 45 lanes
  check_require_alias_dialect.py     exit 0   tools surface floor 0
  _browser-dom-lane-partition.test   exit 0   filename<->ns partition, unconditional in CI
  WITNESS: browser lane with faults planted in BOTH new files
                                     exit 1   3 failures naming
                                              toolbar_persistence_dom_cljs_test.cljs:340 and
                                              xray_preset_dom_cljs_test.cljs:89 + :91
  Plants reverted; restore verified by content hash against the committed
  objects and independently by git diff --quiet HEAD (exit 0).

NO NEW REDS. Nothing newly live failed, so no product defect surfaced from
these two files. No assertion was weakened to make a newly-live row green.

A GATE-DESIGN NOTE worth keeping: scripts/check_test_lane_bijection.py's B1
rule grades lane SELECTION, not lane EXECUTION. The old
toolbar_persistence_cljs_test.cljs WAS selected by :node-test — it just skipped
every row at runtime — so B1 passed on it throughout. Likewise the RF2_MIN_TESTS
floor counts TEST VARS, not assertions, and check-per-ns-isolation.cjs refuses
only on `tests === 0`, never on an assertion count. A namespace with N deftest
vars and zero executed assertions passes every floor in the repo. That is the
structural reason this class went unnoticed, and it is the question behind the
"should a lint rule catch this" item the censusing worker deliberately did not
file.
PROGRESS: PR #9685 merged 6a16c8085ec13038f57b2cb87d86df127db0d0b2 -- toolbar_persistence and
xray_preset are now live in the browser lane. With recents (PR #9681) that is 3 of the census's 16.
The title's "15 files" was already an undercount by one when written and is now wrong by three; the
remaining set is ~13. RE-DERIVE IT rather than trusting any number here.

`lanefix-b` is live on the remainder as of this note.

TWO MEASURED RESULTS FROM #9685 THAT CHANGE HOW THE REST SHOULD BE READ:

  * THE VACUITY WAS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not by reading. With the bridge suppressed in a real
    browser, xray_preset's `attached?` returned TRUE -- a listener genuinely installed, which can
    never happen on node. That is WHY the old unguarded assertion passed: it was reporting a removed
    keyboard listener to CI on every PR without one ever having been installed. Expect more of this
    shape in the remaining files; a dead PRECONDITION row silently hollows any live row below it.
  * THE COUNT IN THIS BEAD FOR toolbar_persistence WAS "20 of 20 rows". Measured: 11 deftests / 22
    assertion sites. The finding stood; the count did not.

NO NEWLY-LIVE ROW WENT RED in #9685, so no product defect surfaced there and no assertion was
weakened to force green.
=== WORKER lanefix-b — PR #9688 (5 of the remaining files; 60 assertions revived) ===

SCOPE DONE: static/shell, filters/persistence, spine-filters,
views/resizable-table-persistence, settings/effects — all under tools/xray/test/.
60 never-executed assertions now run in the browser lane.

THE CORRECTION IN THIS BEAD'S NOTES IS RIGHT AND WAS RE-VERIFIED AT SOURCE.
implementation/shadow-cljs.edn: :node-test ns-regexp is "cljs-test$", :browser-test
is ".*-dom-cljs-test$". The former is a bare suffix match that -dom-cljs-test also
satisfies, so a dom file loads on BOTH targets. Moving a row ADDS the browser lane.
The guard stays; the file LOCATION was the defect.

=== THE COUNT: I MAKE IT 13 REPAIRABLE, AND THE MAYOR'S 13 RECONCILES ===

A census keyed on both spellings found 18 non-DOM files carrying host-guard needles.
TWO OF THOSE 18 ARE FALSE POSITIVES OF POLARITY, and this is the one census refinement
worth keeping: resources_revalidation_cljs_test.cljc and keybinding_cljs_test.cljs
guard with when-not, not when. On node the host is ABSENT, so when-not is TRUE and
those rows RUN. They are a legitimate node-baseline shape, not this defect. A
polarity-blind census would have flagged 25 and 2 rows respectively and sent a worker
to "fix" tests that were already live.

Measured, not inferred. Static is-forms minus assertions actually executed on node,
per focused node run:
  resources_revalidation   19 vars  65 static  64 exec  gap 1     <- runs fine
  keybinding               57 vars 165 static 196 exec  gap -31   <- runs fine
  filters/persistence      15 vars  22 static  16 exec  gap 6     <- dead, repaired
  settings/effects         30 vars  68 static  40 exec  gap 28    <- dead, repaired
  spine_filters            29 vars  72 static  63 exec  gap 9     <- dead, repaired
  resizable_table_persist  15 vars  23 static  11 exec  gap 12    <- dead, repaired
  static/shell             27 vars  77 static 100 exec  gap n/a   <- dead 5 (loops inflate)
  resize_handle            33 vars  48 static  37 exec  gap 11    <- dead, NOT DONE (see below)
For five of the six the gap equals the independently-counted guarded rows EXACTLY.
Two instruments, one answer.

resizable_table_persistence is the sharpest case in the whole census: 15 test VARS
containing 11 ASSERTIONS — fewer assertions than vars, because whole deftests
contributed nothing at all.

=== ONE FILE DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: resize_handle_cljs_test.cljs (11 assertions) ===

NOT a premise failure — a live sequencing conflict the dispatch fence could not see.
Branch worker/resizeh-a is in that exact file migrating the resize-handle satellite
onto Fresco (rf2-k97c.3), 112 insertions / 32 deletions, and its diff RENAMES one of
the very deftests this item would move: handle-renders-nil-when-host-yields becomes
handle-yields-when-host-asserts-own-handle. Two workers in one file conflict every
time. Needs a follow-on once that PR lands; the 11 dead assertions are unchanged and
the census figures above are the starting point.

A NOTE ON THE SWEEP THAT FOUND IT, because the obvious form fails OPEN. A sweep over
REMOTE worker branches returned ZERO — only 11 of 39 worker branches were pushed, and
resizeh-a was local-only. The zero was a broken instrument, caught only because a
positive control (resizeh-a, already known to touch the file) failed to appear. Sweep
LOCAL refs (git for-each-ref refs/heads/worker/) and take the control from a branch
you have already proved touches the target.

The same corrected sweep surfaced worker/spinefilt-a in spine_filters_cljs_test.cljs.
Checked rather than assumed: its hunks all start at line 245+, every excision here is
below line 200, so the two do not overlap and neither reverts the other.

=== TWO FALSE DOCSTRINGS CORRECTED — THE AUTHORS' INTENT, NEVER REALISED ===

filters/persistence_cljs_test.cljs claimed localStorage exists under the node lane
"via the dom-storage polyfill the test-support harness installs". There is no such
polyfill and no such dependency: implementation/package.json carries 17 deps with zero
matches for jsdom, happy-dom or dom-storage, and that sentence was the ONLY occurrence
of the string dom-storage anywhere in the tree.

settings/effects_cljs_test.cljs carried the same fiction: ensure-stub-shell-root!
was commented "Some node test runtimes provide js/document". It opened with
(exists? js/document) ITSELF, so on node it created nothing and every
(when-let [el (shell-root)] (is ...)) bound nil. That helper is why the effects file
LOOKS like it supplies a host and does not — the single most misleading thing in the
census, and the reason its 28 dead assertions read as live to a casual reader.

=== CHOICES MADE PER PROPERTY, NOT PER FILE ===

1. resize-pair-tick-clamps-sub-floor-width asserts only over app-db and never reads
   storage. Its guard was INCIDENTAL, so the guard came off and the row STAYED on
   node, where it now runs for the first time. Moving it would have bought nothing.
2. Three settings/effects tests MIXED dead DOM claims with assertions that genuinely
   run on node. They were SPLIT, not moved — moving them whole would have taken LIVE
   assertions OFF the node lane, which is this bug in reverse. Two gained a real
   settings-slot assertion for a second dispatch that had asserted nothing.
3. Moved DOM rows bind the root, ASSERT it is present, then reach through some->.
   The (when-let [el (shell-root)] (is ...)) shape fails OPEN: a nil root silently
   skips the assertion rather than reporting one, which is exactly how these rows
   died. some-> also matters because the browser lane runs every namespace inside one
   cljs.test/run-block with no try/catch.

=== VACUITY FOUND AND TIGHTENED (the <= -> = shape, four instances) ===

Negative and default-valued assertions pass trivially against a storage that silently
swallows every write. Given sentinel preconditions:
  - static-shell empty-slot fallback: saves a NON-default and proves it persisted
    before asserting clear! restores :dynamic.
  - filters + resizable-table per-instance isolation: prove instance A's write LANDED
    before reading instance B empty.
  - spine-filters clear-muted-event-ids: proves both mutes persisted before asserting
    clear emptied them.
  - resizable-table tick-does-not-persist: writes a sentinel and reads it back before
    clearing, so the empty read afterwards is evidence the TICK withheld the write
    rather than evidence the host has no storage.

=== THE RED THAT ARRIVED, AND IT WAS THE TEST'S FAULT RATHER THAN THE PRODUCT'S ===

First browser run went red on exactly one assertion — the tick-does-not-persist
sentinel this PR added:
    expected: (= {:sentinel {:col 1}} (rt/load))
      actual: (not (= {:sentinel {:col 1}} {:sentinel {:col 24}}))
1 went to storage and came back 24: the load path clamping a sub-floor width to the
documented 24px minimum, exactly as resize-pair-tick-clamps-sub-floor-width says it
should. The test had picked an illegal sentinel. Raised to 150.

NO PRODUCT DEFECT SURFACED from any of the 60 newly-live assertions, and no assertion
was weakened to make a newly-live row green. The red is worth keeping on the record
because it is the DISCRIMINATING WITNESS that these rows now execute for real: the row
reached a genuine localStorage round-trip in a genuine browser, which it had never
done in either lane.

=== THE ASYMMETRY, MEASURED BOTH WAYS ===

The five new -dom-cljs-test namespaces carry 32 test vars, each with one skip marker
and a real branch.
  NODE, focused run, captured exit 0:  Ran 32 tests containing 32 assertions
    -> exactly one marker per test. Every revived row LOADS under :node-test and
       reports its stated skip. None vanished, none failed, no deftest holds zero
       assertions.
  BROWSER: the same 32 tests execute 78 real assertions.

=== GATES — every number from the run's own captured .exit file ===

  compile node-test                     exit 0
  node out/node-test.js (full)          exit 0   11748 tests / 58716 assertions,
                                                 0 failures 0 errors
  focused node, 5 new dom namespaces    exit 0   32 tests / 32 assertions (markers only)
  compile browser-test                  exit 0
  browser lane (port 8179)              exit 0   1029 tests / 5684 assertions,
                                                 0 failures 0 errors
  check_test_lane_bijection.py          exit 0   1645 test-defining files, 45 lanes,
                                                 every file selected, every selector reached
  _browser-dom-lane-partition.test.cjs  exit 0   2 passed (filename<->ns partition)
  check_require_alias_dialect.py        exit 0
  check_retired_spellings.py            exit 0
  check_fast_pr_gap.py --brief          exit 0   report only; 101 required checks no
                                                 local spine decides
Browser lane run twice: attempt 1 red with the single sentinel failure above, attempt
2 green after the fix.

=== STILL OPEN AFTER THIS PR ===

  - resize_handle_cljs_test.cljs — 11 assertions, blocked on worker/resizeh-a (above).
  - backgrounds_test.cljc and viewport_test.cljc — dead ONE LEVEL FURTHER OUT and
    unchanged by this work. Their namespaces end -test, not cljs-test, so :node-test

    help; they need a rename or a lane decision. Both sit under the fenced
    tools/story/** tree, so they were reported rather than improvised on.
  - The six tools/story/** files remain lanefix-a's tree (PR #9685 open).

title: Xray does not render under reagent-slim, while mount.cljs tells developers it does
description:
FOUND BY `acchar-a` WHILE BUILDING THE rf2-k97c ACCEPTANCE HARNESS (PR #9669). Reported, deliberately
NOT fixed — it is a production change and that dispatch was test-only.

## THE DEFECT

**Xray does not render under reagent-slim.** Measured across three adapters in one browser run, two
mount paths each:

    adapter        public `open!`                    Xray's own React root
    Reagent        paints                            paints
    reagent-slim   MOUNTS, THEN RAISES, NOTHING PAINTS   RAISES, NOTHING PAINTS
    UIx            refuses (documented diagnostic)   PAINTS

`frame-switcher/frame-switcher-view` raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context` and React takes the subtree
down.

## WHY, AND IT IS A ONE-LINE MECHANISM

Five Xray sources require `reagent.core` DIRECTLY and cross into the surviving Reagent islands using
FULL REAGENT's `as-element` — not the installed adapter's door. Under reagent-slim the installed
adapter is not full Reagent, so the crossing resolves nothing and the frame context is lost.

## WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN AN ORDINARY BUG: THE TOOL ADVERTISES THE SUPPORT IT LACKS

`mount.cljs`'s own `unsupported-substrate-diagnostic` tells developers the shell renders "through the
ratom-family adapters (Reagent / **reagent-slim**)". So a developer on reagent-slim is told by the
product that their substrate is supported, and gets a blank surface.

reagent-slim is one of the THREE adapters `implementation/adapters/README.md` says ship today.

## THE INVERSION WORTH NOTING

UIx — which the public `open!` REFUSES by the denylist — renders perfectly through Xray's own React
root. reagent-slim — which `open!` ACCEPTS — does not render at all. The denylist is refusing a
substrate that works and admitting one that does not.

That is directly relevant to child rf2-k97c.4 (retire the denylist), and it strengthens the case for
it rather than weakening it.

## IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT PINNED BY A TEST ROW, AND THAT REASONING IS SOUND

Reproducing it requires an UNCAUGHT RENDER-PHASE THROW, which reds the whole browser lane for every
unrelated suite — the browser runner fails any run with an uncaught `pageerror` independently of the
cljs.test summary. So a pin would make one real defect look like a broken lane. The finder chose to
report rather than pin, and I agree.

## THE LIKELY DISPOSITION — CHECK THIS BEFORE SPENDING A WORKER

The finder's own read: **the root swap may fix this for free.** The five direct `reagent.core`
requires exist to cross into the four surviving Reagent islands; when the root swap deletes those
islands, the crossings go with them.

So the first question is not "how do we fix this" but "does rf2-k97c.3's root swap already remove the
five crossings?" If yes, this closes as overtaken. If no, the residue is the work.

**DO NOT dispatch a separate repair while rf2-k97c.3 is in flight** — it would edit the same files the
swap is about to restructure.

## SEQUENCING

Blocked behind rf2-k97c.3. Re-read this bead when the root swap lands, verify whether the five
crossings survive, and close-as-overtaken or scope the residue then.
notes:
Merged-PR audit #9669: exact open finding reused for the reported reagent-slim blank-render/frame-context defect and false supported-adapter diagnostic. The new acceptance arms install full Reagent and UIx; neither verifies reagent-slim. Preserve the existing root-swap-first correction sequence. Added discovered-from rf2-k97c.3; no status transition, mayor notification or acknowledgment is claimed.
=== IMPLEMENTED, 2026-09-11. PR #9686, branch worker/slimfix-a. Worker slimfix-a. ===

THE PREMISE HOLDS AT TIP. Six sources carried `[reagent.core :as r]` with NINE executable
`r/as-element` sites — the count in the dispatch brief, not the "five sources" in the
description above. Re-measured on trunk 7bdb2253e2.

## THE MECHANISM, AND IT IS NOT THE ONE THE DESCRIPTION STATES

The description says "the crossing resolves nothing and the frame context is lost". That is
not what happens, and the real mechanism matters because it explains why the failure is
SILENT rather than loud.

Crossing with stock Reagent's `as-element` under reagent-slim works perfectly as far as
React is concerned. The element mounts, and the `:contextType` the `reg-view` head carries
IS honoured — `reagent2.impl.component` reads `(:contextType (meta f))` exactly as stock's
`fn-to-class` does — so the frame keyword genuinely reaches the mounted class. Nothing
resolves to nothing.

What breaks is one level lower. The FOREIGN build renders the subtree with ITS
in-flight-component slot bound, while `:adapter/current-component` routes to the INSTALLED
build and answers nil inside that subtree. `re-frame.views.provider/current-frame` reads
`(.-context cmp)` off that component, has no component to read, and returns nil — so every
ambient subscribe/dispatch beneath raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context` in React's render
phase and React takes the subtree down.

Both adapters register `:current-component` from their OWN build (`reagent.core` vs
`reagent2.core`); both share one `rf.views/current-frame`. That asymmetry is the defect.

## THE FIX

`:adapter/as-element` — the installed ratom build's own hiccup walk — published as a ROUTED
late-bind hook, the exact twin of `:adapter/current-component` whose mismatch causes the
defect. Directory entry carries the reasoning. Both ratom adapters publish it; no other
substrate does, because there is no substrate-neutral React element.

`day8.re-frame2-xray.substrate/as-element` is the single door all nine sites now use.

## A SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT FOUND IN THE SAME PLACE

`tools/xray/deps.edn` declared stock `reagent/reagent` BECAUSE those six sources required
`reagent.core` directly, so a reagent-slim page carrying Xray shipped BOTH ratom runtimes.
The dep's comment named `views.resizable-table` as the reason — whose `reagent.core` use had
already been removed, so the comment was stale before this bead touched it. Corrected rather
than deleted.

The dep STAYS, for exactly one production require (the fallback arm below). So this is now a
BUNDLE concern rather than a correctness one, confined to one file instead of six. Retiring
it needs a non-Reagent answer for the Fresco-root path. Worth a follow-up bead; not filed, as
that is the mayor's call.

## THE TRAP I FELL INTO, RECORDED BECAUSE IT NEARLY SHIPPED

The routed hook answers only while its own adapter is installed and returns nil otherwise. I
read that nil as unreachable, on the ground that `mount.cljs` refuses element-shaped
substrates — true of the public `open!`, and beside the point. Xray can own its own React
root, and the acceptance harness mounts the Static surface through FRESCO's root with UIx
installed as the application adapter. No ratom walk answers there, so my door returned nil,
`detail-panel` handed React a nil child, and the whole L4 panel vanished.

That is this bead's own blank-surface failure, reintroduced one substrate over by the fix for
it. Caught by the browser lane: captured exit 1, two failures in
`acceptance.uix-dom-cljs-test` criterion 2.

The door therefore PREFERS the installed ratom walk and FALLS BACK to stock Reagent's, which
is byte-for-byte what every crossing did before. The fallback cannot mask the defect: under
reagent-slim the routed hook answers, so it is never reached, and W1 pins that.

## THIS BEAD'S "CANNOT BE PINNED" CLAIM IS ANSWERED, NOT IGNORED

The description argues a pin is impossible because reproducing needs an uncaught render-phase
throw, which reds the whole browser lane independently of the cljs.test summary and would make
one real defect look like a broken runner. That is correct for a NAKED mount.

W2 mounts under `h/error-boundary`, which makes the throw a HANDLED one. Measured under a
deliberate plant: 5 rows failed, ALL FIVE in W2 and nowhere else, and the lane still ran all
992 tests to a full summary. So the defect IS pinnable, and the finder's reasoning was right
only about the instrument it had in mind.

## EVIDENCE (every figure from the gate's own captured .exit file)

* `npm run test:browser`, final rebased base — exit 0, 999 tests / 5615 assertions, 0
  failures, 0 errors, port 8163.
* `npm run test:browser`, SABOTAGE (stock arm forced; plant restored and verified by blob
  hash) — exit 1, 5 failures all in W2, lane completed. The caught error is verbatim
  `:rf.error/no-frame-context`, which is this bead's reported symptom reproduced under
  control.
* `npm run test:reagent-slim:smoke` — exit 0, 1 smoke, 0 failures.
* `npm run test:cljs` — exit 1 on first run; BOTH failures real and repaired (see below).
  Not re-run on the final base; left to CI per the gate time box.
* Retired-spelling / composition-vocab / image-key / ai-tracking ratchets — exit 0 each.

NOTE ON INSTRUMENTS: the harness reported "exit code 0" for three runs whose captured .exit
file read 1. Every number above is the captured one.

## TWO GATE FAILURES WORTH KEEPING

1. Each ratom adapter PINS the closed set of late-bind hooks it publishes, and the
   reagent-slim pin cross-checks that set against the late-bind directory for EQUALITY — so
   publishing a hook without pinning it is an automatic red. Both pins updated. The stock
   Reagent pin is one-directional and did not red, but was updated in the same act.

2. `get-fn-cached` answers the ROUTED-HOOK WRAPPER, not the raw published fn — `route-hook!`
   wraps so the chain can pick the installed adapter at call time. An `identical?` assertion
   against the raw var therefore FAILS on perfectly healthy wiring. W1 now measures the
   component type React receives for a fn head, reading all three through the SAME probe fn:
   stock caches its minted class on `.-cljsReactClass` and reagent2 on
   `.-cljsReagentClass-fn`, so one fn carries both independently, while a fresh fn per build
   would make the negative trivially true and prove nothing.

## SCOPE HELD

The UIx inversion is untouched — the `open!` denylist refusal path stands exactly as it was
(that is rf2-k97c.4, sequenced behind rf2-k97c.3). `mount.cljs`'s
`unsupported-substrate-diagnostic` needed NO edit: its sentence about the ratom-family
adapters is now simply true.

## A DISAGREEMENT THE MAYOR SHOULD SEE

This bead's description says "Blocked behind rf2-k97c.3" and "DO NOT dispatch a separate
repair while rf2-k97c.3 is in flight — it would edit the same files the swap is about to
restructure." rf2-k97c.3 IS in flight (status in_progress, PR #9573 described as increment 1
of N). I was dispatched anyway, with a brief that named rf2-k97c.3 and fenced one file for a
live PR, so the fence was overridden knowingly rather than missed. Flagged, not resolved.

The description's "the root swap may fix this for free" disposition does NOT hold yet: the
swap has migrated one panel (module_view), and none of the six crossing sources is it. The
residue was real and is what this PR fixes.
=== MAYOR ERROR: I DISPATCHED A REPAIR AGAINST THIS BEAD'S EXPLICIT "DO NOT DISPATCH" ===

This bead's SEQUENCING section says, in terms: "DO NOT dispatch a separate repair while rf2-k97c.3
is in flight -- it would edit the same files the swap is about to restructure", and "Blocked behind
rf2-k97c.3". rf2-k97c.3 is `in_progress` and was when I dispatched. I dispatched anyway, as
`slimfix-a`, and the result is PR #9686 (15 files, ready, green so far).

THE MECHANISM, BECAUSE IT IS MECHANICAL AND WILL RECUR OTHERWISE. I read this bead with
`bd show <id> --json | jq -r '.[0].description' | head -c 1600`. The blocking passage sits at
description line 56, past that cut. So the fence WAS recorded on the item exactly as the method
requires, and the item WAS the authority -- I truncated the read and never saw it. `bd ready` listed
this bead as ready, which is the "a ready list overstates readiness" trap doing precisely what it is
documented to do; the instrument was not wrong, it was answering a different question.

THE WORKER SAW THE CONFLICT AND FLAGGED IT RATHER THAN ASSUMING. Its words: the brief "named that
epic and fenced a file for it, so the fence looked knowingly overridden rather than missed". It was
missed. Recording that here so nobody reads the dispatch as a considered override.

WHAT THE WORKER MEASURED ABOUT THIS BEAD'S OWN PREMISE, WHICH CHANGES THE SEQUENCING QUESTION:

  * The finder's read -- "the root swap may fix this for free", because the crossings exist only to
    reach islands the swap will delete -- DOES NOT HOLD YET. The swap has migrated ONE panel
    (`module_view`) and NONE of the six crossing sources. So the restructuring this fence was
    protecting has not reached these files.
  * The stated MECHANISM in this bead (and in my brief) was wrong. It is not that the crossing
    "resolves nothing": React mounts the element and honours the reg-view head's `:contextType`, so
    the frame keyword does reach the class. The break is one level lower -- the foreign build binds
    ITS in-flight-component slot while `:adapter/current-component` routes to the INSTALLED build
    and answers nil, so `current-frame` has no component to read `(.-context cmp)` off. Two
    `:current-component` registrations, one shared `current-frame`.
  * This bead says the defect cannot be pinned without reddening the whole browser lane. That is
    true of a naked mount and is now ANSWERED: the witness mounts under `h/error-boundary`, and
    under sabotage it failed 5 rows while the lane still ran all 992 tests to a full summary.
  * The count: six sources, nine sites (this bead says five).

STATUS OF THE WORK: PR #9686 is NOT being merged on my judgement. It is held pending Mike's call,
recorded as a decision on this bead and surfaced in chat. It is not mergeable yet in any case (86
checks, 7 pending at the time of writing). The Public-API manifest drift-check is GREEN, so
publishing `:adapter/as-element` is not a public-name change by this project's own definition.

A SECOND DEFECT THE WORKER FOUND IN THE SAME PLACE is filed separately rather than absorbed here:
`tools/xray/deps.edn` declared stock Reagent BECAUSE of these requires, so a slim page carrying Xray
shipped both ratom runtimes.
HOLD STATUS AND WHAT IT IS COSTING, recorded per the backlog-reread loop's rule that a hold with no
cost written on it reads as free.

PR #9686 is now FULLY GREEN -- 87 checks, 0 pending, 0 failed, aggregator present, merge-tree clean
against trunk. It satisfies the merge criterion in full. It is held solely on the operator decision

WHAT THE HOLD COSTS, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED:

  * rf2-99qn is blocked behind it by construction -- that bead is about the residue #9686 leaves in
    tools/xray/deps.edn, so it cannot be measured until this lands.
  * The branch ages against a moving trunk. Nine changes have merged since #9686 went green. Its
    surface is 15 files including core (spine.cljs, late_bind/directory.cljc) and both adapters, so
    the conflict exposure grows rather than holds steady -- which is the opposite of what the

  * The user-facing defect stays shipped: Xray renders blank on reagent-slim, one of the three

WHAT THE HOLD IS NOT COSTING: no worker is idle on it, and no other bead is waiting on its surface.

THE FENCE'S ORIGINAL PREMISE REMAINS MEASURABLY FALSE, re-measured on trunk this tick rather than

title: Incomplete: Fresco self-exclusion misses Xray instances with custom frame IDs
description:
Audit of PR #9652 (4c5019d423f8c5dd5bdf39129e21e11957a3ebae). The new Fresco self-exclusion filter fixes the default frame but hardcodes own-frame? to (= :rf/xray frame), in panels/fresco_helpers.cljc around 650-665. The :rf.xray.fresco/data subscription calls without-own-frame with no instance/frame information. Xray supports custom own frame IDs: spec/008-Embedding-Contract.md:436-451 explicitly permits N shells with distinct :frame-id values, and ensure-xray-frame! accepts them. Once one of these shells mounts the migrated Fresco panel, its boundary and reads belong to that custom frame and survive all four filters; Mounted, Reads, Why, Advisor and Causal can therefore still present the tool as application evidence. The new browser witnesses use only :rf/xray for the tool.

Measured with Babashka loading the exact landed helper blob 79c6492d68f2449f5a899101deda91238e60ccc8: valid four-envelope input with frames [:rf/xray :xray/custom :app/main :unknown] returns [:xray/custom :app/main :unknown] in all four rosters. title: [implementation/epoch] Strict replay executes redacted inputs and reports success
description:
Snapshot: 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd. Before filing, main HEAD 37fe77aad297bda18684d1904e37f207ad72f795 has no diff on implementation/epoch or core trace/classification source.

Expected / actual
Strict replay is faithful-or-fail-loud: Tool-Pair.md:134-170 requires re-presenting recorded inputs, refusing incomplete evidence before dispatch where detectable. `rf/replay-epoch!` currently treats a redacted trigger vector as complete evidence, dispatches it, and reports :ok? true. A handler originally given a password string is invoked with :rf/redacted instead, changing app state and potentially firing external effects with substituted data.

Exact cause
- core trace.cljc:838-858,890-900 projects trace tags before deliver!, whose :epoch/capture-event call is at :732-772. classification.cljc:424-457,1157-1160 projects registration-owned event arguments; cofx projection similarly substitutes marks at :611-646.
- epoch/capture.cljc:661-766 builds :event and :rf.cofx from these ALREADY-PROJECTED run-start/generated trace tags. epoch/assembly.cljc:334-399 installs them as :trigger-event/:rf.cofx in the retained record. The raw in-process record is therefore not necessarily complete replay evidence, despite being raw relative to later off-box epoch projection.
- epoch/tool_pair.cljc:541-551 checks only outcome, synthetic id, trigger vector presence and cofx map presence. It does not reject input loss. :632-666 redispatches the substituted trigger and token and returns success. :strict only suppresses minting missing keys; a present redacted value is not absent.
- Actual tool caller: Pair preload runtime.cljs:2232-2295 invokes rf/replay-epoch! from a retained id; Pair-MCP tools/replay_epoch.cljs:62 onward forwards that gesture. The user need not read, copy, or supply the sentinel.

Actual-source isolated reproduction (bb classpath implementation/core/src + implementation/epoch/src):
```clojure
(require '[re-frame.core :as rf] '[re-frame.epoch]
         '[re-frame.substrate.adapter :as adapter]
         '[re-frame.substrate.plain-atom :as plain])
(adapter/install-adapter! plain/adapter)
(def seen (atom []))
(rf/reg-event :review/save {:sensitive [[:password]]}
  (fn [{:keys [db]} [_ payload]]
    (swap! seen conj (:password payload))
    {:db (assoc db :last-password (:password payload))}))
(rf/make-frame {:id :review/epoch})
(rf/dispatch-sync [:review/save {:password "secret"}] {:frame :review/epoch})
(def recorded (last (rf/epoch-history :review/epoch)))
(println (:trigger-event recorded))
(println (rf/replay-epoch! :review/epoch (:epoch-id recorded)))
(println @seen)
(println (rf/app-db-value :review/epoch))
```
Executed exit 0, with discriminating assertions:
`:recorded-trigger [:review/save {:password :rf/redacted}]`
`:handler-before-replay [secret]`
`:replay-result {:ok? true, :frame :review/epoch, :source-epoch-id 1, :event-id :review/save, :epoch-id 2}`
`:handler-after-replay [secret :rf/redacted]`
`:app-db {:last-password :rf/redacted}`
Root independently reran this actual-source witness and confirmed exit 0.

Impact / smallest repair
P2: the supported one-call strict replay executes with known-incomplete inputs and mutates app state while presenting success. Preserve existing privacy policy. The minimal correctness repair is to recognize capture-time loss of replay inputs and refuse that record through the existing structured non-replayable-record path BEFORE dispatch, with a useful loss reason. Do not add a parallel sensitive store, weaken emit/off-box projection, silently substitute data, or mint replacements. Preserve faithful replay for complete inputs. A legitimate author-supplied value equal to a marker should not be confused with proven capture loss if the existing capture seam can distinguish them.

Focused acceptance
- Real classified event arg is redacted at trace capture; replay refuses before the handler, external effects or app-db change, with a clear structured reason.
- Cover :large input elision and classified recordable coeffects (including mid-run generated facts) through the same incomplete-evidence check, not separate replay implementations.
- Unclassified argument/fact control still replays exactly; strict missing-key and fn-override refusals stay unchanged; no raw input appears on the wire.
- Pair-MCP forwards the refusal honestly; focused CLJ/CLJS tests exercise public replay-by-id rather than only fabricating a malformed record.

Dedupe / decisions / limits
Searched open and closed epoch/replay/redacted records plus relevant memories. rf2-ov144 is CLOSED for the one-call API, with acceptance for faithful args and fail-loud incomplete records; its replay tests cover unclassified args, not emit-projected inputs. epoch_privacy_test.clj:657-684 only checks the off-box trigger result, not raw replay completeness. rf2-kuky.7/.92 concern egress door/hook retirement; neither owns this failure. This is not rf2-ifzi's wrong-owner egress bug: the target declaration is correctly applied here; replay then misuses the lossy result. No implementation edits, full suite, CLJS compilation, or production-bundle run; only the isolated bb source probe and source/spec/tool inspection.
acceptance_criteria: Classified/lossy trigger and cofx records refuse before dispatch and mutation; complete-input replay still faithfully re-presents facts without minting; privacy remains intact, and public CLJ/CLJS plus Pair refusal tests discriminate.
notes:
--- 2026-09-07 (worker/epoch-a, PR #9362) — FIXED, failing-first evidence recorded ---

PREMISE CHECK. The bead's snapshot claim still held at dispatch: `git diff --stat
7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd origin/main -- implementation/epoch` and the same
against 37fe77aad297bda18684d1904e37f207ad72f795 both returned EMPTY at base 90e9b0008a, so
trunk had not moved under the finding. The reported behaviour reproduced exactly, in the
repository's own JVM suite rather than a bb probe.

FAILING FIRST (implementation/epoch, `clojure -M:test -n re-frame.epoch-replay-cljs-test`,
captured exit 1, 17 failures / 104 assertions across 13 tests). The discriminating ones:

  replay-refuses-a-record-whose-event-args-were-redacted-at-capture
    - the RAW record's `:trigger-event` asserted as `[:replay/save {:password :rf/redacted}]`
      — that assertion PASSED, which is the finding: capture-time loss reaches the raw ring.
    - `(false? (:ok? res))` → actual `{:ok? true, :source-epoch-id 22, :event-id :replay/save,
      :epoch-id 23}`
    - `(= ["topsecret"] @seen)` → actual `["topsecret" :rf/redacted]` — the handler WAS
      re-invoked with the substitution
    - `(= 1 @fired)` → actual 2 — the external effect re-fired
    - `(= "topsecret" (:last-password (rf/app-db-value ...)))` → actual `:rf/redacted` —
      app-db was mutated with substituted data
  replay-refuses-a-record-whose-event-args-were-size-elided-at-capture
    - same shape on the `:large` axis; the `:rf.size/large-elided` marker in the raw trigger
      asserted PASSING, `:ok? true`, handler re-invoked.
  replay-refuses-a-record-whose-recorded-cofx-was-classified-at-capture
    - the recorded token asserted as `{:token :rf/redacted :user "ada"}` — PASSED; the replay
      then succeeded and the handler saw `:rf/redacted` in place of "jwt-abc".
  replay-still-succeeds-for-an-unclassified-control — PASSED before AND after (the control).

AFTER THE FIX the same command is exit 0, 13 tests / 104 assertions, 0 failures.

THE FIX (code-only in behaviour; `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/tool_pair.cljc`).
`lost-replay-inputs` walks the record's replay MATERIAL — `:trigger-event` and the `:rf.cofx`
token — over the shared `re-frame.elision/walk-tree` skeleton, collecting every capture-loss
substitution (`:rf/redacted`, or a `:rf.size/large-elided` marker) with its concrete path.
A non-empty result is refused BEFORE dispatch through the EXISTING structured
non-replayable-record path, as `:cause :incomplete-inputs` with
`:lost [{:slot :trigger-event|:rf.cofx :path <path> :loss :redacted|:elided} ...]`, sorted for
determinism. No configuration key that would permit the unfaithful replay, no warn-and-proceed,
no redaction-repair mechanism, no parallel sensitive store, no minting; emit/off-box projection
untouched.

DESIGN DECISION, and the bead's conditional. The bead asked that an author-supplied value equal
to a marker not be confused with proven capture loss "IF the existing capture seam can
distinguish them". It cannot, reliably, and a seam-based gate FAILS OPEN. Redaction reaches
recorded replay material from three sources besides a static `reg-event`/`reg-cofx`
declaration: the unconditional summarisation of framework-owned synthetic payloads
(`project-spawn-synthetic-payloads` substitutes regardless of any declaration), the per-event-id
DYNAMIC projectors (`:rf.mutation/execute` defers to a late-bound hook whose classification
lives on the mutation spec, not the event registration), and the fail-closed arms that
substitute when a frame cannot be resolved. Gating the check on "does the registration declare
this path?" would silently admit every one of those. It would also read TODAY's declarations
against YESTERDAY's record. So the test is the PRESENCE of a reserved substitution in the
recorded material — the conservative direction, and the only one compatible with
faithful-or-fail-loud. Recorded here because the bead raised the question explicitly.

SPEC. `spec/Tool-Pair.md`'s replay bullet enumerated the `:cause` values as a closed list, so a
new cause would have made the spec wrong about its own surface: one cause added to that list
plus one bullet stating when `:incomplete-inputs` fires and what `:lost` carries. `spec/API.md`
already described the refusal as "a halted / synthetic / INCOMPLETE record
(`:rf.epoch/replay-non-replayable-record` + `:cause`)" WITHOUT enumerating causes, so neither it
nor the `spec/api-manifest*.edn` family moved. No facade export added or changed —
`rf/replay-epoch!`'s arities, return shape and false-when-elided behaviour are unchanged, so no
classification entry is due and `implementation/core/**` was not touched.

CONSUMERS. `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/.../replay_epoch.cljs` is already refusal-reason-agnostic —
every `{:ok? false …}` rides as `isError: true` — so the new refusal forwards honestly with no
code change; its catalogue spec row (`tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md`) and
`docs/api/re-frame.epoch.md` were the two other places enumerating the causes and were kept in
step.

GATES (captured exit codes, all from `gate root: <this worktree>`, verified on the post-rebase
base): `sh scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` exit 0 — PASS fast PR spine; JVM core 2239/11526, JVM epoch
563/7307, CLJS :node-test 11322/57119, all 0 failures 0 errors; mkdocs --strict built; clj-kondo
clean. `sh scripts/test-jvm-tools.sh` exit 0 — PASS tools JVM artefacts (ten artefacts, all
green). Ratchets: beads-PR-boundary, ai-tracking, commit-attribution, workflow-job-timeouts,
allocation-non-claim all exit 0. The CLJS half is positively evidenced rather than inferred: the
compiled `re_frame.epoch_replay_cljs_test.js` in the build this run produced contains all six new
deftests (control: a pre-existing deftest in the same namespace reads the same count).
close_reason: PR #9362 merged; verified HEAD == origin/main at be72e23763. 6 files, 374 insertions / 26 deletions. Strict replay now refuses incomplete evidence before dispatch instead of executing a redacted trigger vector and reporting :ok? true — which is what spec/Tool-Pair.md's faithful-or-fail-loud requirement demands. This was the one with a real safety edge: a handler originally given a password string was being re-invoked with :rf/redacted, changing app state and potentially firing external effects with substituted data. No worker report (fleet starved); close rests on the merged diff and a green rollup at band 87.

title: [implementation/adapters/reagent-slim] Form-3 factories invoke their returned class constructor as a Form-2 renderer
description:
Surface: implementation/adapters/reagent-slim. Source snapshot 7ffdacf24d797b67864af78a4625b2c1cb3ef8fd; compared with mayor HEAD e8afc5fba80a638c1cdf436ae5f27127c3fc677b, with no diff anywhere under this adapter.

Expected: the supported per-instance Form-3 factory `(defn panel [props] (let [...] (r/create-class ...)))` mounts its returned class, preserving its closure state and lifecycle. This is not a proposed API: implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/FORM-3.md:274-309 uses exactly that shape for its canonical Google Maps wrapper, and lines318 onward explicitly say each `[google-map ...]` mount owns separate closure atoms. The stock-Reagent Form-3 lifecycle recipe and core's reg-view* example use the same factory shape.

Actual: the live slim renderer classifies the returned create-class constructor as a Form-2 inner function and invokes the constructor with ordinary render arguments. No Form-3 instance is mounted and its render/lifecycle methods are not reached correctly.

Exact causal path:
- template.cljs:1075-1083 wraps a plain factory via component/fn-to-class and constructs the OUTER class. Its render delegates to component.cljs:wrap-render (make-render-method at 566-577).
- wrap-render's untagged path calls the factory at component.cljs:313. A create-class result is a JS function, so `(fn? out)` at 322 succeeds. It stores the CLASS as cljsRenderFn and calls `(apply out args)` at 325. There is no reagent-class? check before this branch. The already-cached path at 286-288 then continues calling that same constructor on later renders. The tagged Form-1 fallback at 305-309 has the same discrimination problem.
- create-class*'s constructor at component.cljs:665-674 calls React.Component with this, assigns instance fields and returns this. Its real render lives on the prototype (687-688), with lifecycle methods installed separately. Calling the constructor as an ordinary render function is not mounting it; the exact error depends on the this/argv shape, but the class render and lifecycle cannot be correct through this path.
- template/react-component-element and source_coord_annotation both already recognize reagent classes, but only at vector-head/output boundaries respectively. Neither gets to handle the class before wrap-render applies it.
- The static serializer mirrors the same mistake for a RETURNED class: reagent2/dom/server.cljs:951-956 applies any fn? output as Form-2. Its existing class dispatch at 1009 handles only a class directly in the hiccup head. Preserve static markup parity for the factory shape when repairing the distinction.

Minimal reproduction, using only reagent2 (no re-frame reg-view pipeline):

```clojure
(def lifecycle (atom []))
(defn panel [_initial-label]
  (let [instance (js-obj)]
    (r/create-class
      {:reagent-render (fn [label] [:div {:id "factory-panel"} label])
       :component-did-mount (fn [_] (swap! lifecycle conj [:mount instance]))
       :component-will-unmount (fn [_] (swap! lifecycle conj [:unmount instance]))})))
(def root (rdc/create-root mount-element))
(rdc/render root [panel "hello"])
;; Flush using the existing DOM harness. Expected DOM: hello, one mount.
(rdc/render root [panel "updated"])
;; Expected: updated, same class/closure, no second mount.
(rdc/unmount root)
;; Expected: one unmount with the same instance token.
;; Also: (reagent2.dom.server/render-to-static-markup [panel "hello"])
;; should emit the div without running mount/unmount lifecycle.
```

Concrete impact: the adapter's own principal imperative-widget recipe (maps, charts, popovers and cleanup-owning widgets) fails to render/mount, despite direct create-class vector heads working. This is separate from rf2-xccd: that core issue accepts a class directly into reg-view* and calls it there. Here the caller correctly supplies an outer factory, and even plain reagent2 with no re-frame registration breaks downstream in slim's runtime.

Smallest repair: discriminate a returned Reagent class before the ordinary Form-2 function branch, using the existing reagent-class? predicate. Cache a stable class-mounting render path with fresh args rather than invoking the constructor, retaining per-mounted-factory identity and closure ownership. Keep direct class heads and true Form-2 inner functions unchanged. Apply the same classification at the static serializer's factory-output boundary while continuing to omit static lifecycle execution. No new public API, cap keys or general renderer redesign.

Existing tests and limits: reagent_slim_source_coord_form3_cljs_test.cljs:103-115 only calls rf/view and asserts that the wrapper returns the class; its lifecycle row manually does `(new out ...)`. That proves annotation preserves identity, not that the normal slim renderer mounts a factory-returned class. Component tests predominantly construct classes directly. The claimed defect is source-proven, NOT a test-count complaint. This review did not compile CLJS, run React/browser tests, modify implementation, install dependencies or change shared runtime. The reproduction above is source-derived, not executed; exact thrown text is deliberately not claimed.

Dedupe: current all-status tracker results plus tracked historical issues inspected for reagent-slim/Form-3/wrap-render; relevant Form-3/reg-view memories read. Existing rf2-08hx1 repairs callback-argv documentation, not class-output classification; rf2-6r9j.31 addresses error-boundary test execution. Historic rf2-e6hsn no longer resolves in bd; its durable source pins were inspected as above. rf2-xccd is explicitly distinguished. No existing issue found owning the factory-returned-class runtime outcome.
acceptance_criteria: A real slim DOM mount of a plain factory returning create-class renders initial and updated props, retains per-factory class/closure identity and runs mount/unmount exactly once. Include two sibling factory instances and keep a genuine Form-2 plus direct-class control. Static markup of the same factory emits matching content without lifecycle execution. No manual new/prototype invocation can substitute for the factory mount witness.
notes:
--- 2026-09-07 AUSEST — implemented on worker/adapters-b, PR #9361 (bead left OPEN for the mayor) ---

PREMISE VERIFIED AT SOURCE.

The factory shape IS documented, exactly as the bead says: FORM-3.md's canonical
`google-map` example is a plain `defn` taking `_initial-props` whose body
`let`-binds `el-ref` / `map-instance` atoms and returns `(r/create-class {...})`,
and the "Five moving parts" list under it states each mount of `[google-map ...]`
gets its own pair of atoms. So this is a documented recipe that did not work, not
a proposed API — the bead's fence holds.

"No diff anywhere under this adapter" since mayor HEAD e8afc5fba8 — STILL HELD at
my base 90e9b0008a: `git diff e8afc5fba8 90e9b0008a -- implementation/adapters/reagent-slim`
is empty.

Causal path confirmed by reading the constructs (not the line numbers):
`wrap-render`'s `:else` branch tests `(fn? out)` with no `reagent-class?` check
before it, and a class from `create-class*` is a plain JS fn (it is
`(fn [props] (this-as this ...))` with `.-cljsReagentClass` set), so it took the
Form-2 branch, was cached as `.-cljsRenderFn`, and was APPLIED. The
compile-time-tagged Form-1 fallback carries the identical defect — and that is
the branch `reg-view` actually reaches for this shape, because
`classify-form-body` tags a body Form-1 whenever its last form is not a literal
`(fn …)`, which a `(let [...] (create-class ...))` body is not.

WHAT CHANGED.

- component.cljs gains two private helpers next to `wrap-render`:
  `class-mounting-render-fn` (returns `(fn [& args] (into [klass] args))`) and
  `form-2-inner-fn` (returns the class-mounting wrapper for a `reagent-class?`
  output, the value unchanged otherwise). Both the tagged-Form-1 fallback and the
  `:else` Form-2 branch now cache `(form-2-inner-fn out)` instead of `out`.
- WHY `[klass & args]` RATHER THAN A CONSTRUCTOR CALL: handing the class back as
  a hiccup HEAD re-enters machinery that already exists — `vec-to-elem`'s
  `(component/reagent-class? tag)` arm routes to `react-component-element`, which
  does `React.createElement(klass, #js {:__rfArgv argv})`. React then owns the
  instance. The class TYPE is stable across renders (the wrapper closes over the
  one class the factory returned), so an update reconciles in place: no remount,
  and the factory's per-mount closure survives. This is exactly stock Reagent's
  `reagent.impl.component/wrap-render`, which caches
  `(fn [& args] (as-element (apply vector res args)))` for a `reagent-class?`
  render result — so the repair is the upstream shape, not an invention.
- server.cljs `emit-render-fn` gains the mirrored discrimination: its `if` becomes
  a `cond` whose FIRST arm is `(component/reagent-class? out)` →
  `(emit-element sb (into [out] args))`, which re-enters `emit-hiccup-vector`
  where the existing `reagent-class?` head dispatch renders `:reagent-render`
  through the Form-1/Form-2 path. Static markup therefore matches the live DOM
  content while still executing NO lifecycle, which is the parity the bead asked
  to preserve.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: no new public API, no cap keys, no renderer redesign, no
change to direct class heads or to genuine Form-2 inner fns (both are pinned as
controls in the new suite). `reagent-class?` alone is the discriminator, per the
bead; a generic foreign React class returned from a factory is out of scope and
is not a documented shape.

NEW SUITE: test/reagent2/impl/form3_factory_dom_cljs_test.cljs. The live
assertions are `-dom-cljs-test` so the `:browser-test` runner executes them
against a real `react-dom/client` root (the bead's acceptance criteria refuses a
manual `new`/prototype invocation as a substitute, and this obeys that); under
`:node-test` they gate on `(browser?)` and no-op. The static-markup deftest is
deliberately NOT gated — `render-to-static-markup` is pure string building — so
it runs on BOTH lanes. Coverage: initial mount, update preserving closure token
and firing no second mount, exactly-once unmount with the same token, two sibling
factory mounts owning DISTINCT tokens, a genuine Form-2 control (asserting its
setup fn ran exactly once, so the inner-fn cache is still doing its job), a
direct-class-head control, and static markup with an empty lifecycle log.

FAILING-TEST-FIRST EVIDENCE (both states quoted).
- Pre-fix, focused `:node-test` run of this ns: exit 1 — 4 tests, 4 assertions,
  1 error. The static-markup assertion threw
  `:rf.error/static-markup-bad-element`, "Cannot render {:type :fn} as static
  markup", which is the factory-returned class being applied as a Form-2 inner
  render fn and yielding a non-renderable value. The three live deftests reported
  their node-lane no-op.
- Post-fix, same focused run: exit 0 — 4 tests, 6 assertions, 0 failures 0
  errors. The assertion count rises because the static deftest now runs all three
  of its assertions instead of erroring on the first.

Filed by the Codex correctness review. No worker report (fleet starved); close rests on the merged diff and a green rollup at band 87.

title: api(schema): validator port as a value (set-schema-fns! + default-schema-fns + schema-fns); delete six names
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from schema.md (ref schema.1); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

The framework consults exactly three functions — validate, explain, print — held in three private atoms in `re-frame.schemas.validator`. Seven public names on `re-frame.schemas` mutate or read them, and every one lowers to `reset!`/deref on the same atoms:

| Name (`re-frame.schemas`, tier) | Lowers to | Distinct job? |
|---|---|---|
| `set-schema-fns! {:validate f :explain g :print h}` (advanced, "preferred" — `spec/API.md:553`) | partial `reset!` per PRESENT key; returns the full bundle | the door |
| `set-schema-validator! f` (advanced) | `(reset! validator-fn f)` | `= (set-schema-fns! {:validate f})` |
| `set-schema-explainer! g` (advanced) | `(reset! explainer-fn g)` | `= (set-schema-fns! {:explain g})` |
| `set-schema-printer! h` (advanced) | `(reset! printer-fn (or h default-edn-print))` | `= (set-schema-fns! {:print h})` (same nil coercion) |
| `reset-schema-validator!` (advanced) | three `reset!`s to the framework defaults | `= (set-schema-fns! <defaults>)` — but the defaults are private (`defn-` at `validator.cljc:48,61`), so this verb is the only way to spell it; its own docstring calls it a test-support helper, and it resets all three despite the name |
| `snapshot-schema-fns` (implementation) | deref the three atoms | the only READ, named like a test helper |
| `restore-schema-fns! bundle` (implementation) | `(set-schema-fns! bundle)` — literally, `validator.cljc:330` | none |

Beneath those, `re-frame.core-schemas` still carries four `defwrapper`s (`set-schema-validator!`, `set-schema-fns!`, `set-schema-explainer!`, `set-schema-printer!`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_schemas.cljc:57-131`) served by four late-bind hooks (`:schemas/set-schema-validator!` / `-explainer!` / `-printer!` / `-fns!`, `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:362-377`, published at `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas.cljc:134-137`). rf2-wad2fl removed their `re-frame.core` re-exports (`core.cljc:1036-1048` records it), so the wrappers and hooks have ZERO consumers: `git grep -E "core-schemas/set-schema"` → 0; `git grep -E "get-fn(-cached)? :schemas/set-schema"` → 0.

Two documents still teach the deleted facade spelling `rf/set-schema-validator!`, which does not resolve: `spec/Conventions.md:1434-1435` (and the bucket-3 list/example at `:1339,1344`) and `docs/core/how-to/configure-dev-and-prod.md:127`.

## Evidence (tip 6445d0611b; `git grep -c -F <name> -- . ':!ai'`, app = `examples/`+`testbeds/`, tool = `tools/`)

| Name | app | tool | framework tests | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `set-schema-fns!` | 0 | 0 | 12 files | every non-schemas-artefact fixture (routing, ssr, ssr-ring, flows, security) already uses this one |
| `set-schema-validator!` | 0 | 0 | 20 files | most calls install `nil` or a `(fn [_ _] …)` stub |
| `set-schema-explainer!` | 0 | 0 | 3 files | |
| `set-schema-printer!` | 0 | 0 | 2 files (19 lines in `printer_seam_test.clj`) | |
| `reset-schema-validator!` | 0 | 0 | 14 files | always in a `finally` or a fixture (`schemas/test_fixture.clj:85`) |
| `snapshot-schema-fns` / `restore-schema-fns!` | 0 | 0 | 7 files | always `let` + `finally` pairs |
| `core-schemas/set-schema-*` wrappers + hooks | 0 | 0 | 0 | dead since rf2-wad2fl |

The only live pattern outside boot docs is test isolation: capture → stub → restore. That is Clojure's `let` + `finally` over a VALUE, which is what the read + installer already give once the default bundle is a public value.

## Target API

```clojure
;; re-frame.schemas (home namespace re-frame.schemas.validator; re-exported as today)
(def default-schema-fns                 ; the framework default bundle, as a public VALUE
  {:validate default-malli-validate     ; late-binds to :schemas/malli-validate, soft-passes when unbound (unchanged)
   :explain  default-malli-explain
   :print    default-edn-print})

(schema-fns)                            ; => {:validate f|nil :explain g|nil :print h}   the READ, no bang
(set-schema-fns! {:validate f})         ; partial or full install; returns the installed bundle (UNCHANGED)
```

| Use case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| install a port at boot | `(set-schema-fns! {…})` | unchanged |
| swap one fn | `(set-schema-validator! f)` | `(set-schema-fns! {:validate f})` |
| disable validation | `(set-schema-validator! nil)` | `(set-schema-fns! {:validate nil})` — explicit nil keeps its meaning; an OMITTED key still retains the prior value |
| reset to defaults | `(reset-schema-validator!)` | `(set-schema-fns! schemas/default-schema-fns)` |
| capture / restore | `(let [s (snapshot-schema-fns)] … (finally (restore-schema-fns! s)))` | `(let [s (schema-fns)] … (finally (set-schema-fns! s)))` |
| read what is installed | `(snapshot-schema-fns)` | `(schema-fns)` |

Semantics that MUST NOT change: omitted-vs-explicit-nil per key; `:print nil` coerces to `default-edn-print` inside `set-schema-fns!` (the printer is never nil — `run-printer` relies on it); the bundle setter returns the full installed map; installs are NOT transactional (the implementation says so; do not describe them as atomic — codex). `using-default-validator?` (`validator.cljc:332`, `identical?` against `default-malli-validate`) still answers true after `(set-schema-fns! default-schema-fns)` because the value carries the same fn objects — keep it, and pin that in a test. Return-value migration: the scalar setters returned the installed fn; a caller that used the return selects the key from the bundle (`(:validate (set-schema-fns! …))`) — matters for `:print nil`, whose installed value is the default printer, not nil.

Naming note: the fable doc spelled the value `malli-schema-fns`. `default-schema-fns` is proposed here because the bundle is "the framework default" — its `:print` is the EDN canonicaliser (not Malli) and `:validate`/`:explain` soft-pass when the Malli adapter is unbound — and it is exactly what `reset-schema-validator!` restored. Either spelling is fine; pick one and use it everywhere.

## Corroboration

TWO-REVIEWER (dispatchable). Codex (`schema-backend.md`) independently reached "keep `set-schema-fns!` as the sole installer; delete the three scalar setters; preserve omitted-vs-nil and the bundle return; `reset-schema-validator!` is misnamed as well as unconsumed". The fable README's reconciled map lists "the schema setters folding into `set-schema-fns!`" under two-reviewer findings. Codex's narrower option is recorded: it would keep snapshot/restore as internal fixture helpers and publish a defaults value or reader "only if custom-backend authors actually need to compose or inspect those values". This bead takes the fable shape because the public value and read are precisely what make `reset-schema-validator!`, `snapshot-schema-fns` and `restore-schema-fns!` deletable rather than renamed — take the three together or not at all. Codex on the wrappers: delete "after checking symbol-based consumers, not just qualified call sites" — done above (0 either way).

KEEP `set-schema-fns!` (:198) with its nil-print coercion, `using-default-validator?` (:332), `run-validator`/`run-explainer`/`run-printer` (:341-369), `clear-edn-print-cache!`.
