title: api(observability): delete the sink-entry :opts bag that make-frame validates and route-stream! never delivers
description:
_Filed 2026-09-05 12:37:46 AUSEST by the API-review wave-3 coordinator from observability.md (ref observability.1); parent epic rf2-kuky. Local-only dossiers: ai/findings/API-review/{fable,codex}/ (gitignored; may be deleted)._

## Problem

A frame's `:observability` sink entry accepts an `:opts` map. `make-frame` validates its shape and fails loud on a non-map (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame_classification.cljc:240-252`, pinned by `implementation/core/test/re_frame/frame_classification_cljs_test.cljc:189-206` `fail-loud-on-bad-observability-opts`). Nothing ever reads it: `route-stream!` (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/observability.cljc:172-189`) reads only `:sink` (:181) and `:rf.egress/profile` (:183), and `deliver-to-sink!` (:159-170) calls `(f projected)` (:168) with the record alone. Every teaching sample carries the bag (`:opts {:service "checkout-spa" :env "prod"}`): `observability.cljc:22`, `frame_classification.cljc:14`, `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:281-285`, `spec/API.md:701`, `spec/002-Frames.md:654`, `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:4325-4332` (`FrameSinkEntry`, rowed "vendor-specific, framework does not own the vocabulary"), `docs/core/how-to/configure-dev-and-prod.md:143`, `docs/core/how-to/keep-secrets-out-of-traces.md:254,258`, `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/api-cheatsheet.md:153`, `skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/privacy-and-elision.md:140,143,152`. A slot designed as a pass-through that does not pass through is the textbook `spec/Principles.md` §No silent swallow violation, on the door the spec calls the NORMAL production observation surface (`spec/API.md:585`, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1258`, `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:270`).

## Evidence

- `observability.cljc:159-170` `deliver-to-sink!` — `(f projected)`; `:172-189` `route-stream!` — `(:sink entry)`, `(get entry :rf.egress/profile default-profile)`; no other key is read anywhere in the namespace (`grep -n ":opts" observability.cljc` → line 22 only, the docstring sample).
- `frame_classification.cljc:240-252` — the validation; `:143-150` the section comment naming `:opts` as part of the entry grammar; `:84` lists `:opts` among the bare keys of the frame config.
- Consumers writing `:opts` outside docs/spec/skills: 0 (`git grep -n ":opts {:service"` → only the files above plus `observability_routing_cljs_test.cljc:78` and `frame_classification_cljs_test.cljc:109,156`). `register-observability-sink!` has 0 non-test callers (expected — `spec/015:292`), so no external sink relies on the bag.
- `spec/conformance/fixtures/data-classification-observability-sink-receives-projected-record.edn` does not carry `:opts` — the conformance corpus is unaffected.

## Target API

The sink entry becomes a CLOSED map. Vendor configuration is the sink fn's own business (it closes over it); per-frame branching reads the record's `:frame` slot, which every projected record carries.

```clojure
;; before
(rf/make-frame {:id :app/main
                :observability {:errors [{:sink :my-app.sinks/sentry
                                          :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-observability
                                          :opts {:service "checkout-spa" :env "prod"}}]}})
(rf/register-observability-sink! :my-app.sinks/sentry (fn [record] (sentry/capture record)))

;; after — the entry is {:sink kw} + optional :rf.egress/profile, nothing else;
;; an unknown key (`:opts` included) fails loud at make-frame like a bad profile does.
(rf/make-frame {:id :app/main
                :observability {:errors [{:sink :my-app.sinks/sentry
                                          :rf.egress/profile :rf.egress/off-box-observability}]}})
(let [tags {:service "checkout-spa" :env "prod"}]
  (rf/register-observability-sink! :my-app.sinks/sentry
    (fn [record] (sentry/capture (assoc record :tags tags)))))
```

`validate-sink-entry!` gains one clause: any key outside `#{:sink :rf.egress/profile}` throws `:rf.error/bad-frame-classification` with `:bad-key [:observability <stream> <k>]` and `:bad-entry entry` (the same shape the profile clause uses at :228-239). Deleting the `:opts` clause WITHOUT closing the map would leave `:opts` silently ignored — the same accept-and-drop shape, one validator short — so the closed map is part of the fix, not gold plating. (If a shared vendor sink ever needs per-frame configuration, the record's `:frame` is the key; delivering a second argument is the documented alternative and is NOT done here — codex and fable both favour removal on the measured consumers.)

## Corroboration

One-reviewer area; codex cross-check confirmed this defect at source ("frame validation accepts an `:opts` map, while sink routing passes only the projected record… For today's measured consumers I favor removal, with configuration captured in the registered function and existing `:frame` attribution available… Either choice must remove the accept-and-drop contract from code and examples"). Grok: "Delete `:opts`… never accept-and-drop."

## Deletion list

- `frame_classification.cljc:240-252` (the `:opts` clause) — replaced by the closed-map clause; `:143-150` comment and `:84` and `:14` docstring mentions.
- `observability.cljc:22` docstring sample.
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:4325-4332` — the `[:opts {:optional true} [:map-of :keyword :any]]` row of `FrameSinkEntry` and the comment line "`:rf.egress/profile` and `:opts` are optional"; make the map closed (`{:closed true}`) so the schema says what the validator does. HOT-ZONE.
- `spec/015-Data-Classification.md:206` (principle 4: "Vendor-specific sink fields live under a local `:opts` map" → vendor configuration is closed over by the sink fn; the sink id stays outside the framework namespace), `:281-285` sample, `:289` ("or a non-map `:opts`" → "or any key beyond `:sink` / `:rf.egress/profile`"). Not hot-zone.
- `spec/002-Frames.md:654` ("with an optional `:rf.egress/profile` and `:opts` map"). HOT-ZONE.
- `spec/API.md:701` (`{:handled-events [{:sink <id> :rf.egress/profile … :opts {…}}] …}`). HOT-ZONE.
- Docs: `configure-dev-and-prod.md:143`, `keep-secrets-out-of-traces.md:254,258`.
- Skills: `api-cheatsheet.md:153`, `privacy-and-elision.md:140,143,152`.
- Tests: `frame_classification_cljs_test.cljc:109` (drop `:opts` from the good entry), `:156` (the missing-`:sink` bad entry `{:opts {:service "x"}}` — keep the case, spell the entry without `:opts`), `:189-206` (replace `fail-loud-on-bad-observability-opts` with `fail-loud-on-unknown-sink-entry-key`, asserting `:bad-key [:observability :handled-events :opts]` for `{:sink :x :opts {}}` and a second unknown key), `observability_routing_cljs_test.cljc:78`.
- `docs/EP/EP-0015-frame-owned-egress-policy.md:440,692,696` — an EP is a dated design record, not normative; leave it, and say so in the PR body.

## Consumers to migrate

None in code (0 non-test `register-observability-sink!` callers; 0 non-test `:opts` writers). Examples: 0 (`examples/` contains no `:observability` policy).

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

As listed. `spec/api-manifest.edn` — no var changes, no regeneration; run `cd implementation/scripts/api-manifest && clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.gen --check` anyway. Conformance corpus and mcp-conformance: unaffected (measured above). Migration README: no v1-era name involved.

Gate note: the `Spec-Schemas.md` edit is inside a fenced block — neither `check_doc_slugs.py` nor `mkdocs build --strict` inspects it; hand-check the schema reads as valid Malli and say so in the PR body. The 002/API/015 edits are prose; both link gates apply.

## Sequencing and hot-zone

Touches three one-toucher files (`Spec-Schemas.md`, `002-Frames.md`, `API.md`). Serialise with observability.5 (also `API.md`) and with any `@egress` bead editing `Spec-Schemas.md`'s `:rf/project-egress-opts` — different sections, same file. Independent of observability.2/3/4 and of the ruling in observability.6 (whose process-default entry grammar inherits the closed map).

## Risks

Low. A consumer outside the repo passing `:opts` fails loud at `make-frame` with the key named — pre-alpha, no shim. Fail direction is closed (a frame that fails to register routes nothing).

## Local dossier

title: flows: direct clear-flow leaves dependent materialized outputs stale until an unrelated drain
description:
## Scope

Correct the plain/direct `re-frame.flows/clear-flow` lifecycle path when it is called outside an active event drain. Clearing a producer flow must not return with other registered flows still materialized from the producer value that was just removed. Keep the existing id/opts API, frame scoping, leaf-only vacation, and the already-correct `:rf.fx/clear-flow` behavior.

## Verified finding

At HEAD 52b2579e9b53816abddd3406f72db5a5278bed1c, a live JVM probe registered producer `:probe/a` (`[:x] -> [:a]`) and dependent `:probe/b` (`[:a] -> [:b]`), then seeded `{:x 2}`. Before clear, app-db was `{:x 2, :a 2, :b 2}`. Calling `(flows/clear-flow :probe/a {:frame :probe})` returned with `{:x 2, :b 2}`: the source slot was gone but its dependent still published the value derived from that removed slot. Only a later unrelated no-op dispatch changed it to `{:x 2, :b :absent}`. The probe exited 0 and used the package's plain-atom runtime.

This follows directly from `implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc` `clear-flow` / `vacate-output-path!` (currently lines 798-891): outside a drain it writes the vacated live app-db immediately, removes the registry/cache row, and returns; no flow pass is requested. The next ordinary drain finally dirty-checks `:probe/b` against nil and repairs it.

## Impact and ergonomics

This is an observable split-brain app-db state, not a trace-only detail: a view, handler, test, or per-tenant setup reading app-db immediately after the documented synchronous function returns can trust a dependent value whose declared input no longer exists. `docs/core/flows.md` lines 325-341 explicitly advertises the plain functions for boot code, tests, and per-tenant setup, while `docs/api/re-frame.flows.md` lines 55-73 describes `clear-flow` as a synchronous deregister-and-vacate function. Requiring each such caller to invent an unrelated event to repair the dependency graph recreates the ceremony already removed from the effect route.

The existing direct-clear test, `implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_test.clj` `clear-flow-removes-from-registry-and-vacates-output-slot` (lines 102-118), checks only the cleared producer row and leaf. The stronger dependent-flow behavior exists only for the effect route in `implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_settle_on_dispatch_test.clj` `settle-runs-once-and-recomputes-dependents` (lines 85 onward), leaving the plain function gap untested.

## Bounded recommendation

After a successful out-of-drain direct clear, settle the selected frame's remaining flows through the existing private/ordinary flow-pass machinery before the synchronous call completes, so dependents observe the producer's absence without an application-authored nudge. Reuse the established settle/error semantics where practical; do not add a public settle command, option, alternate clear API, fixed-point engine, or general scheduler. Preserve in-drain behavior, where `clear-flow` already queues the vacation for the current pending-db flow pass, and preserve no-op behavior for an unknown flow or absent frame.

The precise internal bridge (for example, reusing the private settle transport after releasing the drain lock versus a smaller exact-owner helper) is intentionally left to implementation review. It must not deadlock/re-enter the current serialization gate, and it must retain the exact-incarnation fences around direct vacation and teardown.

## Posture rationale

Flows are deliberately a small convenience, so the right fix is one consistent lifecycle boundary, not more API. The effect form already guarantees cleared inputs and their dependents settle together. Making the documented plain function honor the same observable invariant removes a surprising manual drain and keeps boot/test/per-tenant use low-friction for people and generated code without broadening flows into a dataflow system.

## Duplicate and history search

Searched all tracker statuses across titles, descriptions, and notes for `flow`, `clear-flow`, `direct clear`, `outside a drain`, `dependent flow`, `initial output`, `settle`, and `unrelated event`. No issue owns this direct-clear/dependent-output boundary. Closest is closed `rf2-kh73v`, which fixed automatic settling only for `:rf.fx/reg-flow` / `:rf.fx/clear-flow`; its scope and tests are effect-specific and its non-goals explicitly exclude static/direct registration work. Closed `rf2-pt637` fixes only the cart example's hot-reload callback.

History confirms the split: `clear-flow` dates to 691c892564e; direct path vacation was added in 7e83e7c691 and later exact-owner-fenced by b5c4599df0/a3ca268cdc0/5c660f2fda. Commits 47e90cf3b4 and 7b6d1e75a3 added and ordered private settling for lifecycle effects without changing the plain direct path.

## Uncertainties

The spec currently states direct clear's deregistration/vacation but does not explicitly say whether dependent flows settle before return; the public synchronous shape and advertised outside-handler use make the current inconsistent graph the actionable defect. The fixing worker should record the chosen direct-call failure boundary if a remaining dependent's derive throws, aligning with the existing private settle semantics rather than inventing rollback behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- A focused CLJ regression reproduces producer A -> dependent B and proves that after direct `(flows/clear-flow A {:frame frame-id})` returns: A is unregistered, A's output leaf is absent, and B has recomputed once against that absence without any unrelated/app-authored dispatch.
- The regression has a negative control: it fails against the current implementation with B retaining the pre-clear value.
- Unknown-id and absent-frame direct clears remain silent no-ops; clearing one frame does not settle or mutate a sibling frame.
- In-drain direct clear and `:rf.fx/clear-flow` keep their current one-settle/topological behavior; existing settle ordering tests remain green.
- The implementation does not expose a public settle event/function/flag, add fixed-point iteration, or change `clear-flow`'s public arities.
- Exact-incarnation loss cannot let an old direct clear or its settle tail mutate a same-id successor frame, and the implementation does not deadlock by dispatching while holding the drain lock.
- Spec/API/core guide wording states the observable direct-clear boundary and its downstream behavior; JVM and CLJS coverage is added in proportion to the cross-host `.cljc` lifecycle code.
notes:
PR #9204 audit follow-up (2026-09-05): the direct settle itself repairs dependents synchronously, but the specified failure boundary is not represented truthfully by the exception diagnostic. `settle-frame-flows!` invokes the ordinary `run-flows-on-db`; `flow-eval-failure!` still hard-codes that the derive ran "during the drain", "the event aborts before the :db install", and "app-db [is] unchanged". Those statements are false for this newly added caller: direct `clear-flow` has already deregistered the producer and committed its output-path vacation, which intentionally stands when a dependent throws.

Deterministic JVM probe at merge commit 27762aa6f9fa1a32db32a59994aa85a5ab0472b8: producer A (`[:x] -> [:a]`), dependent B (`[:a] -> [:b]`) that throws on nil, seed `{:x 2 :a 2 :b 2}`, then direct clear A. The thrown message said "during the drain; the event aborts before the :db install (no partial commit, app-db unchanged)", while immediate state was `{:x 2 :b 2}` and A was absent from the registry. Thus app-db did change (A's leaf was vacated), no event existed, and the clear did not abort. The same mismatch exists for the `:output-write` branch.

This is the exact remaining edge of rf2-g1zb: its original description explicitly required the implementation to record the direct-call failure boundary, and PR #9204's spec/API prose does so correctly. Keep the existing error category and phase taxonomy, but make the user-facing diagnostic context-aware (or neutral across drain/direct callers), and add a focused cross-host regression proving both the propagated exception wording/data and the intended post-failure state: clear stands, settle candidate is unwritten, dependent retries later. Do not add a new error category or rollback the clear.
Diagnostic edge closed on PR #9257 (branch worker/flowsettle-a). settle-frame-flows! now runs its pass under a private *pass-caller* binding, and flow-eval-failure! varies only the two clauses that describe the caller's commit boundary: where the evaluation ran, and what its failure left behind. Error id, :derive/:output-write phase discrimination, trace tags, ex-data and :recovery are byte-identical across callers; no new error category and no rollback of the clear.

Reproduced first, at origin/main, on BOTH phases. :derive -> app-db {:x 2 :a 2 :b 2} became {:x 2 :b 2} with :probe/a deregistered, while the message asserted 'during the drain; the event aborts before the :db install (no partial commit, app-db unchanged)'. :output-write -> {:x 2 :v [1 2] :a 2} became {:x 2 :v [1 2]} carrying the same three false clauses plus 'the pending app-db' for a db that is committed rather than pending.

New cross-host regression implementation/flows/test/re_frame/flows_direct_clear_settle_failure_cljs_test.cljc: 3 tests / 43 assertions. Measured RED against the unmodified source (exit 1, 9 failures) and green after (exit 0). It proves the propagated wording and ex-data on both phases and the intended post-failure state — clear stands, settle candidate unwritten, dependent retries on the next drain — and its third test is the control that keeps the DRAIN's own sentence intact, without which the fix could have been satisfied by deleting that sentence.

Gate: clojure -M:test from implementation/flows, exit 0, 261 tests / 6187 assertions. CLJS arm relied on CI (sibling workers live; a second shadow-cljs build wedges).
close_reason:
MERGED as PR #9257 (rebased; mayor fast-forwarded to dec77429ce). Five clauses: 87 checks, 0 non-terminal, 87 passed-or-skipped, 0 live runs at head oid, 0 structural workflow lines on trunk since merge base.

WHAT CLOSED IS THE BEAD'S NOTE, NOT ITS DESCRIPTION. The description's defect — direct clear-flow leaving dependents stale — was fixed and merged earlier as PR #9204. The live instruction was the PR #9204 AUDIT follow-up note, which the worker confirmed by a controlled bd history walk: exactly ONE text mutation in 388 entries, notes 0->1768 chars at 2026-09-05T02:05:29, everything newer being checkpoint/status noise.

THE REMAINING EDGE, reproduced at origin/main before editing, on BOTH phases. :derive — app-db {:x 2 :a 2 :b 2} became {:x 2 :b 2} with :probe/a deregistered, while the thrown message asserted 'during the drain; the event aborts before the :db install (no partial commit, app-db unchanged)'. All three clauses false for this caller: app-db DID change (the leaf was vacated), no event existed, and the clear did not abort. :output-write carried the same three plus 'the pending app-db' for a db already committed.

THE FIX IS CONFINED TO THE HUMAN :reason. A private *pass-caller* var names the caller's commit boundary and only the two clauses describing it vary. Error id, phase discrimination, trace tags, ex-data and :recovery are IDENTICAL across callers — asserted as hard as the difference, which is the part that keeps this a diagnostic repair rather than a contract change. Dynamic var chosen over a threaded parameter because the hot loop already carries seven args, there is one read site, and the settle is synchronous.

EVIDENCE: new file flows_direct_clear_settle_failure_cljs_test.cljc, 3 tests / 43 assertions, exit 1 with 9 failures against unmodified source and exit 0 after. Its third test is the CONTROL that keeps the drain's own sentence intact, so the change cannot silently neutralise the original wording. Full flows artefact suite exit 0 at 261 tests / 6187 assertions, delta +5 tests / +51 assertions. The docs gate was proven non-vacuous rather than trusted: a planted broken anchor took check_doc_slugs.py to exit 1 naming spec/013-Flows.md:508, exit 0 on restore. CLJS arm relied on CI and declared in the PR body — correct, with five siblings live.

title: hic tooling: the migration reporter's census scores a re-frame2-native app on the Reagent adapter at ZERO, because it decides by namespace and re-frame.adapter.reagent is not reagent.core
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal - pilot 1 (RealWorld/Conduit), a
BLINDED agent reading only the 29 published pages under docs/core/hicasso/, at pin
6e9bb105fc9b1569d63fdebc212b7787a2a023ba. NOT SECTION 13 EVIDENCE: a rehearsal on
:local/root does not satisfy the adoption proof and discharges no artefact gate.

The pilot's own friction-log entry follows verbatim. The 'Bead' field is the PILOT's
recommendation - evidence about the surface, not a ratified design, since a pilot
proposing a framework change is outside its brief by the log protocol's own rule.
Full log: ai/findings/2026-09-03.pilot-b-rehearsal-realworld.friction-log.md (local-only).

----------------------------------------------------------------------

### P1-F04 · outcome 2 · `unresolved` · `tooling`

**Trying to**

Read the migration report and use it to plan the port, as the chapter directs:
"Do not start with the codemod. Read the report, port and prove a screen…"

**Expected**

A census. The chapter is emphatic that the census half exists precisely so a
migrator is not misled by an empty fixer half: "A migrator reading only that
sees 88 files the report never mentions. So the same run also emits a
**census**… On that same corpus it reports **59 sites across 28 files**."

**Instead**

Zero on both halves, over the whole application:

```clojure
:summary {:files-scanned 18, :sites-total 0, :entries 0, :by-class {}}
:census  {:summary {:files-scanned 18, :files-with-reagent 0,
                    :files-unresolved 0, :files-clean 0, :entries 0,
                    :by-verdict {:human-decision 0, :mechanical 0,
                                 :runtime-blocker 0}}}
:suggestions nil
```

The report is not wrong — this application genuinely calls no Reagent API. It
renders through Reagent by way of re-frame2's **own** view surface: views are
declared with core's `reg-view` macro, reads are `@(subscribe […])` and
dispatches are `#(dispatch […])` under the bindings that macro installs, and
the substrate is chosen once with `(rf/init! reagent-adapter/adapter)`. Not one
`reagent.core` name appears anywhere in `app/src/`. The census population is
"Reagent API call sites", and there are none.

So the report's zero is a true statement about a population that is not this
application's migration surface. Measured over the two screens I was given
(`articles.cljs` + `article_editor.cljs`), the work the port actually needed
was: **15** `reg-view` declarations to convert (8 + 7), **24** `@(subscribe …)`
/ `@(rf/subscribe …)` reads (13 + 11), **10** `#(dispatch …)` closures (2 + 8),
**6** `.preventDefault` sites (5 + 1), **4** `^{:key …}` metadata sites (4 + 0),
and **3** `[rf/route-link …]` heads that have to become **calls** (3 + 0). The
report names none of them, and its framing — "absence from the report is
meaningful" — invites exactly the wrong conclusion.

**Looked at**

- `20-migration-from-reagent.md` §1 and "The report's second half: the census"
- the generated `reagent-to-hicasso-report.edn`
- `app/src/**` (grep for `reagent.core` — no hits outside `core.cljs`'s adapter
  require)

**Resolved by**

Nothing in the documentation. I ported by hand off §2's translation table,
which does cover most of the shapes once you translate them one level up
(`reg-view` behaves like "a `defn` component returning Hiccup"; `@(subscribe
[:q])` is spelled the same as `@(rf/subscribe [:q])`). Recording as
`unresolved` rather than `inferred` because the *tool* has a gap here, not just
the prose: a re-frame2 application on the Reagent adapter is the single most
likely thing to be migrated to Hicasso, and it is invisible to both halves of
the reporter.

A smaller bookkeeping oddity in the same output: `:files-scanned 18` with
`:files-with-reagent 0`, `:files-unresolved 0` and `:files-clean 0`. The three
sub-counts sum to 0, not 18, so "clean" appears to mean something narrower than
"scanned and not implicated" — the report does not say what.

**Bead**

Teach the census `reg-view` / bare `subscribe` / bare `dispatch` / `rf/route-link`
as a second roster, or state plainly in §1 that a re-frame2-native Reagent app
will report zero and why.
notes:
Merged-PR audit #9132: the closure is incomplete. The new reagent2 namespace recognition can still emit exactly the confident zero this bead says is impossible. Reproduction on the landed tree: scanning a file that requires reagent2.dom.server and calls its sole documented public function, render-to-static-markup, yields files-recognised 1, files-clean 1, entries 0, recognition full, and the caveat A zero below is a measurement. The namespace was added to rewrite/reagent-namespaces, but census/surface has no render-to-static-markup row. The same mismatch exists inside other newly recognised reagent2 namespaces: reagent2.dom.client documents unmount and flush-views! as public Vars, while the census roster has neither spelling in the Reagent surface; reagent2.ratom likewise documents public calls beyond the two rostered names. This is not the separate prose follow-up rf2-onfy. Reconcile every newly recognised reagent2 namespace against its supported migration-relevant public calls, add the missing classifications and recovery notes, and add a test proving a known public call from each newly recognised namespace cannot produce recognition full with zero entries. Also make the full-recognition wording no stronger than the actual roster coverage.
MERGED-PR AUDIT #9147 (2026-09-04): REOPENED. The advertised roster-completeness law is not achieved. census_test's recognised-namespace-calls holds ONE chosen call per namespace and its “completeness” assertion compares only the namespace keys; it never compares census/surface with the supported public Vars of those namespaces. Stock Reagent 2.0.1's reagent.core publicly defines at least class-names, wrap, rswap!, create-compiler, set-default-compiler!, and unsafe-html; none is rostered or covered by the documented exclusions. Six one-call files were run against the landed census, and every one reported {:recognition :full, :files-recognised 1, :files-clean 1, :entries 0}. The weakened caveat now admits the roster bound, but :files-clean and the closure's claim that every supported migration-relevant call was reconciled remain false. Reconcile or explicitly disposition these public calls, and make the ratchet cover the per-namespace supported-call inventory rather than one sample.
close_reason:
RE-CLOSED 2026-09-04 by the mayor: fourth instance of the .beads checkout/checkpoint race today. Payload verified in the WORKING TREE at HEAD==origin/main (ref-addressed git reads are unreliable here — see memory ref-addressed-git-search-false-empty): migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod/src/re_frame/migration/hicasso/census.clj carries 5 occurrences of render-to-static-markup, the call whose absence from the roster produced the confident zero.

Delivered by worker/census-a in PR #9147, MERGED at 0c22a9df29, then repaired on-branch by worker/censusfix-a for a require-alias violation. The worker REPRODUCED the audit's confident zero verbatim before fixing anything (files-recognised 1, files-clean 1, entries 0, recognition :full, with the caveat 'A zero below is a measurement'), then closed it with ten roster rows, three new classes and recovery notes, reagent.dom.server joining the recognition set, a completeness ratchet so a namespace added without a sample reds the suite, and the :full caveat weakened to what the roster supports. It also closed the same hole at a second address the bead never named — the prefix rule recognised re-frame.adapter.test-react with no roster row.

Its own statement of the cause is the durable part: rewrite/reagent-namespaces decides per FILE, census/surface finds entries per NAME, and the gap between them is exactly a confident zero. A recognised-and-unrostered file is strictly worse than an unrecognised one, because the unrecognised file is a bucket the caveat names aloud.

title: Make implementor skill trigger description validator-safe
description:
## Scope

Repair the frontmatter description in `skills/re-frame2-implementor/SKILL.md` so
the skill-creator validator accepts the shipped skill. Keep the public skill
directory, frontmatter name, trigger behavior, exclusions, and all body/reference
content unchanged except for the invalid trigger-example placeholder wording.

## Finding

The description contains the trigger example `implement re-frame2 in
<language>`. The required `quick_validate.py` validator rejects any `<` or `>`
in frontmatter descriptions, so the current skill fails validation before any
normal skill routing can occur.

## Evidence

- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/SKILL.md:16` contains the literal trigger text
  `implement re-frame2 in <language>` in the YAML `description`.
- `C:\\Users\\miket\\.codex\\skills\\.system\\skill-creator\\scripts\\quick_validate.py`
  rejects descriptions containing `<` or `>`.
- Running the validator against the current package returns exit 1 with
  `Description cannot contain angle brackets (< or >)`.

## Compatibility and exclusions

This is a frontmatter-description clarity/validator-compatibility fix only.
Preserve `name: re-frame2-implementor`, the eight-host scope, the three trigger
concepts (port re-frame2, implement re-frame2 in a host language, conformance
corpus), all do-not-use routing, allowed tools, eval fixtures, filenames,
references, package/plugin metadata, and skill body semantics. Do not rename the
public skill or directory, alter invocation policy, or change any spec/conformance
terminology. No Phase-1 vestigial/removal target is in scope.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The frontmatter description contains no angle brackets or unfinished
   placeholders and still clearly triggers on porting re-frame2 to a host
   language and on conformance-corpus work.
2. `quick_validate.py` run against the absolute skill directory exits 0 and
   prints `Skill is valid!`.
3. A planted angle-bracket trigger placeholder in a temporary validation copy
   makes `quick_validate.py` exit 1 with the expected diagnostic; restoring the
   clean skill returns exit 0.
4. `git diff --check` is clean and the diff is limited to the one frontmatter
   description phrase.
acceptance_criteria: Validator clean pass; planted angle-bracket control red; restored clean pass; exact one-phrase diff and no routing/public-name changes.
close_reason: Duplicate contention-created records; canonical implementor validator-safe naming bead is rf2-6r9j.252.

title: test-quiet exit-integrity regression misses both safeguarded branches
description:
## Correctness finding

The CLJS exit-integrity regression added with the two production safeguards does not exercise either safeguarded failure mode. It repeats a normal red fixture invocation that was already covered before the safeguards landed, so both safeguards can be removed while the named regression remains green.

## Evidence

- `implementation/test-quiet/src/re_frame/test_quiet/shadow_node.cljs:122-156` documents and implements two independent protections: catch a throw from `replay-buffered-warnings!` before `js/process.exit 1`, and seed `process.exitCode = 1` before a run so a missing `:end-run-tests` dispatch cannot drain to exit 0.
- Commit `45fbaaa4dd` introduced both protections and `deliberately-failing-test-exits-nonzero` together. Its parent already had the ordinary default reporter branch `(do (replay-buffered-warnings!) (js/process.exit 1))`, so a normal red run already exited 1 whenever replay completed.
- `implementation/test-quiet/test/re_frame/test_quiet_shadow_node_cljs_test.cljs:712-756` invokes the ordinary armed warning fixture and ordinary unarmed fixture. It neither makes replay throw nor prevents/delays the custom `:end-run-tests` method. Therefore it traverses the pre-existing normal red/green exits, not either new protection.
- The exact armed child invocation was already present before the fix in `red-run-replays-buffered-console-warn` (introduced by `a89226ca3f`): current lines 612-635 use the same namespace and `RF2_TQ_RED_WARN_FIXTURE=1`, and already assert no spawn error, no timeout, nonzero status, and the replayed marker. Current lines 636-657 already repeat the same fixture unarmed and assert exit 0 and quiet canonical output. The later test adds only `Ran`/`FAIL in` assertions to duplicate child processes.
- `end-run-tests-exit-decision` at lines 270-281 calls upstream `cljs.test/successful?` and checks only that some method exists. ClojureScript 1.12.145 itself defines a no-op `[:cljs.test/default :end-run-tests]` method at `cljs/test.cljs:359`, so method presence does not prove that test-quiet owns the exit behavior.
- All-state bead searches for the regression names, seeded exit, replay exception, copied/default predicate, and duplicate spawn found no existing issue. The legacy `rf2-jmrdhn` identifier referenced by the commit is not present in the current bead store.

## Impact

A regression can remove the replay exception guard or the seeded fallback while every current exit-integrity assertion stays green. The suite therefore claims protection against the exact false-green hazards described by the production code without discriminating them, while paying for two redundant Node child starts.

## Proposed disposition

Replace or augment the ordinary red process row with controlled process-level fixtures for the two protected branches. Add an env-gated seam that makes replay throw after a genuine failure, and a separate env-gated seam that lets a started run drain without the test-quiet `:end-run-tests` exit (for example a controlled no-op reporter dispatch). Fold the ordinary `Ran`/`FAIL in` checks into the existing warning-replay row instead of spawning the same armed/unarmed pair twice. Remove or repurpose `end-run-tests-exit-decision`; a direct pure helper is acceptable only if it is the helper the production defmethod invokes.

## Risks / retained contracts

Keep the real child-process boundary because exit status cannot be proven in-process. A control must prove its fixture ran and reached the intended exceptional/missing-dispatch state; an unrelated parse error, uncaught fixture error, timeout, or skipped suite also exits nonzero and must not satisfy it. Preserve normal red warning replay, normal green quietness, both focused and whole-suite seeding call sites, and the compile-cycle boundary that keeps `shadow-node` out of the test namespace's requires.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the existing `deliberately-failing-test-exits-nonzero` regression and confirm its ordinary armed-red and unarmed-green child rows pass.
2. In a disposable branch, remove the `seed-failure-exit!` calls from the focused and whole-suite entry points, leaving the ordinary reporter path intact; rerun the named regression. It remains green because the normal `:end-run-tests` path still exits 1.
3. Restore the seed, remove the `try`/`catch` around `replay-buffered-warnings!`, and rerun the same regression. It remains green because its fixture never makes replay throw.
4. Compare the child invocations with `red-run-replays-buffered-console-warn`; they use the same ordinary warning fixture, demonstrating that neither protected exceptional branch is selected.
5. Treat a future control as valid only when it emits a reached-state marker for the replay-throws or missing-dispatch branch; a generic nonzero child status is not sufficient.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A real spawned red run forces warning replay itself to throw, proves a genuine test failure was reached, and still exits nonzero; removing the replay `try`/`catch` makes this control fail for the intended reason.
2. A real spawned run starts tests but deliberately bypasses or no-ops the test-quiet `:end-run-tests` exit, then drains with status 1 from the seeded `process.exitCode`; removing `seed-failure-exit!` makes this control fail with status 0.
3. Each fault fixture emits an unambiguous reached-state marker and assertions reject spawn errors, timeouts, parse failures, skipped tests, and unrelated uncaught exceptions as alternate explanations for nonzero status.
4. Ordinary armed red warning replay and unarmed green quietness remain covered once each, including `Ran`/`FAIL in`, warning marker, canonical green output, and exit status; the duplicate armed/unarmed child invocations are removed.
5. `end-run-tests-exit-decision` no longer treats upstream `successful?` behavior or mere presence of ClojureScript's default no-op method as proof of test-quiet's custom exit logic.
6. Both focused `run-test-vars` and whole-suite `run-all-tests` paths retain the seeded-failure behavior.
close_reason: PR #9120. Premise held. Both safeguards now have their own fault fixture in the new re-frame.test-quiet-exit-integrity-fixture-cljs-test, each proven by a plant: removing the replay try/catch reds red-replay-throw-cannot-mask-the-nonzero-exit at :833:11 (the poison message escapes as an uncaught crash - status alone cannot discriminate, since an uncaught exception also exits 1), and neutering seed-failure-exit! at both call sites reds run-that-never-dispatches-the-exit-defmethod-drains-nonzero at :867:11 with 'got status 0'. Each fixture emits a reached-state marker and the rows reject spawn errors, timeouts, parse errors, unmatched selectors and skipped suites. deliberately-failing-test-exits-nonzero deleted, its Ran/FAIL-in pins folded into red-run-replays-warnings-and-exits-nonzero (renamed); duplicate armed/unarmed spawn pair gone. end-run-tests-exit-decision retired - the seeded exit code makes the green process row prove defmethod ownership instead. Both seed-failure-exit! call sites retained. 16/16 contract rows green, exit 0.

title: framework logs ExceptionInfo to console.error as a raw CLJS object — the browser shows {meta: null, cnt: 7, arr: Array(14)} instead of the error message
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 02:55 AUSEST by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal, while diagnosing the route-link boot failure (rf2-nvcp). Tip d1e6a707a3.

WHAT AN ADOPTER SEES. When the runtime reports an error through its own console channel, the browser console shows:

  [re-frame2] {meta: null, cnt: 7, arr: Array(14), __hash: null, cljs$: 16647951}

That is a raw cljs.core/ExceptionInfo (or its ex-data map) handed to console.error as an object. Chrome renders its JS fields. The actual message — a long, genuinely well-written recovery ladder naming the operation, the recovery and three ways to establish a frame scope — is inside the object and is never printed.

MEASURED. Captured from headless Chrome on the linearlite example at this tip: three such lines, each an ExceptionInfo. The same run's window 'error' event carried the full text, so the message exists and is reachable; only the console rendering loses it. The realworld example produced the same shape. Both were reached through ordinary page load, not through any test harness.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE PILOTS. Outcome 5 is 'diagnose one induced failure through the documented diagnostic path', and the console is where a reader looks first — chapter 16 sends them to Xray, but every reader checks the console before installing a tool. An opaque object teaches the reader that re-frame2's errors are unreadable, which is the opposite of what the error text actually achieves. Three of my own diagnostic steps were spent recovering a message the framework already had.

THE CONTRAST IS SHARP. In the same console, the framework's own reg-view warning prints perfectly as text: '[re-frame] reg-view :linearlite.core/root-view — root element is #object[cljs.core.MetaFn]; data-rf2-source-coord skipped (Spec 006 §Source-coord annotation ...)'. So the string path is fine; it is the error path that hands over an object.

LIKELY FIX. At the console sink, print (ex-message e) — and the id from (ex-data e) — as a string, and attach the object as a second argument if the inspectable value is wanted. That keeps the object expandable in devtools while making the first line readable.

NOT the same defect as rf2-nvcp. That one is why the error is raised at all; this one is that the error is unreadable when it is. Fixing route-link removes these three particular lines and leaves the rendering defect in place for the next error.

FILED, NOT FIXED — implementation/ is held by live workers.
notes:
PRODUCTION EVIDENCE, added 2026-09-03 03:00 AUSEST by the same rehearsal.

Under advanced compilation the error is not merely opaque, it is anonymous. A production release of pilot 1's workspace (npx shadow-cljs release app, exit 0, 332 files, 0 warnings, main.js 1.66MB) loads to a blank page whose only diagnostic is:

  Error: zm

That is the minified constructor name. The recovery ladder, the [:rf.error/no-frame-context] id, the :operation / :recovery / :where keys — everything an adopter could act on, and everything the catalogue could be looked up by — is gone from the shipped bundle.

This is the same underlying failure as the dev build (rf2-nvcp), seen through the release path, and it sharpens this bead in two ways. First, it is the exact case friction-log.md says outcome 6 exists to catch: 'Advanced compilation removes diagnostics and warning strings, and a bundle that compiles but does not boot is the failure this outcome exists to catch.' Second, it means the console-rendering defect recorded above degrades from unreadable to unattributable in production: in dev the message at least exists inside the logged object, and in release there is no message at all.

Worth considering alongside any fix here: whether a stable complaint id (not the minified symbol) should survive advanced compilation, so a production error can still be looked up. Chapter 16 promises stable complaint ids and a catalogue; 'Error: zm' cannot reach either. Recording the observation, not proposing the design.
close_reason:
FIXED in PR #9060 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9060). Two halves, both measured in headless Chromium on the linearlite dev build, not asserted in a unit test.

(1) CONSOLE CHANNEL. re-frame.error-emit/report-unowned-error! passed only the record, and a CLJS map is not a JS object — Chrome rendered PersistentArrayMap's interior fields, which is the reported '{meta: null, cnt: 7, arr: Array(14), ...}' (cnt 7 = the seven-key record). A readable summary line now LEADS: the exception's ex-message, else the record's :reason, else the bare category keyword. Composes no new error text. The record AND the exception still ride as their own console arguments, so structured consumers and DevTools inspection are unchanged.

(2) THE EMIT SITE, which a console-only fix could not have reached. The bead's diagnosis was one step off and it mattered: the logged object is the error-emit RECORD, not an ExceptionInfo or its ex-data, and for :rf.error/no-frame-context that record carried NEITHER an exception NOR a reason — emit-no-frame-context! dropped the payload's composed ladder. Measured: {:error :rf.error/no-frame-context, :event :rf/redacted, :event-id nil, :frame nil, :time 334.3, :exception nil, :elapsed-ms 0}. The premise 'the message exists and is reachable, only the console rendering loses it' is therefore FALSE for this category, and so is 'the window error event carried the full text' — the pageerror message was 23 characters: cljs$core$ExceptionInfo. The emit site now threads :reason/:recovery through dispatch-on-error!'s EXISTING attrs attribution seam. Its mirrored sibling emit-bad-frame-provider-arg! had the identical shape and got the same one-line treatment.

BEFORE: [re-frame2] {meta: null, cnt: 7, arr: Array(14), __hash: null, cljs$lang$protocol_mask$partition0$: 16647951, ...}
AFTER:  [re-frame2] :rf.error/no-frame-context — a frame-scoped route-link ran with no frame context — ... (full recovery ladder) ... Per Spec 002 §The error and its ladder. {meta: null, cnt: 9, root: Object, ...}

error_emit_dev_console_dom_cljs_test.cljs pinned the old two-argument shape and is updated; two new tests pin the ladder reaching the line and the sibling's symmetry. No assertion weakened. Gates: test:cljs 11197/55794 exit 0; core JVM 2175/11144 exit 0; test:browser 778/4233 exit 0; fast-pr spine exit 0, clj-kondo errors 0.

NOT DONE (deliberately, per the stance): the production-anonymity observation in this bead's NOTES ('Error: zm' under advanced compilation) is a separate design question and is untouched.

title: CLAUDE.md prescribes naming remote+branch as the fix for 'Cannot rebase onto multiple branches'; measured insufficient
notes:
MEASURED 2026-09-01 22:4x AUSEST by the acting mayor, in the mayor checkout, six worker worktrees live.

WHAT HAPPENED. Ran the checkpoint sequence's third step in its PRESCRIBED named form - 'git pull --rebase origin main' - and it aborted:

  From https://github.com/day8/re-frame2
   * branch                  main       -> FETCH_HEAD
  fatal: Cannot rebase onto multiple branches.

Tree was clean and undiverged. HEAD == origin/main afterwards and the push landed, so no damage this time - but the rebase silently did not happen, which is the step the sequence exists to perform.

WHY THE PRESCRIBED REMEDY DOES NOT HOLD. CLAUDE.md's Beads-durability bullet says a BARE 'git pull --rebase' takes its target from FETCH_HEAD and therefore aborts this way, and prescribes naming remote and branch. But naming them does not immunise the pull, because a pull is TWO steps: it fetches into FETCH_HEAD, then rebases onto what FETCH_HEAD says. FETCH_HEAD lives in the SHARED common git directory - 'git rev-parse --git-common-dir' returns .git from the mayor checkout, and linked worktrees do NOT get their own copy. So any concurrent fetch from any of the six live worker worktrees rewrites it inside that window, and the rebase step reads the peer's multi-ref version no matter how the pull was invoked. Naming the remote and branch controls only the FETCH half.

The doc's own measured instance (2026-08-29 22:31) was the bare form, which is why the named form was taken to be the fix. This is the named form failing identically.

THE FIX IS ALREADY IN CLAUDE.md FOR THE OTHER CASE. The post-merge bullet deliberately replaced 'git pull --ff-only origin main' with 'git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main', reasoning that 'A ref can't be captured that way' - FETCH_HEAD is a scratch file any concurrent git process rewrites, an explicit ref is not. That reasoning applies verbatim to the rebase pull, but the checkpoint sequence still prescribes the pull form. The merge case was fixed and the rebase case was left.

PROPOSED: in the Beads-durability sequence and the session-completion block, replace 'git pull --rebase origin main' with 'git fetch origin main && git rebase origin/main', keeping the && so a failed fetch cannot be followed by a rebase against a stale ref. Then rewrite the naming guidance to say what it actually buys (the fetch half) rather than presenting it as the remedy for this abort.

SECOND, SMALLER FINDING - the abort was INVISIBLE. It was run as 'git pull --rebase origin main 2>&1 | tail -3 && bd dolt push && git push'. A pipeline's exit status is its LAST command's, so tail returned 0 and the && chain continued straight past a fatal abort. This is the same hazard the dispatch template's gate-mechanics block states for gates ('Never pipe a gate through a filter'), reached through git rather than through a gate runner, and it is what made the doc's phrase 'inert only because the push that follows still lands' literally true here. Worth a line where the sequence is written down: do not pipe the steps of this sequence.

---

RESOLVED by PR #8964 (draft -> ready), CLAUDE.md only, 14 insertions / 10 deletions.

The bead's PROPOSED action was carried out as written. Three sites prescribing the
pull form now run 'git fetch origin main && git rebase origin/main' with the &&
retained: the Session Completion block, the Beads-durability sequence, and -- a
site the bead did not name -- the fast-forward bullet's own 'Not possible to
fast-forward' remedy under Workflow, which still prescribed 'git pull --rebase
origin main'. The naming guidance is rewritten to say what naming buys (the fetch
half); the 2026-08-29 measurement is kept as evidence about that half. The
no-piping line is added where the sequence is written. The reasoning is stated
once, in Beads durability, pointing at the fast-forward bullet for "a ref can't be
captured that way".

TWO OF THIS BEAD'S OWN PREMISES WERE MEASURED WRONG AND ARE NOT REPRODUCED IN THE DOC.

1. FETCH_HEAD IS PER-WORKTREE, not shared across worktrees. The bead reasoned that
   because 'git rev-parse --git-common-dir' returns the mayor checkout's .git,
   linked worktrees have no FETCH_HEAD of their own and any peer worker's fetch
   rewrites the mayor's. Measured on git 2.53.0.windows.2: 'git rev-parse
   --git-path FETCH_HEAD' resolves INSIDE the linked worktree's own git directory,
   and a 'git fetch origin main' run from a linked worktree wrote that per-worktree
   file while leaving the common-dir FETCH_HEAD byte-identical and its mtime
   untouched. So a peer worktree is not the contaminating process.

   THE BEAD'S CONCLUSION SURVIVES ANYWAY, and CLAUDE.md already had the accurate
   wording: the fast-forward bullet says FETCH_HEAD is "a scratch file any
   concurrent git process IN THE SAME CHECKOUT rewrites". The mayor checkout runs
   several git processes at once, which is where this bites -- and it is where the
   abort was measured. The doc now carries the same-checkout framing plus one
   clause recording that FETCH_HEAD is per-worktree, because the old phrase "the
   shared fetch-head file" invites exactly the wrong mental model.

2. THE ABORT MESSAGES ATTRIBUTED TO THE SEQUENCE WERE WRONG, pre-existing and now
   corrected. Measured in a throwaway repo:
     - dirty tree, 'git rebase origin/main'      -> "cannot rebase: You have
       unstaged changes" (exit 1), and it refuses on ANY unstaged change, not only
       one the incoming commits would overwrite;
     - dirty tree, 'git merge --ff-only origin/main' -> "local changes would be
       overwritten" (exit 1);
     - diverged but clean, 'git rebase origin/main'  -> no abort, rebases the
       checkpoint on top, exit 0.
   So "local changes would be overwritten" is a merge-family message: correct where
   the fast-forward bullet uses it, wrong where Beads durability and the Workflow
   summary attributed it to the checkpoint step. And "Not possible to fast-forward"
   cannot arise from the rebase step at all. Both are now attributed correctly, and
   the stricter rebase behaviour is noted, since it makes clearing .beads more
   necessary rather than less.

GATES (captured exit codes, redirect + echo on one command line):
  python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci  -> 0
  scripts/test-fast-pr.sh                    -> 0
check_doc_slugs.py was NOT nominated: CLAUDE.md is repo-root markdown, outside its
roots, where it exits 0 on a broken link. Gate discrimination was checked by
planting a broken anchor at the edited line -- check_readme_links.py went red,
exit 1, naming CLAUDE.md:66 and the planted anchor -- so the green is earned.
Restore verified by blob hash against the committed object.

VERIFIED BY HAND (no gate covers it): neither link gate reads inside fenced code
blocks, and this change touches two fenced command blocks; both were read by hand
and neither contains any link or anchor, so the fence-blindness is inert here. The
one added link, [Workflow](#workflow), resolves to the unique '## Workflow'
heading; no heading slug in the file is duplicated, so no GitHub -N suffix is in
play. The file contains no tables.
AUDIT PR #8964: REOPENED.

COMPLETENESS / IMPLEMENTATION QUALITY — the command is corrected in `CLAUDE.md`, but the same active workflow still prescribes the retired pull form elsewhere. `AGENTS.md:237-242` is the sibling agent-facing Session Completion block and still says `git pull --rebase`; `scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh:338-342` and `scripts/beads-checkpoint.ps1:655-660` still print `git pull --rebase` as the recovery sequence when they refuse an unsafe clear. Those are executable guidance that users and agents follow, not historical citations or tests. The edited generated block even warns that regeneration may restore the bad form, which confirms the repair was applied to a copy rather than durably reconciled across its active carriers.

Keep this small: make the AGENTS block and both checkpoint-script messages prescribe `git fetch origin main && git rebase origin/main` (or the platform-equivalent two checked steps), reconcile the generator/template if it is repository-owned, and leave genuine hook tests/history that intentionally exercise `git pull --rebase` alone. A semantic active-instruction census, not a global string purge, is the control. No new wrapper or retry framework.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #8968, verified on main (AGENTS.md, scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh, scripts/beads-checkpoint.ps1, CLAUDE.md; +23/-6). Verified by MERGE, not by PR state. Second pass, closing the AUDIT PR #8964 reopen. Census: 54 'git pull' occurrences across 18 files, line-oriented and whitespace-collapsed passes agreeing, sorted three ways - 3 ACTIVE INSTRUCTIONS changed (AGENTS.md:239, beads-checkpoint.sh:341, beads-checkpoint.ps1:659, exactly the three the audit named, no fourth exists, all three the BARE form), 13 CITATIONS of the retired form kept, 6 TESTS/FIXTURES kept. TWO STRUCTURAL FINDINGS worth carrying: (1) AGENTS.md IS generated, but by the external bd binary rather than by anything repository-owned - lines 208-253 sit in a BEADS INTEGRATION marker, and CLAUDE.md:5-50 carries the same block under the SAME hash ca08a54f, which is precisely how the two silently diverged when #8964 edited only one. No repo file holds the template, so there is no generator here to reconcile; the copies were brought back into step and CLAUDE.md's regeneration note extended to cover both. (2) The .ps1 could NOT take the && form - it is a parse error in Windows PowerShell 5.x, which the script explicitly supports via #requires -Version 5, so a literal reading of the audit would have shipped a line Windows users cannot run. It prints 'git fetch origin main; if ($?) { git rebase origin/main }', verified gating in BOTH directions under 5.1 and pwsh 7.6.5, with a comment at each site recording why the siblings differ. Gates: check_readme_links.py --ci exit 0, --self-test exit 0, beads-checkpoint.sh --pre-pull exit 0, test-fast-pr.sh exit 0; discrimination by planted fault (red, exit 1, naming AGENTS.md:246), restore by blob hash. Both link gates strip fenced blocks and this change is almost entirely inside fences, so the worker executed both edited messages end-to-end in a throwaway repo with a tracker ahead of HEAD and read the real output - that, not the green, is the evidence for the changed lines.

title: bug(realworld-http): optimistic comment replies can settle into a different article route
description:
## Scope

Keep RealWorld HTTP comment mutations owned by the `/article/:slug` page that issued them. Scope is `examples/real-apps/realworld_http/comments.cljs` plus the existing production-source CLJS suite. Reuse the `:comments :slug` fact and `reply-for-current-slug?` introduced by PR #8845; no framework or mutation abstraction work.

## Correctness finding

PR #8845 correlates article/comments READ replies, but the optimistic comment WRITE callbacks in the same file remain slug-free and mutate the one shared comments/form state unconditionally.

- `:comment-form/submit` reads the current slug for the POST path, but emits `:on-success [:comment-form/submit-success temp-id]` and `:on-failure [:comment-form/submit-error temp-id]`. A reply from alpha after navigation to beta can reset beta's current draft/form on success or surface alpha's failure on beta.
- `:comment/delete` likewise sends `:on-failure [:comment/delete-rollback prior]`. If alpha's DELETE fails after beta has loaded, the rollback inserts alpha's saved comment into beta's comments vector.
- None of those terminal handlers consults the new `reply-for-current-slug?` gate. The new source commentary says every reply target carries the requested slug and every terminal handler gates its write, but that is true only of the two reads.

This is not hypothetical request-id protection: these writes carry no shared cross-route request id that would suppress a late terminal reply. The current main still has the slug-free target vectors above.

## Reproduction

Load alpha, begin either an optimistic comment submit or delete with its HTTP reply held, navigate to beta and settle beta's comments load, then deliver alpha's terminal reply. Alpha submit failure writes beta's form error; alpha delete failure inserts alpha's comment into beta's list. The beta route and `[:comments :slug]` remain beta throughout.

## Minimal fix

Carry the issuing slug in the submit success/failure and delete rollback target vectors, and gate each state-changing terminal handler with the existing comments-slice correlation predicate before touching comments or form state. The delete success handler is a no-op and needs no machinery. Keep temp-id/prior payloads for their current optimistic reconciliation jobs.

## Non-goals

No generic route-owned mutation layer, request cancellation scheme, cache, comment-form redesign, or changes to managed HTTP. Do not broaden this into unrelated article social controls without a reproduced defect.

## Duplicate search

All-status searches covered cross-slug comments, comment submit/delete rollback, late comment replies, route correlation, `comment/delete`, and the RealWorld handler names. No owner was found. `rf2-iy3d6` deliberately scoped itself to route-driven reads and explicitly listed optimistic comment behavior as a non-goal, so this is a discovered follow-up rather than a duplicate.
acceptance_criteria:
- A focused production-source CLJS test holds an alpha comment submit or delete reply, navigates to and loads beta, then delivers alpha's submit success/failure and delete failure; beta's comments slice and current form remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
- The request target vectors carry the issuing slug, and all state-changing terminal handlers refuse a slug that differs from `[:comments :slug]` via the existing correlation helper.
- Current-slug controls prove submit reconciliation and delete rollback still work normally; the gate must not swallow every reply.
- The focused RealWorld CLJS suite and examples compile gate pass. No framework API or new abstraction is added.
notes:
## Resolution (PR #8898)

Fixed as specified. The three optimistic comment WRITE settles now carry the
issuing slug and gate on the existing reply-for-current-slug? predicate against
[:comments :slug]:

  - :comment-form/submit-success  [slug temp-id reply]
  - :comment-form/submit-error    [slug temp-id reply]
  - :comment/delete-rollback      [slug prior reply]

:comment/delete-success writes nothing, so it took neither slug nor gate, as the
item anticipated. Verified by census: the gate expression now occurs exactly 5
times in comments.cljs -- the two route-driven reads plus these three.

### The judgement the item left open: what a late write owes its route

A dropped READ is simply discarded; a dropped WRITE can strand optimistic state.
Walked each path:

  - submit-success: drop the whole write. The optimistic temp card was ALREADY
    discarded when :comments/load reset the slice on the slug change, and the
    comment really is saved server-side, so returning to the article re-reads it.
  - submit-error: drop the whole write. Same -- the temp card it would have
    yanked out is already gone.
  - delete-rollback: drop the whole write. Alpha's list was reset on the way out,
    and the server still holds the comment (the DELETE failed), so a return
    re-reads it. Re-inserting into another article's list would FABRICATE a
    comment that article never had.

### One fact had to be added, and it is load-bearing

[:comments :data] is route-owned already, but [:comment-form] is NOT: it is a
boot-time singleton set once by :comment-form/initialise from :app/initialise,
and the article route's on-match is only [[:article/load] [:comments/load]]. So
the form rode across a navigation still :status :submitting -- and the textarea
AND the Post button are both :disabled while submitting. Gating alone would have
left the destination article's comment form PERMANENTLY LOCKED: a worse bug than
the one reported, and invisible to a test that only asserts the slice.

So :comments/load now also resets [:comment-form] when it takes on a NEW article
identity, reusing the refresh? decision it already computes two lines up. A
same-slug refresh leaves the form alone, so a background re-load never eats an
in-progress draft. No new key, no new event, no new abstraction. Gate and reset
are two halves of one fix; either alone is wrong.

### The commentary trap

Confirmed at source: the block comment added by #8845 asserted that every reply
target carried its slug and every terminal handler gated its write, which was
true only of the two reads -- the file asserted the invariant it violated. It now
names exactly which five settles are correlated, names the two deliberate
NON-members, and states that the gate gives ROUTE identity rather than request
identity (so an alpha-beta-alpha return readmits an old alpha reply; deliberate,
since a per-request epoch was an explicit non-goal).

### Out of scope, deliberately, and now named in the source

The article SOCIAL controls in the same file are ungated and remain so per this
item's non-goal: :article/author-follow-synced, :article/author-follow-rollback
and :article/delete-failed all write [:article :data ...] unconditionally from a
button press. :article/author-follow-rollback looks like the same class of defect
(alpha's failed follow could flip the author flag on the article now on screen),
but no defect has been reproduced against it, so it was left alone and instead
called out by name in the correlation-gate comment so no future reader mistakes
it for covered. Worth a bead if the mayor wants it chased.

### Tests and gates

Six new cases in the existing production-source CLJS suite
(implementation/adapters/reagent/test/re_frame/realworld_cljs_test.cljs, deftest
realworld-comment-mutations-cross-slug): three cross-slug refusals asserting the
whole comments slice and whole form map; a non-vacuity control proving all three
settles still do their ordinary optimistic job on the current slug; a strand
control pinning that the destination form arrives usable and can post its own
comment; and a same-slug-refresh control. The pre-existing stale-index rollback
test moved to the new arity.

Gates, captured exits:
  - npm run test:cljs, split into its two phases and run foreground:
    compile exit 0; full suite exit 0, 11105 tests / 54792 assertions,
    0 failures 0 errors. Re-run after rebase onto the final base.
  - npm run test:examples-compile: exit 0, all 56 swept builds, zero warnings
    (:examples/realworld is the build carrying this file).
  - No markdown in the diff, so neither doc-link gate applies.

Sabotage witness: disabling the gate in :comment/delete-rollback alone turned the
focused suite RED (exit 1) with exactly the reported symptom -- the other
article's comment spliced into the current list -- at the same 18 tests / 343
assertions as the control, then restored, blob hash identical to the committed
object.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #8898. The three optimistic comment WRITE settles (comment-form/submit-success, comment-form/submit-error, comment/delete-rollback) now carry the issuing slug and gate on the existing reply-for-current-slug? predicate; comment/delete-success writes nothing so it needed neither. Each late write is DROPPED outright -- nothing is stranded, because the slice reset on the slug change already discarded the optimistic card and the server holds the truth. One fact had to be added and it is load-bearing: the comment form is a boot-time singleton the route never revisits, so it rode across a navigation still :submitting, and since the textarea and Post button are both disabled while submitting, gating ALONE would have locked the destination form permanently. comments/load therefore also resets the form on a NEW article identity, reusing the refresh? decision it already computes; a same-slug refresh leaves an in-progress draft alone. The false #8845 commentary claiming every target carried its slug and every handler gated is corrected: it now names the five correlated settles, the two deliberate non-members, and the route-identity (not request-identity) strength of the gate. Six new cases in the existing production-source CLJS suite, including a non-vacuity control and the strand control. Gates: test:cljs compile exit 0 and full run exit 0 (11105 tests / 54792 assertions, 0 failures 0 errors) re-run on the post-rebase base; test:examples-compile exit 0 across all 56 builds with zero warnings. Sabotage witness: removing the delete-rollback gate turned the focused suite red with exactly the reported symptom, then restored to an identical blob hash. No framework change, no new abstraction.

title: template: after-load hooks leave the app schema stale after edits
description:
## Scope

The generated browser entry points and schema guidance under `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template`: the default Reagent scaffold, UIx scaffold, Reagent Story scaffold, and Reagent SSR client's hot-reload path. Add focused generator/emitted-project regression coverage; no framework API redesign.

## Correctness finding

Every emitted app registers its app-db schema only from the module `init`, while Shadow CLJS calls that init function once and invokes only `^:dev/after-load` hooks after a save. Those hooks rerender the retained app but never re-register the newly loaded schema value. Consequently the framework continues validating the live frame with the boot-time schema after `schema.cljs` changes, even though the generated UI and event code hot-reload. The scaffold's advertised hot-reload loop is therefore internally inconsistent and can reject a source-valid write (or accept a write forbidden by a tightened schema) until a full page refresh.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Generate a default app, run `npm install` and `npx shadow-cljs watch app`, and open the counter page.
2. Increment the counter so preserving live state across reload is observable.
3. In `schema.cljs`, extend the closed `CounterDb` map with an optional string key such as `[:counter/label {:optional true} :string]`.
4. Change an event handler to associate `:counter/label` with a string, then save both files and let Shadow CLJS run the emitted `^:dev/after-load` hook.
5. Dispatch that event without refreshing the page. The write is validated against the original closed map, emits `:rf.error/schema-validation-failure`, and rolls back. Refreshing the page runs `init` again and makes the same write succeed.

The inverse is also incorrect: tightening a schema during the same session leaves the former permissive schema active until refresh.

## Evidence

- `_shared/schema.cljs` defines `register-schema!` with the instruction "Call once at boot (see core/init)" and passes the current `CounterDb` value to `rf/reg-app-schema`.
- `_reagent/core.cljs` lines 41-49 and `_uix/core.cljs` lines 36-45 tag `mount!` as `^:dev/after-load`, but it only retains/creates the React root and renders. Their `init` functions call `schema/register-schema!` only at lines 71 and 67 respectively.
- `_reagent/core_with_stories.cljs` lines 95-97 make `reload!` reinstall routing and render, while schema registration exists only in `init` at line 111.
- `_reagent/core_with_ssr.cljc` lines 156-164 make `render!` rerender the retained root, while the client schema is registered only in `init` at line 178.
- The emitted `root/README.md` lines 25-35 correctly says Shadow invokes `init` once and then calls after-load hooks, but lines 419-435 teach schema registration only once at boot.
- `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc` lines 567-572 stores the schema value in `schemas-by-frame`; it does not retain a Var that follows a redefinition. Lines 698-704 explicitly define hot-reload semantics as re-registering the `(frame-id, path)` so the new value replaces the prior validation-cache entry.
- Existing HMR emission tests exercise retained-root rerendering for Reagent, UIx, Story, and SSR, but do not assert schema replacement after a reload. Initial browser smoke tests cannot expose this post-save failure.

## Failure scenario / invariant

After any successful generated-app hot reload, validation and tooling must observe the schema definitions in the just-loaded source while preserving the existing frame, app-db, React root, and routing/hydration state. A source-valid event write must not fail solely because a stale boot-time schema remains cached, and a newly invalid write must not pass for the same reason.

## Recommended minimal fix

Have each emitted `^:dev/after-load` path re-register the current app schema for its existing frame before rerendering. Preserve the current boot ordering so initial events are still validated, and do not recreate/reseed the frame. In the SSR client, re-register against `app-frame` but do not repeat hydration. Update the generated schema comments/README to describe registration at boot and after load. The runtime already makes same-frame/path re-registration atomic and hot-reload-safe, so no framework change is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A focused executable CLJS regression drives the actual generated after-load path (or a small extracted reload seam used by that path): it boots with the original closed schema, retains non-default counter state, substitutes a schema that admits optional `:counter/label`, invokes reload without recreating the frame, and asserts `rf/app-schema-at [] {:frame :rf/default}` returns the new schema.
- The same test dispatches an ordinary generated event that writes `:counter/label` and proves the write commits while the pre-reload counter value remains intact.
- Coverage pins schema re-registration for all four emitted browser entry variants: default Reagent, UIx, Story, and the SSR client. SSR coverage additionally proves reload does not call `ssr/hydrate!` or replay seed events.
- The proof is non-vacuous: before the production fix, the fixture observes the old schema and the new-key write is rejected/rolled back; equivalently, a mutation/control that removes the after-load registration makes the regression fail.
- Existing emitted-project compile tests, initial browser smoke tests, and retained-root HMR tests remain green.
- Generated comments and README no longer claim that registration happens only once at boot; they explain that after-load re-registration updates validation while retaining app state.

## Non-goals

- Re-running module init, initial events, frame creation, hydration, or routing setup beyond what each current reload hook already requires.
- Changing runtime schema storage, validation policy, production elision, or public schema APIs.
- Adding watcher/process orchestration when a deterministic generated-code CLJS test can prove the reload invariant.
- Compatibility machinery for older generated projects.

## Related / duplicate search

Searched all-status beads for `stale schema`, `after-load schema`, `schema hot reload`, `schema re-registration`, `register-schema hot reload`, `CounterDb reload`, `schema.cljs after-load`, and `template HMR`; no matching issue exists. Closed `rf2-r0kk7` fixed the distinct absence of generated after-load rerender hooks and deliberately kept one-time boot ceremony in `init`; it did not refresh the schema registry and is not a duplicate.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #8897, confined to tools/template/**.

DEFECT CONFIRMED AT SOURCE in all four emitted entry points. reg-app-schema is frame-local, so the scaffold cannot call it at namespace load (a load-time call raises :rf.error/no-frame-context); it lives inside schema/register-schema!. A hot reload therefore re-evaluates the CounterDb def and re-registers nothing on its own, and every entry point called register-schema! from init alone -- which shadow runs once, at bundle load.

FIX: each ^:dev/after-load hook re-attaches the schema, BEFORE its render work. Reagent and UIx fold the call into mount!, which init already delegates to, so boot and reload traverse one path; Story (reload!) and the SSR client (render!) keep their one-time boot ceremony in init and re-attach from the hook. The SSR hook does not re-hydrate or replay seed events. Ordering matters as much as presence: the boot call still lands before frame-root creates the frame, so the :initial-events seed is validated from the first write, and a DOM-free host that skips the render still registers.

QUESTION 1 -- is hook-side re-registration correct, or does it paper over a framework gap? CORRECT; no framework change and no follow-up bead. Spec 010 Multiple-schemas-at-the-same-path makes re-registration last-write-wins and calls a hot-reload re-register benign; Spec 010 Schema-migration-on-hot-reload defines the tightened-schema case (a :rf.schema/violation warning, app-db not cleared or rewound); storage.cljc's hot-reload-semantics block makes it an atomic swap! into the map that IS the validation cache; and executable framework coverage already exists (schemas_storage_test meta-at-reflects-hot-reload-replacement, schemas_reg_side_effects_test, a hot-reload race stress test).

QUESTION 2 -- one shared helper or four parallel edits? FOUR PARALLEL EDITS. A helper would still have to be called from each hook, so it saves nothing at the call site; it could not cover all four anyway, since the SSR scaffold has no schema.cljs and its register-schema! is inline in core.cljc with a different arity; the emitted files are user-facing source, so the reader must see in the hook what a reload re-does; and fixing at the defect site leaves rf2-zq34m unprejudiced.

COVERAGE. Static and unconditional in the artefact's default clojure -M:test: every hook calls register-schema! before its render (all four variants); the SSR hook re-attaches against the live app-frame and neither re-hydrates nor replays the seed; schema.cljs keeps reg-app-schema out of the top level; both emitted READMEs teach boot AND after-load. Executable: a regression namespace copied into a generated project's test tree, compiled and run by the emitted :test build against real generated source -- it models one save (re-evaluate the def, then call what the hook calls), boots closed with a counter at 3, proves the closed schema REJECTS a :counter/label write, reloads widened, proves the live schema is replaced and the write now commits with the counter intact, then drives the inverse direction (tightening takes effect; app-db is not cleared). It rides RF2_TEMPLATE_RUN_EMITTED_TESTS, which CI's jvm-tools-template job sets on every PR.

TWO DEVIATIONS FROM THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, both deliberate. (a) The criteria name rf/app-schema-at; that symbol does NOT exist on the re-frame.core facade -- the schemas query helpers were removed from the front porch by rf2-wad2fl and live on re-frame.schemas. The regression uses re-frame.schemas/app-schema-at. (b) The executable regression drives the extracted reload seam the criteria explicitly permit, not the hook fn itself: requiring the emitted core.cljs pulls reagent.dom.client and React into a node-test bundle, which would need a :browser-grade node_modules for no added signal. The hook's CALL is pinned statically for all four variants instead, so the composite is covered.

GATES (captured exits, post-rebase): tools/template clojure -M:test = 0 (71 tests, 728 assertions); the gated emitted-run regression = 0 (1 test, 10 assertions); check_doc_slugs.py = 0; check_readme_links.py --ci = 0; clj-kondo --fail-level error on tools/template/{src,test} = 0; splint --fail-on-errors over the template lint surface = 0. Three sabotage controls each went red naming the planted fault, and each plant was restored and verified by git blob hash.

title: surface-review(skill-reagent-migration): teach only Hicasso's live read and navigation doors
description:
## Scope

Update skills/reagent-migration/** so the published skill teaches only the current post-dead-weight Hicasso authoring vocabulary at the two seams changed by rf2-6c12m.15:

- h/sub is the sole public subscription-read door.
- navigation is authored through h/route-link or ordinary routing events; the navigate intent head is implementation-owned and is not written as ::h/navigate.

Cover the distributable SKILL/references and the authoring-time spec/eval material that can reintroduce the old forms. Keep this a skill-only change.

## Findings

1. The skill violates its own cardinal rule 6 (“emit only what has shipped; read the door”). Current re-frame.hicasso exports h/sub and no h/use-subs, but references/mental-model.md and references/catalog-mechanical.md still teach h/use-subs as a deliberate control, while spec/inputs.md still rosters it as public.

2. The public navigate spelling also moved. rf2-6c12m.15 demoted the navigate head to re-frame.hicasso.impl.intent/navigate; h/route-link mints that internal value. references/gotchas.md still calls ::h/navigate one of two public reserved heads and says the draft guide is incomplete without it, while spec/authoring-prompt.md preserves that claim for the next reauthor. An authored ::h/navigate now resolves to a different keyword from the internal head and is not the shipped navigation contract.

3. This is high-friction in the failure direction. An AI following the read leaf can emit an unresolved h/use-subs call; one following the gotcha can emit a vector the current intent lowering does not recognize as its navigation head. The programmer is asked to choose between doors that no longer exist instead of using the single simple path Hicasso intentionally kept.

4. Progressive disclosure currently hides, rather than contains, the drift: the top-level router says “read the door,” but the false advice appears only when the relevant read/gotcha leaf is loaded. The eval corpus has no expectation that rejects either retired form, so its behavioural fixtures do not expose the contradiction.

5. This is recent history, not a request to redesign Hicasso. Commit 4c9fa03def (rf2-6c12m.15) removed h/use-subs as below the ergonomics bar and internalised navigation as part of the open dead-weight programme. Other same-wave skill updates carried hframe, native and defhost changes, but these six live teaching references remained.

## Recommended Action

Carry rf2-6c12m.15 into this skill directly:
