- Teach repeated, conditional and looped reads as ordinary h/sub calls. Remove the grouped-read alternative rather than replacing it with another abstraction.
- Remove ::h/navigate from the author-facing marker/reserved-head vocabulary. Where navigation is relevant, point to h/route-link or a normal routing event; do not expose the internal intent value.
- Correct spec/inputs.md and spec/authoring-prompt.md so a future reauthor cannot resurrect either form.
- Add or amend one focused behavioural eval that grades the live outcome: h/sub is the only read emitted, and neither h/use-subs nor ::h/navigate is proposed.

Keep the explanation short. The outcome is fewer concepts and code that compiles against the current door, not a new compatibility story.

## Evidence

- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc: the current public door aliases h/sub and has no use-subs export.
- docs/core/hicasso/api-reference.md, “Reads”: the complete current roster contains h/sub only.
- implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso/impl/intent.cljs:284: navigate-head is namespaced to the implementation.
- docs/core/hicasso/07-routing-and-navigation.md:68-80: route-link owns and mints that head; application authors do not.
- skills/reagent-migration/references/mental-model.md:84 and references/catalog-mechanical.md:61 still teach h/use-subs.
- skills/reagent-migration/spec/inputs.md:17 still lists use-subs on the door.
- skills/reagent-migration/references/gotchas.md:108,204 and spec/authoring-prompt.md:23 still teach ::h/navigate as public.
- git commit 4c9fa03def: “hicasso: drop h/use-subs, the grouped read control (rf2-6c12m.15)”.
- skills/reagent-migration/README.md says the skill is pre-alpha and has not been exercised end to end; the static eval set contains no retired-read/navigation control.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No live instruction, source-of-truth roster, reauthoring prompt or eval expectation under skills/reagent-migration/** presents h/use-subs as callable or ::h/navigate as author-written.
- The read guidance has one direct answer: use h/sub at each read site, including conditional/loop/helper cases.
- Navigation guidance, if retained in this migration skill, uses only h/route-link or ordinary routing events and clearly leaves the opaque navigate head to Hicasso.
- A focused behavioural eval would fail an answer that emits h/use-subs or ::h/navigate and pass one that stays on the live public doors.
- Existing M/D/R routing, whole-view coherence, reporter/census workflow, compile/test verification and programmer-owned render check remain intact.
- JSON parses, skill/package structural checks pass, and the relevant markdown link/anchor gate passes. The handoff names the current public-door source that was checked.

## Non-goals

- No Hicasso runtime or public API change.
- No compatibility alias or shim for h/use-subs or ::h/navigate.
- No automated view rewrite engine, new linter, surface-sync gate or defensive policy.
- No broad API audit, catalogue expansion, reporter change, migration of application dataflow, or redesign of route-link.
- No unrelated polish or exhaustive wording sweep.

## Related beads

- rf2-6c12m.15 — exact landed facade-hygiene change this skill missed.
- rf2-6c12m — open Hicasso dead-weight epic; establishes the minimum-ceremony/trust-the-programmer direction.
- rf2-r3r00 — current complementary surface review reducing Hicasso’s clj-kondo export to useful macro-shape analysis; no dependency or overlap.
- rf2-r4j91 — original Reagent-migration retarget to Hicasso.
- rf2-0jl8s, rf2-6c12m.24, rf2-6c12m.30 and rf2-6c12m.13 — prior API changes successfully carried into this skill, useful history for the same bounded update pattern.
notes: TRIAGE 2026-08-31 00:56:58 AUSEST (read-only agent at 5d35356469): premises HOLD (hicasso.cljc:429 exports sub; zero use-subs under hicasso src; intent.cljs:284 navigate-head is impl-owned; the six stale lines as cited). Mechanical, about an hour, no collisions, no hot zone. Worker confirms ::h/prevent (gotchas.md:108) and ::h/clear (:204) against hicasso.cljc before keeping them; adds one behavioural evals.json entry. Gates: check_skill_package_refs.py, check_skill_eval_packaging.py, check_doc_slugs.py, a JSON parse of evals.json. DISPATCHABLE solo NOW.
close_reason: PR #8804 (worker/reagent-mig-doors-qxca8, ready for review): the six stale lines corrected — mental-model.md and catalog-mechanical.md drop the h/use-subs grouped read (h/sub at each read site, no replacement abstraction), inputs.md roster now matches the shipped door (sub/error-boundary/reg-state/portal/route-link/as-element/as-component/mount!/hydrate!/render!/unmount!), gotchas.md:108+204 and authoring-prompt.md:23 stop teaching ::h/navigate as author-written (h/route-link or ordinary routing events; navigate head is re-frame.hicasso.impl.intent/navigate). ::h/prevent and ::h/clear confirmed live against hicasso.cljc/intent.cljs/state.cljc and kept. Behavioural eval 28 added: fails h/use-subs or ::h/navigate, passes live doors. Gates all exit 0 post-rebase onto 1a3a6dc9dc: check_skill_package_refs, check_skill_eval_packaging, check_doc_slugs, JSON parse (27 evals). Planted-fault controls red-then-green with blob-hash-verified restores.

title: surface-review(mcp-conformance): make one command explain and run the live compatibility profile
description:
## Scope

Turn the existing repository-level `test:mcp-conformance` runner into the one documented front door for understanding and running MCP compatibility. Preserve its current medium-cost default run, add one explicit opt-in mode that chains the existing hermetic live Pair suite, and make every terminal verdict state which profile actually ran. Limit implementation to the existing runner, its small regression surface, and the MCP testing docs/package entry points needed to make the command copyable; keep the split CI jobs and focused per-suite commands.

## Findings

- The compatibility corpus already has strong teeth. The Node workflows use the official `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` client, SDK-call every advertised tool, validate descriptor classifications and result envelopes, and run real Story and degraded Pair workflows. The JVM wire suite auto-discovers its focused namespaces and combines canonical schemas, fixtures, reachable builders, source pins, near-miss rejection, and cross-encoding checks. The high-leverage need is not another protocol checklist or host matrix.
- There is already a single repository operator command: `npm run test:mcp-conformance` from `implementation/`. It installs/builds prerequisites and chains Story JVM/stdio, Pair compile/tests, the conformance Node inventory, and wire-vocab. Commit `7f1f93234a` created it specifically because the prior workflow required reading CI and invoking commands across four directories.
- The command is not the front door of the artefact it verifies. `tools/mcp-conformance/README.md` still teaches dependency installation plus separate unit, Pair compile/e2e, Story, hermetic-live, and wire-vocab recipes, and never names the existing single command. A reader or coding agent arriving at the conformance package has to reconstruct which recipe means “compatibility”.
- The default command's final verdict loses a load-bearing distinction. `tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/test-all.cjs` correctly records live rows as `SKIP` when no nREPL port is supplied and explains that the hermetic suite did not run. One level up, `implementation/scripts/test-mcp-conformance.cjs` reduces that whole child run to one status row and unconditionally ends with `ALL MCP-CONFORMANCE GATES GREEN`.
- The outer runner's own header says it chains the six PR-time MCP gates, while the same header explicitly excludes the hermetic live suite. CI's Pair conformance job does include that suite after the SDK/degraded rows. The omission is an intentional cost profile, not a missing test, but the terminal success line makes the default profile look complete.
- `TESTING.md` knows the real split: `test:mcp-conformance` is the medium command and `test:re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite` is a separate expensive command. That distinction lives in a large repository testing catalogue rather than in the command's help/output or the conformance README.
- Existing inventory ownership is sufficient: `scripts/test-all.cjs` owns Node rows, `scripts/live-test-inventory.cjs` owns live rows, and the JVM runner discovers `*_test.clj`. A new manifest, report schema, compliance database, or duplicated roster would add drift without improving compatibility feedback.
- Exact current/closed tracker searches for `surface-review(mcp-conformance)`, `test:mcp-conformance`, `single entry`, `hermetic live`, `SKIP`, and the current all-green sentinel found no bead owning this outcome.

## Recommended Action

Extend the existing `implementation` runner, rather than creating a second orchestrator:

1. Keep the no-argument command as today's medium profile. Its final summary must identify the server/unit + SDK/degraded + wire-vocab layers that passed and show the existing hermetic live Pair suite as `NOT RUN`, with the exact opt-in command beside it. It must not print an unqualified “all MCP conformance gates green” verdict.
2. Add one explicit `--live` mode that runs the same default steps and then invokes the existing `test:re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite` entry point. A full-green verdict is available only after the hermetic runner observes every registered live sentinel and proves cleanup, preserving its existing exit-code distinction between conformance and orchestration failure.
3. Add side-effect-free `--help` output that names both modes, their prerequisites/cost boundary, what `npm test` inside `tools/mcp-conformance` does, and which mode proves live runtime behavior.
4. Front-load the two copyable repository-root commands in `tools/mcp-conformance/README.md`; keep focused scripts below them for diagnosis. Align `TESTING.md` wording if necessary, but retain one canonical project command rather than adding aliases in several packages.

Reuse the existing Node and live inventories and the wire-vocab test discovery. The improvement is an honest, executable profile boundary, not a new compliance framework.

## Evidence

- `implementation/scripts/test-mcp-conformance.cjs:3-47` describes the six-gate operator runner, says the hermetic suite is intentionally excluded, and points to a second manual command.
- `implementation/scripts/test-mcp-conformance.cjs:186-245` declares the current prep and six gate steps; lines 303-318 collapse their result to the unqualified all-green sentinel.
- `implementation/package.json` exposes the runner only as `test:mcp-conformance` from the implementation package.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/README.md:101-148` gives five separate run recipes, uses `npm install` despite the committed lock/reproducible `npm ci` posture, and describes `npm test` as the Node inventory without pointing to the repository-level runner.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/test-all.cjs:13-18,87-96,130-156` derives the live rows, marks them `SKIP`, and prints the coverage caveat that the outer runner later loses.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/live-test-inventory.cjs:6-41` is the one live roster; the hermetic runner derives `INNER_TESTS` from it.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/scripts/run-re-frame2-pair-live-hermetic-suite.cjs:1266-1302,1361-1378` refuses skipped/missing sentinels and emits green only after cleanup grading.
- `tools/mcp-conformance/package.json` exposes focused Node/server/live scripts but no project compatibility profile or CLI help.
- `TESTING.md:32-34` separately lists the medium conformance command and expensive live command.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml:5345-5423,5488-5500,5562-5566` shows the actual CI split and that the Pair job includes the hermetic suite.
- History: `7f1f93234a` introduced the single runner; `ddb3ec91f3` made its installs reproducible. The current package README was rewritten later in `deb03d1d01` and still exposes only the multi-command route.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. From the repository root, one documented command runs the current medium compatibility profile; its terminal summary explicitly marks the hermetic live Pair profile `NOT RUN` and prints the exact `--live` invocation. No unqualified all-green sentence is emitted for that partial profile.
2. The same command with `--live` invokes the existing hermetic suite after the default steps. It reports full compatibility green only when every live row from `LIVE_TESTS` ran to its sentinel and the hermetic cleanup grade is clean; inner exit 1 and orchestration/cleanup exit 2 continue to propagate distinctly.
3. `--help` exits zero before installs, compiles, or server boots and concisely explains default versus live coverage, prerequisites, expected relative cost, and the narrower meaning of `tools/mcp-conformance/npm test`. Unknown options fail before any setup mutation.
4. A lightweight runner regression test exercises default, `--live`, help, and unknown-option selection without launching Clojure, shadow-cljs, Chromium, or either MCP server, and proves the live step is absent/present in the corresponding planned summary.
5. `tools/mcp-conformance/README.md` starts its run guidance with the two repository-root commands and a small included/omitted profile table. Focused unit, per-server, wire-vocab, and direct hermetic commands remain available as diagnostic recipes and agree with package scripts.
6. The implementation reuses `TESTS`, `LIVE_TESTS`, the current hermetic entry point, and JVM test discovery; it introduces no second test roster, copied tool catalogue, new result/report format, or new CI job.
7. Existing CI jobs, changed-surface scheduling, default medium cost, server behavior, tool descriptors, and wire schemas remain unchanged. The existing focused suites and runner policy tests pass.

## Non-goals

- No MCP certification product, compatibility score, persisted report, dashboard, badge, or release-compliance database.
- No matrix across MCP hosts, SDK languages/versions, protocol versions, transports, operating systems, or published-package combinations.
- No new protocol assertions, tool semantics, wire markers, schemas, vocabulary rules, or server launch flags.

title: client-root adoption: canonical skills and the pair fixture still own raw Reagent roots
description:
## Scope

The stock Reagent adapter's browser-root surface: `implementation/adapters/reagent/**`, the shared ratom-spine root machinery only where needed, the Spec 006/public API contract, and the Reagent boot paths in the canonical guide, adapter testbed, examples, and generated templates. Preserve the canonical-namespace parity promised by the published full and slim Reagent artefacts.

## Verified Findings

- `re-frame.adapter.reagent` exposes exactly `adapter`, `flush-views!`, and `set-hiccup-emitter!`; there is no app-facing mount/root lifecycle. Spec 006 nevertheless calls adapter `:render` the client-side mount entry point, and core implements it only at `re-frame.substrate.adapter/render`, not on the documented front porch.
- The ratom spine already does the hard work: first render can call `create-root` or `hydrate-root`, it tracks the resulting React Root, and adapter disposal drains tracked roots. But the operation returns only an unmount thunk. It cannot render a new tree through that same root, so it cannot express the ordinary Shadow hot-reload loop.
- Consequently, normal applications bypass the adapter lifecycle. The boot guide, generated Reagent templates, examples, and the adapter's own browser testbed each retain a raw React Root and call `reagent.dom.client` directly. Those roots are invisible to `destroy-adapter!`, and every caller must independently get create-once, hydrate-once, rerender, and teardown ordering right.
- The SSR template makes the missing operation especially clear: `init` chooses `hydrate-root` versus `create-root`, stores the raw root, and its `^:dev/after-load` hook later calls `rdc/render` on that root. The existing one-shot adapter entry cannot replace this correct hot-reload shape.
- Spec 006 requires the returned unmount function to be idempotent, but `track-active-root!` removes the root from its set and invokes the underlying unmount operation on every call; a second call reaches React again.

## Recommended Action

Give the canonical Reagent adapter namespace one small, explicit, reusable client-root lifecycle. A caller should be able to allocate an inert root handle at namespace load, render through it repeatedly, and unmount it explicitly:

1. the first render creates or hydrates exactly one React Root from the supplied mount point and options;
2. later renders update that same Root, which makes the same call usable from `^:dev/after-load` without caller-owned raw React state;
3. explicit unmount is idempotent, and `destroy-adapter!` releases a still-live root exactly once;
4. the raw React Root remains private to the adapter.

Back the handle with the existing active-root ownership rather than adding a second lifecycle. Keep the handle caller-owned and explicit; do not introduce a process-global mount-point registry. Name the operations plainly and document the tiny boot recipe. Full Reagent and the published slim variant must present the same canonical namespace surface.

Migrate the canonical guide, generated Reagent templates (including SSR), the adapter browser testbed, and ordinary Reagent example entrypoints to this lifecycle. After the sweep, direct `reagent.dom.client` root bookkeeping should remain only in the adapter implementation, focused lower-level DOM tests, or integrations that intentionally own a foreign React root.

## Evidence

- `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.reagent.md` says requiring the namespace gives exactly three things and documents no mount operation.
- `spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:227-239` defines `(render render-tree mount-point opts) -> unmount-fn` as the client mount contract and requires idempotent unmount.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/adapter.cljc:605-613` implements the entry only in the substrate namespace; no `re-frame.core` export exists.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:3432-3448` creates/hydrates and tracks a Root but exposes only the unmount thunk. `:987-1000` shows that thunk calls the underlying unmount on every invocation.
- `docs/core/how-to/boot-and-mount-an-app.md:39-60` teaches `defonce react-root`, `rdc/create-root`, and `rdc/render`.
- `tools/template/resources/day8/re_frame2_template/_reagent/core.cljs:41-49` repeats that bookkeeping. `_reagent/core_with_ssr.cljc:146-162,183-209` stores a raw hydrated/created root specifically so hot reload can rerender it.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/testbed/adapter_testbed_reagent/core.cljs:57-72` bypasses adapter `:render` in the adapter's own end-to-end mount smoke.
- A repository census finds 30 files under `examples/` and `tools/template/resources/` containing `rdc/create-root`.
- `implementation/adapters/reagent/deps.edn` deliberately keeps Reagent 2.0.1 in the adapter artefact and out of core, so the Reagent-specific handle belongs at the adapter boundary without adding a Reagent dependency to core.
- History shows the split accreting: `16ec884492` established the one-shot create-root/render/unmount adapter path; `cd6cf3ebf8` added adapter-owned root draining; `9cf8f2e54c` fixed generated-app hot reload by rerendering caller-owned raw roots instead of extending the adapter surface.
- Duplicate search: `bd search` over `reagent mount`, `client mount`, `root lifecycle`, `adapter-owned root`, `create-root`, `rerender root`, and `reusable root` found no matching open or closed task for this outcome.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The canonical Reagent adapter API provides a documented caller-owned client-root handle (or an equivalently small explicit lifecycle) that performs no DOM work when constructed.
- Browser contract tests prove: a cold first render calls `create-root` once; a hydrating first render calls `hydrate-root` once; two or more later renders reuse the identical Root and call neither constructor again; a hydrated root is updated with normal render rather than hydrated again.
- Calling explicit unmount more than once invokes the underlying React unmount once. Destroying the adapter releases every still-live handle once, while an already-unmounted handle is not released again.
- Normal boot requires no caller-owned raw React Root or create/hydrate branch. The core boot guide, adapter testbed, generated Reagent templates, and ordinary Reagent example entrypoints use the canonical lifecycle; the SSR template still hydrates exactly once and hot reload still rerenders without reseeding app state.
- The full and published slim Reagent variants expose the same canonical namespace API and behavior; public API docs and Spec 006 describe ownership, update, hydration, and teardown semantics.
- Focused low-level tests and deliberate foreign-root integrations may keep direct `reagent.dom.client` calls, but remaining occurrences are reviewed and explicitly outside the normal app boot path.

## Non-goals

- No implicit default adapter, implicit frame creation, automatic DOM-id lookup, or auto-mount on namespace load.
- No process-global root registry and no exposure of the substrate's raw React Root.
- No Reagent 1 or React 17/18 compatibility path.
- No redesign of `reg-view`, Form-3 component authoring, subscriptions, or render-flush helpers.
- No requirement to rewrite focused DOM tests whose subject is raw React/Reagent behavior.

## Related beads

- `rf2-r0kk7` (closed) fixed Shadow hot reload by adding `^:dev/after-load` rerenders; this task keeps that behavior while moving root ownership behind the adapter.

title: A fifth cross-ref still teaches the edge stripe and the 4-signal count (015)
description:
A FIFTH live cross-reference still teaches the retired mode-signal contract, in a spelling none of the
patterns used by rf2-76tj7 or rf2-g8jh9 matches. Found out of fence by rf2-76tj7's worker, which widened its
census to other count spellings; the mayor verified it at source at trunk `5a521c4a60` before filing.

**The site**, `tools/xray/spec/015-Configuration.md:773-777`, one Cross-reference paragraph carrying BOTH
defects:

- `:774-775` — "§Static mode (visual-language treatment of the mode pill, **edge stripe**, motion dampening,
  chrome silhouette)". The edge stripe is REMOVED.
- `:776-777` — "§Static surface (the architectural contract — 3-layer silhouette, **4-signal**
  mode-recognition mechanism, mode-state lifecycle)". The count is retired.

**The authority**, read at tip: `tools/xray/spec/018-Event-Spine.md:129` is
`### The mode signals (chrome silhouette + 2 reinforcing)`, and 018's stripe row says removed outright.

**Why this is filed rather than recorded.** Posture ruling rf2-09c8s files stale prose only where a FALSE
claim leads a reader into a WRONG ACTION. 015 is the CONFIGURATION spec, and this paragraph is its pointer
into the mode contract: a reader configuring static mode from it builds an edge stripe that no longer exists
and reasons about a four-signal mechanism that is now three. That is the same judgement under which
rf2-qrgtt and rf2-76tj7 were filed and fixed.

**NOT covered by the two existing items, which is why this is new rather than a duplicate.** rf2-76tj7
(PR #10079, open) and its audit shadow rf2-g8jh9 both enumerate exactly FOUR sites — `000-Vision.md:211` and
`:213-214`, `003-Machine-Inspector.md:1446`, `DESIGN-RATIONALE.md:676` — and neither names 015 anywhere.
rf2-g8jh9's own disposition test is "verify rf2-76tj7's eventual merged diff resolves these four sites", so
this fifth site would survive both items being closed.

**Precedent for the wording, so a third phrasing is not invented.** PR #10075 dropped the count rather than
recounting it to 3, at `018:127`; rf2-76tj7 followed that at all four of its sites and reused #10075's
wording from `003:1447` for the signal list. Follow the same precedent here: drop the count, and replace
`edge stripe` with the surviving signals. Do not invent a new phrasing, and do not touch the unrelated live
L4 stripe or any historical lock text.

**Gate reality, stated unfavourably.** `check_doc_slugs.py` DOES cover `tools/*/spec`, but it grades links
and anchors only — it cannot see a false claim in a cross-reference. `mkdocs build --strict` stages only
`spec/` and `migration/`, never `tools/`, so it is the wrong gate. The verification is resolving the claim
against `018-Event-Spine.md:129`.

**Census note:** the `4-signal` spelling WRAPS across a line break, so a line-oriented pass alone cannot see
it — rf2-76tj7's worker measured `edge stripe colour tokens` at line-oriented **0** and flattened **1** on
its own sites for exactly this reason. Run a flattened pass and a comment-stripped pass, and take the
control from the target.

**Surface:** `015-Configuration.md` is held by no open PR (its last change was rf2-oyguj, merged at
`06c0fcaea5`).

title: xray: coalesce the redaction-counter dispatch per task so a host burst cannot exceed the :rf/xray drain depth (Mike ruled A)
description:
RULING (Mike, in chat 2026-09-15: "rule A"): coalesce Xray's redaction-counter dispatch per task. Spec 015's one-dispatch-per-bump sentence changes to match.

WHY: rf2-izhgo (PR #9839) fixed a boot-time :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded on :rf/xray, caused by Xray counting 126 of its own frameless sub reads as redactions. That fix removed the trigger but not the amplifier.
- config/note-suppressed! still dispatches one :rf.xray/note-sensitive-suppressed per suppressed trace, as tools/xray/spec/015-Configuration.md requires: "every atom bump fires a matching dispatch; every dispatch comes from an atom bump" (about :796).
- So a genuine host burst of more than ~100 frameless sensitive trace events in one task still exceeds the :rf/xray drain depth.
- That error is misattributed to Xray, and Xray's own UI events can be dropped, as in rf2-chs7.

THE CHANGE:
- Keep bumping the atom per event, so the count stays exact.
- Schedule at most one :rf.xray/note-sensitive-suppressed per task, carrying the per-frame totals, following Xray's existing task-coalesced precedent: install.cljs's epoch pump (rf2-chs7, about :56-135) and trace-collector/request-mirror-sync! (rf2-wq6gx).
- Spec 015: the lockstep sentence becomes "the frame slot converges to the atom within one task". Keep the atom-as-JVM-primitive rationale.
- Do NOT raise or special-case the drain depth.

ACCEPTANCE:
- A regression, RED before the change: 150 frameless sensitive HOST traces emitted in one task through the real rf.trace/emit! path produce a count of 150, exactly one dispatch, and no :rf.error/drain-depth-exceeded.
- Existing tests that pin one dispatch per bump are updated to the new contract, not deleted.
- The count still lands in the "REDACTED N" badge within one task.
- The control: revert only the coalescing, and the regression goes red again.

title: docs(reagent-slim): IMPL-SPEC R-007 says re-frame.interop still requires stock Reagent — it carries ZERO such requires, and the row's gzip figures rest on that claim
description:
Found by `xraydeps-a` while answering rf2-99qn (PR #9692), reported rather than absorbed — the
right call, since reagent-slim's spec is a different surface from `tools/xray/deps.edn`.

## THE FALSE CLAIM, VERIFIED AT SOURCE BY THE MAYOR AT TRUNK ce893bbe9b

`implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md`, risk-register row **R-007** (one long table
row, around line 1224) says:

  "...in the in-tree shadow-cljs build both adapter trees live on the same classpath, and
   `re-frame.interop` still statically `:require`s stock `reagent.core` / `reagent.ratom`, so a
   per-build classpath-pruning hook is needed before the realised-gzip-reduction measurement is
   meaningful."

`re-frame.interop` STILL EXISTS (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.cljs`), so this is not a
dangling reference to a deleted namespace — it is a live namespace the row is WRONG ABOUT.

MEASURED: `implementation/core/src` carries **ZERO** `[reagent.` requires. The single textual hit in
that whole tree is a COMMENT at `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/provider.cljs:230` which
says a `:require [reagent.core]` "would hard-couple this ns to stock Reagent" — i.e. the absence is
deliberate and documented. Control on the same instrument in the same run:
`implementation/adapters/reagent/src` DOES match, so the pattern bites and the zero is absence.

## WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A TYPO

The row's NUMBERS rest on the false claim. It reports "stock counter ~93 KB gz, slim counter ~93 KB
gz" and explains the non-difference by the shared-classpath shape it has just mis-described, then
says those figures "are NOT the binding slim claim". If the stated cause is gone, the reader cannot
tell whether the figures are still explained, whether the "per-build classpath-pruning hook" is
still needed, or whether the Stage-5 follow-up this row defers is now answerable. A risk register
whose stated mechanism has been repaired underneath it is worse than one with no entry: it tells the
next reader a blocker stands when it may not.

## SCOPE

Re-derive the claim at your own tip (mine is hours old and is a mayor's measurement). Then either:

(a) the coupling is genuinely gone — correct R-007 to say so, dated, and say plainly what is now
    TRUE about why the two counters measure the same: read the actual build graph rather than
    assuming, since `xraydeps-a` found a live stock-Reagent edge in the XRAY tree through
    `machines-viz`'s chart, and something analogous may or may not exist here. If the pruning-hook
    follow-up is now unblocked, say that; if it is blocked for a DIFFERENT reason, name that reason;
    if the measurement is now takeable, say so and do not take it — that is a separate item with a
    cost.
(b) some coupling survives by a route the grep missed — then the row is right for the wrong reason,
    and the fix is to name the real route. Report it either way.

DO NOT take the gzip measurement itself in this bead, and do not build a classpath-pruning hook.
This is a correction to a written record. The project stance rules out gold-plating a bundle-size
investigation with no demand attached, and there is none today.

WHAT IS NOT IN SCOPE: `tools/xray/deps.edn` (rf2-99qn, PR #9692), and any change to the adapters'
production sources. Read the rest of the R-001..R-007 register while you are in there and report —
do not fix — anything else that reads stale, so the widening decision stays mine.

title: Incomplete EP template: raw title placeholder hides its rendered body
description:
Merged-PR audit #9615, landing 6c53bf433734f952bd10fa36ce248f7f7fd3a3cd, investigated the PR's explicit unmeasurable-file observation. docs/EP/EP-template.md:1 writes '# EP-NNNN: <Title>'. Python-Markdown preserves the raw opening title element. This is more than a limitation of the new list walker: Chromium treats the remainder of the document as title text, hiding the template's body.

Independent browser proof: render the exact landed file with the actual loaded MkDocs Markdown configuration, put that HTML in a normal document body and open it in headless Chromium via the repository's Playwright. The landed result has only 8 visible body characters ('EP-NNNN:'), zero h2 elements, zero paragraphs, and 8112 characters swallowed by body title. Changing only the first literal <Title> to <Title> before rendering gives 328 visible characters, 8 h2 elements, 2 paragraphs and no body title. The rest of the source is largely instructional HTML comments, so it is intentionally not all visible. This proves the local rendered-content failure; it is not a claim that a deployed site URL was inspected.

Escape or code-format the title placeholder so it is shown literally and the template's actual sections render. Verify the exact source through the real renderer and browser, and confirm the list gate can measure it rather than merely suppressing the warning. No change to the gate's intentionally explicit UNMEASURABLE policy is requested. Fresh exact-owner search found only the closed rf2-gyq4 observation, no open repair owner; preserve that closed record and add this separate follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: The rendered EP template visibly contains its literal title placeholder and the expected section headings/body instead of swallowing them into a title element. A raw-placeholder negative control demonstrates the failure and the corrected file is measurable by the existing list gate. Preserve instructional comments and template content; a focused one-file documentation correction is sufficient.

RENDERING, measured through the actual loaded MkDocs config (11 extensions via mkdocs' own config loader) in headless Chromium, HEAD vs repaired: visible body characters 8 -> 341 h1 / h2 / paragraphs 1/0/0 -> 1/8/2 chars swallowed by body title 8114 -> 0 non-standard elements in body [title] -> [] All eight section headings render (Abstract, Motivation, Specification, Rationale, Backwards Compatibility, Resolved Decisions, Open Issues, References). GATE CAN NOW MEASURE, shown positively rather than by silence. Driven through `check_flattened_lists.py`'s own API: HEAD : UNMEASURABLE — rendered HTML leaves <h1, title> unclosed repaired : MEASURED, 0 defects; 2 of 2 sentinels placed in the tag walk corpus : "291 scanned, 0 flattened, 1 unmeasurable" -> "... 0 unmeasurable" Decisive control: a flattened list planted in the repaired file's visible body is REPORTED (FLATTENED line 100, renders at the same depth — a SIBLING); the same control planted in the landed file stays UNMEASURABLE. title: spec/Security.md and attr-string's docstring carry the same short SSR strip roster that rf2-2fes is fixing in 011
description:
THE SSR ATTRIBUTE-STRIP ROSTER IS ENUMERATED IN THREE PLACES AND ALL THREE WENT STALE.
rf2-2fes / PR #9598 repairs ONE of them. This bead is the other two.

MEASURED BY THE MAYOR ON TRUNK a0e48243321d0c37d132a672beaf519405dbe92f (fact):

`strip-prop?` in implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc drops SIX classes,
through five predicates at lines 679-681 and their name sets above:

  1. `on*` event-handler props
  2. function-valued props
  3. reserved prototype-pollution keys  (`prototype-pollution-prop-names`, line 407)
  4. JSX source-coord props             (`jsx-source-prop-names`, line 517)
  5. React structural slots `:key` `:ref`         (`structural-slot-names`, line 546)
  6. React content channels `:children` `:dangerouslySetInnerHTML`
                                        (`content-channel-names`, line 617)

Its OWN docstring at line 620 lists all six correctly. Three other sites list three.

=== SITE A: spec/Security.md, the bullet at line 65 ===

"**Event-handler-prop filter + reserved-prop-keys gate at static-markup emission.**" It
names classes 1, 2 and 3 and stops. This is the FRAMEWORK-WIDE security mirror of the
011 bullet — the page a reader consults for "what does this framework refuse to
serialise across the trust boundary" — so it is short in the same way and for the same
reader. NOT hot-zone.

=== SITE B: the `attr-string` docstring in html_helpers.cljc, line ~1019 ===

    "Props matching `strip-prop?` — `on*` event-handler props, function-
     valued props, and reserved prototype-pollution keys — are dropped at
     emit time per Spec 011 rule rf2-dwds9 ..."

Classes 1, 2 and 3 again. **This one is the sharpest, because it sits INSIDE the file
that every other site is told to defer to.** The whole argument for keeping the spec's
enumeration in step is that `strip-prop?` is the single realisation point; a second,
shorter enumeration four hundred lines below it in the same file undercuts that.

=== WHAT IS NOT DRIFT — CHECKED, SO NOBODY RE-CHECKS IT ===

A census on `prototype-pollution` returns eight tracked files. Two of the remaining
prose hits are NOT this roster and must not be "fixed":

  * implementation/SECURITY.md:163 is a DECISION-REGISTER TABLE ROW recording what bead
    rf2-dwds9 called, on the REAGENT-SLIM CLIENT path (`emit-attribute`, before `aset`),
    not the SSR emitter. It is dated bookkeeping about a call, not a live contract
    enumeration. LEAVE IT.
  * implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs:224 is
    reagent-slim's own commentary about its own props object. Different surface.
    LEAVE IT.

That distinction is the CLAUDE.md instrument item (g) trap — a census that treats prose
as the evidence is contaminated in both directions — and it was caught here by reading
the ranked files rather than trusting the rank. Do not re-litigate it; do not widen.

=== ONE THING TO CHECK, WHICH MAY OR MAY NOT BE A FINDING ===

implementation/ssr/test/re_frame/ssr_emit_test.clj names `prototype-pollution` and reads
ZERO for all three newer classes, while its sibling ssr_attr_filter_test.clj reads 6 and
12. That is CONSISTENT with the two files simply owning different halves of the surface,
and it is equally consistent with an assertion set that never grew. **Look, and report
which it is.** If it is a real coverage gap, FILE IT — do not fold a test expansion into
a prose bead.

=== THE DURABLE QUESTION, AND IT IS YOURS TO ARGUE ===

Four enumerations of one roster, three of them stale, two landings deep, all within one
day. The rf2-2fes worker chose to DUPLICATE AND COMPLETE rather than defer, and gave a
measured reason: every one of the four name sets is `^:private` and `strip-prop?` is
absent from spec/api-manifest.edn, so there is nothing public to cite. That reasoning is
sound and this bead does NOT reopen it — bring both sites into step the same way.

But it leaves the recurrence unanswered, and the repo has a standing idiom for exactly
this: a DRIFT GATE. `scripts/check_keyword_catalogue_drift.py` describes itself as that
pattern applied to keywords, and the api-manifest job is the same shape. A gate reading
`strip-prop?`'s name sets and grading the enumerations against them would make the next
addition impossible to land short.

**DO NOT BUILD THE GATE ON THIS BEAD.** Argue for or against it in the PR body from what
you find — how many sites, how mechanically extractable the name sets are, what a gate
would have to parse — and FILE IT as its own bead with that argument attached. A gate is
a new permanent obligation and it deserves its own decision. Bringing two prose sites
into step is this bead.

=== BOUNDARIES ===

Yours: spec/Security.md and the `attr-string` docstring in html_helpers.cljc.

**spec/011-SSR.md IS NOT YOURS** — PR #9598 is open against it and unmerged. Read it for
the wording the sibling settled on (it is worth matching), but do not edit it. If you
believe your change needs it, STOP AND REPORT.

Do not change `strip-prop?` or any name set. They are correct; you are transcribing.
notes: Merged-PR audit #9602: rf2-w2ql separately tracks the false roster-authority sentence added to attr-string. It places Spec 011 downstream of both implementation descriptions, while the landed Spec 011 explicitly places strip-prop? downstream of the normative list. The requested correction is confined to that comparison; the completed roster and runtime behavior are sound. This is distinct from rf2-7ntc's optional drift-gate decision. Existing status, criteria, notes, close_reason and closed_at are preserved.
close_reason:
CLOSED ON PR #9602, merged as c123aa2889. Two files, +16/-3:
`spec/Security.md` and the `attr-string` docstring in `implementation/ssr/.../html_helpers.cljc`.

=== WHAT LANDED, AND ONE DELIBERATE DEPARTURE FROM THE BRIEF ===

Both sites completed from `strip-prop?`'s own (correct) docstring. `spec/Security.md` got a
non-enumerating lede **byte-identical to the one PR #9598 settled for spec/011**, so the two pages
read as one contract; the roster is complete and stated as a closed set in both directions.

**The departure, and it is a good one.** On 011 the six classes sit in one list. On a SECURITY page
listing all six under a threat-model heading OVER-CLAIMS three of them: only the first three close a
live vector, and the other three — JSX source-coords, structural slots, content channels — are wire
correctness rather than attack surface. The worker split them into two registers on that ground.
Mirroring the sibling exactly would have been the safer-looking choice and the less accurate one.

The `attr-string` docstring was completed and explicitly DEMOTED to a gloss, naming `strip-prop?`
as the single realisation point — which is the repair the bead actually wanted, since a second
enumeration in the same file was undercutting the argument for keeping the spec's in step.

=== THE SITE-B FINDING IS SHARPER THAN THE BEAD EXPECTED ===

The bead treated the in-file gloss as simply a third stale copy. Measured: it was written
2026-05-21 (`3d34b32e87`) and went short **SIX DAYS LATER**, when the JSX class landed 400 lines
above it **in the same file** (`62d5b57e75`). The 011 bullet took twelve days to drift.

**The in-file duplicate had no distance to blame.** That is the strongest available argument that
enumerating a roster anywhere but at its realisation point decays regardless of proximity, and it
is worth more than the edit it justifies.

=== THE TEST QUESTION WAS ANSWERED "BOTH", SPLIT BY CLASS ===

The bead asked whether `ssr_emit_test.clj`'s zero on the newer classes was a coverage gap or two
files owning different halves. The answer is both, and the split is the finding:

  * Classes 5-6 (structural slots, content channels) are NOT a gap — `ssr_attr_filter_test.clj`

  * **Class 4, the JSX source-coord props, has NO TEST ANYWHERE.** A case-insensitive `jsx` census

    and `62d5b57e75`'s own stat is one file, source only. Filed as **rf2-ounh**.

That is a real hole found by asking a question the bead was not sure was worth asking.

=== THE DRIFT GATE: FEASIBLE, NARROWER THAN IT LOOKS, CORRECTLY NOT BUILT ===

The worker wrote the PROBE, not the gate — the right restraint — and reported both directions:
extracting all ten literal names from the four `def ^:private` forms, it reads **RED on both spec
pages at the merge base** (011 missing 4, Security missing 6) and **GREEN on both at head**. So it
would have caught both drifts.

Against it, and this is the part that makes the report useful rather than enthusiastic:

  * whole-file matching is contaminated — 011 went red on only 4 of 6, because `:key`, `:ref` and
    `:children` occur elsewhere in that file for unrelated reasons (the same census trap the 011
    dispatch recorded);
  * it can only ever grade 4 of 6 classes: two arms of `strip-prop?` are a regex and `(fn? v)`,
    which have no literal names to extract;
  * a count invariant is **already violated by two correct documents** — merged 011 lists five
    items for six classes;
  * the gloss cannot be included without per-site config.

Filed as **rf2-7ntc** with a recommendation and explicitly not a ruling.

=== A CORRECTION TO THE MAYOR, THE THIRD OF FOUR THIS SESSION ===

`--no-filters` is the wrong hash form for `spec/Security.md`, and **it inverts INSIDE `spec/`**:
`011-SSR.md` is `i/crlf` so `--no-filters` is right there, while `Security.md` is `i/lf` where

title: spec: 011's XSS-at-output-boundaries roster is two landings behind strip-prop?
description:
FLAGGED BY THE rf2-dgyi WORKER AND DELIBERATELY NOT ABSORBED, because the file is outside that dispatch's
fence. The restraint was correct; the drift is real.

THE DRIFT. `spec/011`'s "XSS at output boundaries" section ENUMERATES the SSR attribute-stripping roster, and
it names NEITHER of the two rosters added to that filter today:

  * the STRUCTURAL SLOTS (`:key`, `:ref`) — added by rf2-gw87, PR #9593;
  * the CONTENT CHANNELS (`:children`, `:dangerouslySetInnerHTML`) — added by rf2-dgyi, PR #9596.

rf2-gw87 did not update the spec either, so this is two landings deep rather than one, and **the only record
of either roster is the `strip-prop?` docstring in
`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/html_helpers.cljc`.** For a project whose stated posture is that the
SPEC IS THE ARTEFACT and the code is downstream, a normative filter whose contents live only in an
implementation docstring is the wrong way round.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN ORDINARY DOC LAG: that section is a SECURITY boundary. A reader auditing what SSR
refuses to serialise reads the spec, finds an enumeration that looks complete, and gets an answer that is
missing four entries. An enumeration that is silently short is worse than one that admits it is partial.

THE DELIVERABLE IS SMALL AND IS PROSE: bring the spec's enumeration into step with the filter, and — since
this has now drifted twice in one day — consider whether the section should CITE the roster's home rather
than duplicate it, so the next addition cannot drift. That is a judgement, not an instruction; a spec that
defers its own enumeration to code has costs too, and this project's posture may prefer the duplication with
a pointer. Argue whichever you choose.

BEFORE EDITING, RE-DERIVE THE ROSTER FROM SOURCE rather than from this bead: read `strip-prop?` and its two
name sets (`structural-slot-names`, `content-channel-names`) at tip. This bead is a claim and the filter has
moved twice today.

CHECK WHETHER THE PROTOTYPE-POLLUTION AND JSX SOURCE-COORD ENTRIES ARE PRESENT IN THE SPEC TOO — the filter
carries `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` and the three `_jsx*` props, and if the enumeration predates
those as well, the drift is older and wider than the two landings above. Measure it; do not assume either way.

NOT HOT-ZONE, but adjacent to files that are: `spec/004B` IS hot-zone and was read-not-edited by the rf2-dgyi
worker, and `spec/Conventions.md`, `spec/API.md` and the manifest sidecars are all fenced. If the repair
needs any of those, STOP AND REPORT — a citation is not permission.

title: docs(loops): section 5 claims a head-ref forge query 'cannot be windowed' — gh pr list caps at --limit (default 30), so an empty result is not proof of absence
description:
**`docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md` section 5 (Branches) tells the reader that a forge head-ref query "cannot be windowed". For the tool this project actually uses, that is FALSE — and the error is the exact reassuring-zero failure the surrounding paragraph exists to warn about.**

The passage (around line 1518) argues, correctly, that a windowed listing filtered by you is only as wide as the listing, and therefore says:

> **So prefer an instrument that takes the identity as INPUT** — most forges accept the head reference as a query parameter, which asks the whole set at once and cannot be windowed.

`gh pr list --head <branch>` does filter server-side on the exact head ref, so it beats a client-side filter over a listing. But it is still capped: `gh pr list --help` documents `-L, --limit int  Maximum number of items to fetch (default 30)`. So the result set IS windowed, just less severely.

**Why this matters rather than being pedantry.** The paragraph's whole subject is that a zero over the wrong range reads exactly like a zero over the right one. A reader who takes "cannot be windowed" literally will treat an EMPTY result as proof that no PR ever proposed the branch — and that is the reading that authorises deleting it. Finding a matching head is positive evidence; an empty bounded list is not proof of absence.

Discovered while ruling rf2-bipw, where the instrument was exercised for real. Relevant measurement from that pass: `gh pr list --state all --head worker/epoch-a --limit 100` returns **five** PRs for one branch name (worker branch names are reused), so a default-30 window is not obviously generous once a name has history.

## The fix

Narrow the claim in that sentence. Something like: the head-ref query asks the whole set at once rather than a recent window, *but still returns at most `--limit` items (default 30), so pass an explicit limit and treat an empty result as inconclusive rather than as proof of absence.* Keep the document's existing tool-agnostic register — it has zero code fences and names no literal commands — so phrase it as a property of the instrument, not as a `gh` invocation.

## Scope

One sentence in one hot-zone-adjacent file. `docs/the-mayor-method/loops.md` is not in the hot-zone list but is high-traffic; check no other worker is editing it before dispatching.

**Gate:** `docs/the-mayor-method/**` is inside `docs_dir`, so `python -m mkdocs build --strict` covers it, and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` is the anchor/link gate. Verify prose by hand — no gate reads it.

on this repository rather than from help text alone:

  --head <branch> --limit 100  -> 5 PRs (worker branch names are reused)

  a head matching nothing      -> 0      <- the instrument reports a real absence honestly

Help text confirms the two flags are independent: `-H, --head string` and `-L, --limit int
Maximum number of items to fetch (default 30)`. So "cannot be windowed" is false, and the
bead's reasoning for why that matters is correct as written.

Keep the accurate explicit-limit/full-history warning: an at-limit result may omit older PRs for a reused branch name, so enumerate/paginate when their states or identities matter. Remove the assertion that this positive result cap itself makes an empty exact-head response a recent-window false negative. If an empty response remains inconclusive for branch deletion, ground that in actual unresolved repository/state/head identity, permissions, or independent ownership/containment evidence, not this nonexistent pagination mechanism. Preserve the tool-agnostic prose register and existing destructive-operation safeguards; no new wrapper or API. title: docs(hicasso): teach h/frame-provider as the verb for a PURE JOIN — frame-root docstring's copy-the-creator's-opts advice is a footgun
description:
Filed 2026-09-08 23:13 AUSEST out of the rf2-kuky.58 ratification (see that bead's DECISION note, correction (4)). DOCSTRING TEACHING ONLY — no behaviour change, no spec change. The D1 semantics are RATIFIED as shipped and are not reopened here.

## Problem

Ratified D1 semantics: `[h/frame-root {:id f ...}]` is a DECLARATION, not a join. Re-acquiring a live `:id` runs `make-frame` unconditionally (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/views/frame_boundary.cljs:127-128`), which REPLACES `:config` wholesale rather than merging it (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:3501,:3524`). Durable state (app-db, runtime-db, sub-cache, queue) survives and `:initial-events` are re-recorded but never replayed.

The `frame-root` docstring currently teaches the join case the wrong way round. At `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:583-585`:

> "So a joining boundary that passes DIFFERENT opts installs them; pass the creator's opts to join without changing anything."

That advice is coupling, and it is a footgun given wholesale replacement: copy the creator's opts INCOMPLETELY and you silently strip the creator's config. Measured (isolated Babashka constructor probe, exit 0, recorded on rf2-kuky.58): a bare `(rf/make-frame {:id f})` against a live frame left `:config {}` and REMOVED the prior `:fx-overrides`, while the seeded control retained `{:probe 42}` in the same verified non-nil app-db container.

For a PURE JOIN the right verb already exists and needs no opts at all: `[h/frame-provider {:frame f} ...]`. Its docstring already names "a second root on the page sharing a frame the first ensured" as one of three principal uses (`hicasso.cljc:619`) — it is simply not the FIRST thing a reader meets.

## Change

Promote `frame-provider` to the primary spelling for a pure join, and demote the copy-the-creator's-opts advice:

1. `implementation/hicasso/src/re_frame/hicasso.cljc:583-585` — replace the "pass the creator's opts" sentence with a pointer to `h/frame-provider` as the verb for joining an existing frame without re-declaring it. Keep the re-def mental model (re-declaring an id refreshes its config while its state survives) — that part is correct and is good teaching.
2. Check the shared `rf/frame-root` and `re-frame.adapter.uix/frame-root` docstrings for the same advice and make the same edit — the semantics are cross-substrate, so the teaching should be too.
3. Check `docs/core/hicasso/` guide pages and `docs/api/re-frame.hicasso.md` for the same "copy the creator's opts to join" phrasing. NOTE the guide-code-block trap: editing any fenced block under `docs/core/` reds `samples_coverage_jvm_test.clj`, which hashes each block's exact text — a guide edit is a two-file change.

## Out of scope

- Changing the D1 behaviour (create-only ENSURE). RULED against on rf2-kuky.58; it is an EP-0024 duplicate-id amendment across three substrates, not a docstring fix.
- Any warning, refresh-mode or merge-policy option on a divergent join. Rejected as nag-diagnostic on rf2-kuky.58.
- New tests. This records unchanged semantics; the existing W3 witness (`implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/frame_boundary_heads_dom_cljs_test.cljs:235-288`) already pins the behaviour being described.

## Gates

Docstring-only edits to `implementation/**` are outside `check_doc_slugs.py`'s roots — if any `README.md` or non-README markdown beside source is touched, the gate is `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` (`test.yml` job `verify-readme-links`). If a `docs/` page is touched, `mkdocs build --strict` plus `check_doc_slugs.py`. If a fenced block under `docs/core/` is touched, re-run the guide-samples JVM test.

notes:

that `re-frame.core` does not export.

FOUND 2026-09-08 by the rf2-kuky.84 residual worker, which correctly DID NOT fix it — the #9489 audit says
"the implementation behavior does not need changing for this residual", and touching implementation/ pulls
in the schemas and flows suites. It reported the finding instead of growing its scope, which is the right
call and why this is a separate bead.

THE SITES, verified at source by me on origin/main at 268a8c4de8:
  implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc:702   (read-frame-id opts 'rf/app-schemas)
  implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/storage.cljc:720   (read-frame-id opts 'rf/app-schema-meta)
  implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/digest.cljc:162    (read-frame-id opts 'rf/app-schemas-digest)
  implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:95       (read-frame-id opts 'rf/flows)
  implementation/flows/src/re_frame/flows/registry.cljc:103      (read-frame-id opts 'rf/flow-meta)

WHY IT MATTERS, and it is sharper than "a stale name in a string": these five are exactly the readers
rf2-kuky.84 reshaped to require a `{:frame f}` map. So the failure is SEQUENTIAL and it wastes the
author's next move. Call one without `:frame`, get an error naming `rf/app-schemas`, type that, and get
"no such var" — because `re-frame.core` deliberately exports none of the three schema readers
(`core.cljc:1078-1090` says so and publishes only the `reg-*` macros; the owning namespace is
`re-frame.schemas`, and the flows pair is the same shape in `re-frame.flows`). The diagnostic points at a
door that is not there.

WHAT THE FIX PROBABLY IS — a ruling is NOT needed, but a choice of spelling is: name the symbol the reader
can actually type. Either the conventional bound alias (`schemas/app-schemas`, `flows/flows`) or the fully
qualified owning namespace (`re-frame.schemas/app-schemas`). The qualified form is unambiguous and cannot

title: spec: API.md normatively teaches ':as reagent-adapter'/':as uix-adapter' while 006 teaches 'rf.adapter.*' and Conventions.md forbids the bare form — two dialects, ~20 sites, no gate sees it
description:
Two normative specs give contradictory require-alias instructions for the adapter namespaces, and `spec/Conventions.md` both FORBIDS and USES the non-canonical form. Roughly 20 sites across 5 pages. This needs a one-word ruling: standing exemption, or defect.

THE CONTRADICTION, verbatim.

`spec/API.md:246`:
    Apps targeting Reagent `:require [re-frame.adapter.reagent :as reagent-adapter]` and pass
    `reagent-adapter/adapter` to `(rf/init! ...)`.

`spec/API.md:261`:
    Apps targeting UIx `:require [re-frame.adapter.uix :as uix-adapter]` and call the surfaces directly.

`spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:2061-2062` teaches the opposite dialect for the same namespace:
    '[re-frame.adapter.reagent :as rf.adapter.reagent])
    (rf/init! rf.adapter.reagent/adapter)

Both are normative spec pages. An app author following `API.md` writes `reagent-adapter/adapter`; one following `006` writes `rf.adapter.reagent/adapter`. Both cannot be the house dialect.

MEASURED 2026-09-08 with a discriminating control (both axes non-zero, so neither figure is a false zero):
    `reagent-adapter` across spec/*.md  -> 21 hits
    `rf.adapter`      across spec/*.md  -> 38 hits

WHY NO GATE CATCHES IT. The require-alias ratchet (`scripts/check-ai-tracking-ratchet.sh`'s sibling alias ratchet) grades CODE and is genuinely at floor zero — re-verified during the rf2-gbuh dossier: 11,061 edges, 0 non-canonical, all 27 surfaces at 0. Prose is out of its scope by design. And the two link gates (`check_doc_slugs.py`, `check_readme_links.py --ci`) grade link targets and anchors, never prose content. So a normative contradiction between two spec pages is invisible to every gate in the repo.

WHY THIS IS THE PART WORTH RULING ON, when the rest of rf2-gbuh is a decline. The rf2-gbuh dossier's census found the bead's "427 bare-leaf alias references in prose" is a category error — 427 is approximately the COUNT OF TRACKED `.md` FILES UNDER `docs/` (425 today), not a hit count — and that the genuine drift class it was reaching for is EMPTY: 14 raw candidates, 0 genuine after hand-reading, with 230 of the raw hits being the English abbreviation `n/a` and 24 of 25 sampled bare-prose hits being English slash-pairs (`server/client`, `mount/unmount`). So the sweep is correctly declined. THIS contradiction is the one real defect the file-scoped instrument structurally could not see, because it is a disagreement BETWEEN pages rather than a bad token within one.

THE RULING WANTED, one word:
  (a) STANDING EXEMPTION — `API.md`'s `<thing>-adapter` form is deliberate for the app-facing quickstart (it reads better in a one-line require than `rf.adapter.reagent`), and `Conventions.md` gets a sentence recording the carve-out so nobody "fixes" it.
  (b) DEFECT — `API.md` is wrong; align its ~20 sites to `rf.adapter.*` and the contradiction closes.
RECOMMEND (b) unless there is a reason for the split I have not found: `006` is the substrate spec and the deeper authority on adapter wiring, `Conventions.md` already forbids the bare form, and two dialects for one namespace across two normative pages is exactly the drift the alias convention exists to prevent. But (a) is defensible and this is Mike's call, not an agent's.

WHOEVER ACTIONS IT: `spec/API.md` is a hot-zone file and is ONE HOLDING with the two generated `spec/api-manifest*.edn` sidecars — a public-name change moves all three together and `lint.yml`'s `api-manifest` job grades them on one surface. Aliases in prose are not public names, so this edit probably does NOT move the manifest; confirm by regenerating rather than assuming, and sequence against any other `spec/API.md` work.

DISCOVERED-FROM rf2-gbuh, whose dossier (ai/decisions/rf2-gbuh.alias-prose-references.md, local-only) carries the full two-axis census.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded ruling: standing exemption (with a Conventions.md sentence) or defect (API.md aligned to rf.adapter.*). If defect, manifest re-checked rather than assumed unchanged.

CLOSED BY A RULING THAT LANDED AFTER THE QUESTION WAS POSED, NOT BY MY PREFERENCE — and the tree was then measured against it rather than assumed to comply.

THE BEAD SET ITS OWN TEST, and I am answering it in its own words: "is the wider documentation tree a defect to sweep, or does the new Conventions paragraph ... already settle it as ACCEPTABLE? **If the paragraph settles it, this bead closes with no work.**"

**IT SETTLES IT.** The paragraph is on trunk at `spec/Conventions.md:218`, under §Require-alias dialect, ruled by rf2-gbuh and executed by rf2-z5zy (both merged). Quoted verbatim, because the operative clause is the last one:

  **not** oblige a repository-wide alias migration."

So the 35-against-15 binding count that this bead spent three notes pricing is **not a defect measure at all** under the landed rule. It measures application-local aliases in samples, which the rule expressly permits. Nothing to sweep.

**WHAT THE PARAGRAPH DOES STILL OBLIGE, I MEASURED — AND THE TREE IS ALREADY CONFORMANT.** The one surviving MUST is per-sample internal consistency: a fence that binds one alias and calls another teaches a form that does not compile. title: TESTING.md / dispatch policy: the fast-PR spine's CLJS tier is UNRUNNABLE in a worker worktree by construction
description:
Reported by worker/ssr-b (PR #9377) with a captured exit code, and it explains a cost the fleet has been paying all session.

THE FINDING. A freshly created worker worktree has NO implementation/node_modules — only the primary checkout has one. So scripts/test-fast-pr.sh reaches its CLJS node-integration tier and dies: 'compile-node-test: could not resolve shadow-cljs: Cannot find module shadow-cljs/cli/runner.js'. Everything BEFORE that tier ran green (clj-kondo errors: 0 across implementation/examples/testbeds/six tool trees, implementation/core JVM, 123 JS-harness tests, version lockstep across 19 artefacts). The spine then exits non-zero.

AND THE OBVIOUS FIX IS UNSAFE, which is what makes this structural rather than a setup omission. Linking the mayor's implementation/node_modules into the worktree is exactly the hazard CLAUDE.md and the dispatch gate block both warn about: a link into a shared dependency tree is WRITABLE THROUGH, so any gate step that runs an installer (npm ci / npm install, or any tool that reinstalls a dependency tree) rewrites the SHARED target rather than the worker's copy. That has already emptied the coordinator's real tree once. ssr-b correctly declined to link and reported the tier as unreachable instead.

SO THE SPINE CANNOT BE FULLY GREEN IN A WORKER WORKTREE, EVER, and a brief that nominates it is asking for an exit 1 that means nothing about the diff. This is now moot for new dispatches — the GATE NOMINATION POLICY added to the dispatch blocks on 2026-09-07 tells workers not to run the spine at all, and TESTING.md's own Windows-local policy already said CI (Linux) is authoritative — but nothing in the REPO records why, so the next person to nominate the spine to a worker will rediscover it.

WHAT IS WANTED, and it is small: record the constraint where a brief-writer will meet it. Either a line in TESTING.md's Local commands table beside scripts/test-fast-pr.sh saying its CLJS tier requires a checkout with implementation/node_modules and is therefore unrunnable in a linked worktree, or an explicit skip in the spine that detects the absent tree and reports the tier as SKIPPED-with-reason rather than failing the run. The second is better if cheap — a spine that exits 1 for an environmental reason trains readers to discount its exit code, which is the failure mode the gate rules exist to prevent.

ONE MORE THING WORTH RECORDING FROM THE SAME RUN, because it is the gate block's own warning observed live: ssr-b's CAPTURED exit code was 1 while its HARNESS reported exit 0 for the same run. Quote the captured number, never the harness's.
notes: Merged-PR audit #9390 (4f9f15949564170bb2ad1dd6e72b42e5f3609918): reopen this exact spine owner for the breadth of the new missing-node_modules skip. scripts/test-fast-pr.sh:1583-1613 guards the entire run_node block, so it now skips test:hicasso-invariants (:1653), whose package.json command is only check_optional_module_reachability.py and check_guide_samples.py plus their self-tests. Those scripts import only Python stdlib and read source; they do not need node_modules or invoke shadow-cljs. It also skips the standalone per-namespace isolation self-test and the JS harness tests which the original brief explicitly measured green before shadow-cljs failed. Retain checks whose prerequisites are present, and loud-skip only the compile/bundle-dependent lanes. The new assertion that test.yml's cljs job runs every skipped lane is also false for test:hicasso-lint: that job runs invariants/isolation/compile, not the lint-export fixture runner; the existing spine comment at :1666-1673 distinguishes lint.yml's export loading from this local fixture coverage.
