title: XState v6 parity review 2026-09-07: FSM semantics, microsteps and interpretation compared against 6.0.0-alpha.52 — four actionable divergences, four confirmations
description:
Comparison of re-frame2 machine semantics against XState v6 on FSM semantics, microsteps and interpretation, per Mike's 2026-09-07 request. Read against spec/005-StateMachines.md (4,638 lines) and EP-0029, with the v6 side taken from PRIMARY SOURCES ONLY (the npm registry and the xstate "next" branch changelog), never from recollection.

=== FRAME: v6 IS STILL ALPHA, AND THAT SHAPES EVERY ITEM BELOW ===
Measured 2026-09-07 from registry.npmjs.org/xstate: dist-tags are latest=5.32.6, beta=5.0.0-beta.54, alpha=6.0.0-alpha.52. The v6 line has 52 alphas and NO stable release. The changelog on the main branch tops out at 5.32.6 with no v6 entries at all; the v6 entries live on the "next" branch. So "XState v6" is a moving target, and EP-0029 C17 ("Alpha-churn exactness" — rejected) was the right call and stays right. The recommendation running through every bead below is PERIODIC RE-VALIDATION AT A CHOSEN ALPHA, not continuous tracking.

=== WHERE re-frame2 ALREADY MATCHES OR LEADS v6 — record these so nobody "fixes" them backwards ===

1. EFFECTS AS DATA. v6 alpha.22: "Pure transitions now return every effect needed to interpret actor logic in execution order", moving from direct side effects to declarative effect arrays. This is a move TOWARD re-frame2's long-standing action effect map (spec/005 §Action effect map, the {:data :fx} shape). re-frame2 got here first and should not be re-described as following v6.

2. PARALLEL SIBLING REGIONS ARE NOT RESET. v6 alpha.17: "A transition targeting a state inside one region no longer exits and resets sibling regions", and "A cross-region transition now only exits the region containing its targets. The source region and other sibling regions stay in their current states." re-frame2 ALREADY behaves this way — spec/005 line 1715: "Regions that didn't transition keep their prior value in place." So re-frame2 matched v6's corrected semantics before v6 shipped them, while its spec text still cites the SUPERSEDED v5 behaviour as its authority. That citation risk is filed separately.

3. EXACT DESCRIPTOR BEFORE WILDCARD, WITH GUARD FALLBACK. xstate 5.32.2: "When a state has both an exact event descriptor and a matching wildcard descriptor, transitions from the exact descriptor are now tried first; if all their guards fail, matching wildcard descriptor transitions are tried as fallback." re-frame2 implements exactly this, in more detail — spec/005 §Transition resolution steps 1-8, with the worked case of :mouse/down guard-false falling through to same-level :mouse/* rather than to the no-op. Note the precision point: this behaviour arrived in xstate at 5.32.2, not at v5.0, so the spec's bare "XState v5's transition-selection order" is imprecise about WHEN.

4. UNHANDLED EVENTS ARE A SILENT NO-OP. Still true in v6 and re-frame2 keeps the benign :rf.machine.event/unhandled-no-op trace on top, which xstate does not emit. Do not conflate this with v6 alpha.50's rejection of INVALID events — different mechanism, filed separately.

=== WHERE v6 HAS MOVED AND re-frame2 HAS NOT — the actionable set ===
Filed as separate beads, in descending order of how actionable they are:
  (a) [:schemas :events] is declared-but-inert while v6 wired event validation at the delivery boundary (alpha.50) and split internal-event schemas out of the public protocol (alpha.42).
  (b) :after timers are CANCELLED on restore, where v6 alpha.41 now resumes them against the original deadline; re-frame2's SSR hydration handoff is explicitly host-defined and v6 has since specified the analogous case.
  (c) spec/005's XState citations are pinned to v5 / xstate@5.32.0 and at least one now cites behaviour v6 corrected.
  (d) Final-state versus live-sibling-region conflict resolution (v6 alpha.17) needs verifying against re-frame2's finalization first-region tie-break.

=== v6 CHANGES ASSESSED AND DELIBERATELY NOT FILED ===
- alpha.20 spawn/start split (@xstate.spawn at the authored position, @xstate.start deferred to the end): re-frame2 has its own strict ordering contract at spec/005 §Spawn lifecycle — ordering, eight enumerated steps, already covering the create-then-kick sequencing EP-0029 A7 settled. No gap found; the shapes differ but the observable ordering question is answered.
- alpha.51 state-level context schemas refining rather than replacing the root: re-frame2 does not have state-level data schemas, and [:schemas :input] is deliberately REJECTED at registration (spec/005 line 528) because state input was not adopted. Downstream of EP-0029 B1, already decided.
- alpha.1 invoked/spawned actors started via deferred start action, sync failures via onError: re-frame2 has :on-error as first-class child-failure control flow (spec/005 line 2966). Covered.
- alpha.39 listeners usable inside transition functions: an artefact of XState's imperative enq API, which EP-0029 C3 rejected. Not applicable.
- alpha.23 actor source identity preserved across persist/rehydrate: re-frame2 carries :rf/machine-type plus the identity envelope across recovery (spec/005 line 63). Covered.

=== METHOD NOTE ===
The v6 side of this comparison came from two primary fetches: the npm registry document for dist-tags, and raw.githubusercontent.com/statelyai/xstate/next/packages/core/CHANGELOG.md for the alpha entries. The main-branch changelog returns NO v6 entries and would have produced a confident, wrong "v6 does not exist" reading — the branch matters. Anyone re-running this must fetch the next branch and re-read dist-tags, because both move.
acceptance_criteria: Analysis record. Its child beads are the actionable work.
close_reason: PR #9399. The four divergences were already filed as beads (rf2-1r69, rf2-ry7x, rf2-uvby, rf2-hu69) — no new bead needed for any of them. The four CONFIRMATIONS were recorded nowhere in the spec and are now written down so nobody fixes them backwards: effects-as-data (v6 alpha.22 converges toward re-frame2's {:data :fx}) added at spec/005 §Action effect map; non-resetting parallel sibling regions covered by the corrected §Transition broadcast paragraph; exact-before-wildcard and unhandled-versus-invalid already delivered by #9388 in §Transition resolution. A new §Parity re-validation subsection under Lessons from xstate consolidates all four with the named alpha (6.0.0-alpha.52), the measured dist-tags, the next-branch caveat, and the three outstanding divergences against their beads. Posture unchanged: periodic re-validation at a named alpha, EP-0029 C17 stays rejected. One new bead filed, rf2-ovhj, for a genuine behavioural gap found while checking the premise at source.

title: docs: correct Git pathspec and exit-status claims in CLAUDE.md item (f)
description:
PR #9347 adds CLAUDE.md:104 item (f), describing implementation/*/src as a machine-specific broken mid-path glob and claiming the command exits 0. Reproduced on merged commit b3a3c41537f7250a6867d58e5c849be083accad9 and with the exact no-ref command in both native argv and Git Bash: git grep -c -F defn -- "implementation/*/src" produces no output and exits 1; tools/*/src behaves the same. Adding the descendant suffix works: implementation/*/src/** matches 4107 lines across 305 files, tools/*/src/** matches 4895 across 389, both exit 0. So a mid-path wildcard itself works; the written pattern does not select descendant file paths. The new explanation would propagate a false machine diagnosis and teaches workers to expect a successful native exit where Git actually reports no match.

Correct only item (f): distinguish the nonmatching pattern from a broken wildcard, show a working descendant pattern or the existing plain-directory alternative, and report the native no-match exit as 1. If an outer counting pipeline returned 0, attribute that status to the pipeline rather than git grep. Preserve the useful known-present control and the removal of the stale list count. No runtime change or new test framework is needed. Verify the documented commands with direct exit capture, without a counting pipeline.

Evidence saved in ai/pr-audit-9347/pathspec-probe.json and pathspec-working-tree-probe.json (local audit evidence). Git documentation: https://git-scm.com/docs/gitglossary#def_pathspec and https://git-scm.com/docs/git-grep. Dedup checked all Beads: rf2-wcps owns the earlier six distinct hazards, rf2-jwlh owns the CRLF alternation problem, and rf2-kuky.8 owns the predicate migration; none owns this newly added item (f) diagnosis.
acceptance_criteria: Item (f) describes the nonmatching pathspec and native exit 1 accurately, includes a working descendant or literal-directory pattern, and retains the known-present control. Directly run the documented command and control and record their own exit codes; no unrelated changes.
notes:
--- 2026-09-07 worker pathspec-a: item (f) corrected, PR #9350 (open, ready for review) ---

MECHANISM (re-derived, not taken from the brief). A Git pathspec CONTAINING a
wildcard must match the WHOLE path; a wildcard-free pathspec is a leading-
DIRECTORY prefix. `implementation/*/src` names no complete tracked path (every
real path continues past `src`), so it matches nothing. Mid-path wildcards are
not broken. Documented Git semantics, not a property of this box.

MEASUREMENTS (this tree, git 2.53.0.windows.2, needle `defn` via `git grep -c -F`
unless noted; exit codes taken from git grep itself, no pipeline):
  implementation/*/src                 exit 1   0 files      0 hits
  implementation/*/src/*               exit 0   305 files    4107 hits
  implementation/*/src/**              exit 0   305 files    4107 hits
  implementation                       exit 0   1271 files   9480 hits
  implementation/core/src              exit 0   78 files     1286 hits
  implementation/co                    exit 1   0 files      0 hits
  implementation/core                  exit 0   313 files    2488 hits
  implementation/*.cljc                exit 0   438 files    4481 hits
  spec/*/README.md (needle `the`)      exit 0   1 file       219 hits
  tools/*/test                         exit 1   0 files      0 hits
  tools/*/test/**                      exit 0   444 files    1933 hits

Four independent things those rows establish:
  1. `implementation/*/src` vs `.../src/*` - the wildcard is not the problem;
     STOPPING AT A DIRECTORY is.
  2. `spec/*/README.md` - a mid-path wildcard that DOES end where the path ends
     works.
  3. `implementation/co` (0) vs `implementation/core` (2488) - the wildcard-free
     form is a leading-DIRECTORY match on whole components, not a string prefix.
  4. `implementation/*.cljc` matching 438 nested files - a default-magic `*`
     spans `/`, which is why appending `/*` repairs the pathspec. `:(glob)` magic
     turns that off: `:(glob)implementation/*/src/*` reads 0,
     `:(glob)implementation/*/src/**` reads 3706 across 260 files.

EXIT STATUS. `git grep -q -F 'defn' -- 'implementation/*/src'` exits 1; the
control `-- 'implementation/core/src'` exits 0. So the item's "the command exits
0, stderr is empty" was false, and the whole "nothing on screen betrays it"
argument collapsed with it.

WHERE THE 0-AND-EXIT-0 CAME FROM (the bead's own hypothesis, confirmed). Bare
`git grep -c -F 'defn' -- 'implementation/*/src'` exits 1. Through `| wc -l` it
prints `0` and exits 0. Through `| awk -F: '{s+=$NF} END{print s+0}'` it prints
`0` and exits 0. Through `| grep -c .` it prints `0` and exits 1. The same
`| wc -l` pipeline over the control `implementation/core/src` prints 78. So the
census wrapper manufactured both the number and the status.

NOT MACHINE-SPECIFIC. Every row reproduces identically from Git Bash and from
native PowerShell argv (no MSYS in the path), so neither the shell nor MSYS path
conversion is involved. Independent in-repo corroboration: this repo's own
`scripts/check_readme_links.py`, in `_git_ls_files`, documents "git pathspecs are
fnmatch WITHOUT FNM_PATHNAME, so `*` crosses `/`".

WHAT WAS KEPT. The reason the item exists is true and survives verbatim in
substance: a pathspec that LOOKS careful can read zero where a plain-directory
pathspec over the same tree reads thousands, and on a deletion or retired-
spelling census that zero reads as "the work is done". rf2-kuky.8's `-- tools/*/test`
is exactly this shape (it reads 0; `tools/*/test/**` reads 1933). The control
discipline is kept with its exit-status half sharpened: run the search once
against something it SHOULD find, and read the RUNNER's own exit status rather
than a pipeline's. The bullet's opening sentence and letters (a)-(e) are
untouched; no renumbering. The only collateral edit is inside (f): the "Same
class through a different door" half lost the clause "and this half is not
machine-specific", which no longer distinguishes the two halves now that neither
is.

SIZE. Item (f)'s first half is 1514 characters against the 1263 it replaces.
Whole PR is 1 file, 1 line, 1 insertion / 1 deletion.

GATES (foreground, exit captured on the same command line as the redirect):
  python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci                 0   <- the gate for repo-root markdown
  python scripts/check_doc_slugs.py                         0   (regression cover only)
  python -m mkdocs build --strict                           0
  sh scripts/check-commit-attribution.sh origin/main        0
  python scripts/check_retired_composition_vocab.py         0   (roster includes CLAUDE.md)
  python scripts/check_retired_spellings.py                 0
  sh scripts/check-no-hardcoded-paths.sh                    0
  sh scripts/check-ai-tracking-ratchet.sh                   0
  sh scripts/check-beads-pr-boundary.sh origin/main         0
Gate discrimination proved: with a broken link appended to CLAUDE.md,
check_readme_links.py --ci went to exit 1 naming CLAUDE.md:143. Plant reverted and
restore verified by blob hash equality, not by reading a diff.

INSTRUMENT NOTE worth carrying forward, met while measuring this bead: a probe
loop whose stderr redirect targeted an unset variable ($TMPDIR, empty here) died
on `/err.txt: Permission denied` and reported exit=1 / total=0 for EVERY pathspec
- including the plain-directory control that should have read 9480. The control
is what caught it. Same class as (f) itself: the failure was in the wrapper, not
in git.
close_reason: PR #9350 merged to main as c5e4e17e1a (verified: git rev-parse HEAD == origin/main). CLAUDE.md item (f) now states the correct Git pathspec semantics (a wildcard-bearing pathspec must match the whole path; wildcard-free is a leading-directory prefix), reports git grep's own exit 1 on no-match, and attributes the 0-and-exit-0 to the counting pipeline rather than to the machine.

title: uix adapter README's imperative-effect recipe still shows (.-current ref) — the source the trunk-red transcription copied
description:
FOUND 2026-09-05 by the uixlint-a worker while landing rf2-8crk (PR #9293), the P1 trunk-red. Reported as real work outside its fence and deliberately not done there.

THE SITE: implementation/adapters/uix/README.md:61 carries `(.-current ref)` inside the canonical imperative-effect recipe — the SAME expression, in the SAME shape, that rf2-8crk just fixed at implementation/adapters/uix/test/re_frame/adapter/uix_effect_frame_deps_dom_cljs_test.cljs:120 and :139.

WHY IT MATTERS DESPITE REDDING NOTHING. Markdown is never compiled, so no gate touches it and it will sit there indefinitely. But it is the SOURCE THE NEXT TRANSCRIPTION COPIES: rf2-8crk's own trunk-red arrived exactly that way — commit 570d07d286 added a 251-line test transcribing this recipe, and the two `.-current` reads came with it, redding the zero-warning compile gate for EVERY CLJS diff in the repo until the fix landed. Leaving the README as-is means the next person who follows the documented recipe re-creates the same repo-wide red.

THE FIX IS THE IDIOM, AND ITS EQUIVALENCE IS ESTABLISHED AT SOURCE rather than assumed — the rf2-8crk worker read com.pitch/uix.core 1.4.4's uix/core.cljs and found `use-ref` returns `(specify! #js {:current value} IDeref (-deref [this] (.-current this)) ...)`. So `-deref` IS `(.-current this)`: same property, same object, no coercion. That object is also what `($ :div {:ref ref})` hands React, so React writes the DOM node into the very `.current` both forms read. `@ref` and `(.-current ref)` are therefore interchangeable AT THESE SITES, and the linter's preference is idiom rather than correctness.

SO THIS IS A ONE-EXPRESSION PROSE FIX, and its value is preventing a recurrence rather than fixing a defect. Change the recipe to `@ref` and, if the surrounding prose explains the ref read, make the explanation match. Nothing else.

CHECK BEFORE ACTING — these are the worker's claims and mine, not findings:
- Re-derive the line number; :61 was measured before #9293 merged.
- Confirm the expression is inside the recipe rather than in a passage deliberately contrasting the two forms. If the README is teaching the interop read on purpose, the right answer may be to keep it and ADD the linter's preference — say so rather than silently rewriting a deliberate contrast.
- Run the census on all three axes (line-oriented, whitespace-collapsed, comment-markers-stripped-then-collapsed) with a control sharing the target's shape. The rf2-8crk census found 3 `.-current` under the UIx adapter — the two fixed sites plus this README — and 18 more repo-wide, none flagged. Confirm that at tip: if another README or doc under a DIFFERENT adapter carries the same recipe, it has the same problem and belongs in this bead.

WHY THE LINTER DOES NOT CATCH THE OTHER 18, established by the same worker and worth not re-deriving: `interop-ref-read?` requires the target's LOCAL BINDING INIT FORM to be a `use-ref` call, and `lint-body!` is reached only via `uix.linter/lint!`, which `uix.core` calls from `defui` / `uix.core/fn` alone. So the gate is scoped to UIx component bodies by construction — it is not inconsistent, and no ratchet needs adjusting.

FENCE. IN: `implementation/adapters/uix/README.md`, plus any sibling adapter README the census proves carries the identical recipe.
OUT: `implementation/adapters/uix/test/**` (rf2-8crk owns the test fix), `implementation/scripts/compile-node-test.cjs` and every linter or gate configuration (the gate is correct — it caught a real idiom violation within hours), and all of `spec/`.

GATE: `python scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` is the gate for a README beside source — NOT `check_doc_slugs.py`, whose roots exclude it, so nominating that one returns a green that inspected nothing. Neither reads inside a fenced code block, and this edit is almost certainly INSIDE a fence, so BOTH are blind to it: check any link or anchor in the block by hand and say so. The real verification here is reading the recipe against uix.core's `use-ref` and confirming the replacement compiles in the adapter's own testbed.
notes:
2026-09-05 — PR #9303 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9303), branch worker/uixdoc-a, left in_progress.

PREMISE HELD. Line number re-derived at tip: still :61 (the file is 87 lines; #9293 touches only test/, so the README did not move).

JUDGEMENT CALL — RECIPE, not a deliberate contrast. Decided on three grounds: (1) the README mentions @ref / deref / the atom-like nature of use-ref NOWHERE, and a contrast needs both forms present — repo-wide, @ref appears in ZERO markdown files; (2) the '4 things matter' list under the block teaches four points (frame api via hook, mandatory cleanup, deps vector, no use-subscribe in the effect body), none about the ref read, so the read is incidental mechanism; (3) it was in fact transcribed verbatim into a test, which is what a recipe is for. Fixed to @ref plus ONE clause of inline comment in the block's own existing trailing-;; idiom (lines 58 and 66 already carry such comments) so the next reader does not revert it — flagged in the PR as one line beyond the bead's 'nothing else', trim if unwanted.

EQUIVALENCE RE-VERIFIED AT SOURCE from the pinned jar (com.pitch/uix.core 1.4.4, uix/core.cljs:104-131), not taken on the bead's word: use-ref returns the specify!'d #js {:current value} object itself and its IDeref -deref IS (.-current this). Same property, same object, no coercion; that object is also what ($ :div {:ref ref}) hands React. uix/linter.clj:283's own error message names the wanted spelling: 'use @ instead of .-current'. title: ssr html-helpers: presence attributes with a non-boolean value emit name="value" where react-dom emits name=""
description:
Filed by the mayor 2026-09-05 from an observation the rf2-owml worker made, verified, and deliberately did NOT act on because `implementation/ssr/**` was outside its fence. It filed nothing and said "your call". This bead is that call being put where it will not be lost.

THE OBSERVATION. `re-frame.ssr.html-helpers` takes a different branch entirely for a NON-BOOLEAN value on a presence attribute: it emits `name="value"` with no collapse, so `{:disabled "yes"}` renders `disabled="yes"`, where react-dom renders `disabled=""`. The reagent-slim serializer, after PR #9244, collapses both spellings on the EMPTY VALUE and matches react-dom.

WHY THIS IS A QUESTION AND NOT YET A DEFECT — and this is the part to settle before writing any code. It depends entirely on WHICH CONTRACT that serializer is held to:
  * If `re-frame.ssr.html-helpers` is held to REACT-DOM BYTE-PARITY, this is a divergence and should be fixed the way #9244 fixed the slim path.
  * If it is held to the SPEC 004B CONTRACT, it may be correct as written. IMPL-SPEC already records that 004B is DELIBERATELY different from react-dom for `value`, so a deliberate difference here would have precedent rather than being an oversight.
**Establish which, from the spec and from IMPL-SPEC, before touching the code.** A worker that assumes byte-parity and "fixes" a deliberate difference has broken a contract to satisfy a comparison nobody asked for.

WHY IT MATTERS IF IT IS A DIVERGENCE, and this is the argument for P3 rather than P4: `reagent2.dom.client/hydrate-root` hydrates server-rendered markup, and `spec/011` records that React does NOT guarantee to patch an attribute-only hydration mismatch. So a server emitting `disabled="yes"` against a client expecting `disabled=""` is exactly the class that survives into production silently. That is the same mechanism the whole #9207/#9224 line of work has been closing.

THE PROBE THAT SETTLES THE FACTS, already run once on the slim side and worth repeating here: probe react-dom 19.2.0 directly for all 28 presence names with the values `""`, `0`, `"0"`, `"yes"` and `true`. The rf2-owml worker measured 28/28 with zero anomalies on the slim path — react-dom OMITS on `""` and `0` and EMITS on `"yes"` and `true` — and pinned the asymmetry that invites a second bug: the STRING `"0"` is truthy, only the NUMBER `0` is not.

A CAUTION FROM THE SAME WORK, because it nearly caused damage. The slim test's own docstring claimed React 19 emits the bare short form and only React 18 emits `disabled=""`. **That was false** — probing react-dom 19.2.0 showed it emits `disabled=""`, which made the canonicalisation load-bearing rather than vestigial. **Do not trust a docstring's claim about React's output; probe the installed react-dom.** A tempting "just delete the special case" reading would have reddened the suite.

SEQUENCING: `implementation/ssr/**` is not hot zone, but check it is free — it has taken merges recently (#9215, and #9207 before it).
notes:
--- worker ssrhelp-a, PR #9267 ---
THE CONTRACT QUESTION IS SETTLED, AND NOT BY PREFERENCE. 004B §Booleans and
their neighbours already RULES this case, in its `hidden` row: a boolean
attribute is "a pure boolean attr, not an enumerated exception: true /
'until-found' / ANY TRUTHY -> bare presence", and the pre-probe draft's

`identical?`, `NaN === NaN` is false), which is what made it look
cross-platform: right on one runtime, inert on the other, and the JVM is the
runtime that renders server-side.

hosts, and self-describing. `==` also discriminates correctly (Numbers/equiv
takes no identity shortcut) but has to be decoded before it reads as a NaN test.

title: hygiene: 111 remote worker/* branches, none deletable under the two-clause rule (needs an operator call)
description:
Filed by the mayor 2026-09-05 during a hygiene tick. This needs a decision, not work.

THE STATE. `git ls-remote --heads origin 'worker/*'` returns 111 branches. The hygiene rule deletes a branch only when BOTH clauses hold: `git cherry origin/main <branch>` reads all `-` (every commit has an equivalent in main) AND the PR state reads MERGED via `gh pr view`. Applying both, **0 of 111 qualify.**

WHY ZERO. 104 of them satisfy the FIRST clause cleanly — cherry reads all `-`, so their work is demonstrably in main and deleting them would lose nothing. But `gh pr list --head <branch>` returns NOTHING for every one of those: `pr=none`. And "none" is not "MERGED", so the second clause refuses them all. They are almost entirely a single campaign from 2026-09-03 (`worker/naming-*` and `worker/codex-naming-*`), which appears to have landed without per-branch PRs.

SEVEN HOLD COMMITS NOT IN MAIN and are keeps regardless of any ruling: worker/liveframe-ma8r (2, PR CLOSED — abandoned but unique), worker/receipts-hic081 (3), worker/retire-delete (1), worker/naming-tools-story-20260903 (1), worker/naming-tools-story-20260903-r1 (1), plus the two live ones with open PRs.

THE QUESTION FOR MIKE, and it is genuinely his: should the second clause admit "no PR ever existed" as equivalent to MERGED when the first clause already proves the work is in main? The first clause is the one carrying the safety property — cherry comparing patch-ids is what makes deletion lossless. The PR check is a second, independent confirmation, and it is the one that cannot be satisfied for a campaign that did not use PRs.

THREE OPTIONS.
  (a) Leave the rule as written and let these accumulate. Cost: 111 remote refs and ~110 local, growing; every `git ls-remote` and branch listing is noisy; but nothing is ever lost.
  (b) Amend the rule to: cherry all `-` AND (PR MERGED **or** no PR has ever existed for the branch). Deletes ~104 immediately. The safety argument is that cherry alone is sufficient — a branch whose every commit has a patch-equivalent in main holds nothing unique by construction.
  (c) One-off sweep of the 2026-09-03 naming campaign only, leaving the rule untouched, on the ground that this was a single unusual event rather than a pattern.

MY RECOMMENDATION IS (b), with the rule change recorded in the method doc rather than applied ad hoc — because (c) leaves the same situation to recur unrecognised, and (a) is a slow accumulation with no end state. But this is a destructive-operation policy and the mayor should not widen its own deletion authority; hence the bead rather than an action.

DO NOT ACT ON THIS WITHOUT MIKE'S RULING. Deleting a remote branch is irreversible from this side, and the whole reason the two-clause rule exists is that a merged-PR proxy once nearly authorised destroying a live worker's tree.

ALSO DONE THIS TICK, needing no decision: `git remote prune origin` removed 20 stale remote-tracking refs (132 -> 112). That is safe and unrelated — it only drops local refs for branches already gone from the remote.

Guessing that the two-out-of-three reading is right — that `h/as-component`
needs *a frame above it*, not *a Hicasso root above it* — and proceeding on
that guess. It turned out correct (the ported screens render and dispatch under
the app's existing `:rf/default` frame). Logging it because a guess that works
leaves no other trace: the phrase "outside a Hicasso root" is the one a reader
migrating from Reagent will hit first, and it points away from the thing that
works.

**Bead**

`09-interop.md` should say "outside every frame" — the wording
`api-reference.md` already uses for `n/use-frame` / `n/use-sub` — rather than
"outside a Hicasso root".
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9149. Settled at source, and the bead's claim was right: api-reference.md's 'outside every frame' is the true wording. as-component's boundary shell reads re-frame.adapter.context/frame-context — one defonce'd createContext that h/mount!'s provider, rf/frame-provider and rf/frame-root ALL write (the Reagent adapter aliases it rather than minting its own) — and resolve-frame! refuses only when that context holds nil or the no-provider sentinel. So the requirement is any frame from any React-shaped adapter, not a Hicasso root. A committed test already proves it: foreign_root_bridge_dom_cljs_test.cljs drives :crossed/reagent-as-component (Reagent root, rf/frame-provider above, bridge inside, no Hicasso root) and asserts a write repaints. 09-interop.md was the sole outlier against four pages that already said it correctly; it now says 'outside every frame' and names the three doors. The same wrong wording survives in codec.cljs's own docstring (implementation was read-only for this task) — filed as rf2-ip7a.

title: Epoch capture/back-fill: name reducer state and attribution roles explicitly
description:

title: Clarify SSR Ring Node renderer transport stages
description:
## Finding

The JVM-to-Node adapter's private transport implementation uses names that obscure distinct stages and overload frame terminology: where, deadline-status, defaults, opt/got/v, wire, header, exchange!, answer!, req/resp, and a local frame that is actually a parsed sidecar error payload. ## Risks / contracts

title: Call the transition cascade model geometry, not paths
description:

title: reagent-slim template: clarify prop conversion, key lookup, and shared interop path
description:
## Finding

The private Hiccup/React conversion pipeline in `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/impl/template.cljs` obscures three important distinctions with abbreviated or misleading names: nested versus top-level prop mutation (`kv-conv`/`top-prop-conv`), the already-located key rule versus argv key lookup (`react-key`/`get-react-key`), and the shared DOM-plus-`:>` path named `native-element` even though the source explicitly says it handles foreign React components too.

## Evidence and ambiguity cost

- Lines 490-548 show both `*-conv` helpers mutate a JS accumulator with `aset`; only their long docstrings reveal nested-map versus target-aware top-level behavior, and neither name signals mutation.
- Lines 740-789 distinguish a rule receiving an already-located props slot from a finder that searches argv, but `react-key` and `get-react-key` do not communicate that distinction.
- Lines 988-996 name the value tested by `props-slot?` `head`, then immediately warn in prose that it is a slot value, not a vector head.
- Lines 998-1033 state `native-element` is the path for both native DOM tags and `:>` interop; lines 1148-1158 create a synthetic tag for the foreign component and call it. The current name therefore makes the interop call look categorically wrong.
- `dont-camel-case` and `capitalize` at lines 358-381 omit that the values are prop-name prefixes/segments.
- Exact searches find no external Var consumers because these candidates are private. The remaining matches are comments/spec text, tests, or independent benchmark-local functions. History shows `native-element` began as a DOM path and later accumulated interop responsibilities, explaining the drift.

## Recommendation

Use `add-converted-nested-prop!`, `add-converted-top-level-prop!`, `react-key-from-meta-or-props`, `react-key-from-argv`, `converted-props-element`, `verbatim-prop-prefixes`, and `capitalize-prop-segment`; rename `head` to `slot-value`, `native?` to `dom-element?`, and `synth-*` locals to `synthetic-*`. Update every in-slice source/test/doc reference.

## Contracts and risk

Preserve public template Vars, Hiccup sentinel heads, dynamic vars, metadata/prop keys, React element/props shapes, cache objects, mutation and lookup order, source-coordinate consumption, and hot-path allocation behavior. Do not rename namespaces/files or add compatibility wrappers. Do not change the callable-prop branches/tests owned by `rf2-6r9j.30`.

## Duplicate search

All-status bead data was searched for each old name plus template/interop naming concepts. No bead owns this naming cluster; `rf2-6r9j.30` is a separate test-validity/correctness task and remains untouched.
acceptance_criteria:
- The proposed private/local names replace their ambiguous predecessors in template source and all directly referencing reagent-slim comments/tests/docs.
- Exact old-name searches over `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim` are empty, apart from any explicitly retained historical quotation that is justified in the bead close notes.
- Nested versus top-level prop conversion, DOM versus interop target awareness, meta-over-props key precedence, source-coordinate stamping, and React output remain behaviorally identical.
- The callable-prop behavior/tests owned by `rf2-6r9j.30`, public Vars, keys, metadata, and interop heads are unchanged.
- Focused template tests plus lint/compile checks pass, and `git diff --check` is clean.

Branch order, hot-path shapes, reserved-key filtering, public convert-prop-value/props-slot?/vec-to-elem names, emitted keys, and React interop fields are unchanged. Final focused CLJS suite compiled with 0 warnings and passed 401 tests / 1045 assertions; exact search and diff-check pass.

title: Retire the drifted tools-root Shadow build mirror
description:
## Finding

`tools/shadow-cljs.edn` is an ungated, handwritten duplicate that still claims to mirror the tool tier's per-tool CLJS builds but has not followed that tier's evolution. It exposes only namespaced copies of Pair MCP's `server` and `server-test` builds.

## Evidence

- `tools/shadow-cljs.edn` was introduced 2026-05-15 and its last change was the 2026-05-24 Causa/Xray rename. Its comments still say Pair MCP is the only tool with a Shadow surface and call mcp-base JVM-only.
- `tools/mcp-base/shadow-cljs.edn` has provided a canonical `cljs-test` build since 2026-05-21.
- Pair MCP added the build-time `descriptor-gen` build on 2026-06-01; its descriptor check is CI-enforced, but the root mirror never added the build. A bounded probe from `tools/`, `clojure -M -m shadow.cljs.devtools.cli compile re-frame2-pair-mcp/descriptor-gen`, exits 1 with known builds only `re-frame2-pair-mcp/server` and `re-frame2-pair-mcp/server-test` (plus Shadow's implicit `npm`).
- `tools/machines-viz/shadow-cljs.edn` added its owned `machines-viz-node-test` lane on 2026-07-26. It requires a per-tool `:cljs-test` alias and JS package path, another evolution absent from the root mirror.
- Exact searches find no workflow, package script, gate, or documentation outside the root README invoking either namespaced root build ID. CI and npm scripts invoke each tool's adjacent canonical config. `implementation/scripts/_changed-surfaces.test.cjs` records the root Shadow coordinator as having no CI consumer.
- All-status `bd search` by `tools shadow coordinator`, `root shadow mirror`, `descriptor-gen shadow`, `re-frame2-pair-mcp/descriptor-gen`, `tools/shadow-cljs.edn`, and `rf2-nuuk3`, plus direct tracker search, found no existing bead owning this outcome.

## Impact

The advertised alternate root build surface is incomplete and silently drifts while the per-tool configurations are the only exercised authority. A contributor can reasonably expect a root mirror to expose the descriptor generator or newer CLJS lanes and receive a build-not-found error. The duplicate Pair server definitions also create a future second place for release-affecting compiler options to diverge.

## Recommendation

Delete `tools/shadow-cljs.edn` and the root README's mirrored-build promise; direct all builds to the per-tool configs that their package scripts and CI already exercise. Then remove any `tools/deps.edn` base dependencies that existed only to feed this mirror, subject to the separate JVM-aggregate decision. If a root Shadow entry point is intentionally retained, narrow and name its contract honestly, generate/validate its inventory against every canonical per-tool config, include Pair's descriptor build, and add a real consumer that makes drift red.

## Risks / contracts

Preserve Pair's output paths/npm `bin`, production closure define, test reporter, descriptor-manifest gate, mcp-base's optional-validation CLJS lane, and machines-viz's isolated alias/npm resolution. Do not merge their incompatible classpath options into a nominal aggregate without proving each build under its own required lane.
acceptance_criteria:
- There is one exercised authority for each tool Shadow build; no ungated handwritten root copy can drift from Pair MCP, mcp-base, or machines-viz.
- Root documentation no longer claims that `tools/shadow-cljs.edn` mirrors all per-tool CLJS builds unless an automated inventory/parity test proves it.
- Pair's server, server-test, and descriptor-gen commands still work through the canonical config, including identical production compiler options and output locations.
- mcp-base and machines-viz retain their per-tool alias and JS-resolution semantics.
- If the root coordinator is retained, the previously failing root descriptor-gen probe succeeds, new per-tool build additions make a negative-control parity test fail, and the root surface gains a real CI/package consumer; otherwise root-only build IDs and stale docs are removed.
- Changed-surface classification is updated to match the resulting live/retired root surface.
close_reason: PR #9093: tools/shadow-cljs.edn deleted and tools/README.md's mirrored-build promise removed. Proved unconsumed with two independent instruments plus a control that fired: a fixed-string census (git grep -F, .beads excluded) found re-frame2-pair-mcp/server only in the file itself and one README sentence, zero hits under .github/, while the same census for the live build id machines-viz-viewer returned workflow steps, an npm script and pinned assertions; and _changed-surfaces.test.cjs's tools declared-hole entry already MEASURED that no workflow runs from tools/ and that CI compiles pair-mcp from its own shadow-cljs.edn. Execution: clojure -Spath exits 0 from tools/ and tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/ after the deletion, and the per-tool config is byte-identical to main with server/server-test/descriptor-gen, same closure-defines, same out/server.js. Post-change census finds no namespaced root build id anywhere. The changed-surface tools note is updated to the three files now under tools/ (last acceptance criterion); the classifier itself is untouched and its self-test still passes 335.

title: Epoch: retire the superseded reserve-only delayed-silence helpers
description:
Evidence
- implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc:1238-1265 defines claim-delayed-silence!, a reserve-only operation. Its own contract says it emits an unqualified signal, leaves a claim-to-emit race, and remains only for staged tests or hypothetical callers that cannot race registry mutation.
- state.cljc:1377-1388 defines the matching rollback-delayed-silence!. Exact repository search finds both functions called only from epoch tests; there is no production, tool, example, skill, specification, or API consumer.
- The live destroy path at implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/listeners.cljc:478-507 calls claim-and-publish-delayed-silence! instead. That current helper uses the same private eligible-and-reserve! primitive and implements compare-and-prune rollback in its exception path at state.cljc:1355-1375.
- Commit e9475426bf moved production publication to claim-and-publish-delayed-silence! so the generation-qualified emit runs outside ledger locks and avoids the ledger-to-drain-lock deadlock. The older reserve/rollback pair remained as a test seam, not a runtime path.
- Existing direct users are tests at epoch_silencing_lineage_285_test.clj:235-246,344, epoch_cljs_test.cljs:719, and docstring assertions in epoch_silence_contract_test.clj:170-189.

Impact
The shipped source exposes two operations for delayed-silence claiming although only the integrated generation-qualified operation is safe on the live concurrent path. The test-only pair duplicates rollback protocol, preserves an incomplete unqualified-call workflow, and can invite a future caller onto the known race-prone seam.

Proposed disposition
Remove claim-delayed-silence! and rollback-delayed-silence! while retaining eligible-and-reserve! as the private shared implementation and claim-and-publish-delayed-silence! as the sole live operation. Rewrite staged tests through integrated behavior or a test-local/private seam, and update source comments/docstring ratchets that describe the retired pair.

Risks
The helper pair currently makes reservation ordering and compare-and-prune behavior easy to test and seeds marks in CLJ/CLJS reset tests. Preserve equivalent behavioral coverage: one winner, failed publication permits retry, a stale rollback cannot remove a fresher mark, and reset/cleanup boundedness. Do not move external publish under either ledger lock or remove observed-gen qualification.
acceptance_criteria:
1. No executable or documented reference to claim-delayed-silence! or rollback-delayed-silence! remains.
2. claim-and-publish-delayed-silence! remains the sole delayed-silence entry and still reserves under both ledger locks, publishes outside them, carries observed-gen at the caller, and compare-prunes only its own failed reservation.

title: Remove unreachable walk-schema? branch from schemas validation
description:
## Finding

The private `run-validation` helper in `implementation/schemas/src/re_frame/schemas/validate.cljc` still accepts a `walk-schema?` boolean and guards both schema sensitivity/opacity inspection and `:large?` inspection with it, but every surviving production caller passes the literal `true`. The false branch is unreachable residue from a retired validation topology.

## Evidence

- `run-validation` declares `[reg-meta value walk-schema? build-base-tags continue?]` (currently line 454).
- Its only reads are the guards around `walker/schema-has-sensitive?` / `schema-has-opaque-child?` (currently lines 544-546) and `walker/schema-has-large?` (currently lines 553-555).
- Repository caller census finds exactly three source calls: `validate-event!`, `validate-sub!`, and `validate-fx!` (currently lines 921, 957, and 1003). Each passes literal `true`; there is no dynamic caller and `run-validation` is private.
- History establishes why the knob existed and why it no longer does. Commit `f899bdd8e4` introduced it as `false` for event validation and `true` for cofx/fx/sub. Commit `14a91d956f` changed event validation to `true` so event payload schemas could drive fail-closed sensitive redaction. Injection-time cofx validation was subsequently retired (`99d37fa6bf`, `f56f5495e7`). The three remaining callers are therefore all on the walking arm.
- All-status bead title and description searches for `walk-schema`, `run-validation walk`, and the validate helper/path found no issue owning this residue.

## Impact

The parameter and two conditional branches advertise a per-surface privacy/size policy choice that no caller can make. That obscures the current invariant: every meta-bearing validation failure consults its schema for sensitivity, opaque children, and large-value elision. A future caller could accidentally pass false and bypass fail-closed diagnostic protection even though no supported contract needs that posture.

## Proposed disposition

Remove `walk-schema?` from the private helper's parameter vector and from all three calls. Make the existing sensitivity/opacity and large-schema walks unconditional within the already-failing branch, preserving sensitive-wins-over-large ordering and all existing redaction markers/tags.

## Risks

This is privacy-sensitive code. Do not move either walk onto the successful hot path, weaken opaque-schema fail-closed handling, change the whole-payload versus leaf-scoped decisions, or disturb the outer `interop/debug-enabled?` gates required for production DCE. Keep the edit mechanical and behavior-neutral for every reachable call.
acceptance_criteria:
- `run-validation` no longer declares or documents `walk-schema?`, and its three callers no longer pass a boolean in that slot.
- A source census shows no `walk-schema?` occurrence and exactly the same three private-helper callers.
- Event, fx, and sub-return tests prove sensitive schema slots and nested opaque children still redact failure payloads; non-sensitive failures remain verbatim.
- Large-schema tests prove non-sensitive values still use `:rf.size/large-elided`, while sensitivity continues to win over large classification.
- Schemas JVM and CLJS suites pass, including stale-incarnation checkpoints.
- The schemas production bundle/elision gate remains green and confirms the dev-only validation body is not newly retained under `:advanced` plus `goog.DEBUG=false`.
close_reason: PR #9113 (head 6711fbafe1). Removed walk-schema? from run-validation's parameter vector and from all three callers (validate-event!/sub!/fx!), which each passed the literal true; both the sensitivity/opacity walk and the :large? walk are now unconditional inside the already-failing branch. Sensitive-wins-over-large ordering, fail-closed opaque handling, whole-payload decision scope, redaction markers and the outer interop/debug-enabled? gates are unchanged. Unreachability proven by execution probe, not census alone: a marker in the false direction fired 0 times across the schemas JVM suite while the same marker in the live true arm fired 50. The parameter bullet's substance was folded into the fn's opening prose rather than deleted. Schemas JVM suite exit 0 (373 tests / 19223 assertions); clj-kondo exit 0, errors 0, and identical findings on the HEAD and changed versions of the file. One walk-schema? token survives repo-wide: a dated past-tense comment at schemas_sensitive_test.clj:1118 recording the rf2-a5kzs fix, which is accurate history in a file rf2-6r9j.55 owns, deliberately left alone.

title: Remove redaction helper pair superseded by collect-redaction-paths
description:

Why this is vestigial
The old half-walk and its private predicate are a superseded implementation path. They duplicate the fused collector's logic and leave misleading reachability documentation around privacy plumbing.

Risks / constraints
Privacy behavior is security-sensitive. This cleanup must not change path collection order/deduplication, the handler's raw event, pre-chain trace projection, schema/classification overlap, or egress redaction. Treat `schema-redaction-paths`' explicit compatibility retention as authoritative.

So this is internal plumbing, not a public-surface change. Retained and verified resolving: schema-redaction-paths, redact-interceptor, redact-interceptor-id, collect-redaction-paths. title: pilots briefs + friction-log.md instruct outcome 7 by moving the checkout pin, which rf2-hic-063's 2026-09-02 ruling forbids for the rehearsal
description:
FOUND 2026-09-03 02:55 AUSEST by the rf2-t4jpz PRE-PILOT rehearsal. Tip d1e6a707a3.

THE CONTRADICTION. rf2-hic-063's RULING of 2026-09-02, clause (iii), fixes the rehearsal's method and says outcome 7 is 'recorded BLOCKED' — and its GATES AND TRAPS item 7 is explicit: 'the rehearsal's pinned commit goes in the log header and is not moved mid-pilot; outcome 7 is BLOCKED, not simulated.' rf2-t4jpz's own description repeats it: 'Outcome 7 (upgrade across the RC) is recorded BLOCKED — there is no second published pin — and is not simulated with a git pin move.'

The pilot-facing material, delivered earlier under rf2-v04s, says the opposite and is handed to the agent unmodified:

- brief-realworld.md and brief-linearlite.md, outcome 7: 'Move the version pin and upgrade across it. Your setup pins the library to one commit; record it, then move it to a later one at the end and record what the move cost.'
- friction-log.md, Part 1 rules: 'Outcome 7 needs two pins, and moving the checkout pin is what stands in for an upgrade until a release coordinate exists.'
- friction-log.md's blank template ends with an attestation asking for 'Checkout pin at start' and 'Checkout pin at end', which presupposes the move.

A pilot handed these does exactly what the brief says, moves the pin, and returns an outcome-7 verdict the ruling says must read BLOCKED. The operator then either accepts evidence the ruling excluded or discards work the brief demanded.

WHY IT IS NOT JUST A LABEL. The ruling's reason is substantive: 'UPGRADE on a checkout is moving a git pin, not moving a version across an RC', which is one of the three verbs that makes :local/root fail as §13 adoption proof. A simulated pin move produces a row that LOOKS like upgrade evidence, and the counted run is later read against the rehearsal's dispositioned log. That is the reading the ruling closes.

SCOPE. The briefs and friction-log.md are correct as written for the COUNTED run on a published artefact, where two pins genuinely exist. What is missing is the rehearsal's own override. The cleanest fix is not to edit the briefs' outcome 7 — the ruling wants them untouched for the counted run — but to have the rehearsal's dispatch carry the override explicitly, and to head the copied FRICTION-LOG.md with outcome 7 pre-marked BLOCKED so the pilot cannot spend effort on it.

NOTE ON CUSTODY. pilots/ has a custody rule ('a substantive amendment to any page here names its authorizing bead at the site') and rf2-hic-063's ruling says rf2-v04s is NOT reopened. So whoever fixes this names its authority at the site.

FILED, NOT FIXED.
notes:
MAYOR RULING 2026-09-03 03:5x AUSEST. THE COUNTED-RUN INSTRUCTION IS CORRECT AND STAYS. THE REHEARSAL VERSION MUST READ BLOCKED. Do not resolve this by deleting either one.

The bead has this exactly right and its own SCOPE paragraph names the shape: the briefs and friction-log.md are correct AS WRITTEN for the counted run on a published artefact, where two pins genuinely exist. What is missing is that the rehearsal is running on :local/root where they do not, and the pilot-facing material is handed over unmodified.

SO THE FIX IS CONDITIONAL MATERIAL, NOT A CORRECTION. Outcome 7 on a checkout is BLOCKED and is not simulated by moving a git pin. The reason is substantive and rf2-hic-063 states it: "UPGRADE on a checkout is moving a git pin, not moving a version across an RC" is one of the three verbs that makes :local/root fail as section 13 adoption proof. A simulated pin move produces a row that LOOKS like upgrade evidence, and the counted run is later read against the rehearsal dispositioned log — that is the reading the ruling closes, and it closes it for a good reason.

MECHANISM IS YOURS TO CHOOSE, and I am not prescribing one because the package has conventions I have not read. A rehearsal addendum, a conditional block, or a rehearsal-specific copy are all acceptable. WHAT IS NOT ACCEPTABLE: (a) deleting the counted-run instruction, which will be needed and correct the day a release coordinate exists; (b) leaving the friction-log attestation asking for "Checkout pin at start" and "Checkout pin at end" in the rehearsal copy, since that presupposes the move and a pilot will honour it; (c) making a pilot decide which run it is in — the pilot is blinded and must not be asked to reason about the method.

Whatever you choose, the pilot-facing text for a REHEARSAL must be unambiguous on its own, read alone, with no knowledge of the ruling. That is the test to apply to your own wording before you finish.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #9049 (https://github.com/day8/re-frame2/pull/9049), per the mayor ruling of 2026-09-03. MECHANISM CHOSEN: a rehearsal variant applied by the OPERATOR, in workspace.md's assembly immediately after step 6, under a new heading 'Rehearsal runs: outcome 7 is BLOCKED'. Chosen from the package's own conventions: workspace.md is the operator's page and the pilot is never sent to it (README.md), so a conditional there can never reach the pilot — which is what rules out (c); step 6 is where the two pilot-facing copies are made, so the delta sits against the step that produces the thing it changes; and the package already expresses variants as base-plus-delta ('Pilot 2 — LinearLite: the same file with the ... rows dropped'). A separate rehearsal PAGE was rejected because README.md's heading is '## The four pages' and a fifth would force a heading change, which the scope fence forbids. THE THREE UNACCEPTABLE OUTCOMES ARE ALL AVOIDED: (a) the counted-run instruction is untouched in both briefs and in friction-log.md; (b) the variant collapses the rehearsal copy's two-pin attestation to the single pin true of the run, and pre-fills outcome 7's row as BLOCKED so no effort is spent reaching it; (c) the pilot is never asked which kind of run it is in — the replacement text names neither 'rehearsal' nor 'counted run'. READ-ALONE TEST APPLIED, as the ruling required. The pilot's outcome 7 becomes: 'Not part of this run. Your project resolves the library from the checkout beside it rather than from a released version, so there is no released version to upgrade across and nothing here to attempt. title: skill(re-frame2): ssr-authoring.md teaches four head-surface claims implementation/ssr does not back — an :rf/head sub (none registered), compute-head (no such fn), render-head defaulting to (subscribe [:route]), and <meta charset> in the default head
description:
Four claims in skills/re-frame2/references/cross-cutting/ssr-authoring.md about the head surface do not match implementation/ssr.

CLAIM 1 — :57 "The `:rf/head` sub returns the same value reactively for views/tools."
TRUTH 1 — git grep -nE ':rf/head([^-]|$)' implementation tools (excluding head-model / head-snapshot) -> 0 hits; implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/head/registry.cljc registers no subscription. (spec/API.md:374 lists `:rf/head` as a 011 sub — a spec/impl drift for the SSR owner; cardinal rule 1 says the implementation wins, so the leaf must not teach it.)

CLAIM 2 — :49 "Equivalent value-shape to `(compute-head head-id db route)` for any registered `head-id`."
TRUTH 2 — git grep compute-head implementation -> 0. Only spec/011-SSR.md:1235 uses the phrase "(or equivalently `(compute-head head-id db route)`)". No such fn exists.

CLAIM 3 — :46 `;; :route optional; defaults to (subscribe [:route])`
TRUTH 3 — registry.cljc `render-head` docstring: a keyword arg is shorthand for `{:frame kw}`; "When `:route` is absent, the active route slice (at ...) is used" — read from the frame's runtime-db routing slice. There is no `[:route]` sub; the routing sub id is `:rf/route`.

CLAIM 4 — :38 "Routes without `:head` get the silent default — `<title>` derived from frame metadata's `:doc`, plus `<meta charset>` and `<meta viewport>`."
TRUTH 4 — registry.cljc:102-125 `default-head` returns `{:title (or doc "") :meta [{:name "viewport" ...}]}`; docstring: "Does not carry `{:charset "utf-8"}`. Charset is an envelope concern owned by the shell ... Carrying it here too produced two `<meta charset>` tags."

IMPACT
`(subscribe [:rf/head])` and `compute-head` are two dead calls an author will make; the charset sentence misleads anyone reading the head-model or building a custom envelope with `head-model->html` (they would double the charset tag).

FIX SHAPE (one file)
:57 -> "read it with `(rf/active-head frame-id)`; no subscription is registered"; :49 drop the compute-head parenthetical; :46 -> ";; :route optional; defaults to the frame's active route slice"; :38 -> "`:title` from frame `:doc` plus the viewport `<meta>`; `<meta charset>` comes from the document envelope, not the head-model". Not in this bead's file set: spec/API.md:374 and spec/011:1235 carry the same two phantoms — the SSR owner should reconcile them (rf2-8arzr.6 already reconciles 011/API.md for the ssr-node crossing; flag it there).

GATE
No gate (prose). Verify by hand against registry.cljc `render-head` / `active-head` / `default-head`; say so in the PR body.

ACCEPTANCE
ssr-authoring.md contains no `:rf/head` sub claim, no `compute-head`, no `(subscribe [:route])`, and its default-head sentence matches `default-head`'s docstring.

     :dispatch-id …            ; alternative to :epoch-id
     :path        [<k> ...]}   ; app-db path to highlight in the App-db panel

A shipped launch/navigate path the skill never routes to. Prose only. No tools/xray change.

## GATE

No gate — verify by hand. If the panel-id set is quoted, `python scripts/check_skill_xray_tab_inventory_drift.py --verbose` must stay green.

## ACCEPTANCE

The skill names `focus!`, its command keys, the `:routes` alias, and that it navigates but does not mount.

title: hicasso: trim docstrings to the contract in the 4 src files no cut task touches (controlled, server, forms, overlay; slot.cljc after .1)
description:

THE RULE (binding): a docstring carries (a) what the var is or returns; (b) the contract - takes, returns, promises, effects, ordering, failure behaviour, in full for a public var, and for a private var what it does plus the one non-obvious invariant behind its shape; (c) one sentence of why; (d) where the argument lives, as a repo-relative path into docs/design/hicasso (architecture.md, studio/<page>.md, decisions.md HD-NNN). Links are repo-relative paths, NEVER [[wikilinks]] - 892 exist in src and nothing resolves them; check each retained path exists by hand and say so in the PR body. A measured figure stays only with its page named beside it. A source comment stays only where it protects nearby code from a plausible-but-wrong edit (a local correctness proof); module history, benchmark narrative, rejected alternatives, HD derivations and explanations of other namespaces' mechanisms do not. Content rule, not a number: no 40-line cap, no 1:1 enforcement, no link checker, no script. Untouched: retained-inventory's :what strings and the rf2:builder-bypass-ok block.

MOVE vs DELETE: durable design reasoning with no home in docs/design/hicasso is MOVED there - measurements and traces to studio/, rulings and rejected alternatives to decisions.md, mechanism reasoning to architecture.md; prose a design page already carries, superseded prose and change-narration is DELETED. Check the others against the studio/ and decisions.md pages they name before moving anything. WORKED EXAMPLES (shape to copy; full text in rf2-6c12m.4 notes part 2): the collector ns docstring 392 -> 12 lines (what it owns, why those share a namespace, one design-record path); commit-basis 58 -> ~18 lines (three terms, why three, the .19 reincarnation counter-example kept as the one-sentence why, one architecture.md path); cold-read! 59 -> 9 lines (contract, fallback, why the memo is per read with the figure and its studio page).

title: docs-gate: 128 tracked markdown files are covered by NEITHER link gate — implementation/SECURITY.md is the instance that surfaced it
description:
MEASURED by the mayor 2026-08-20, prompted by a worker refuting my gate nomination on PR #8542. Every figure is a CLAIM — re-derive before acting.

HOW IT SURFACED. I briefed a worker that `scripts/check_readme_links.py --ci` covers `implementation/SECURITY.md`, citing CLAUDE.md's "every README.md beside source code, implementation/** included". The worker MEASURED it instead of trusting me: it planted a broken cross-file anchor, then a broken FILE target, and the gate returned exit 0 on both. Reading the source, `_iter_root_markdown` DROPS any entry containing "/", so that gate's roster is READMEs anywhere plus ROOT markdown only. `implementation/SECURITY.md` is not a README, so NO GATE COVERS IT. My nomination silently generalised "READMEs beside source" to "any markdown beside source". CLAUDE.md itself is accurate; I misread it.

THE GAP IS NOT ONE FILE. Partitioning all tracked markdown at the tip:
  * 977 tracked `.md` files.
  * `check_doc_slugs.py` covers 747 — its DEFAULT_ROOTS (docs, spec, skills, migration) plus the `tools/*/spec` tier `_iter_markdown` adds.
  * `check_readme_links.py --ci` covers 138 — READMEs anywhere plus root markdown.
  * **128 files are covered by NEITHER**, once the 7 `.claude/commands/*.md` are set aside.

CAVEAT ON THAT NUMBER, and it matters: `.claude/commands/*.md` ARE reached by `check_readme_links.py`'s third arm (rf2-1yy75), which resolves path-shaped REFERENCES rather than anchors. I excluded them above. They are therefore partially covered, not orphaned, and any fix must not double-cover them.

WHAT IS IN THE ORPHANED SET — a sample, not the roster:
  * examples/TESTING.md
  * implementation/SECURITY.md
  * implementation/adapters/TESTING.md
  * implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/DESIGN-RATIONALE.md
  * implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/FORM-3.md
  * implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md
  * scripts/_test_fixtures/check_doc_slugs/absolute_path_ok/docs/index.md
  * scripts/_test_fixtures/check_doc_slugs/absolute_path_ok/docs/target.md
  * scripts/_test_fixtures/check_doc_slugs/ai_findings_dir_link_flagged/docs/index.md
  * scripts/_test_fixtures/check_doc_slugs/ai_findings_link_flagged/docs/index.md

Nothing validates link targets or heading anchors in any of them. A broken link there is invisible to CI forever.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A DECISION RATHER THAN AN AUTOMATIC FIX. The stance rejects gold-plating, and "every markdown file must be link-checked" may simply not be worth it for design rationales and internal notes that no reader navigates by link. The honest question is which of the 128 are NAVIGATED — cited from elsewhere, or carrying cross-references someone follows — and those are the ones that want covering. A blanket widening of either gate's roots is the over-engineered answer and would also change what those gates mean.

SO THE DELIVERABLE IS: classify the orphaned set, propose the narrowest widening that covers the navigated part, and say explicitly what is left uncovered and why that is acceptable. **A reasoned refusal — "these are all internal notes, leave them" — is a complete and good deliverable**, provided it names what it examined.

DO NOT widen a gate's roots without checking the CI arming: a root added to `check_doc_slugs.py` validates nothing if no PR-time job runs it on that surface. rf2-v7fui is the precedent — `skills` sat in DEFAULT_ROOTS for months while no PR job ran the script on a skills path.

HOT ZONE: `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` and `scripts/check_readme_links.py` are one-toucher-at-a-time surfaces, and `.github/workflows/*` likewise. Sequence behind PR #8539, which is changing `.github/workflows/` right now.
close_reason: Delivered in PR #8546 as a classification plus a narrow widening. RE-DERIVED the counts and three of the four moved: 977 tracked .md CONFIRMED; check_doc_slugs.py covers 744 not 747 (four tools/*/spec/findings/ docs excluded by name); check_readme_links.py --ci scans 76 not 138 (the 138 counted every README, but 62 sit under the docs-gate roots and are deliberately excluded — the two rosters are DISJOINT by construction); so the orphaned set is 150, not 128. BUT 137 OF THE 150 ARE GATE TEST FIXTURES under scripts/_test_fixtures/ — deliberately-broken markdown the gates' own self-tests consume; covering them is wrong, not merely gold-plating, and _test_fixtures is already an exclusion in check_readme_links.py. Four more are tools/*/spec/findings/ design records: MEASURED, they carry 33 stale relative targets between them (../spec/012-Routing.md from inside tools/xray/spec/findings/ resolves to tools/xray/spec/spec/...), exactly the exploratory link rot the standing 'findings' exclusion exists to leave alone — covering them would red main on day one. REFUSED both, 141 files. That leaves 13, of which 8 are unambiguously NAVIGATED: implementation/SECURITY.md (root README cites it, 36 relative targets, cross-file anchors into spec/), examples/TESTING.md (14 inbound citations), implementation/adapters/TESTING.md, the reagent-slim design trio, and tools/mcp-conformance/{NAMING,TOKEN-BUDGETS}.md which spec/Conventions.md and spec/Tool-Pair.md cite NORMATIVELY. New _iter_source_markdown roster covers them and needs NO new exclusion — _is_excluded already refuses fixtures, docs-gate roots and tools/*/spec/. It takes one extra file, a template payload whose sibling this gate already walks under the same mustache guard. Zero findings today, so it lands green as a ratchet. ARMING CHECKED (the rf2-v7fui trap): verify-readme-links has no if: and no surface guard, test.yml's PR trigger is unfiltered, and the job is in all-required-passed's needs — which is why the roster went here and not in check_doc_slugs.py. Proven by planting: a broken target in implementation/SECURITY.md now reds this gate naming that line, where the PRE-CHANGE gate exited 0 on the identical fault and check_doc_slugs.py still does. Self-test asserts each REFUSAL, not only membership, and both refusals were confirmed to bite.

description:
FOUND by rf2-g633h's worker (PR #8415) and verified by the mayor at
origin/main d68526c477, 2026-08-16 21:05 AUSEST.

CLAUDE.md:114 says: "mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs block deliberately keeps
design/freehand/ and design/hicasso/ out of the site".

mkdocs.yml's exclude_docs ACTUALLY holds SIX entries:
  tools/playground/
  migration/from-re-frame-v1/codemod/
  migration/reagent-to-hicasso/codemod/
  design/freehand/
  design/hicasso/
  design/retirement/

WHY THIS IS NOT A TYPO-CLASS DEFECT. That very paragraph exists to stop a
worker nominating 'mkdocs build --strict' as the gate for a tree the build
does not reach, and the dispatch template states the general rule: 'a gate run
over an excluded path exits green having verified nothing — the same fail-open
defect worth hunting anywhere else, except it is now the brief telling the
worker to trust it.' AN INCOMPLETE EXCLUSION LIST MAKES THAT PARAGRAPH ITSELF
FAIL OPEN, for four paths, in the file every worker is instructed to read.

IT ALREADY BIT, mildly. PR #8415 edited docs/design/retirement/freehand-and-ui.md.
Its worker ran 'mkdocs build --strict' green, then checked site/ BOTH WAYS
rather than trusting it, and found the build had never reached the page. A
worker following CLAUDE.md alone would have read design/retirement/ as covered
and reported a green that meant nothing.

THE FIX IS ONE SENTENCE, and the anti-gold-plating clause applies: name the
six, or say 'six trees including design/*' and point at mkdocs.yml as the
source. DO NOT write a synchronisation gate for this; that is exactly the
over-engineering the stance rejects. Prefer the form that cannot go stale
again — point at the config rather than restating its contents, if that reads
cleanly.

CHECK FOR SIBLING COPIES BEFORE EDITING: the same claim may appear in
docs/the-mayor-method/ or the dispatch template. Two copies of one rule
disagree within days — that defect class has been recorded three times in this
repository this week, most recently when three copies of the aborted-pull rule
disagreed (rf2-guyte, PR #8412). If a second copy exists, put the reasoning in
one place and a pointer in the other.
