title: RULED: no bd flatten — real yield is single-digit MB, not 1.3 GB (default DOLT_GC never collects the oldgen that is 98% of its target)
description:
> **SUPERSEDED IN PART — see the RULING note (2026-09-08). DECISION: NO FLATTEN, and no `.git/lost-found` deletion either.**
> Two claims in the finding below did not survive measurement. (a) The store is **4.0 GB, not 1.3 GB** — flatten's entire
> target is the 513 MB `noms` directory, 12.8% of the footprint. (b) Flatten's REAL yield is **single-digit MB**, because bd
> issues a bare `CALL DOLT_GC()` and Dolt's default GC never collects the `oldgen` that is **98.4%** of that target; the
> 509 MB figure was only ever an upper bound. The stated COST is also smaller than assumed: the audit trail lives in current
> row data (49 of 49 earlier notes states contained verbatim in the current value), which flatten preserves — so the case
> against flatten rests on yield, not on data loss. The original finding is kept verbatim below and its GC-run
> measurements stand; only its conclusion is superseded.

---

## Finding — from the 2026-09-08 beads GC (14-day retention)

The daily GC ran and did what was asked: it deleted the 5 closed beads older than
14 days and left the graph intact. It did NOT reclaim the space, and it cannot.

MEASURED during that run:
- Dolt store before 1333 MB / 18110 commits; after 1306 MB / 18116 commits.
- The Dolt GC phase completed in 1.8 seconds and freed 27 MB — about 2%.
- The commit count went UP across the run, not down.

WHY: essentially every chunk is still referenced by the 18,116 live commits. Deleting
five issues frees almost nothing, because the store's size is history, not rows.

`bd gc`'s COMPACT phase is a NO-OP in bd 1.1.2 despite its help text saying it squashes
commits — it prints a count and tips the caller at `bd flatten`.

## The decision

`bd flatten` squashes ALL history to a single commit. That is the only lever that
reclaims the 1.3 GB, and it is destructive to exactly the thing this project leans on:
`bd history` and `bd diff` are how a backlog reread distinguishes an audit REOPENING
from a lost close, and that distinction has been load-bearing twice today alone
(rf2-kuky.10 and rf2-kuky.69 both reappeared and both were legitimate audit reopenings;
re-closing either on the "reverted" reading would have destroyed a real finding).

So this is a trade Mike makes, not a worker:
  (a) Leave it. 1.3 GB is not hurting anything measurable today, and the tracker's own
      history stays queryable. Cheapest, and consistent with not gold-plating.
  (b) `bd flatten` now, accepting the loss of per-bead history. Reclaims the space.
      Note the EXPORT is unaffected — `.beads/issues.jsonl` in git history still carries
      every bead's content at every checkpoint, so close reasons survive; what is lost is
      bd's own per-field change trail.
  (c) Flatten on a schedule with a retained window, if bd supports one — unverified.

RECOMMENDATION: (a) for now, and revisit if the store's size starts costing something
concrete (clone time, `bd prime` latency, disk pressure). Nothing measured today says it
does. rf2-ornb is the bead that DOES have a measured cost attached (prime latency at
p99 20s), and it has a cheaper remedy that does not touch history.

## Not to be done without a ruling

Do NOT run `bd flatten` on this bead's authority. It is filed to record the finding and
put the choice in front of the operator, not to authorise the act.
notes:
## RULING 2026-09-08 23:17 AUSEST — no flatten, and no lost-found deletion either

**DECISION: decline `bd flatten`. Also decline the alternative the dossier proposed in its place — DO NOT delete `.git/lost-found`. Net storage action today: NONE.** The store stays as it is, under a watch trigger. Two candidate actions were examined and both failed, for opposite reasons: flatten buys almost nothing, and the "safe reversible 4.7 GB win" turns out to be the most irreversible act either analysis proposed.

Two independent analyses were weighed — the original decision dossier and a later Codex review. They AGREE on the disposition (no flatten) and agree on every size figure to within measurement noise. They CONFLICT on the two findings that would have caused ACTION. **Codex won both.** I re-measured both conflicts myself rather than taking either on trust; both corrections held, and on the lost-found one Codex understated its own case.

### WHY, compressed

The bead's premise — that flatten is "the only lever that reclaims the 1.3 GB" — fails twice over:

1. **Wrong denominator.** `.beads` is 4.0 GB, not 1.3 GB. Flatten's entire target is the 513 MB `noms` directory — **12.8% of the footprint**. The bead measured `embeddeddolt` and called it the store; the larger sibling `.beads/backup` (2.66 GB) is not mentioned in the bead at all.
2. **Wrong numerator, and this is the finding that ends the discussion.** Of `noms`, **504.7 MB (98.4%) is `oldgen`** — and the garbage collection that flatten runs **does not collect oldgen**. Flatten's realistic yield is the newgen remainder: **single-digit MB**, not 509 MB and not 1.3 GB.

An irreversible, fleet-zero operation that permanently deletes the tracker's own change trail, to reclaim on the order of 8 MB from a 4.0 GB directory on a disk with 411 GB free, is not a trade worth making at any priority.

### Conflicts, and who won each

**(1) `.git/lost-found` is NOT a safe reversible win — CODEX WINS; re-measured and extended.**
The dossier proposed deleting `.git/lost-found` (4,982,432,111 bytes = 4751.6 MB) as "9x flatten's yield, effectively reversible — a fresh `git fsck --lost-found` regenerates it". **That is false.** `fsck --lost-found` writes copies of DANGLING objects; it cannot regenerate an object that is no longer in the store. Measured 2026-09-08 ~23:12 AUSEST via `git cat-file --batch-check` over the filenames:
- `.git/lost-found/other`: **2,433 of 2,433 missing** from the object store (Codex's figure, reproduced independently).
- `.git/lost-found/commit`: **2,306 of 2,306 missing** — Codex tested only `other/`; this set is my addition.
- **So all 4,739 entries name objects that no longer exist in `.git/objects`.**
- POSITIVE control through the same pipeline: `HEAD` (`8e53b1f68f9fe2d5111d937da80c9dad3e32e4ae`) returned `commit 255`. NEGATIVE control: a fabricated 40-hex hash returned `missing`. The probe discriminates; the zeros are honest.
- Payload intactness, on the sample Codex named: `.git/lost-found/other/000490f9446c76f9822679b2ddc15b8f46a987cb` is 1,852,733 bytes, non-writing `git hash-object --no-filters` reproduces its filename exactly, and `git cat-file -t` on that hash exits 128. Payload intact, object absent.
- Size split: `other/` 4751.5 MB, `commit/` 0.1 MB. Directory mtime 2026-05-16.

**Conclusion: these 4,739 files are the ONLY surviving copies of their objects. Deleting them is irreversible and unregenerable — a clean `git fsck` afterwards would coexist with the loss and prove nothing.** Their contents were not audited and their human value is unknown. Age establishes staleness, not that the recovery which produced them concluded.

**(2) Flatten's true yield — CODEX WINS; both halves verified by me from primary sources.**
- bd's GC path issues **`CALL DOLT_GC()`** — no arguments, no `--full`. Verified by fetching the pinned source (`beads@20e493e569c9`, `internal/storage/versioncontrolops/gc.go`).
- Dolt's own documentation on default GC: **"Dolt GC will only visit data in the new generation, and so will never collect data from deleted branches which has previously made its way to the old generation"**; `--full` is what performs "a more thorough garbage collection, fully collecting the old gen and new gen".
- Local measurement: `noms` 513.1 MB, of which `oldgen` **504.7 MB = 98.4%**.

**Therefore 509 MB was only ever an UPPER BOUND, and unreachable without a `--full` GC that bd never issues.** This also retires a secondary inference carried in the bead: the earlier "GC freed only 27 MB, so ~98% of chunks must still be referenced" does NOT follow — the default GC never looked at oldgen, so the 2% result is explained by GC MODE, not by reachability. The dossier reached the right disposition partly on a wrong mechanism.

**(3) "git recovers 32 of the ~34 distinct states" — CODEX WINS on arithmetic.** The dossier's own breakdown is 27 in both, 7 Dolt-only, 5 git-only. Git recovered **27 of Dolt's 34** and separately held 5 states Dolt never had; "32 of 34 recovered" conflates the two sets. The corrected reading still supports the dossier's larger point — the two records are independent samplings of the same history, neither a superset — but less strongly than stated.

**(4) The `.beads/backup` "recoverable tail" — CODEX WINS.** The dossier carried forward rf2-kdnf's ~74.5 MB tail figure. Codex parsed the current manifest into exact archive identifiers with present-and-absent controls: **all 41 `.darc` archives are referenced**, including the third-largest at 106,488,152 bytes. There is no demonstrated reclaim target in `backup/` at all. Neither analysis proposed pruning it; the correction is recorded so nobody revives the tail figure as a target.

**(5) The backup's "15-minute auto-sync" — CODEX WINS.** Per the pinned `cmd/bd/backup_auto.go`, auto-backup is **command-triggered with a fifteen-minute throttle, not a guaranteed timer** — it fires on the next bd command after the throttle expires. Any reasoning that treats the post-rewrite restore window as a dependable 15-minute clock is wrong. A synchronized backup or remote is not an immutable pre-rewrite archive.

**(6) `bd history --limit` — CODEX WINS, and it corrects standing doctrine.** The pinned `cmd/bd/history.go` applies `--limit` **after** loading history: it reduces OUTPUT, not the retrieval workload. The dispatch template mandates `--limit` as the mitigation for the 891 MB-per-bead cost of `bd history --json` (measured: 891,328,939 bytes for one bead). It does not mitigate the load. Recorded as a known ergonomic limitation — explicitly NOT as an argument for destroying history, and not as an explanation of `bd prime` latency (rf2-ornb's measured root cause is serialising memory bodies into context, not store size).

**(7) Where the two AGREE — recorded once.** The disposition (no flatten). Every directory size. That `bd gc` cannot reclaim this space. That `.beads/embeddeddolt` and `.beads/backup` are gitignored, so a fresh clone or worker worktree receives only the 15.4 MB export — the 4.0 GB exists in this primary checkout alone, and clone time, worktree creation and CI are entirely unaffected. And that nothing measurable is being harmed today.
### LOAD-BEARING MEASUREMENTS

Re-measured by me 2026-09-08 23:10-23:20 AUSEST unless attributed. A live mayor loop was writing to the store throughout, so this is an observation window, not an atomic snapshot. `du -sb`, logical bytes:

```
   4009.2 MB  .beads
   2663.9 MB  .beads/backup                  <- dominates; untouched by flatten; all 41 archives referenced
   1316.2 MB  .beads/embeddeddolt            <- the bead's "1.3 GB"
    803.0 MB  .beads/.../git-remote-cache    <- cache in principle; NOT proven bankable
    513.1 MB  .beads/.../noms                <- flatten's ENTIRE target = 12.8% of .beads
    504.7 MB  .beads/.../noms/oldgen         <- 98.4% of that target; default DOLT_GC() never collects it
     15.4 MB  .beads/issues.jsonl            <- the git-tracked export
     13.4 MB  .beads/interactions.jsonl
   8344.7 MB  .git   (4751.6 MB of it lost-found; 3543.8 MB objects)
```

Disk: **411 GB free of 953 GB (57% used)** — the store is ~0.4% of the disk. Baselines at ruling time (they move; re-read before using them as a check): **34 open beads, 951 memories, 1109 rows total**.

**WHAT FLATTEN ACTUALLY DOES.** Per `bd flatten --help` and the pinned `flatten.go`: branch from the current state, soft-reset to the initial commit "(preserving all data)", commit everything as one snapshot, swap `main`, run GC. Help text: "This is irreversible — all commit history is lost." Codex's source read adds a correction to the mental model: **it soft-resets to the OLDEST commit and commits on top — this is not an orphan-root operation**, so the initial commit plus the snapshot are retained and other refs may preserve further ancestry. **The command prints a literal one-commit result and only warns if the subsequent GC fails, so its success message is not verification of anything.**

**THE AUDIT-TRAIL FINDING — the correction to the bead's stated COST, with its controls.**
The bead assumes flatten costs "the tracker's own history" in the sense of losing audit findings. Measured, it does not: the trail lives in CURRENT ROW DATA, which flatten explicitly preserves.
- Subject rf2-uelji (oldest still-open bead, created 2026-07-27, six weeks of real edits). `bd history` returned **18,184 entries containing only 34 DISTINCT states** (title/desc/notes/status/priority) — signal-to-noise about **1:535**, because every database commit appears in every bead's history whether that bead moved or not (memory `bd-history-newest-entry-is-a-db-commit-not-a-bead-mutation`: help says it shows commits where the issue was modified; measured, it shows all commits, full stop).
- Its notes grow monotonically 3,094 -> 118,527 chars across those 34 states. **33 of 33 earlier states are contained VERBATIM as substrings of the current notes value** (32 of 33 also as prefixes).
- Repeated on three further beads by the git route: rf2-hic-063 **9 of 9**, rf2-kmqx3 **6 of 6**, rf2-59bgn **1 of 1**. **Total 49 of 49.** This is the project's own `--append-notes` convention working as designed.
- CONTROLS, without which this number should not be believed: the FIRST attempt used `head -1`/`tail -1` on the notes field and reported "100 chars" and "52 chars" against fields of 3,094 and 118,527, answering "NO — not a prefix" confidently and wrongly, because notes contain embedded newlines so the line filters read one LINE, not one FIELD. Redone entirely inside `jq`, where the field stays one value. A second trap caught: `select($last | contains(.[2]))` silently rebinds `.` to `$last` inside `select`, indexing a string by number — capture the element into a variable first.
- **BOUND, per Codex, and accepted: containment is established for the NOTES field only.** It does not establish preservation of overwritten close reasons, deleted beads, status transitions, or every field. The result is real and load-bearing; it is not a general proof that history is redundant.
- Independent second record: `.beads/issues.jsonl` is a git-tracked full-database export with **12,348 commits touching it** since 2026-05-06 (Codex counted 12,387 HEAD-reachable in a later window; both are the same measurement on a moving tree), carrying description, notes, close_reason, status, priority, acceptance_criteria, design, labels, dependencies and comments. A 1-in-8 sample of 618 checkpoints recovered 27 of Dolt's 34 states plus 5 that Dolt never had. `.beads/config.yaml` already names a rebuild from this export as "the documented bd bootstrap fallback and our accepted recovery floor".
- **NET: the case against flatten rests on YIELD, not on data loss.** Flatten would not destroy audit findings, close reasons or reopening rationales. It would make the walk more awkward — from `bd history <id> --json` to a `git log -- .beads/issues.jsonl` walk nobody has scripted — against a workflow that two standing documents mandate (`docs/the-mayor-method/dispatch-prompt-template.md` and `loops.md`). Note also that of the two audit-reopen discriminators the project relies on, one (`bd comments <id> --json`) reads current rows and is unaffected by flatten entirely.

**EMBEDDED-DOLT / FLEET-ZERO CAUTION.** `bd dolt show` reports **embedded (in-process) mode** — there is no Dolt server. Every `bd` invocation is a separate OS process sharing `.beads/embeddeddolt/rf2/.dolt/noms`, and Dolt's GC safepoint protocol is per-SERVER. **A `DOLT_GC()` rewriting the chunk store while another process writes is a corruption path, not merely lock contention** — and flatten's final step is exactly that GC. Any flatten or compact is therefore fleet-zero work: every worker stopped, every loop stopped, nothing else touching the tracker. Codex's qualifier is accepted and recorded: this is a design-level concurrency hazard, not a failure reproduced on this box. Related instrument facts: `bd --readonly sql` rejects even SELECT queries in embedded mode, and `bd admin compact --dolt` probes `.beads\dolt` — which does not exist here, the real path being `.beads\embeddeddolt` — and reports "No local Dolt directory found; nothing to collect", a reassuring answer from an instrument that never looked.

**`bd gc` DECAY WARNING — independent of this decision, and a live data-loss path.** `bd gc`'s DECAY phase **silently DELETES CLOSED BEADS** (default 90 days) unless `--skip-decay` is passed. On this project close reasons are normative records and bead ids are cross-file citations, so **`--skip-decay` is mandatory on every standing `bd gc` instruction**. See memory `bd-gc-decay-silently-deletes-closed-beads`. Separately, `bd gc`'s COMPACT phase is a NO-OP on bd 1.1.2 despite help text claiming it squashes commits — it prints a count and points the caller at `bd flatten`.

### DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE
- **Pruning `.beads/backup` (2.66 GB).** All 41 archives are manifest-referenced; size alone does not distinguish garbage. rf2-kdnf's standing trigger (re-measure if backup exceeds 5 GB, or if a new multi-GB archive appears) has not fired.
- **Deleting `git-remote-cache` (803 MB).** Structurally a cache, but Codex found 54 refs (22 blobstore, 30 operation-specific remote) plus an ~791 MiB pack, and neither cache/remote equality nor the sustained saving after a refetch was established. **Not bankable on current evidence, and not proposed.**
- **`bd compact --days N`.** The feature exists — that answers the bead's open question, which was flagged unverified. It reads ~11% of commits older than 30 days (1,785 of 16,441, measured 2026-09-06), is ALSO irreversible, runs the same embedded-mode GC, and per Codex a percentage of COMMITS cannot be multiplied into BYTES because chunks are shared and commits have unequal payloads. Disqualified on the numbers.
- **Any retention policy, scheduler or new tooling.** Not justified by this snapshot.
- **Auditing the 4,739 lost-found payloads.** Not done here — see next steps.
- **The ~657 MB of `.git` that is the export's own blob history.** Real, cloned by everyone, and not addressable without rewriting trunk history.

### NEXT STEPS
1. **No storage action is required.** This bead needs no work. It stays OPEN as the record and the watch trigger.
2. **WATCH TRIGGER, adopted (generalising rf2-kdnf's from the backup to the whole store): re-measure when `.beads` exceeds 8 GB, or when a new multi-GB archive appears.** Read the size DISTRIBUTION, never the total — a `du` on the total is precisely how this bead came to name a number measuring a third of the problem.
3. **`.git/lost-found` disposition is a separate operator call**, filed as its own bead (see discovered-from). It is NOT a reclaim task: it is a decision about 4.75 GB of unregenerable material. **Retain by default. If it is ever discarded, archive it off-box and verify the archive first.**
4. **A history-PRESERVING option exists and is unmeasured: a FULL GC (`--full`) collects oldgen while keeping history.** bd does not expose it; this box carries standalone Dolt 1.86.6, but routing it into the live embedded store was tested by neither analysis. **If disk pressure ever becomes real, this is the lead to pull BEFORE anything irreversible** — proven on an isolated copy first, never on the live store.
5. **Add `--skip-decay` to any standing `bd gc` instruction** — see the DECAY warning above.

### IF THIS RULING IS EVER OVERRULED AND FLATTEN IS TAKEN — the exact safe sequence
Steps 1-4 are not optional; the embedded-mode corruption path in step 1 is the one that bites.

```
# 1. FLEET ZERO. Stop every worker, every loop, every background bd process.
#    Codex's caveat is accepted: an unchanged commit count across sixty seconds is NOT a lock.
#    Use an explicit maintenance window and stop automatic sync; do not infer quiescence.
bd history <id> --json | jq length     # note it; wait 60s; re-read. Movement = something still writes.

# 2. Checkpoint the export FIRST, so the git-side parallel record is current to the instant.
sh scripts/beads-checkpoint.sh
git checkout HEAD -- .beads
git fetch origin main && git rebase origin/main
git push

# 3. Independent, IMMUTABLE archive to ANOTHER disk, outside automatic backup/sync targets.
#    A same-disk copy makes the net reclaim negative: embeddeddolt is 1.3 GB against an ~8 MB yield.
#    PowerShell: Copy-Item -Recurse .beads\embeddeddolt E:\beads-archive-<date>\embeddeddolt
#    VERIFY THE EFFECT: compare file counts and byte totals, then DEMONSTRATE A RESTORE IN
#    ISOLATION before proceeding. A synced backup or the Dolt remote is NOT a pre-rewrite archive.

# 4. Confirm the off-box copy as a second line of retreat:
bd dolt push
gh repo view day8/re-frame2-beads --json pushedAt

# 5. Preview (documented preview-only; NOT run by either analysis):
bd flatten --dry-run

# 6. The act:
bd flatten --force
```

**VERIFY BY EFFECT, never by the success message** (which prints a literal one-commit result regardless of what happened):
- `bd list --status open --limit 0 --json | jq length` and the `bd memories` count must be unchanged (34 / 951 at ruling time — re-read them immediately before, they move). If either moved, STOP and restore from step 3.
- Inspect ACTUAL ancestry rather than trusting the printed commit count. Compare canonical current data across every table, plus config, comments and dependencies. Row counts and matching directory sizes alone are inadequate.
- Spot-check a bead with substantial notes and a close reason; confirm `bd comments <id> --json` still returns comments.
- Re-measure `.beads` in full. **Expect a single-digit-MB drop, not a dramatic one** — if that disappoints, this ruling arrived late.
- Read the NEXT backup/sync result before resuming writers, and keep the step-3 archive for at least one full merge-and-dispatch cycle.

**UNKNOWNS, flagged rather than guessed, and unchanged by this ruling:** what `.beads/backup` does after a history rewrite (refuse as non-fast-forward, sync alongside, or overwrite) is undocumented and untested; whether post-flatten Dolt auto-push force-pushes the remote is undetermined (the global `--sandbox` flag implies auto-push exists); and **no post-flatten byte measurement exists anywhere**, because neither analysis ran flatten in any form — not even `--dry-run`. Nothing in either analysis, or in this ruling, mutated or compacted the store.

title: xray(static-sim): the Sim rail's :on picker claims 'No outgoing transitions declared' for EVERY parallel machine — available-transitions' normalise-path returns [] for a region map
description:
The Static Sim rail's outgoing-transition picker shows **"No outgoing transitions declared on this state."** for EVERY parallel machine, whatever those regions actually declare.

## The measurement

Found and measured by the `rf2-pzuqw` worker on 2026-09-21 while implementing the `:after` timer
rows, and reported rather than acted on because it sits outside that item's fence. It was measured
by RUN, not read off the source: on a parallel fixture whose regions **do** declare `:on`
transitions (`:go`, `:submit`), `available-transitions` returned **`[]`** while the sibling
`available-after-transitions` — added by rf2-pzuqw — correctly returned the region-prefixed timer
row.

So the two halves of the same rail disagree on the same fixture, and the disagreement is the
evidence: the timer half handles a region map correctly, the `:on` half does not.

## The cause, as reported

`available-transitions`' `normalise-path` returns `[]` for a parallel region-map. A parallel root's
snapshot state is a MAP of region → state rather than a single state value, and the path
normalisation does not handle that shape, so the lookup finds nothing and the picker renders its
empty-state copy.

**Re-derive this at tip before acting on it.** It is one worker's account of a function it was not
changing, and `sim_helpers.cljc` moved in the same PR (454 → 598 lines), so the line numbers in that
report are already stale. The behavioural claim is what to reproduce: build a parallel machine whose
regions declare `:on`, open the Sim rail, and read the picker.

## Why it matters more than an empty list usually would

**It fails in the REASSURING direction, and the copy asserts something false.** "No outgoing
transitions declared on this state." is not a neutral empty state — it is a positive claim about the
machine's definition, and for a parallel machine it is wrong. A user reading it concludes their
regions declare no transitions, which is exactly the thing they would then go and "fix" in a
definition that was already correct. An empty picker with no copy would mislead less.

It is also silent: nothing errors, nothing warns, and the rail renders perfectly.

## Scope hints, not a ruling

- The fix is presumably in `normalise-path` / `available-transitions` in
  `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/machines/sim_helpers.cljc`, whose parallel-aware
  sibling `available-after-transitions` now exists in the same file and may be the model.
- **Xray-only as far as anyone has looked** — this is a Static Sim rail defect, and nothing suggests
  the engine is wrong. `rf.machines/machine-transition` is a pure fn and the region-prefixed timer
  rows arrive correctly shaped, so the engine is answering properly and the consumer is mis-asking.
  Confirm that before widening scope to `implementation/machines/`.
- Gates would be the node lane (`npm run test:cljs`, which grades
  `sim_helpers_cljs_test.cljc` and `sim_cljs_test.cljs`) plus `clojure -M:test` from `tools/xray`.
  **The node lane takes the machine-wide shadow-cljs exclusive** — it must be granted, not assumed.
- `sim_helpers_cljs_test.cljc` gained 8 tests under rf2-pzuqw and already exercises the parallel
  timer path, so there is a place to put the regression test and a working parallel fixture to
  borrow.

## Related, and deliberately kept separate

The same worker recorded a SECOND parallel observation it did not conflate with this one: a parallel
**root** `:after` (decl-path `[]`) is listed in the rail as ruled, but a probe firing one returned
`:ok` with the state unchanged. It asserted only that the row LISTS, never that it FIRES. That is a
different question about the engine rather than about the picker, it may well be correct behaviour,
and it should not be folded into this item — but whoever takes this one is the best-placed person to
look at it, because they will already have a parallel fixture in hand.
notes:
---

`rf2-kmr2i` (P2, filed 2026-09-20T22:59:12Z by the merged-PR audit of #10130) reports a DIFFERENT

> `after-rows-at` at `:203-217` filters candidates with `:when (some? t)`, so legal

close_reason:
FIXED. PR #10133 (branch worker/simpicker-ky034, commit 772ac3a015), base 2a3b8a2911.

THE DEFECT, RE-DERIVED AT TIP AND CONFIRMED LIVE. `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/static/machines/sim_helpers.cljc` is 598 lines at 2a3b8a2911; `normalise-path` at :127-135 coerces one state value into a path and a parallel snapshot's `:state` is a MAP of region -> state, which matched none of its three arms, so `:else` returned `[]`, `node-at` was handed an empty path, and `available-transitions` (opening :151) returned `[]` for every parallel machine. The picker then rendered "No outgoing transitions declared on this state." — a positive claim about the user's definition, and a false one.

DECISIVE MEASUREMENT, BY RUN (JVM, `clojure -M` from tools/xray, against the real engine; not read off the source). Fixture: a `:type :parallel` root whose regions both declare `:on` — `:form` `{:editing {:on {:submit :submitted}}}`, `:net` `{:idle {:on {:go :busy}} :busy {:after {3000 :timeout} :on {:done :idle}}}` — seeded through `re-frame.machines.parallel/build-initial-snapshot`.

  BEFORE, at `{:form :editing, :net :idle}`:
    available-transitions       => []
    available-after-transitions => []
  BEFORE, after stepping [:go], at `{:form :editing, :net :busy}`:
    available-transitions       => []
    available-after-transitions => [{:delay-key 3000 :target :timeout :guard? false :guard nil :decl-path [:net :busy]}]

That second pair IS the defect: two halves of one rail, one snapshot, disagreeing — the `:after` half handles the region map, the `:on` half does not.

  AFTER, at `{:form :editing, :net :idle}`:
    available-transitions => [{:event :submit :target :submitted :guard? false :guard nil :decl-path [:form :editing]}
                              {:event :go     :target :busy      :guard? false :guard nil :decl-path [:net :idle]}]
  AFTER, at `{:form :editing, :net :busy}`:
    available-transitions => [{:event :submit :target :submitted :guard? false :guard nil :decl-path [:form :editing]}
                              {:event :done   :target :idle      :guard? false :guard nil :decl-path [:net :busy]}]

CONTROLS IN THE SAME RUN, both directions. A flat machine listed `[{:event :start :target :running ...}]` before and after, and a compound machine listed `[{:event :submit :target :loading ...}]` before and after — so the fn was never broken outright and the zero was specific to the map shape. And the engine answered `:status :ok` with a moved state for BOTH `[:go]` (-> `{:form :editing, :net :busy}`) and `[:submit]` (-> `{:form :submitted, :net :idle}`) from the very snapshot the picker was calling empty, so the transitions were genuinely fireable.

THE FIX. Branch on the map at the CALLER, mirroring the sibling `available-after-transitions` rather than inventing a second convention. `node-at` now takes a STATE-MAP rather than the whole definition, so a region's own `:states` at `[:regions <region> :states]` is walked by the same code, and it still returns nil unless the whole path resolves. New `leaf-pairs` yields one `[decl-path leaf-node]` per region for a parallel snapshot and one pair otherwise — the leaf-only counterpart of `path-nodes`, which walks ancestors because an `:after` is commonly declared on one. New `on-rows-at` mirrors `after-rows-at`, stamping the region-prefixed `:decl-path` the engine itself puts on its fx. `normalise-path` is UNCHANGED in behaviour and now documented as deliberately single-valued, so the next reader does not "fix" it by giving the map an arm there.

TWO DESIGN CALLS, mine to make (this item carried no ruling note and no implementation brief; its 3902-character description was the whole of it, unchanged across all 13 history snapshots from creation to dispatch, with no notes, no comments and no children).

(1) THE PARALLEL ROOT'S OWN `:on` IS NOT LISTED. A parallel root may declare `:on` as the engine's ancestor fallback, consulted when no region handles the event (`implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/parallel.cljc`, the "root parallel `:on` — the ancestor fallback" section and `root-fallback-seed`). It is excluded for exactly the reason a flat machine's machine-root `:on` has never been listed: both are parent inheritance, and `available-transitions` is leaf-only by its own documented policy. This preserves the deliberate asymmetry with `available-after-transitions`, which walks ancestors BY DESIGN because an `:after` is commonly declared on one — each fn is now consistent with its own stated policy rather than with the other's. Pinned both ways by `available-transitions-excludes-the-parallel-root-on-fallback`, whose control shows a FLAT machine's root `:on` is excluded identically, so parallel is consistent rather than special-cased.

(2) THE EMPTY-STATE COPY NO LONGER ASSERTS WHAT THE DEFINITION CONTAINS. It now reads: "Nothing to fire from the current state. The picker lists :on transitions declared on the active state, and :after timers on the active path." Fixing the shape handling removes the falsehood for a parallel machine that declares transitions, but the old copy would STILL overclaim, because the picker is leaf-only: a root `:on`, an `:always`, or a parent's `:on` can all be declared and fireable while the list is legitimately empty. Saying what was LOOKED AT lets the user draw the conclusion instead of being handed a wrong one. "The current state" is the rail's own existing vocabulary and reads correctly for a region map.

FILES. `sim_helpers.cljc` (the fix, 598 -> 673 lines), `sim_helpers_cljs_test.cljc` (+7 deftests, all seeded and driven through the real engine), and `sim.cljs` by TWO expressions — the row key now carries the declaring path as well as the event id, because a parallel machine's regions may each declare the same event (one broadcast handled in two places, the idiomatic parallel shape) and keyed on the event alone those rows collide, which React mis-reconciles and which the tree already has a dedicated test pinning for the flat case; plus the empty-state string above. `tools/xray/spec/003-Machine-Inspector.md` was NOT touched: its UC1 Rail bullet says the list is "the current state's `:on` transitions", so this change makes the implementation match the spec rather than contradict it, and the fence's only-if condition was not met. The full rule, root exclusion included, is in the `available-transitions` docstring, which is where the sibling keeps its own three-shape rule.

GATES. Node lane `npm run test:cljs`, captured exit codes, merge-base baseline then change: baseline 2025 compiled / 0 warnings, 12390 tests / 62197 assertions / 0 failures, exit 0; change 292 compiled / 0 warnings, 12397 / 62219 / 0 failures, exit 0. The +7 tests / +22 assertions delta was PREDICTED from the diff before the run and matched exactly, which is the right instrument here because this tree's quiet reporter prints its `Testing <ns>` banner only on a namespace's first failure, so a green log is silent about a namespace that passed (banner count 0 on both runs). `clojure -M:test` from tools/xray: 1362 / 6670 baseline, 1369 / 6692 with the change, 0 failures, exit 0 — the same +7 / +22. clj-kondo run in the PLAIN form deliberately: with `--fail-level error` it exits 0 on an unresolved symbol because `.clj-kondo/config.edn` grades those at warning level. Plain form on tools/xray: errors 0, warnings 134, all pre-existing; the only findings in my three files are two warnings in `sim.cljs` at :453 and :455, which the COMMITTED version of that file produces identically and which sit far above every hunk in this diff. The CI-pinned gate `python scripts/lint_kondo.py` (clj-kondo 2026.04.15): exit 0, errors 0.

GATE CONTROLS, both shown to FAIL before being believed. clj-kondo: one unresolved symbol planted at a line I was already editing took the plain form to exit 2 with the warning count moving 0 -> 2 and the finding naming file, line and column; the SAME broken tree under `--fail-level error` exited 0, which is that flag's documented blindness reproduced at tip. Node lane: one assertion broken inside the new parallel test took the lane red, naming the test, with the test and assertion counts otherwise identical to the green run so nothing was truncated. Both restores verified BY EFFECT, not by reading a diff: `git hash-object` in its default form equalled `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` and `git diff --quiet HEAD -- <path>` exited 0. (`--no-filters` returned a well-formed hash naming no object on these `i/lf` files, which is why one form alone is not evidence of a failed restore.)

SCOPE HELD. `implementation/machines/` untouched, and the bead's own reading of the engine is confirmed: `rf.machines/machine-transition` answered correctly on every fixture here and the region-prefixed decl-paths arrive correctly shaped, so the engine was answering properly and the consumer was mis-asking.

NOT FOLDED IN, deliberately, per this item's own "Related, and deliberately kept separate" section: the parallel ROOT `:after` (decl-path `[]`) that lists but reportedly does not fire is a question about the engine rather than about the picker and stays a separate item. Nothing in this change touches root `:after` listing, which `available-after-transitions` still includes at `:decl-path []` exactly as before.

title: ci(nightly): test:xray-feature-gate has failed three consecutive nightlies (09-18, 09-19, 09-20) and the board never saw it — reported only to GitHub issue #10068, outside the beads spine
description:
**`Gate — Xray feature matrix (test:xray-feature-gate)` has failed on THREE consecutive nightlies and nothing on this board carries it.** Found by the mayor during a §5 method reread at trunk `9a670f0d4d`, while checking a claim it had been repeating rather than re-measuring.

## MEASURED, step-level rather than inferred from the run conclusion

| nightly | run id | head sha | failing step |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-18T15:25:31Z | `35362331984` | `2db60e52fd` | `Gate — Xray feature matrix (test:xray-feature-gate)` |
| 2026-09-19T15:22:36Z | `35451619780` | `2db60e52fd` | same step |
| 2026-09-20T15:22:58Z | `35519398372` | `c98567fa89` | same step |

The two nightlies before those — `35240234183` (09-17) and `35115223542` (09-16) — are `completed/success`, so the red has a clean left edge between 09-17T15:26Z and 09-18T15:25Z and this is a regression rather than a long-standing state.

**Taken from the jobs API (`/actions/runs/<id>/jobs`), reading `.steps[]`, NOT from the run-level conclusion.** That distinction is load-bearing: the run is red, and the obvious inference — that the gate everyone is currently worried about is what reddened it — is FALSE. On `35519398372` the failing job is `Browser, bundle, examples, Story/Xray gates`, in which step 21 `test:xray-feature-gate` FAILED while step 22 `Gate — Story static export (test:story-static)` SUCCEEDED. Two gates in one job, opposite verdicts, and only the step view separates them.

## WHY IT WENT UNSEEN, which is the part that generalises

**It is reported, just not anywhere this project looks.** `.github/workflows/expensive-tests.yml` ends with a job `Nightly result -> tracking issue`, which is working correctly and maintains GitHub issue **#10068 "Nightly `expensive tests` is red"** — open, last updated `2026-09-20T15:40:51Z`, minutes after that run finished.

So the failure is not silent. It is announced on a surface OUTSIDE the beads tracker, which this project treats as its single spine — and the coordinator's board, `bd ready`, and every dispatch decision read the spine and never the issue tracker. **A report nobody reads is operationally identical to no report**, and it fails in the reassuring direction twice over: whoever built the tracking-issue job can point at a working mechanism, and whoever reads the beads board sees nothing wrong.

This is a SIBLING of rf2-5dihy rather than a duplicate. That item is about a gate that did not RUN and so produced no verdict; this is a gate that ran, produced a red verdict, announced it, and the announcement landed where the spine does not look. Related enough that whoever works either should read both.

## WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED

**The cause is not diagnosed and no fix is proposed here.** Nobody has read the failing step's log. `test:xray-feature-gate` is the Xray feature-matrix gate whose PR-smoke tier runs per-PR and whose full sweep runs nightly (see CLAUDE.md § Build & Test), so a nightly-only failure is consistent with the full sweep covering scenarios the PR-smoke tier does not — but that is a hypothesis stated to be tested, not a finding, and a reader who treats it as one will look in the wrong place.

The `2db60e52fd` sha on two consecutive nightlies is worth a glance: the same head twice means the second run re-tested an unchanged tree, so whatever it is reproduces deterministically rather than flaking.

## FIRST STEPS FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT

Read the failing step's log from the per-job endpoint (`/actions/jobs/<job-id>/logs`) rather than `gh run view --log --job`, which refuses while any sibling job in the run is unfinished even for a job that has completed — and these runs are complete, so either works, but the per-job form is the one that always does. Then decide whether the fix belongs to the gate or to the code it grades.
notes:
## DIAGNOSED 2026-09-21 — first bad commit `98f5405256` (rf2-c4abp), proven by a one-line A/B

**The cause is `98f5405256` "fix(xray): Machines resolves a pinned no-epoch bundle to no record (rf2-c4abp)", and the production fix is CORRECT — what it removed was a head-fallback the deep-machine gate scenario had been passing on by ACCIDENT.** No fix landed: the repair is not unambiguous (see FENCE below).

### The two local readings, both captured in the worker's own worktree off `bbec956c10`

| attempt | tree | captured exit | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | unmodified `bbec956c10` | **1** | 15 PASS, `FAIL deep machine inspector substrate` |
| 2 | same tree, ONE line reverted | **0** | 16 scenarios, **0 failures** |

The reverted line is `machine_inspector_helpers.cljc`'s `focused-epoch-record` body, put back to the pre-rf2-c4abp 2-arity call. Nothing else changed; the plant was in the build graph (deep-machine recompiled 13 namespaces). Restored afterwards and verified by blob hash against the committed object (`git hash-object` default form == `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>`, tree clean, `git diff --quiet HEAD` exit 0).

Attempt 1's diag is byte-shape-identical to nightly `35519398372`'s: `dbPresent false`, `epochCount 0`, `traceEventCount 0`, `transitionEvents []`, `focus null`, `inspectorBlankPresent true`, all four mount counts 0.

**NOTE for anyone re-running this: the harness reported "exit code 0" for BOTH runs while the captured exit files read 1 and 0. Quote the captured number.**

### The mechanism, end to end

1. `:rf.xray/machine-transitions-for-focused-event` reads `[:rf.xray/focus]` — the COMPOSED focus from `spine/compose-focus`, not the stored `:focus` slot.
2. In `:live` + unpaused mode with a non-nil effective dispatch-id, `compose-focus`'s 4-arity RE-DERIVES `:epoch-id` as `(epoch-id-for-event-bundle epoch-history eff-id)`, discarding the stored slot's `:epoch-id`.
3. The gate scenario seeds a SYNTHETIC one-record `:epoch-history` (`:epoch-id 9999`) and writes `:epoch-id 9999` into the `:focus` slot via `:rf.xray/set-focus-epoch-id-for-test`. But by then the testbed has real trace traffic, so `eff-id` is the REAL head dispatch-id, which does not occur in the synthetic history — so the composed `:epoch-id` comes back **nil** while `:dispatch-id` is non-nil.
4. `focused-epoch-record` then calls `focus/find-epoch-record`. Pre-rf2-c4abp (2-arity) that hit the head-fallback branch `(and (nil? epoch-id) (seq history))` and returned `(peek history)` — which, the history holding exactly one synthetic record, happened to BE epoch 9999. The chart rendered. Post-rf2-c4abp (3-arity) the new first branch `(and (nil? focus-epoch-id) (some? focus-dispatch-id))` returns **nil** — no record, no transition rows, `blank-state`, no chart.

**So the scenario never actually focused epoch 9999. It was rescued every run by a head-fallback landing on the only record in the vector.** That is why this broke without any change to the chart, the machines-viz re-export shims, or the panel's rendering — and why the gate's own message names the wrong first suspect.

**And it is why 1314 JVM/DOM tests stayed green through rf2-c4abp.** In a unit/DOM test the trace buffer is empty, so `head-id` and therefore `eff-id` are nil, `compose-focus`'s live branch is not taken, and the stored slot's `:epoch-id` survives — the seeding event works there. Only a surface with LIVE traffic plus a seeded history can reach the broken state, and the nightly-full sweep holds the only one (the scenario is not `smoke: true`, which is the whole of why it is nightly-only).

### A REAL contradiction between two committed designs — this is the part that outlives the gate

`spine.cljs`'s `compose-focus` documents, in the comment on the very branch that returns nil, that it does so deliberately and that **"Panels uniformly treat nil as 'no pin, use the head fallback' (App-DB Diff's `(peek history)`, Views' `(dec (count history))`, Machine Inspector's `(peek history)`)"**. rf2-c4abp removed exactly that fallback for the Machine Inspector whenever a `:dispatch-id` is pinned — and in LIVE+unpaused mode one always is. So either that comment is now stale prose, or App-DB Diff and Views still rely on a contract the Machine Inspector has left.

Worth deciding explicitly, because the two cases arrive in the SAME shape `{:epoch-id nil, :dispatch-id <non-nil>}` and `:mode` does not separate them (clicking the HEAD bundle keeps `:live`): (a) the operator pinned a bundle that settled no epoch — rf2-c4abp's target, blank is right; (b) LIVE head-tracking where the head's settling epoch is not in the currently-keyed `epoch-history` — which `compose-focus`'s own comment names as routine under a multi-frame picker or ring eviction.

### FENCE — why no fix landed

The natural repairs both fall outside "unambiguous and confined":
- Making `:rf.xray/set-focus-epoch-id-for-test` stamp `:mode :retro` so the seed actually pins would change a test affordance with **seven** other consumers (four DOM/unit test files, a registry catalogue row, a registry test and the gate).
- Fixing the scenario's injection is an edit to `testbeds/feature_matrix/scenarios.cjs`, the feature-matrix gate's own harness.
- Restoring a mode-aware head-fallback in `focused-epoch-record` reopens a production discriminator rf2-c4abp landed deliberately with tests.

### THREE INCIDENTAL DEFECTS FOUND, none fixed

1. **The gate's failure diagnostics are structurally uninformative.** The diag block reads `re_frame.core.get_frame_db`, a name DELETED by the frame-affordance API shrink — `implementation/core/test/re_frame/capture_frame_test.clj`'s `removed-public-names-are-absent` pins its absence. Measured in the compiled deep-machine bundle: `get_frame_db` occurs in **0** files against a control of **20** carrying `dispatch_BANG_`. So `db` is unconditionally null and `dbPresent`/`focus`/`epochCount`/`focusedRecordKeys`/`traceEventCount`/`transitionEvents` are FORCED to their empty values on every failure, whatever the app actually holds. They are one signal reported five ways, not five signals. `inspectorBlankPresent` is the only independent field in the block — and it was the one that mattered. `ok: true` means ONLY that `window.cljs.core` and `window.re_frame.core` both resolved and the probe ran to completion; it is not a health statement about anything.
2. **The failure message cites a bead that does not exist.** `rf2-bz72m` is named in the thrown message and used as an id prefix in three synthetic values; it matches **0** of 1928 beads and **0** lines of the tracker export.
3. **The scenario's stated purpose is not what the gate measures.** Its comment says the probe proves "the shims survive `:advanced` compilation", but `serve-and-run-xray-feature-gate.cjs` invokes `shadow-cljs compile` and the token `release` occurs **0** times in that file — the testbeds are built in development mode, so nothing here exercises `:advanced` at all.
## RESOLVED 2026-09-21 — the contradiction is settled: `compose-focus`'s comment was STALE

PR #10142. The repair is (b), the scenario, landed through a PRODUCTION affordance. rf2-c4abp is NOT reverted and its discriminator is NOT reopened.

### The decisive measurement the fence asked for

The fence asked which of two holds: is `compose-focus`'s comment stale, or do App-DB Diff and Views still rely on the head-fallback contract the Machine Inspector left? **The comment is stale, and the Machine Inspector was the LAST of five panels to leave, not the first.** Read at tip, not inferred from the comment:

| panel | site at tip | shape for `{:epoch-id nil, :dispatch-id non-nil}` | left at |
|---|---|---|---|
| Epoch | `epoch_panel.cljs:295` | 3-arity, no record | rf2-y8doi.19 (led) |
| Trace | `trace.cljs:1283` | 3-arity, no record | rf2-c4abp `bc741cb23a` (2026-09-18 07:19:48) |
| Machine Inspector | `machine_inspector_helpers.cljc:1061` | 3-arity, no record | rf2-c4abp `98f5405256` (same second) |
| Issues ribbon | `registry.cljs:990` | 3-arity, no record | rf2-hiri8 `fe96e0acaa` (2026-09-18 14:12:38) |
| Views | `reactive_panel_subs.cljs:172` | 3-arity, no record | rf2-hiri8 `fe96e0acaa` |
| App-DB Diff | `app_db_diff_subs.cljs` | **never had a head fallback** | n/a |

App-DB Diff does not use the shared resolver at all. Its inlined `find-epoch-in-history` is guarded `(when (some? epoch-id) ...)` so a nil id yields nil, `:value` falls back to the live db and `:before` is nil; its own comment says in terms that "`(peek history)` is NOT a fallback here — the App-DB diff follows the FOCUSED epoch". Checked with `git log -S 'peek history'` on that file: it never carried one.

The comment was written 2026-05-19 under rf2-70tkv (`87d71807f8`) and last touched 2026-07-04 by an unrelated rename. It described a world that ended in stages across 2026-09-18. It is wrong in three separate ways — wrong about App-DB Diff, wrong about Views, wrong about Machine Inspector — and the `(dec (count history))` it attributes to Views is not in Views at all: that spelling lives in `machine_inspector.cljs`'s `step-focus`, a keyboard prev/next anchor, not a record lookup.

The only 2-arity callers left in `tools/xray/src` are the 2-arity's own delegation in `focus_resolver.cljc:148` and `install-legacy-reactive-data-sub-for-test!`, which models predecessor code deliberately and whose docstring says it "must not be `fixed`".

**Therefore repair (c) is refuted by measurement.** Restoring a mode-aware head fallback would make the Machine Inspector the only panel of six answering the head for a pinned no-epoch bundle, reversing a deliberate three-commit convergence. The panels are right; the comment was the defect. It is corrected in this PR — leaving it standing is what invites the next reader to reach for (c), which is exactly what happened here.

### Why not (a)

Making `:rf.xray/set-focus-epoch-id-for-test` stamp `:mode :retro` would change a shared seeding seam with seven other consumers so that a seeding event lies about mode for all of them, to paper over one scenario's incomplete setup. The affordance is not at fault: it does exactly what its name and the registry catalogue say, writing the `:focus` SLOT.

### The repair (b)

The scenario seeded `:epoch-history` and the slot's `:epoch-id` but left the spine in LIVE + unpaused, where `compose-focus` re-derives `:epoch-id` from the head bundle by design and discards the slot. It now dispatches `:rf.xray/toggle-live-pause` — the production "freeze inspection" gesture `compose-focus`'s own docstring names, bound to Space in `keybinding.cljs` — BEFORE the seed.

**Order is load-bearing and is the non-obvious part**: `toggle-live-pause-reducer` stamps the PRE-TOGGLE composed `:epoch-id` into the slot (rf2-fzbj.2), so pausing AFTER the seed would overwrite 9999 with the nil derived from head. Pause first, seed second. Paused LIVE composes from the stored slot, so the panel resolves record 9999 by an actual `:epoch-id` MATCH — no fallback, no accident.

A read-back assertion on the `:focus` slot now requires `:paused?` true, `:epoch-id` 9999 and a one-record history before the chart assertion runs. `toggle-live-pause` is a toggle, so this also catches it running the wrong way, and it converts a silent mis-seed from a 15-second chart timeout blaming the re-export shims into a loud, specific failure.

### Red / green, captured numbers

All three runs local, full nightly sweep, same command, same worktree; the gate names its own config root in its first lines and it is this worktree.

| attempt | tree | captured exit | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | unmodified trunk | **1** | 15 PASS, `FAIL deep machine inspector substrate`; diag byte-shape-identical to nightly `35519398372` |
| 2 | with the fix | **0** | 16 scenarios, 0 failures, 13 matrix rows |
| 3 | fix + planted fault | **1** | sabotage witness (below) |

Attempt 1's failure message carried the OLD `rf2-bz72m` text, which proves the running process had loaded the pre-edit driver even though the file was edited mid-run — the CommonJS require cache, and a self-proving control on the reproduction.

**The harness reported "exit code 0" for attempt 1, whose captured exit file reads 1.** Third independent sighting of that disagreement on this gate. Quote the captured number.

**Sabotage witness**: swapping the pause for `:rf.xray/follow-head` — a real registered event that clears `:paused?`, i.e. exactly the pre-fix condition — turns the gate red at the new read-back, naming `paused: false`, rather than 15 seconds later at the chart. So the read-back is load-bearing and the pause is what makes the gate green. Restored afterwards and verified by blob hash against the committed object.

### Three incidental defects, all fixed in the same PR

1. **The diag block read `re-frame.core/get-frame-db`, DELETED by the frame-affordance API shrink.** Confirmed live in attempt 1's own output: `dbPresent: false`, `focus: null`, `epochCount: 0`, `focusedRecordKeys: null`, `traceEventCount: 0`, `transitionEvents: []` — six fields forced to empty by one dead read, exactly as this bead's notes predicted. Now reads the public `app-db-value` (spec/API.md §Public registrar query API).
2. **`rf2-bz72m` has never existed** — independently re-measured at 0 occurrences in the tracker export against 11 for `rf2-c4abp`, and `bd show` reports no issue found. Removed from the thrown message and from the three synthetic values, which now carry an `xray-feature-gate-` prefix that reads as what it is rather than as a tracker reference.
3. **The `:advanced` claim is false** — `release` occurs 0 times in `serve-and-run-xray-feature-gate.cjs`, which invokes `shadow-cljs compile`, so every surface is a development build. The comment now states what the scenario actually grades and explicitly says NOT to convert the gate to a release build to make the old claim true.

### One correction to this bead's own notes

The notes say rf2-c4abp removed the fallback "for the Machine Inspector" as though it were a lone departure. It was one of a pair in that commit-second (Trace left in `bc741cb23a`), and rf2-hiri8 took Views and the Issues ribbon seven hours later the same day. The convergence is the context that makes (c) clearly wrong, and it is not visible from the Machine Inspector alone.

## THE GATE HAD BEEN GREEN BY ACCIDENT SINCE IT WAS WRITTEN — THAT IS THE FINDING

The first bad commit is `98f5405256` (rf2-c4abp), and **it is a correct production fix that removed an accident rather than introducing a bug.** The scenario never actually focused epoch 9999: `:rf.xray/set-focus-epoch-id-for-test` writes the `:focus` SLOT, but the panel reads the COMPOSED focus, and `compose-focus` in LIVE+unpaused mode re-derives `:epoch-id` from the head bundle — absent from the injected synthetic history, so nil.
