`compose-focus`'s comment claimed panels treat a nil `:epoch-id` as "use the head fallback", naming Machine Inspector's `(peek history)`. Measured at tip, every production consumer now passes the pinned `:dispatch-id` to the 3-arity:

| panel | site | left the fallback at |
|---|---|---|
| Epoch | `epoch_panel.cljs:295` | rf2-y8doi.19 |
| Trace | `trace.cljs:1283` | rf2-c4abp `bc741cb23a` |
| Machine Inspector | `machine_inspector_helpers.cljc:1061` | rf2-c4abp `98f5405256`, same second |
| Issues ribbon | `registry.cljs:990` | rf2-hiri8 `fe96e0acaa` |
| Views | `reactive_panel_subs.cljs:172` | rf2-hiri8 `fe96e0acaa` |
| App-DB Diff | `app_db_diff_subs.cljs` | **never had one** |

**Machine Inspector was the LAST of five to leave, not the first**, and App-DB Diff's `find-epoch-in-history` is guarded `(when (some? epoch-id) …)` with a comment saying in terms that `(peek history)` is not a fallback there; `git log -S` confirms it never carried one. The comment dates from 2026-05-19 (rf2-70tkv) and is wrong three ways — the `(dec (count history))` it attributes to Views is a keyboard-nav anchor in `machine_inspector.cljs`, not a record lookup.

**This breadth is what refutes repair (c).** Restoring a mode-aware fallback would have made Machine Inspector the only panel of six answering the head for a pinned no-epoch bundle, reversing a deliberate three-commit convergence. The mayor was sceptical of (c) on instinct; the measurement is what settles it.

## THE REPAIR: (b), AND THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING

The scenario now dispatches `:rf.xray/toggle-live-pause` — the production gesture `compose-focus`'s own docstring names — **before** the seed. That order matters: the reducer stamps the pre-toggle composed `:epoch-id` into the slot, so pausing after the seed would overwrite 9999 with nil. The stale `spine.cljs` comment was corrected in the same change, because leaving it is what invites the next reader to reach for (c).

(a) lost because it would make a seeding seam lie about mode for a spread of other consumers, to cover one scenario's incomplete setup.

## NUMBERS, EACH CAPTURED BY THE WORKER

| tree | captured exit | result |
|---|---|---|
| unmodified | **1** | 15 PASS, 1 FAIL, diag identical to nightly `35519398372` |
| with fix | **0** | 16 scenarios, 0 failures |
| fix + planted fault | **1** | red at the new read-back |
| after rebase onto `2aa4f8aa99` | **0** | 16 scenarios, 0 failures |
| `npm run test:cljs` | **0** | 12407 tests, 62289 assertions, 0 failures |

**The harness reported "exit code 0" for BOTH runs that captured 1.** The trap held again, on this exact gate, for the second worker running. Attempt 1's failure carried the OLD `rf2-bz72m` text, which proves the process had the pre-edit driver — a self-proving control.

## THREE SECONDARY DEFECTS FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE

1. The failure message cited `rf2-bz72m`, **which has never existed** — 0 occurrences across the whole tracker export against a control of 4 for a real id. A diagnostic pointing at a phantom record sends its reader nowhere.
2. The scenario's comment claimed it proved the shims survive `:advanced`. It does not: `release` occurs 0 times in `serve-and-run-xray-feature-gate.cjs` against a control of 6 in `story-build.cjs`, and the runner invokes `shadow-cljs compile` — development mode throughout. The comment was corrected to say what the scenario actually proves; the gate was NOT converted to a release build.
3. **A fourth defect nobody had listed**: the diag block read `re_frame.core.get_frame_db`, deleted by the frame-affordance API shrink (measured 0 compiled files against a control of 20 for `dispatch_BANG_`), so `db` was unconditionally null and all five of those fields were FORCED. They were one dead read reported five ways, and `inspectorBlankPresent` was the only independent field in the block.

## ONE INSTRUMENT FINDING THAT GENERALISES

**`PASS` line counts are not a scenario census.** The runner gates its per-scenario summary on `if (anyFailed)`, so a fully green run prints ZERO `PASS` lines — the worker's green read 0 where its red read 15. That is CLAUDE.md item (z)'s quiet-reporter shape arriving in a new place: a count that moves the wrong way because a successful path never prints. The worker checked the runner rather than assuming.

## LANE

The shadow-cljs lane was granted to this item and is RELEASED, verified by effect machine-wide with no path filter: `java.exe` 0, all 6 `node.exe` accounted for by parent chain as pre-existing Codex and MCP processes, signature scan 0. The mayor re-verified independently before reporting it free. **`rf2-n440v` and `rf2-1t0d5` were fenced behind this item for that lane and are now unfenced.**

title: Examples review: realworld_http flagship with realworld_shared (7 findings: logout leaves the previous user's settings draft behind and the next account can PUT it; two error branches render nothing; favourite and follow toggles have no in-flight latch)
description:
Filed from the review wave under epic rf2-fn0kx (report realworld-http.md). The report below is the reviewer's, verbatim.

## Project stance (verbatim, from CLAUDE.md)

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

## Worker rules

- Every path:line below was read at the FROZEN review tree named in the report header. Re-verify each cite at the current trunk before editing; the review wave's earlier beads found premises that had moved.
- Act on the findings under the stance: a finding you would not spend a morning on yourself is not one to implement. Where a finding says "decide: A or B", it is Mike's call; hold it and say so in the PR body rather than choosing.
- Fences are full repo-relative paths. Hot-zone files (CLAUDE.md § Workflow) are sequential; if a finding lands in one, say so and wait for the mayor's sequencing.
- The shadow-cljs build lane is a machine-wide exclusive granted by the mayor: ask before any build, and prefer static checks and the JVM lanes.
- Examples stay test-free (rf2-8cevm). Skills gates live in scripts/check_skill_*.py; run the ones that name your surface and say which.
- No AI attribution trailers; the PR body carries a "## Quality gates" section naming what ran and its exit codes.

---

# Senior review: real-apps/realworld_http (+ realworld_shared)

Reviewer persona: senior app engineer tracing every RealWorld user flow end to end (event -> handler -> fx -> db -> subs -> view) against the Conduit API contract and Spec 014 managed HTTP
Tree: skills-review-sep21 worktree, trunk b60a20abca
Scope read: examples/real-apps/realworld_http — all 16 tracked files in full (13 .cljs/.cljc, README.md, index.html, default-avatar.svg; ~6,400 lines) + examples/real-apps/realworld_shared — all 5 files in full (schema, http, demo_backend, avatar, markdown; ~1,100 lines); examples/README.md, examples/TESTING.md
Surfaces the examples teach, consulted: spec/014-HTTPRequests.md (args table, §Reply addressing, §Failure categories, §Retry, §Privacy), spec/005-StateMachines.md (unhandled-event no-op, §Registration sub-event routing), spec/013-Flows.md (`:rf.fx/reg-flow` triple), implementation/http/src (handlers.cljc, middleware.cljc, test_support.cljc, machine_wrapper.cljc, reply.cljc), implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc (`route-inner-event`), implementation/routing/src/re_frame/routing/strategy.cljc (`with-base-path`, `strip-base-path`), examples/scripts/serve-example.cjs, examples-staging.cjs, examples-asset-manifest.cjs; docs pages linking here (docs/async/http.md, docs/async/examples.md, docs/routing/examples.md, docs/core/how-to/add-auth.md, docs/core/how-to/build-a-form.md, spec/Pattern-Forms.md, spec/Pattern-RemoteData.md, skills/re-frame2/examples-map.md)
Checks run: `node implementation/scripts/check-examples-compile.cjs --list` exit 0 — `examples/realworld` listed (58 builds); `node examples/scripts/check-examples-assets.cjs` exit 0 — 33 pages resolve, realworld's `default-avatar.svg` staged per manifest; `git log` on the slice (last touch a02f272809, rf2-fzbj.21)

## Findings, ranked

### 1. Logout leaves the previous user's settings draft (and feed) behind; the settings machine ignores `:load` from `:correct` / `:incorrect`  [CONFIRMED] [severity: high] [kind: correctness] [size: S]
- Where: examples/real-apps/realworld_http/settings.cljs:216-259 (state table), :286-302 (`:settings/initialise`, `:settings/load`); examples/real-apps/realworld_http/auth.cljs:400-408 (`:clear-session` action); examples/real-apps/realworld_http/favorites.cljs:54-56 (`:feed/initialise`)
- What: `:load` is accepted only in `:neutral` (settings.cljs:221); a settings visit that ended in a successful save (`:correct`, :251-259) or a failed one (`:incorrect`, :228-238) leaves the machine there, and logout (`:clear-session`, auth.cljs:404-408) resets nothing but the auth slice — so the next account to sign in and open `/settings` gets a form pre-filled with the departed user's username / email / bio / image and, on "Update Settings", PUTs them onto its own account.
- Evidence: traced A saves -> `:submit-succeeded` -> `:correct` + `:store-user` re-seeds `:draft` from A (settings.cljs:194-202, :247) -> navigate to profile; A logs out -> auth.cljs:404-408 dispatches only `:auth/clear-session`, `:auth.session/persist nil`, navigate home; B logs in, `/settings` `:on-match [[:settings/load]]` (routing.cljs:82) -> `[:settings/form [:load …]]` -> no `:load` edge in `:correct` -> Spec 005 §"An unhandled event is a silent no-op" (spec/005-StateMachines.md:4663) -> draft stays A's. Grep control: `[:settings/form [:reset]]` is dispatched only at settings.cljs:290 (boot) and :384/:409 (the two refused-reply branches) — never on logout; `[:feed/initialise]` only at core.cljs:93 (boot). The `:begin-submit` comment (settings.cljs:180-185) already documents "`:load` is only accepted from `:neutral`" and works around it for `:session-owner` instead of fixing it. Does not manifest against the demo backend (one user), so the offline tour never shows it; it does against the hosted API the README tells the reader to point at. Secondary, same root: `[:feed :data]` keeps the departed user's feed; the next user's first "Your Feed" click renders it as a `:refreshing` list (articles.cljs:153-155, :385-395) until the fetch lands.
- Action: accept `:load` in every state (it is the route's "I am here now" signal, so `:correct` / `:incorrect` / `:submitting` should all take `{:target :neutral :action :seed-from-user}`), AND have `:clear-session` also dispatch `[:settings/form [:reset]]` and `[:feed/initialise]` so no per-user state outlives the session. One PR.

### 2. Two error branches show nothing: a failed "Delete Article" and a failed profile list fetch  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness] [size: S]
- Where: examples/real-apps/realworld_http/comments.cljs:644-651 (`:article/delete-failed`), :779-794 (`article-page` cond); examples/real-apps/realworld_http/profile.cljs:365-373, :421-428 (list `load-failed`), :801-805 (list render)
- What: `:article/delete-failed` writes `[:article :error]` but `article-page` renders that error only when `(and article-error (nil? article))` (comments.cljs:790) — with the article loaded (which is the only time Delete is clickable) the `article` branch wins and never reads `article-error`, so a rejected delete is a click that does nothing; the handler's own docstring ("sits on screen until the next load", :646-648) is false. Likewise the profile tab: `:profile.articles/load-failed` / `:profile.favorites/load-failed` write `:error` that no sub reads, and the tab renders the official "No articles here yet." empty marker for a fetch that failed.
- Evidence: cond at comments.cljs:779-794 read in full; a same-slug refresh failure is swallowed the same way (deliberately, per :783-787, but the delete case is not a refresh). Grep `profile\.articles/error|profile\.favorites/error|:profile/error` over realworld_http: only `:profile/error` exists (profile.cljs:605) and is read (:744) — the two list errors have no reader. Control: the banner error path IS rendered (`profile-error`, :742-746).
- Action: in the `article` branch render `(when article-error [:ul.error-messages [:li article-error]])` beside the banner; add `:profile.articles/error` / `:profile.favorites/error` (through `list-for-current-profile`) and show the message in place of the empty-feed marker when the active list's status is `:error`. S.

### 3. The favourite toggle and the article-page follow have no in-flight latch, though profile.cljs argues at length that the toggle must be serialised  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: consistency] [size: S]
- Where: examples/real-apps/realworld_http/favorites.cljs:157-203 (`:article/toggle-favorite`, `:article/favorite-synced`); examples/real-apps/realworld_http/comments.cljs:556-603 (`:article/toggle-follow-author`); contrast examples/real-apps/realworld_http/profile.cljs:456-505 (SERIALISING THE TOGGLE) and :507-597
- What: two quick clicks on a heart put a POST and a DELETE in flight; `:article/favorite-synced` re-seeds the article from whichever reply lands LAST, so out-of-order arrival leaves the card favorited while the server is unfavorited (and a rollback restores a `prior` captured mid-race). profile.cljs spends 50 lines establishing exactly this ("arrival order is not intent order") and latches its follow on `:profile.follow-pending`; the same app's other two optimistic toggles — one of them the README's headline example — take no such precaution and say nothing about why.
- Evidence: favorites.cljs:170-185 snapshots `prior` and fires; :188-197 replaces the article wholesale from `(:article value)` on every success; no pending set, no `:request-id` (deliberately, per profile.cljs:449-454 — abort-mid-write is not proof). Demo backend replies FIFO at 20 ms (demo_backend.cljs:62-67, 573-581) so it cannot reproduce offline; a real network can. README §Optimistic updates (README.md:44) presents all three as one shape.
- Action: decide — (A) mirror the profile latch for favourites (a slug-keyed `:favorite-pending` set: refuse a second click, disable the button, release unconditionally on either settle; ~30 lines, and the article-page follow can reuse `:profile.follow-pending` keyed by author username), or (B) keep favourites unlatched and say so in the favorites.cljs rationale block (:133-155), which currently explains why the ROLLBACKS differ but not why the RACE policy does. The stance leans (A) for the flagship: the app has already argued the latch is necessary.

### 4. A profile identity change renders a blank "loaded" banner (and can show "Edit Profile Settings" to a logged-out visitor); the home tag switch shows the old tag's list under the new URL  [CONFIRMED] [severity: medium] [kind: correctness] [size: S]
- Where: examples/real-apps/realworld_http/profile.cljs:268-287 (`:profile/load`), :194-207 (`:refreshing`), :647-650 (`:profile/own-profile?`), :752-785 (`profile-loaded`); examples/real-apps/realworld_http/articles.cljs:251-272, :153-155; the right shape is examples/real-apps/realworld_http/article_editor.cljs:331-338
- What: on `/profile/alice` -> `/profile/bob`, `:profile/load` correctly resets the slice to `:data nil` but broadcasts only `:fetch-started`; the machine's `:data` region is in `:loaded` and goes to `:refreshing`, which is tagged `:data/loaded`, so `:profile/render` says `:loaded` and `profile-loaded` renders with `profile` nil — an empty `h4`, a "Follow " button with no name, and (because `:profile/own-profile?` compares `nil` with `nil`) an "Edit Profile Settings" link for a logged-out reader — until bob lands. The list under it shows "No articles here yet." for the same window. The home page has the sibling defect in the other direction: `/tag/demo` -> `/tag/clojure` keeps demo's rows on screen under clojure's header while `:refreshing`, which is the "renderable under the wrong URL" state the file's own CORRELATION GATE prose forbids.
- Evidence: `refresh?` false -> `(request-slice)` (:272) -> `:fetch-started` from `:loaded` -> `:refreshing` (:206) tagged `#{:data/loaded …}` (:199) -> render-priority (:663-667) picks `:loaded`; `profile-loaded` has no nil guard (:755-785); `own-profile?` has none either, unlike `:article/own?` (comments.cljs:667-673, `(and me …)`). The editor already does the right thing — `:editor/load-article` broadcasts `:reset` before `:use-edit`/`:fetch-started` with a comment saying why (article_editor.cljs:331-338). Demo delay is 20 ms so this is a flash offline and a real blank on a network.
- Action: when `refresh?` is false, dispatch `[:ui/profile [:reset]]` before `:fetch-started` (and `[:realworld/articles-home [:reset]]` in `:articles/load` when the tag changes — or reset `[:articles :data]` on a tag change the way `:article/load` resets on a slug change); guard `:profile/own-profile?` with `(and me …)`. S.

### 5. `<base href="/">` and `with-base-path "/realworld"` disagree, and no runner serves the app under `/realworld/`  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: teaching-drift] [size: S]
- Where: examples/real-apps/realworld_http/index.html:5-13; examples/real-apps/realworld_http/routing.cljs:18-20, :241-254; examples/real-apps/realworld_http/core.cljs:361-368; the rule it breaks is stated in examples/capabilities/routing/routing/index.html:12-14
- What: the routing example's own host page says "under a sub-path deployment this becomes `<base href="/my-app/">`, with `with-base-path` on the frame's `:url-strategy` so the two agree"; here the page pins `<base href="/">` while the strategy pins `/realworld`, and routing.cljs:18 says the example "is served from a sub-path" when nothing does.
- Evidence: `dev:example` (implementation/package.json:54 -> examples/scripts/serve-example.cjs) serves the staged dir at `/` with a document fallback (serve-example.cjs:225-305); grep `realworld` over examples/scripts finds only staging/manifest comments — no mount at `/realworld/`. So at first load `strip-base-path` passes `/` through unchanged (strategy.cljc:260-281) and the app works, but the first in-app navigation `:encode`s the base back on (strategy.cljc:373) and the address bar hops from `/` to `/realworld/article/…`; under a genuine `/realworld/` mount, `<base href="/">` would resolve `main.js` to `/main.js`. A copier who takes both lines gets a sub-path deployment that cannot load its bundle. The resources twin carries the same pair with `/realworld-resources`.
- Action: decide — drop `with-base-path` (the app then matches its `<base>`, the runner, and the routing example's default), or set `<base href="/realworld/">` and have the runner mount it there. Either is one line per app; do both twins together.

### 6. README drift: "default reply addressing", "19 app-db paths", and two cancel events presented as wired  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: readme-drift] [size: S]
- Where: examples/real-apps/realworld_http/README.md:61 (Files row for `comments.cljs`), :46, :21; examples/real-apps/realworld_http/articles.cljs:324-330; examples/real-apps/realworld_http/favorites.cljs:87-93
- What: (a) the Files table says "`:article/load` uses default reply addressing" — it uses an explicit `:reply-to` (comments.cljs:283), and Spec 014 says the co-located default is retired and omitting every target fails loud (spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:598), so the sentence teaches a retired idiom by name and contradicts README:17 two screens up; (b) "all 19 app-db paths" — `app-db-schemas` (schema.cljs:271-296) has 20 entries; (c) README:21 and both docstrings ("say the user wanders off the home page before it lands") present `:articles/cancel` / `:feed/cancel` as the abort affordance, but nothing dispatches them.
- Evidence: grep `:auth/dismiss|:articles/cancel|:feed/cancel` over examples/: only the three definitions and their own docstrings (articles.cljs:233,324; favorites.cljs:60,87); control: `[:articles/load]` is dispatched at tags.cljs:276 and `[:feed/load]` at :275. Counted the schema map by hand: 20 keys.
- Action: fix the two sentences; either dispatch the cancels from a route-leave (`:can-leave`-style) or delete the two events so a copier does not inherit dead abort plumbing. S.

### 7. Error views `pr-str` a string (quotes rendered around every message); `failure->message` misses the closed set's `:rf.http/cors` arm  [CONFIRMED] [severity: low] [kind: ergonomics] [size: S]
- Where: examples/real-apps/realworld_http/articles.cljs:500; examples/real-apps/realworld_http/comments.cljs:792, :866; examples/real-apps/realworld_http/profile.cljs:746; examples/real-apps/realworld_shared/http.cljs:129-139
- What: every list/article/profile error renders `(pr-str <string>)`, so the user sees `Couldn't load articles: "Network error — please try again."` with literal quotes — and a copier copies it. The shared projection's `case` has no `:rf.http/cors` arm although the README (README.md:23) sells it as an exhaustive `case` over the closed set, and Spec 014's closed set includes `:rf.http/cors` (spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:483-503); a CORS failure — the first thing a reader hits when pointing at the hosted API from a dev origin — prints the generic "Request failed."
- Evidence: `failure->message` always returns a string (http.cljs:129-139); the four `pr-str` sites read in place. `:rf.http/cors` absent from the `case` (http.cljs:130-138); control: `:rf.http/timeout` present at :132.
- Action: `str` instead of `pr-str` at the four sites; add `:rf.http/cors "Blocked by the browser's cross-origin policy — check the API's CORS configuration."`. Shared file, so both apps benefit. S.

## Per-example census
- `examples/realworld` (examples/real-apps/realworld_http): 7 findings above (1 high, 3 medium, 3 low); README DRIFTS (finding 6: "default reply addressing", 19 vs 20 paths, cancel events); roster: listed (compile sweep `--list` and asset manifest, `default-avatar.svg` staged); index.html matches the manifest but see finding 5 for the `<base>` / base-path contradiction.
- `realworld_shared` (examples/real-apps/realworld_shared; no build id, shared model): 1 finding touches it (7, cors arm); no README of its own. Both apps' usage is consistent with its exports — resources uses `ws/User`, `ws/SessionUser`, all six `wh/*` helpers, `demo/fresh-state`, `demo/respond`, `avatar/avatar-src`, `md/render` (grep over realworld_resources, 44 sites), every one defined in shared; both apps `dissoc :token` before storing the session as `SessionUser` documents (auth.cljs:130 here, realworld_resources/auth.cljs:150). Nothing in shared assumes one app's layer: `demo-backend/respond` steps the state on the RAW args-map (demo_backend.cljs:572) and then delegates to the framework canned fx, which are the only implicit coupling (each app must load `re-frame.http.test-support`; both do). One consequence worth knowing, not a finding: because the stub steps the backend before the canned fx runs the `:before` chain (test_support.cljc:63-81), the demo backend never sees the bearer header, so its `GET /user` session check (demo_backend.cljs:413-416) is unreachable offline — which coincides with the documented "never auto-restores" behaviour.

## Considered, left alone
- `:auth/dismiss` (auth.cljs:435) is an edge nothing dispatches (control: `:auth/logout` dispatched at core.cljs:194 and settings.cljs:508); harmless dead transition.
- A signed-in user submitting `/register`: the machine's `:authed` state has no `:auth/register` / `:auth/failure` edge, so a failed register shows no error; Conduit's reference client redirects signed-in users off `/register`, and the success path still works.
- `:auth.login-form/field-error` / register `field-error` subs exist but no validation ever fills `:errors`; cheap dead code, and the forms are deliberately server-validated.
- `:article/toggle-favorite` / `:profile/follow` while logged out navigate to login without stashing `:return-to` (favorites.cljs:168-169); the entry-denied recipe covers the routes that matter and the README does not promise more.
- Switching to "Your Feed" for the first time renders `:refreshing` over an empty list ("Refreshing…" with no rows) rather than the loading placeholder, because `:clear-count` resets the count but not the `:data` region (articles.cljs:169); cosmetic, and finding 4's `:reset` fixes it as a side effect if applied to the home machine too.

## Instruments and controls
- Grep `:auth/dismiss|:articles/cancel|:feed/cancel` over examples/: 3 definitions + docstrings only; control `[:articles/load]` dispatched at tags.cljs:276.
- Grep `profile\.articles/error|profile\.favorites/error|:profile/error` over realworld_http: only `:profile/error` (profile.cljs:605, read at :744); the two list-error subs are absent.
- Grep `\[:settings/form \[:reset\]\]|\[:feed/initialise\]|\[:settings/load\]` over realworld_http: reset at settings.cljs:290/384/409, feed init at core.cljs:93, load only from routing.cljs:82 — none on logout.
- Grep `realworld|basePath|base path|fallback` over examples/scripts: no `/realworld/` mount; serve-example.cjs:225-305 read for the root-served document fallback.
- Grep `with-base-path|<base href` over examples/: routing example index.html:12-14 states the agree-rule; realworld pair pins `/` + `/realworld` and `/` + `/realworld-resources`.
- Read implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc:98-116 (`route-inner-event`): a reply appended to `[:auth/flow [:auth/failure]]` is conj'd onto the inner vector, so `:record-error`'s `[_ {:keys [error]}]` (auth.cljs:379-381) does receive the envelope — the login/register error path is sound.
- Read spec/014-HTTPRequests.md:142-150 (args table): `:decode` accepts a Malli schema, `:retry` shape and closed `:on` set, `:request-id` vectors, `:sensitive?` under `:request` — all match `rh/request` (http.cljs:128-164) and every call site; §Reply addressing :587-630 matches the `:reply-to` use at comments.cljs:283.
- Read implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc:49-133: canned stubs run the `:before` chain, so `:realworld/bearer-auth` (core.cljs:321-326, 445-447) does fire on the canned path; the demo stub steps its backend before that (http.cljs:274-275).
- Grep `realworld-shared\.[ns]/name` (as `(ws|wh|demo|avatar|md)/…`) over realworld_resources: 44 usage sites, every referenced name defined in realworld_shared.
- Grep `dissoc user :token` over realworld_resources: auth.cljs:150 (control for the shared `SessionUser` contract).

The bead cited `SKILL.md:91-100` and `README.md:154-155`. title: Incomplete dry-run documentation: README still promises no observable effects
description:
PR #10265 (f2f9f8459120d473589bec252eba84f27a69c73e) correctly names replace-frame-state! as dispatch-dry-run rollback, but the README correction remains incomplete: tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/README.md:43 still promises a STRUCTURAL no-effect guarantee and says its contract is no observable effect.

That unconditional promise is false. skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:2013-2098 dispatches the reducer/interceptors with declared fx bodies suppressed, then calls replace-frame-state! to restore the captured frame-state. The simulation and synthetic rollback remain observable in the bounded epoch history; listeners execute and arbitrary handler/listener side effects are outside the sink guarantee. The current tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/dispatch_dry_run.cljs:2-17 and spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md:1279-1347 already explain these bounds. A caller relying on the README to mean that listeners or recording cannot observe a simulation is misled.

Required correction: make the existing README row promise suppression of declared fx plus restoration of pre-call frame-state on success; briefly state that diagnostic history/listeners remain observable and arbitrary handler/listener side effects are outside the guarantee, or link to the existing limitations. Preserve the ungated tool policy. This is a small prose correction, not a request for runtime isolation, another gate, or an API change.

Validation: compare the corrected sentence to the runtime and the existing tool docstring/spec limitation; no behavior test is needed for wording alone. No exact open finding recorded this defect when the audit searched the live open ledger.
notes: Merged-PR audit #10271 (86eaeceb970f9cad961aff7f5bb9a5d083a40e1a; merged 2026-09-23T03:39:25Z). Completeness: The single README row now covers every correction requested by rf2-f9p0v: declared-fx suppression, restoration of captured frame-state on success, diagnostic-history/listener observability, arbitrary side-effect limits, and a link to existing edge cases. Ungated tool policy is preserved. Correctness: Compared the new row with dispatch-dry-run runtime effect-sink binding and post-simulation replace-frame-state!, the current tool docstring, and the catalogue Edge cases heading/limitations. The guarantee is now scoped accurately; no behavioral/API change is implied. The relative file and edge-cases anchor exist. Implementation quality: Small documentation-only correction with existing detail linked instead of duplicated. Static source and target-heading verification is sufficient for this audit; no runtime suite rerun. The source Bead was already closed by the implementation workflow and its status/history are preserved. Actionable findings: none. Existing finding updates: none.
close_reason:
DONE — merged as PR #10271, one row of tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/README.md (1 insertion / 1 deletion). No runtime, docstring or spec change.

Frozen review tree `C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2-worktrees/review-sep23`, detached at `034d0c8fc87a0331e8803ff3f82d6f3b15e9b914`, clean.

### Method

1. Read all primary source.
2. Traced the subscribe hit and miss paths, the build, the declared-input release, on-dispose eviction, the render-owned claim (rf2-ty246 / rf2-kk986), hot-reload and generation invalidation, and `compute-sub` and its cycle guard, all against Spec 006.
3. Traced the view registration pipeline, the frame boundaries, the annotation walk, and the derivation graph composer and egress.
4. Ran four bounded, one-shot JVM probes: `clojure -M` run from the scratch dir, with `-Sdeps {:paths [<frozen implementation/core/src>]}`, so nothing was written into the tree. Each probe carried controls in both directions.
5. Searched the tracker from a `bd export` redirected into the scratch dir, selecting issue records by identity in Python. `bd search` matches titles only, so it was not used for this.

### Findings

| Bead | P | Title |
|---|---|---|
| rf2-3x7nj.3.1 | P2 | ratom render-owned claims retain every disposed sub reaction an owner ever read (unbounded, production) |
| rf2-3x7nj.3.2 | P3 | dev annotation walk treats `:r>` / `:f>` interop roots as DOM tags and displaces the component (crash / blank render in dev only) |
| rf2-3x7nj.3.3 | P3 | `live-derivation-graph` throws (whole graph lost) when any live edge carries a float or fn query-vector arg |
| rf2-3x7nj.3.4 | P3 | egress opaque resource handles are a 32-bit `String.hashCode` digest: they collide (merging nodes) and are not one-way |
| rf2-3x7nj.3.5 | P3 | egress resource-identity projection misfires on live sub nodes whose query vector is `[kw kw map]` |

Evidence class:

- .1 inspected. It is a CLJS-only path, with the retention chain read down to the stock Reagent 2.0.1 `Reaction` source.
- .2 executed on the JVM twin, which shares the predicate and the splice. The CLJS copy was inspected.
- .3, .4 and .5 executed.

### Considered and rejected

- **`views.cljs:156-165` `seen-render-keys`** gains one `[view-id token]` per mounted instance for the whole process and is never evicted on unmount. It is dev-only (`debug-enabled?`), costs a tiny amount per entry, and fixture reset clears it. Not worth a morning.
- **`frame_boundary.cljs:348-350`** compares opts with `=`, so opts carrying fresh closures (an inline `:fx-overrides` fn, an inline image) raise `:rf.error/frame-root-reconfigured` on any parent re-render. That fail-loud is deliberate (rf2-nyea0r amendment 4), the error is loud rather than silent, and the fix is to hoist the value. Trust the programmer.
- **Form-2 `reg-view`s.** After the first render, Reagent calls the inner fn directly, bypassing `frame-aware-view`. Re-renders therefore lose `*render-key*`, the handler scope, the deref sink and the `:rf.view/render*` traces. This is tooling-only: frame resolution still works through the class's `:contextType`, and Form-1 is canonical.
- **`*view-deref-sink*` is a vector** (`views.cljs:565`), so `:rf.view/deref-subs` can repeat a query even though its docstring says "union". Trace cosmetics.
- **A parent cached over a not-yet-registered input stays nil after the input's FIRST registration?** Handled. The registration hook dirties the live-frame projection, the generation diff classes the id `:added`, and `invalidate-frame-subs!` clause (a) evicts the parent. This is pinned by `subs_generation_refresh_cljs_test.cljc` `first-registered-late-input-reaches-a-cached-parent`.
- **CLJS `opaque-handle`** renders a negative hash as `-hex`, because `bit-and` yields a signed int32, while the JVM renders unsigned hex. Handles need only be stable within one process, and the fix for .4 subsumes this.
- **`sub-cache-snapshot` / `sub-cache-algebra-view` deref app reactions with `@r`.** Called from Xray's sub body on a ratom substrate, those derefs are captured by Xray's reaction. That is a tools-side concern, and it is not a functional leak, because eviction on unmount now runs through the ref-count release.
- **`graph.cljc:30-33` promises "the explicit sentinel at the foot of this ns"**, which does not exist. The real control is `check-bundle-isolation.cjs`'s emitted-module grep, which `egress.cljc:432-456` documents. Comment drift that misleads nobody.
- **`project-resource-inputs` also opaques a static resource node's `[:param :rf.params]` / `[:scope :rf.scope/global]` markers.** Static graphs carry no secrets. Cosmetic.
- **An owner keeps its claim until the owner disposes, even after it stops reading the slot.** That inflates `:ref-count` while another reader keeps the slot alive, but it is exactly what Spec 006 §Which lifetime governs a ratom adapter prescribes ("releases it when that owner disposes"). Only the retention of ALREADY-DISPOSED reactions (.1) is a defect.
- **`subscribe-once` inside a Reagent render** is still captured by the render reaction's deref. Harmless, and `subscribe-once` is not a render read.
- **The `compute-sub` `::building` stack is not popped** if the always-on error-emit hook itself throws. Theoretical.

### Considered and rejected (one line each, so nobody re-litigates)
- **Params-derived TAGS ride trace rows verbatim** (e.g. `[:user email]` under `:tags` / `:invalidated-tags`). This is EP-0025's no-propagation rule: tags are author-chosen structural names, and the shape default rides scalars by design.
- **A free `:scope` tag with a SCALAR identity** (`[:rf.scope/session "u-42"]`) rides raw while a coarse-sensitive owner's key copy tokenizes. rf2-1zc33's shape rule tokenizes map identities only, and the canonical scope examples use maps. Edge case.
- **`:patch-summary :target-skipped`** carries pr-str'd targets. They do not leak: it is an unnamed slot, so the map-tokenizing default covers it.
- **A stale-suppressed success for a superseded or cleared mutation drops its `:invalidates`** even though the server committed. Spec 016 §Mutations / §Delivery rule explicitly suppress superseded replies. This is design.
- **Mutation instances (including generated ids) persist until `:rf.mutation/clear`.** This is the spec's failure-state lifetime, and a `{:mutation id}` clear exists.
- **`dangle-rollback-optimistic` (`mutation_runtime.cljc:719-720`) writes a NIL-valued entry** when a conflicted key has vanished before an epoch restore. - **`settle-blocking-timeout` installs freshly-minted timeout entries without reindexing `:owner-index`.** The SSR frame renders once and is destroyed.
- **`:optimistic-tags` matching a no-data entry** (a tombstone keeps its tags) hands the author's `:patch` a nil. Trust the programmer.
- **A same-instance re-execute does not abort the superseded HTTP write.** Cancellation is opportunistic per spec, and rf2-zfr7w rules latest-intent-wins for the flagship.
- **A throwing cache-consequence fn, or a corruption-class target at settle, strands the instance `:pending`.** That is an authoring bug that fails loudly with an error trace.
- **Hydrated route owners ride through.** The hydrated routing `:current` nav-token makes the first client navigation release `[:route prev-id prev-nav-token]` (`route.cljc:1338-1343`), so they are not leaked.
- **Hydration does not re-lower the elision registry for installed entries.** The server already redacted the per-slot `:data` declarations on the wire (`project-entry-data`), so no raw value reaches the client.
- **The durable instance row's copy of `:before`** is not a leak. The epoch record's runtime-db partition is default-redacted off-box, so only the TRACE carrier leaks, and that is rf2-3x7nj.11.1.
- **An in-flight read overwriting an optimistic paint mid-flight** is folded into rf2-3x7nj.11.3 as optional scope.

title: resources-queries: ensure of a stale, already-loaded infinite feed ignores its :refetch policy (page 0 only, no sweep) and marks the whole feed fresh
description:
## Defect

An infinite feed can opt into a `:refetch` policy of `:refetch-all-pages? true` or a `:refetch-window`. That policy is honoured only on a force-new refetch. A feed that is already loaded can also be refreshed through `:rf.resource/ensure`, because it is stale, either invalidated while owner-free or past `:stale-after-ms`. That path refreshes page 0 only and arms no sweep. Its page-0 settle (`entry-replace-page`) then clears `:invalidated-at` for the WHOLE feed while the tail pages still hold pre-invalidation data. The feed reads fresh and not stale, and a later ensure fresh-skips, so the declared policy is silently skipped on the most common re-entry path.

This contradicts spec/016-Resources.md:1617: "Tag invalidation ... marks the feed entry stale by its feed tag → the feed refetches per the refetch rule above on the next ensure." The refetch rule is the `:refetch` policy at 016:1616. The code comment on the branch believes this path cannot happen: "an ensure of an already-loaded feed never reaches this `:else` fresh-load branch (fresh-skip / dedupe handle it)". But fresh-skip declines a stale entry, and dedupe declines when no work is live, so a stale loaded feed does reach the branch.

The default policy is unaffected. It preserves the window and has no sweep, so it behaves the same on both paths. Only feeds that opted in are affected.

## Where

At 034d0c8fc8:
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:676-695`, inside `ensure-load` (320-867). The sweep is armed only under `(and infinite? force-new?)` at line 694. The false reachability comment is at lines 679-682.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc:2890-3044`: `page-succeeded-handler`. It chains `:rf.resource.internal/refetch-page` legs only when a sweep cursor exists.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/state.cljc:1254-1301`: `entry-replace-page`, which clears `:invalidated-at` for the entry.

Public entry points:
- `[:rf.resource/ensure {:resource <infinite-id> ...}]`, including route-resource ensures on navigation, for a loaded feed that is invalidated and owner-free, or time-stale
- `[:rf.resource/invalidate-tags ...]` or a mutation's `:invalidates` while the feed is owner-free

## Failure scenario

1. A feed registered with `:refetch {:refetch-all-pages? true}` has 3 pages loaded under a route owner.
2. The user leaves the route (the owner is released) and posts a comment elsewhere. The mutation invalidates the feed tag. The feed is owner-free, so it is only marked stale.
3. The user returns. The route ensures the feed. Page 0 is refetched and pages 1 and 2 are not.
4. The feed now reads `:invalidated-at nil` and `stale? false`, yet pages 1 and 2 show pre-mutation data (for example a stale comment count or an edited item) until the next forced refetch.

The same happens for a feed with `:stale-after-ms` re-entered after it expired.

## Evidence

EXECUTED with a bounded JVM probe (plain-atom substrate, capturing `:rf.http/managed` fx) against the frozen tree `review-sep23` at 034d0c8fc8, run from a scratch directory with `CLJ_CACHE` in scratch. The tree's `git status --porcelain` read 0 lines afterwards. The feed was registered with `:refetch {:refetch-all-pages? true}` and loaded to 3 pages `[p0-v1 p1-v1 p2-v1]`.

- Control: `:rf.resource/refetch` armed `:refetch-sweep [["c1" 1] ["c2" 2]]`, and after the legs settled the pages read `[p0-v2 p1-v2 p2-v2]`. The policy works when it is reached.
- Subject: `release-owner` then `invalidate-tags` left the entry owner-free with `:invalidated-at` set.
- A re-ensure under a new route owner issued 1 request, at `:page-index 0`, with `:refetch-sweep nil`.
- After page 0 settled, the pages read `[p0-v3 p1-v2 p2-v2]`, with `:invalidated-at nil`, `entry-stale?` false, and no queued leg (the last request's `:page-index` was 0).

Tracker searched over a full `bd export` (all statuses) for `refetch-all-pages`, `refetch-sweep` and `ensure.{0,80}infinite.{0,80}stale`. There is no existing bead for this path. The rf2-c64uiz / EP-0021 beads cover the force-new sweep, which works.

## Smallest fix

Arm the sweep whenever the fresh-load branch refetches a feed that already holds pages, not only on force-new. For example, change the condition at `events.cljc:694` to `(and infinite? (or force-new? (rf.resources.state/has-data? entry)))`, or equivalent, and correct the comment at lines 679-682. This keeps a first load (empty `:data`) arming nothing.

Fence: `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/events.cljc`, plus a test next to the infinite refetch tests. No hot-zone files.

## Gates

- `clojure -M:test` from `implementation/resources`. The code is plain `.cljc`, not a `#?(:cljs ...)` branch.
- The same tests run in CI's CLJS node lane (`npm run test:cljs`).

## Decision needed

No. The spec already states the behaviour. One optional choice: whether a time-stale ensure (as distinct from an invalidated one) should also sweep. The spec's "refetches per the refetch rule" reading says it should.

title: resources-mutations-ssr: superseding a pending optimistic mutation (re-execute under the same :instance, or :rf.mutation/clear) discards its inverse - the unconfirmed optimistic paint is left as fresh :loaded data
description:
## Defect

When a pending optimistic mutation instance is superseded, its recorded inverse is thrown away and never replayed. Two things supersede it: a re-execute under the same `:instance` id, and a `:rf.mutation/clear` of that instance. In both cases the first attempt's optimistic paint can become permanent cache data, marked `:loaded`, fresh and not invalidated.

- **Re-execute.** `execute-handler` overwrites the instance row wholesale with a fresh `:pending` row, so the prior `:patch-summary :rollback` is lost. The new optimistic apply then snapshots the entry as it now stands, which already carries the first attempt's unconfirmed paint, and records that as its own `:before`. The first reply is stale-suppressed, so it rolls back nothing. If the second attempt then fails, its rollback restores the first attempt's optimistic value, and the revision check calls that value unmoved.
- **Clear.** `clear-handler` dissocs the instance row, rollback inverse included, and aborts the request. The abort's reply finds no instance and is stale-suppressed. Nothing ever rolls the paint back.

Spec 016 §Optimistic settle justifies discarding the inverse with "the newer apply already recorded the truthful inverse". That holds only when the newer apply snapshotted pre-optimistic truth. After a re-execute it snapshotted the older paint. After a clear there is no newer apply at all.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_events.cljc:1382-1384`: `execute-handler` `assoc-in`s the fresh instance over any live row, and never reads the prior `:patch-summary`.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_events.cljc:1421-1446`: the new apply snapshots the current, already-painted entry and records it as `:rollback`.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_events.cljc:1539-1541`: `clear-handler` dissocs the instance with its inverse. There is no rollback anywhere in the handler (lines 1495-1583).
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_events.cljc:2111-2125` and `:1726-1741`: a reply for a superseded or cleared instance takes the stale branch, so it performs no rollback.
- `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_runtime.cljc:516-517` and `spec/016-Resources.md:1089`: the "newer apply already recorded the truthful inverse" rationale. `mutation_events.cljc:57-59` says "Failure or cancellation rolls it back".
- The same shape reaches epoch restore. `ssr.cljc:1764-1839` (`dangle-pending-mutations!`) rolls back only the inverse on the surviving row.

Public entry points: `[:rf.mutation/execute {:mutation … :instance <id> …}]` issued twice under one instance id, and `[:rf.mutation/clear {:instance <id>}]` while the instance is `:pending`.

## Failure scenario

This is the flagship's own pattern. `examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/views.cljs:107-118` issues `:realworld/favorite` / `:realworld/unfavorite` (both `:optimistic-tags`) under the one instance `[:favorite slug]`, and deliberately does not disable the heart while pending (`views.cljs:280-286`). The rf2-zfr7w ruling records that the runtime's supersession is that app's latch.

1. An article is cached unfavorited. The session has expired or the device is offline.
2. Click 1 runs favorite: the heart is painted on and the count bumped. Its snapshot is the true, unfavorited entry.
3. Click 2 runs unfavorite under the same instance: the heart is painted off. Its snapshot is click 1's painted entry.
4. Both requests fail. Click 1's reply is stale-suppressed. Click 2's rollback sees an unmoved revision and restores click 1's paint: favorited, with a count one too high.
5. The cache now shows `:status :loaded`, `:invalidated-at nil`, fresh. The server says unfavorited. Nothing refetches it until a stale timer, GC or an unrelated invalidation.

For clear: an optimistic save is pending, and the app clears the instance (a cancel button, or form teardown). The painted value stays in the cache as fresh `:loaded` data, whether or not the server ever applied the write.

## Evidence

EXECUTED as a bounded JVM probe. It used the plain-atom substrate and captured the `:rf.http/managed` fx. It ran from the scratch directory, with the classpath taken via `clojure -Spath`, against the frozen tree. The resource was loaded with `{:title "Old"}`, and the mutation's `:optimistic` wrote `:title` into an exact target.
- Control, a single attempt rejected with 422: the title went from `"BAD"` back to `"Old"`, at revision 1. The instrument sees a working rollback.
- Scenario A, execute twice under `[:row 7]` with both attempts rejected: after attempt 1 the title was `"BAD"` at rev 2, and after attempt 2 it was `"BAD"` at rev 3. Attempt 1's 422 was stale-suppressed, leaving `"BAD"` at rev 3. Attempt 2's 422 left `"BAD"`, `:status :loaded`, `:invalidated-at nil`, rev 2, and the instance at `:error`. Server truth was `"Old"`.
- Scenario B, execute then `:rf.mutation/clear`, then the abort reply: `"BAD"`, `:loaded`, `:invalidated-at nil`, rev 2, at every step. The instance row after the clear was `nil`.

Tests: `implementation/resources/test/re_frame/resources_optimistic_validation_cljs_test.cljc` `case-06-stale-superseded-reply-discards-its-inverse` pins only that the stale first reply does not roll back. It never settles the second attempt as a failure, and no test clears a pending optimistic instance. `docs/EP/EP-0019-optimistic-mutation-rollback.md:375-382` describes the re-snapshot "as the optimistic value" as intended. It does not follow that through to a failed second attempt, and for clear there is no newer apply for it to point at.

Tracker: `bd search` for optimistic, superseded, re-execute, rollback, inverse and mutation/clear, plus a full-text regex over a `bd export` (2158 issues): no bead covers this. Control: the same regex set found rf2-zfr7w and rf2-6gzdb, so it can see body text.

## Smallest fix

Replay a superseded pending instance's inverse before its row is replaced or dropped.
- In `execute-handler`, when the row at `instance-path` is non-terminal and carries `:patch-summary :rollback`, run it through the existing conflict-aware `settle-optimistic-rollback` against the runtime-db first. Then apply the new plan, whose snapshot is now pre-paint truth. Keeping the older record's `:before` for overlapping keys is an equivalent alternative.
- In `clear-handler`, run the same rollback for each cleared pending instance, since clear is a cancellation.

Either way the write's server outcome is unknown, so staling the rolled-back keys (the `:dangling-on-restore` reasoning) is the conservative variant. Correct the "newer apply already recorded the truthful inverse" sentence at `spec/016-Resources.md:1089` and `mutation_runtime.cljc:516`.

Fence: `implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/mutation_events.cljc`, `spec/016-Resources.md`, and one test under `implementation/resources/test/`. No hot-zone files.

## Gates

`clojure -M:test` from `implementation/resources`. The code is plain `.cljc`, with no `#?(:cljs …)` branch, so the JVM lane compiles it. The same tests also run in CI's CLJS node lane (`npm run test:cljs`).

## Decision needed

Yes, a small one. When a superseded optimistic apply is rolled back, should the key only be restored to its pre-paint snapshot, or restored and also marked stale, since the superseded write may have landed on the server? EP-0019 §stale/superseded currently calls the discard a determinism guarantee, so its text changes too.

== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-23 23:35:15 AUSEST) ==

RULING: B. A superseded or cleared pending optimistic apply is rolled back rather than having its inverse discarded. Every rollback whose BASELINE came from an attempt whose reply the runtime discarded or abandoned ends STALE: restore the pre-paint snapshot, entry-invalidate it, and arm the exact refetch when the key is owned. An ordinary single-attempt rollback triggered by a reply stays exact, as today, and the epoch-restore dangle is unchanged.

--- WHY ---
- The defect is measured. The dossier's flagship-shaped JVM probe used the toggle-article-fav patch over {:favorited false :favoritesCount 5}, on resources code byte-identical to trunk:
  - S1: favorite, then unfavorite, under [:favorite "w"], both 401. The entry read true/6, :loaded, :invalidated-at nil, with the instance at :error; click 2 had recorded a :before count of 6.
  - S2: click 1's 200 suppressed, click 2's 401. The entry read true/6, right only by the same bug.
  - S3: favorite pending, then :rf.mutation/clear. The entry read true/6, fresh, at every step, and the instance row was nil.
  - Control: a single favorite with a 401 restored false/5 at rev 1.
- Codex measured the same independently:
  - false/5 was painted while pending; both rejected left true/6 at rev 2, :loaded, :invalidated-at nil;
  - a clear during attempt 1 left true/6 fresh, both after the instance was gone and after a late failure;
  - control: false/5 at rev 1.
  - case-03 and case-06 pass today (2 tests, 12 assertions). case-06 never fails the surviving attempt, and that is precisely the gap.
- The mechanism, read at trunk:
  - execute-handler assoc-in's the fresh :pending instance over any live row (mutation_events.cljc:1382-1384) and never reads the old :patch-summary :rollback.
  - The new apply snapshots the already-painted entry (:1421-1446).
  - clear-handler dissocs the row, inverse included (:1539-1541), and rolls nothing back anywhere in :1495-1583.
  - The stale-reply branches (:1726 success, :2111 failure) write nothing to the cache.
- The spec's rationale is a false premise, not a ruling. 016 §Optimistic settle (:1089) says "the newer apply already recorded the truthful inverse", and EP-0019 Decision 3 says "stale / superseded → NEITHER … the determinism guarantee". Both hold only if the newer apply snapshotted pre-optimistic truth. After a re-execute it snapshotted the older paint; after a clear there is no newer apply at all.
  - That text dates from the original proposal (3b8100b6b4, 2026-06-14), not from a later ruling of Mike's, and this bead's own Decision-needed anticipated the EP text change. Correcting it is inside the delegation.
  - Stale-REPLY suppression, the mandatory boundary, is unchanged; only the cache consequence changes.
- A (restore only) loses. In S2 and on a clear after the send, it presents the pre-paint value as fresh :loaded while the server may hold the write. That narrows the defect's shape rather than removing it, and turns S2 from accidentally right into reliably wrong. :invalidate-timing :after-failure does not reach this: it re-reads on EVERY failure of the mutation, and a clear has no reply at all.
- "Stale every uncertain rollback" (timeouts, 5xx) loses. It rewrites settled failure semantics for every optimistic write, and :invalidate-timing already hands the programmer that choice.
- Replay-then-apply (the bead's first re-execute mechanism) loses. Rolling back to false/5 and then running the unfavorite patch paints false/4, because toggle-article-fav sets an absolute flag and moves the count by ±1 (examples/real-apps/realworld_resources/mutations.cljs:95-104). It also turns case-06 red (its (= 11 …) pins, resources_optimistic_validation_cljs_test.cljc ~:322 and :331). INHERIT is the mechanism instead.
- Where the recommendations agreed: B; inherit, not replay; reuse settle-optimistic-rollback, entry-invalidate (state.cljc:867) and conflicted-key-refetch-fx (mutation_events.cljc:599-618); no new public option; amend spec 016, EP-0019 and the tooling text together.
- Where they differed, resolved:
  (i) The dossier's one-line rule "runtime-initiated rollbacks end stale; reply-driven rollbacks stay exact" is mis-worded: its own acceptance case 1 requires the successor's REPLY-triggered rollback of an inherited key to end stale. Codex states it correctly: the deciding fact is the PROVENANCE of the baseline, not what triggered the rollback. The RULING above is worded that way.
  (ii) Convergence. The dossier said B "ends right in every reply ordering". Codex showed it does not, and the source agrees:
     - execute-handler emits no abort of the predecessor; its fx are commit-generation, record-work-handle, the before-fxs and lower-fx only (:1486-1491).
     - Each attempt gets a distinct frame-qualified request-id (:1293-1301), so the transport does not supersede the predecessor either.
     - The superseded write can therefore reach the server AFTER the recovery read. Codex's labelled simulation: restore plus stale, the recovery GET returns false/5, then the old favorite commits on the server, leaving the cache at false/5 fresh against a server at true/6.
     - An abort never proves the write was not processed, either.
     So B is a bounded RECOVERY improvement, not write serialisation, and spec/EP prose must not claim more. An app that needs ordered writes needs its own latch or server policy; the HTTP flagship twin's latch (rf2-zfr7w) is exactly that. This bead does not grow one.

--- WHAT TO BUILD (trunk 950a0cba74; mutation_events.cljc and mutation_runtime.cljc) ---
Rule: a rollback restores the recorded :before when the key is unmoved, with conflict handling as today. If the inverse row carries the REVALIDATE obligation, the restored key is then marked stale with entry-invalidate and gets the exact refetch when it is owned (conflicted-key-refetch-fx). That is the treatment an :on-conflict :invalidate key already gets. A row carries the obligation when its baseline came from a superseded or abandoned attempt; an ordinary single-attempt row does not.
1. In execute-handler, BEFORE the new row is assoc-in'd: act when the row at instance-path is PENDING and carries :patch-summary :rollback.
   - Test PENDING with rf.resources.mutation-runtime/pending?, not by the presence of :rollback. After rf2-3x7nj.11.1, committed rows keep a :rollback vector with :before stripped, and failed rows carry disposition rows.
   a. Keys the successor will NOT re-touch optimistically, including every key when the successor has no optimistic plan or was called with {:optimistic? false}: roll them back now.
      - Use settle-optimistic-rollback with the SUPERSEDED mutation's :on-conflict, from mutation-meta of its :mutation/id. The flagship shares one :instance across two mutation ids.
      - Clock: the execute event's :rf/time-ms.
      - Then apply the obligation: restore, then stale, then refetch if owned.
      - Emit :rf.mutation/optimistic-rolled-back with the SUPERSEDED apply's :snapshot-id and its per-key dispositions.
   b. Keys the successor WILL re-touch: the successor paints on the CURRENT value, exactly as today. That keeps case-06 and the in-flight delta right: the count reads 5, not 4.
      - If a key is unmoved since the superseded apply (its current :revision equals the superseded row's :applied-revision), the successor's inverse row inherits the superseded row's :before.
      - A MOVED key keeps the successor's own snapshot. Never blind-restore an old snapshot across an intervening authoritative write; the conflict rules apply at settle as usual.
      - Either way, the successor's row carries the obligation.
   c. The obligation, and an inherited :before, propagate through repeated supersession, so a three-attempt chain restores the EARLIEST unconfirmed baseline.
   Suggested marker: a boolean on the inverse row, e.g. :revalidate? true.
   - :patch-summary is [:maybe :any] in spec/Spec-Schemas.md (:3268), so no schema edit is needed.
   - rollback-trace-dispositions (mutation_events.cljc:706-719) emits no :before, so the new rolled-back emissions cannot widen the rf2-3x7nj.11.1 egress leak. Keep it that way.
2. The successor's own settle.
   - Failure or accepted cancel: settle-optimistic-rollback as today, plus the obligation on flagged rows. Clock: the reply's :completed-at.
   - Success: commit exactly as today. Inherited baselines are discarded with the rest of the inverse, and no stale mark lands on a populated key.
3. In clear-handler, BEFORE the dissoc: for each cleared instance that is PENDING and carries an inverse, run settle-optimistic-rollback and apply the obligation to every key.
   - Use the cleared mutation's :on-conflict. Clock: the clear event's :rf/time-ms.
   - Put the refetch fx beside the existing abort fx.
   - Emit :rf.mutation/optimistic-rolled-back with that apply's :snapshot-id.
4. UNCHANGED:
   - stale-reply suppression;
   - single-attempt reply-driven rollbacks (case-03, including a 5xx restoring verbatim);
   - the epoch-restore dangle: dangle-rollback-optimistic via ssr.cljc dangle-pending-mutations!, and 016's "Epoch-restore dangle (Q3)" paragraph (~:1102).
   The dangle is the one deliberate exception. An epoch restore is time travel rather than a resync, and this fix already makes the surviving row's :before truthful there. Extending B to it is a two-line follow-up (dangle-rollback-optimistic plus case-13) if anyone wants zero exceptions; this ruling does not include it.

TRAPS
- restore-before seats the snapshot with ITS OWN :revision. reconcile-restored-entry carries only live-work-keys (:generation :current-work :request-id :attempt :active-owners) forward from the current entry. So a restore moves :revision BACK, and entry-invalidate then bumps it. Restore THEN invalidate, in that order, so a still-pending earlier apply sees the stale mark as a conflict.
- A seeded (:absent) baseline restores absence, and there is nothing to stale: no-op, no refetch.
- An owner-free restored key with a read already in flight: today that read's success clears the new mark (state.cljc:1028). The rf2-3x7nj.10.1 ruling makes entry-invalidate record the in-flight attempt and makes the success keep such a mark, so the mark is durable only once 10.1 lands. An owned key is safe regardless, because its refetch supersedes the read.
- reconcile-restored-entry (mutation_runtime.cljc:627) recomputes :status only when the carried :current-work is non-nil.
- Cost: one recovery GET per owned touched key per disposition, only on the rare supersede-then-fail, clear-while-pending and inherited-chain-failure paths. Offline, the GET fails and the mark survives (rf2-ifzg4). Do not promise a global bound on requests.

The apply's keys are rolled back at supersession or inherited by the successor, and a baseline from an abandoned attempt ends stale. Add one clause stating that this is recovery, not write serialisation.

title: machines-lifecycle: :rf.machine/update-snapshot and :rf.machine/destroy write runtime-db after the flow pass and request no settle - a flow over a machine snapshot path stays stale until an unrelated drain
description:
## Defect

Two machine lifecycle fx, `:rf.machine/update-snapshot` and `:rf.machine/destroy`, write the actor's snapshot straight into the live runtime-db during the `:fx` walk (`swap-runtime-db-exact!` / `swap-runtime-db!`). That walk runs after the event's flow pass (the router's outermost `:after`), and neither fx requests a flow settle. So a flow whose input is a machine snapshot path, which is exactly the input Spec 013 uses as its canonical runtime-db example, keeps publishing the pre-write value after the dispatch that changed the snapshot returns. It is repaired only when some later, unrelated event drains the frame. It is the same self-healing staleness Spec 013 §Sequencing calls incoherent for flow lifecycle effects, reached through the machine lifecycle. An ordinary machine transition is NOT affected: it commits through a pending `:rf.db/runtime` effect, which the flow pass reads. `:rf.machine/spawn` is not observably affected either, because it always queues a bootstrap dispatch to the newborn actor, and that event's own flow pass refreshes the flow inside the same run-to-completion. Destroy covers the declarative case too: a parent leaving a `:spawn` state destroys its child through the desugared exit `[:rf.machine/destroy <id>]` (Spec 005:256).

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/update_snapshot.cljc:71` (`update-snapshot-fx`): the store write at `:200-201`.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/destroy.cljc:728` (`destroy-machine-fx`), via `destroy-single-actor!` (`:327`): runtime writes at `:280-281`, `:457-459`, `:540-541`, `:680-681`. Also `exit_cascade.cljc:131-132` for child exits within the cascade.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:1742-1765`: the flow pass is the outermost `:after`, before the install and before the `:fx` walk. `:1796-1808`: it reads the handler's pending `:rf.db/runtime` effect, or the chain-start runtime-db, never a later mid-fx write.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc:725-754, :943-962`: only the two reserved flow-lifecycle effects call `request-flow-settle!`.
- `implementation/core/src/re_frame/frame.cljc:2113-2129`: the `swap-runtime-db!` docstring names these "direct (out-of-cascade / mid-fx) writes (machine spawn / destroy / update-snapshot ...)".
- Spec: `spec/013-Flows.md:94` names `[:rf.db/runtime :rf.runtime/machines :snapshots :app/boot :state]` as the example flow input and says "The dirty-check keys on both partitions: a runtime-only event ... still re-fires a flow that reads the changed runtime-db value". `spec/013-Flows.md:13`: flows "are evaluated automatically on every event". `spec/013-Flows.md:453`: the lag is "not merely late but incoherent". No normative sentence carves out mid-fx runtime writes. The §Sequencing guarantee (`:451`) is stated only for the two flow-lifecycle effects.
- Public entry points: `rf/reg-flow` with a `[:rf.db/runtime :rf.runtime/machines :snapshots <id> ...]` input, then any dispatch whose `:fx` carries `[:rf.machine/update-snapshot ...]` or `[:rf.machine/destroy <id>]`. That includes a machine callback's `:fx` and a parent exiting a declarative `:spawn` state.

## Failure scenario

```clojure
(rf/reg-machine :pm/m {:initial :idle :data {:note "orig"}
                       :states {:idle {:on {:go :busy}} :busy {:on {:go :idle}}}})
(rf/reg-flow :pf/state {:inputs [[:rf.db/runtime :rf.runtime/machines :snapshots :pm/m :state]]
                        :output-path [:mstate]} identity)
(rf/reg-event :patch (fn [_ _] {:fx [[:rf.machine/update-snapshot
                                      {:rf/machine-id :pm/m :rf/patch {:state :busy}}]]}))
(rf/dispatch-sync [:patch])   ; snapshot :state is now :busy; app-db :mstate still :idle
```

After that one dispatch, the snapshot reads `:busy` and `:mstate` reads `:idle`. The same happens for a `:data` patch. After `[:rf.machine/destroy :pm/m]`, the snapshot is gone and `:mstate` still reads `:busy`. Each is corrected only by a later unrelated dispatch.

## Evidence

EXECUTED. I ran a bounded JVM probe from a scratch deps project with `:local/root` pointing at the frozen tree's flows and machines artefacts (plain-atom substrate, standard `make-reset-runtime-fixture`), exit 0, empty stderr. The flows read the machine snapshot's `:state` and `:data :note`. A third flow over a plain app-db input is the control. Readings after ONE dispatch, then after one unrelated no-op dispatch:
- CONTROL, ordinary transition `[:pm/m [:go]]`: snapshot `:busy`, flow `:busy` after the one dispatch. Fresh.
- update-snapshot `:data {:note "patched"}`, from an event that also bumped the plain input: snapshot `"patched"`, flow still `"orig"`, while the plain-input flow in the SAME event did recompute (0 to 1). After the no-op: `"patched"`.
- update-snapshot `:state :busy`: snapshot `:busy`, flow still `:idle`. After the no-op: `:busy`.
- destroy: snapshot `nil`, flow still `:busy` (and `:note` `"orig"`). After the no-op: `nil`.
- spawn with `:fixed-actor-id`: snapshot `:born`, flow `:born` after the one dispatch. NOT affected, because the bootstrap dispatch refreshes it.

Probe source (supporting only): `scratchpad/review-wave/flows/probe2/src/mflowprobe.clj`.

Tracker: nothing filed or ruled. I checked the notes and all children of rf2-3x7nj.8 (machines-core, 4 children) and rf2-3x7nj.9 (machines-lifecycle, 6 children), `bd search "settle" --status all` (27 records, none about machine runtime writes and flows), and a full-text scan of the tracker export for flow plus update-snapshot and flow plus the snapshot path. rf2-3x7nj.9's notes mention update-snapshot only as "bypasses timers, spawns and finality", a documented trade-off unrelated to flows.

Related: rf2-3x7nj.18.3 has the same root cause (a lifecycle write after the flow pass with no settle requested), reached through a user-fx `clear-flow`. One fix at the `:fx`-walk level could close both.

## Smallest fix

Options, all small. (A) Per effect: make the settle request reachable from the machines artefact (for example a late-bind seam over `request-flow-settle!`, which is a no-op outside an `:fx` walk) and call it from `update-snapshot-fx` and `destroy-machine-fx` after a successful write. Fence: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc`, `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/update_snapshot.cljc`, `.../destroy.cljc`, and `implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc` if a hook is added. (B) Generic: at the end of each `:fx` walk in `fx.cljc`, request the one settle when the frame's runtime-db is no longer `identical?` to its value when the walk started. That covers every mid-fx runtime writer at once, the resources artefact included; guard it on the flows artefact being loaded so apps without flows pay nothing. Fence: `implementation/core/src/re_frame/fx.cljc`. (C) Spec: state in `spec/013-Flows.md` that runtime-db written by a lifecycle fx during the `:fx` walk reaches flows on the next drain. None of these touches a hot-zone file, unless `spec/005-StateMachines.md` is edited to document it.

## Gates

(A) and (B) are shared `.cljc` with no reader-conditional branch at these sites. The JVM core lane (`scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh`, which includes `implementation/core`), the flows lane (`clojure -M:test` from `implementation/flows`) and the machines lane (`clojure -M:test` from `implementation/machines`) grade them. A new late-bind hook is also graded by `implementation/core/test/re_frame/late_bind_drift_test.clj`. The natural pin is a cross-host `*_cljs_test.cljc` in the flows test tree, which can require machines. Its CLJS arm is graded by `npm run test:cljs` only. (C) is docs: no gate checks prose, so verify by hand.

## Decision needed

Yes: close the lag per effect (A) or generically at the end of the `:fx` walk (B), which would also cover rf2-3x7nj.18.3 and non-machine runtime writers; or accept it and document that mid-fx runtime writes reach flows on the next drain (C).

Read at trunk f6bb999d6e (= origin/main). Every cited file is byte-identical to the review tree 034d0c8fc8 (git diff --quiet exit 0; control over core/src exit 1).

== RULING (delegated by Mike; mayor-dispatched ruling agent, 2026-09-24 01:08:41 AUSEST) ==

RULING: option (B), GENERIC, with a per-frame guard. At the end of each `:fx` walk, if the frame-state container is no longer `identical?` to its value when the walk started AND the frame holds at least one registered flow, the walk requests the SAME one settle the reserved flow effects already request (one head-inserted framework-private `[:rf/settle-flows]`). The "frame has flows" answer comes from a NEW flows-published late-bind hook; an unbound hook (flows artefact absent) means no settle, so flow-less apps and flow-less frames stay byte-identical. rf2-3x7nj.18.3's own registry-owned request lands in the SAME PR. Invariant to state in Spec 013: whatever an `:fx` walk changes in frame state, flows reflect before any continuation it queued runs, and by the time the dispatch returns.

WHY — the dossier recommended (B), the independent Codex review recommended (A) per-writer requests. What decides it, measured here:
1. THE PER-WRITER LIST WAS WRONG ON DAY ONE. Both analyses scoped the writers to `update-snapshot` + `destroy`; the dossier explicitly called `:rf.machine/spawn` "not observably affected" because its bootstrap dispatch refreshes the flow. That holds only for "after the dispatch returns". The bootstrap is FIFO, NOT head-inserted (spawn.cljc ~:1427-1440: "`:rf.machine/internal?` is dropped so the newborn's first event keeps its FIFO place"), so a continuation queued AHEAD of it reads a stale flow. Measured (probe below): handler `{:fx [[:dispatch [:p/record-child]] [:rf.machine/spawn {:machine-id :m/child :fixed-actor-id :c/one}]]}`, flow over `[:rf.db/runtime :rf.runtime/machines :snapshots :c/one :state]` → `[:cstate]`: the continuation saw `{:flow nil, :live-snapshot :born}` at trunk AND under (A) as scoped; `{:flow :born ...}` under (B) and under (A) widened to also cover spawn (the simulation keyed on the fx ids `:rf.machine/spawn` / `:rf.machine/spawn-all-init` in the walk). Control (spawn BEFORE the dispatch): `{:flow :born}` in every mode. So (A) needs at least three call sites (update-snapshot-fx, destroy-machine-fx, spawn-fx — and probably spawn-all-init-fx, which shares spawn.cljc's write path; that one is inspected, not measured) and the next writer must remember too — exactly the failure mode the dossier predicted for (A) and the way this bug arose (kh73v wrote the settle for two effects and the class was wider). Two careful independent reviews missed the third writer; that is the evidence that a per-writer rule will keep being wrong.
2. THE GUARD IS NOT A COST OF (B). Codex objected that (B) needs a "frame has flows" predicate that does not exist. Measured: (A) needs it just as much. On a frame with NO flows, 50 `update-snapshot` dispatches run 50 events at trunk; with the settle requested unguarded they run 100 (50 extra `[:rf/settle-flows]`) under (A) and under (B) alike; guarded, 50 and 0 settles for both. 3. (B) TOUCHES NO MACHINES FILE, so it cannot collide with the in-flight machines work (rf2-3x7nj.8.1 / .8.3 edit `machines/transition.cljc`; other .9.x fixes move spawn/registration files). (A) would edit update_snapshot.cljc, destroy.cljc and spawn.cljc.
4. (C) "accept and document" is ruled out: Spec 013:94 names `[:rf.db/runtime :rf.runtime/machines :snapshots :app/boot :state]` as THE example runtime flow input, and the lag is the intermittent, self-healing shape 013:453/:484 call incoherent; (C) would bring back the dispatch-a-no-op ceremony rf2-kh73v and rf2-g1zb deleted. The programmer did nothing wrong, so "trust the programmer" does not help.
ADOPTED FROM CODEX (it is right on all of these): (i) (B) does NOT close rf2-3x7nj.18.3 — a user-fx `(rf/clear :flow id)` mutates only side tables and leaves the container identical, so 18.3 still needs its explicit request (the dossier measured this too); (ii) one walk is not one originating event — a parent destroy whose exit cascade destroys a child runs a NESTED `do-fx` (exit_cascade.cljc :140) and both simulations enqueued TWO settles; that is harmless (≈ one no-op event each), do not add coalescing and do not pin exactly-one for nested cascades; (iii) resource removal (`clear-resource`, resources/registry.cljc :640-656) disposes across EVERY frame, so observing one frame cannot settle the others — neither option covers it (see NOT SETTLED); (iv) the continuation-reads-stale case is the real harm, not the visible lag: at trunk a continuation queued by the same handler PERSISTS the stale value.

title: pair-mcp: watch-epochs passes a string :since-id (its schema type) raw to the runtime's integer-id =, so every resume-by-id returns a false :rf.mcp/cursor-stale
description:
## Defect

`watch-epochs` takes `:since-id` straight off the wire (`wire/arg`) and emits it as the argument to the runtime's `epochs-since` without parsing it. Its descriptor declares `:since-id {:type "string"}`, the tool spec says "`since-id` (string ...)", and the descriptor's resume example is `{:since-id "epoch-42"}`. The reference runtime's epoch ids are integers (`next-epoch-id` is `(swap! epoch-counter inc)`), and `epochs-since` finds the id with `=`. So a schema-conforming `"47"` never equals `47`. The runtime then reports `:id-aged-out? true`, and the tool turns that into `{:ok? false :reason :rf.mcp/cursor-stale}`. That tells the agent its epoch has aged out of the ring and it must drop the id and restart, which is false. The id is in the ring. Every resume-by-id poll fails the same way.

The sibling tools that take an epoch id already handle this: `restore-epoch` and `replay-epoch` parse `epoch-id` as EDN (`args/read-edn-arg`), and their descriptors say "an integer id like 7 may be passed as \"7\"". `watch-epochs` is the only one that does not.

## Where

At `034d0c8fc8`:

- `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/src/re_frame2_pair_mcp/tools/watch_epochs.cljs:70`: `since-id (wire/arg raw-args :since-id)`, raw.
- `:103-104`: `effective-after (or (:after-id cursor-in) since-id)`.
- `:125`: `(fr/frame-sym-call 'epochs-since effective-after)` emits the JS string as a CLJS string literal.
- `:194-197`: `aged-out?` with a live `effective-after` produces `cursor/cursor-stale-result`.
- `skills/re-frame2-pair/preload/re_frame2_pair/runtime.cljs:1390-1413` (`epochs-since`: `(some #(= epoch-id (:epoch-id %)) history)`, and on a miss `{:epochs [] :id-aged-out? true ...}`).
- `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/state.cljc:166-167` (`next-epoch-id` = `(swap! epoch-counter inc)`) and `implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/assembly.cljc:318` (`:epoch-id (rf.epoch.state/next-epoch-id)`).
- The contract: `tools/descriptors_data.cljs:808` (example `{:since-id "epoch-42"}`, reply `:head-id "epoch-47"`), `:814` (`:since-id {:type "string"}`), and `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp/spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md:1812` ("`since-id` (string ...)").

Entry point: MCP `tools/call` `watch-epochs` with `:since-id`.

## Failure scenario

1. The agent polls `watch-epochs {}` and receives `:head-id 47` (an integer, which is what the runtime emits).
2. It resumes with `watch-epochs {:since-id "47"}`, a string, as the schema requires.
3. `epochs-since` runs `(= "47" 47)`, which is false for every record, so it returns `:id-aged-out? true`.
4. The tool returns `{:ok? false :reason :rf.mcp/cursor-stale :requested-id "47" :head-id <n>}`, with the hint "Cursor's epoch-id is no longer in the runtime ring. Drop the cursor and restart, or widen the window to recover the missed records." (`tools/cursor.cljs:184-186`). Epoch 47 is still in the ring, and any events after it are never reported through this route.

## Evidence

Inspected only; the tool and preload are `.cljs`. The id type is established at source: `next-epoch-id` returns the `swap!` result of an integer atom. The comparison is `=` with no coercion. The emission is the `ef/rt-call` default path, which prints a JS string as a CLJS string literal.

Why the tests stay green: `test/re_frame2_pair_mcp/epoch_frame_test.cljs:310` and `:646` drive `watch-epochs` with a numeric `{:since-id 2}` / `{:since-id 9}`, which only works because the test passes a JSON number the schema forbids. `watch_epochs_test.cljs:85/:117/:202` pass `":epoch-9"`-style strings, but against a stubbed runtime that never performs the real `=` comparison. So no test exercises a schema-typed string against the real id type.

Control: the cursor route works. `:next-cursor` carries the runtime's own integer `after-id` (base64 EDN), so a cursor continuation compares integer to integer. Only the documented `:since-id` route is broken.

Tracker: there are no beads on watch-epochs `since-id` typing. The `since-id` hits (rf2-9vdmg, rf2-66xy8, rf2-ikbgk.2, rf2-ahjbc) concern skill prose and the retired progress stream.

## Smallest fix

Parse `:since-id` exactly as `restore-epoch` parses `epoch-id` (`args/read-edn-arg`, then `rt-quote`), so `"47"` reads as `47` while a genuinely non-integer id still round-trips. Correct the descriptor example to an integer-shaped id (`"42"`) and mention the EDN parsing in the `:since-id` description. Fence: `tools/watch_epochs.cljs`, `tools/descriptors_data.cljs`, `tool-descriptors.edn` (regenerate if the input surface moves; it does not), `spec/003-Tool-Catalogue.md` §watch-epochs, plus a test that feeds a string id to a runtime stub using the real `epochs-since` semantics. No hot-zone file.

## Gates

`npm test` in `tools/re-frame2-pair-mcp` (CLJS only), and `npm run check:descriptors` if the descriptor text change touches the manifest.

## Decision needed

No.
