title: relabel Checklist Q8, the conformance README, the implementor skill and the 11 http-managed fixture headers to claim override routing only; fix the abort fixture's order
description:
## Bug

The 11 managed-HTTP conformance fixtures install their own stubs:
- they replace `:rf.http/managed` with the fixture's own `[[:noop]]`;
- they replace the canned-reply stub with a literal `:dispatch` of a reply envelope the fixture writes itself.

So no Spec-014 code runs, and the fixtures cannot fail for any Spec-014 reason. A port with no managed-HTTP code that claims `:rf.http/managed` passes all 11. The Implementor Checklist, meanwhile, tells ports these fixtures grade managed HTTP.

## Evidence

All file:line references are at trunk 475bdcaacf (unchanged at b375cd0e42).

- **The fixtures stub the effect under test** (*read*, census 11 of 11). Every `spec/conformance/fixtures/http-managed-*.edn` declares:
  - `:rf.http/managed [[:noop]]` under `:fixture/handlers :fx`;
  - a literal body for `:rf.http/managed-canned-success` or `-failure`;
  - `:fx-overrides {:rf.http/managed :rf.http/managed-canned-…}`.

  For example, `http-managed-get-success.edn:39-48` stubs the success path as `[[:dispatch [:article/loaded {:status :ok :value {:title "hello" :id 42}}]]]`.
- **The runner installs those stubs over the framework's own handlers.** `implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_runner.cljc:442-457` realises each fx id that has an explicit fixture body and calls `rf.fx/reg-fx id …`. That replaces both the framework's `:rf.http/managed` and the real canned stubs in `re-frame.http.test-support`.
- **What goes unexercised.** None of the following runs:
  - request normalisation, decode, `:accept`, retry and backoff, abort, or envelope synthesis;
  - the Spec 014 §Testing canned stubs that the fixture headers cite ("which Spec 014 §Testing guarantees produces the same dispatch shape the real fx would", `http-managed-get-success.edn:9-11`).

  `http-managed-retry-exhaustion.edn:8-11` says outright that it "models the contract with a single canned-failure invocation".
- **What is actually graded is redundant.** The fixtures grade core fx-override routing, routed args and dispatch. Five non-HTTP fixtures already grade those: `fx-override-by-id`, `dispatch-envelope`, `error-override-fallthrough`, `replay-with-interceptor-override` and `cross-spec-portable-story-fx-override`.
- **Contract.** `spec/Implementor-Checklist.md:100-104` (Q8) defines managed HTTP as "decoding, success/failure normalisation, retry-with-backoff, abort, schema-driven decode, and reply-to-origin dispatch", then says "Declaring yes runs the `:rf.http/managed` fixtures." Q8 is graded by these 11 alone.

## Expected

A port that claims `:rf.http/managed` cannot pass the corpus without implementing it. Until then, Q8 and the fixture headers say plainly that the corpus does not grade managed HTTP.

## Fix direction (Mike's call between A and B)

- **(A) Interim, S, spec-only.** Reword Checklist Q8 and the 11 fixture headers to say managed HTTP is not yet corpus-graded and that these fixtures grade reply routing only. Optionally delete the fixtures that add nothing beyond the five core override fixtures.
- **(B) The real fix, M.** Add a `:fixture/transport` seam, the counterpart of `:fixture/clock`:
  - canned wire responses feed a request-attempt seam that sits below request normalisation and body preparation, and above `handle-response!` (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:1517`), with an abort capability;
  - the real `:rf.http/managed` then runs, and together with `:fixture/clock` the fixtures reach retry and backoff;
  - the 11 fixtures are rewritten to declare no `:rf.http/managed` body;
  - the seam must cover binary responses, timeouts and cancellation. Coordinate with the HTTP owner.

## Acceptance

- **(A):** neither Q8 nor any fixture header claims Spec-014 coverage the fixture cannot provide.
- **(B):**
  - no fixture declares a body for `:rf.http/managed`;
  - breaking decode, `:accept` handling or the retry loop in `implementation/http/` turns at least one fixture red;
  - retry exhaustion takes `:max-attempts` attempts on the controlled clock;
  - the whole corpus is green on both hosts.

## Notes

- **Origin:** Opus conformance-security review (Insight 3, action 2). Sol (surface 32, insight 6) found the same canned-dispatch gap independently and narrowed the wording to "cannot fail for any Spec-014 reason".
- **Related:** none open. The managed-HTTP privacy leaks found in the http review are exactly what a transport seam would let the corpus witness.
- **Hot-zone files:** none for (A). `spec/Implementor-Checklist.md` and the fixtures are not on the list. (B) touches `implementation/http/src/` and the conformance runner, which are not hot.
- **Supporting detail:** `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/conformance-security.md` Insight 3 and action 2; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/32-conformance-security.md` §6.
notes:
== RULING (delegated by Mike; decided 2026-10-10 23:47:49 AUSEST at HEAD 200a67df2d) ==

DECISION: Option A. The 11 `spec/conformance/fixtures/http-managed-*.edn` fixtures STAY, relabelled as what they are: examples of core `:fx-overrides` redirection, args forwarding and reply dispatch, shaped like Spec 014 scenarios. Checklist Q8, the conformance README and the implementor skill stop saying the corpus grades managed HTTP. Q8's obligation does NOT change: a port that claims it still ships the whole Spec 014 contract and verifies it with its own tests. The abort fixture's impossible order is fixed in the same change. Option B, a `:fixture/transport` harness seam that runs the real fx, is filed as its own deferred bead, rf2-mn2ht.71, which depends on rf2-mn2ht.61 and on this bead.

WHY: The defect is a false claim, a silent false certification of a hypothetical alternative port, not a runtime bug. The reference's HTTP is graded on its own lane: `implementation/http/test/` holds 54 test files, 16 of which drive the real transport against an in-process `HttpServer` on the JVM. A prose edit removes the false claim completely. B is the right end state for the corpus's purpose ("AI-implementable from the spec alone", `spec/conformance/README.md:4`), but it is a design act rather than a fix:
- it creates a normative boundary Spec 014 does not have;
- it needs HTTP backoff moved onto the clock primitive;
- it adds a fixture key that rf2-mn2ht.61's unknown-key check must know about.
Nobody is building a second port today. Under the stance (pre-alpha, no gold plating) the answer is to fix the claim now and build the teeth when Q8 certification matters. Keeping the fixtures, rather than deleting them (which the bead offered as optional under A), costs nothing and keeps the scenarios and expected envelopes B will reuse: under B the `:fixture/expect` blocks largely survive and only the stub bodies become wire responses.

REJECTED:
- B now: the right end state at the wrong time. It is M-L on both hosts, and the design risk sits in the seam's async shape (a JVM `CompletableFuture` against a Fetch promise), binary bodies, timeouts and cancellation. Filed deferred as rf2-mn2ht.71 instead.
- C (route through the shipped canned stubs: drop the fixture fx bodies and pass `:value` / `:kind` / `:tags` in the args): it does grade real code (args validation, the interceptor chain, reply-target lowering, `:correlation` echo, `:rf.http/aborted` mapping to `:cancelled`). But it certifies test helpers rather than the production fx, and the six classification, retry and abort fixtures stay hollow because the stub echoes whatever kind it is given. A half-measure that still needs A's relabel; B's rewrite supersedes it.
- D (delete the 11): removes the hollow claim but throws away readable scenarios B would re-derive, and the README's worked-example row would need replacing. Nothing gained over A.

WHERE THE REVIEWS AGREED / DISAGREED: The dossier author and Codex both recommend A now with B deferred, and both keep the fixtures. Each ran an independent JVM probe showing 11/11 passing with every `:rf.http/*` fx unregistered. There is no disagreement on facts. Codex sharpened four points; all four are adopted:
1. "Reply routing only" overstates what runs. The fixtures do not test Spec 014 reply-target selection, because the stub body names the target literally (`http-managed-get-success.edn:43` dispatches `[:article/loaded …]` itself). What runs is core fx-override redirection, args forwarding (`:effects-routed`) and ordinary dispatch and frame inheritance.
2. Don't overclaim the other way. The corpus does run real Spec 014 code in one place: `data-classification-http-carrier-extends-defaults.edn` calls `rf.http.privacy-headers/redact-headers` through the runner's `:redact-headers` call op (`conformance_runner.cljc:1142-1155`). It is tagged `:data-classification/classification-effects`, not Q8. So the prose says "the managed-HTTP lifecycle is not corpus-graded", never "no Spec 014 code is graded anywhere".
3. Keep Q8's full obligation, and state the limit where a port EVALUATES its corpus result (the skill's conformance reference), not only in the checklist.
4. B's seam is a conformance-harness contract: portable fixture inputs, attempt observations, controlled completions and cancellation, which a port's harness adapter realises with its own internals. It is not a public app API, and it must carry binary bodies (`handle-response!` consumes `:body-binary`, `transport.cljc:1534`, `:1579`). The dossier's B sketch made the seam a normative Spec 014 surface every Q8 port must expose; Codex's lighter framing is the one carried into rf2-mn2ht.71.
The mayor made no recommendation on the bead.

EVIDENCE (all at HEAD 200a67df2d; none of the cited paths changed between the dossier's read at 9b51da3393 and here, `git diff --stat 9b51da3393 200a67df2d -- <cited paths>` empty):
- Census: 11 files match `spec/conformance/fixtures/http-managed-*.edn`. Every one declares `:rf.http/managed [[:noop]]` under `:fixture/handlers :fx`, a literal body for `:rf.http/managed-canned-success` or `-failure`, and `:fx-overrides {:rf.http/managed :rf.http/managed-canned-…}`.
  - 12 fixtures carry the `:rf.http/managed` capability tag. The 12th is `derivation-graph-algebra-full.edn:65`, which names the transport only as a graph label and grades no HTTP.
  - The 5 `resources-*` and 8 `ep-0037-*` fixtures also stub `:rf.http/managed [[:noop]]` but carry no Q8 tag; they grade the resource runtime and are out of scope here.
- Runner: `implementation/core/test/re_frame/conformance_runner.cljc:441-457`. For every fx id with an explicit fixture body it calls `claim-fixture-id!` and then `rf.fx/reg-fx id …`, replacing both the framework's `:rf.http/managed` and the real canned stubs from `re-frame.http.test-support`.
- The contract text being corrected:
  - `spec/Implementor-Checklist.md:102` (Q8: "decoding, success/failure normalisation, retry-with-backoff, abort, schema-driven decode, and reply-to-origin dispatch") and `:104` ("**Declaring yes runs the `:rf.http/managed` fixtures.**");
  - `:500` (H1 trade-offs: "defeats the stale-suppression contract the `:rf.http/managed` fixtures assert"), although no fixture carrying the tag asserts stale suppression;
  - `spec/conformance/README.md:321` (the capability row) and `:348` (the worked-example row, "The managed-HTTP fx happy path.");
  - `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/conformance.md:72` (the Q8 row).
- False fidelity claim in the headers: `http-managed-get-success.edn:9-11` says "which Spec 014 §Testing guarantees produces the same dispatch shape the real fx would". But the fixture replaces the canned stub too, and even the real stub (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/test_support.cljc`) echoes the `:value` / `:kind` / `:tags` it is given and classifies and decodes nothing. Spec 014 §Testing says so itself: the stubs deliver "a **minimal canonical reply**", and "A stub has no real request lifecycle".
- Probes. Both reviewers ran them independently on the JVM, using the real shared `re-frame.conformance-runner/run-fixture` with the JVM host map.
  - Dossier author, at 9b51da3393: `cd implementation/core; clojure -Spath -A:test > cp.txt` (exit 0), then `java -cp "$(cat cp.txt)" clojure.main probe.clj` (exit 0). A stock host registers `(:rf.http/managed :rf.http/managed-abort :rf.http/managed-canned-failure :rf.http/managed-canned-success)`. All 11 fixtures read A=true on the stock host and B=true with every `:rf.http/*` fx unregistered ("removed 4 ids; remaining after unregister: []").
  - Control C: `get-success` with the fixture's fx bodies removed and `:value` passed in the args, so the shipped canned stub runs. True under A, false under B (`expected trace not seen: {:operation :rf.fx/override-applied …}`), so the sabotage bites.
  - Row E: the real `:rf.http/managed` with no stubs and no override fails with `:final-db {}`, because there is no server. So "just delete the stubs" fails, which is why B needs a seam.
  - Codex reproduced 11/11 under both conditions, and the same control, with process exit 0 and fixture root `C:/Users/miket/code/re-frame2/spec/conformance/fixtures`.
- Abort fixture order: `http-managed-abort-by-request-id.edn:66-67` overrides BOTH `:rf.http/managed` and `:rf.http/managed-abort` to canned-failure, so `:slow/load` itself dispatches the cancelled reply. The expected trace at `:81-91` records `:slow/load-error` running (line 87) BEFORE `:slow/abort` is dispatched (line 88), and then again after it. A cancelled reply before the abort is impossible under Spec 014 §Aborts.
- Clock alias:
  - HTTP backoff arms with `rf.interop/set-timeout!` (`implementation/http/src/re_frame/http/transport.cljc:1352`) and cancels with `clear-timeout!` (`:1247`, `:1396`, `:1408`).
  - The `:fixture/clock` seam redefines only `rf.interop/schedule-after!` / `cancel-scheduled!` (`conformance_runner.cljc:1607-1608`).
  - Those two are `def` aliases holding the same fn values (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/interop.clj:189-190`, `interop.cljs:164-165`). They are separate vars, so `with-redefs` on an alias leaves direct `set-timeout!` callers on the real host timer.
- Spec 014 names no transport seam. A ripgrep over `spec/014-HTTPRequests.md` for `seam|transport abstraction|schedule-after|Clock abstraction` hits only line 484 (the internal `:aborted?`-cell abort-precedence "implementation seam") and incidental long lines (904, 1075, 1530). There is no port-facing attempt boundary and no reference to Spec 005 §Clock abstraction.

IMPLEMENTATION GUIDANCE (one worker, size S, no hot-zone file, safe in parallel with anything):
- `spec/Implementor-Checklist.md`
  - Q8 (`:102-104`): keep the obligation sentence as it is. Replace "Declaring yes runs the `:rf.http/managed` fixtures." with a short honest statement. Declaring yes runs those fixtures, but each one stubs the fx under test, so they grade only core `:fx-overrides` redirection, args forwarding and reply dispatch, and a port passes them without any managed-HTTP code. The Spec 014 lifecycle (status classification, decode, `:accept`, retry/backoff, abort) is not yet corpus-graded; a port claiming Q8 verifies it with its own tests.
  - H1 (`:500`): change "defeats the stale-suppression contract the `:rf.http/managed` fixtures assert" so it points at Spec 014's contract (`014-HTTPRequests.md#stale-suppression--the-four-triggers`), not at the fixtures.
  - H2's "CLJS schedules on the same timer seam the machine `:after` implementation uses" is true at runtime (it is the same fn value) and is left alone. rf2-mn2ht.71 makes it literally true at the var level.
- `spec/conformance/README.md`
  - `:321`: after "claimed whole", add one sentence saying the `http-managed-*` fixtures supply their own stub bodies and grade override routing, so passing them does not establish the managed-HTTP lifecycle.
  - `:348`: reword the description cell ("The managed-HTTP fx happy path.") to say what runs. Keep the tag set, because the table is a tag-vocabulary reference (`:337`).
  - Add a short "Managed-HTTP lifecycle (not yet corpus-graded)" section beside §Render-time observables (`:635-639`), in the same shape. It says what cannot be expressed today (there is no harness seam below the fx), where it is verified instead (host tests; for the CLJS reference, `implementation/http/test/`), and that a transport seam is future work. No bead id in the prose (the present-tense rule, CLAUDE.md §Conventions & Patterns).
- `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/conformance.md:72` (the Q8 row): add that the fixtures it runs grade override routing only, so Q8 behaviour is self-tested, not corpus-graded. Where the skill tells a port to report its gate-2 score, add one sentence that a Q8 pass is no evidence of the Spec 014 lifecycle. Check `docs/skills/re-frame2-implementor.md` for a mirrored claim.
- The 11 fixtures: rewrite each header comment and `:fixture/doc` so it claims only what runs. The fixture supplies stub bodies for `:rf.http/managed` and the canned stub, and grades `:fx-overrides` redirection, args forwarding (`:effects-routed`) and reply dispatch; its scenario and envelope mirror the Spec 014 section it names, for readability.
  - Delete every "Spec 014 §Testing guarantees … same dispatch shape" claim.
  - The retry headers (`retry-exhaustion :8-11`, `retry-recover :9-12`) already half-admit this; make them consistent with the rest.
  - Do not change any `:fixture/id`, capability set or `:fixture/expect` block, except in the abort fixture.
- Abort fixture (`http-managed-abort-by-request-id.edn`):
  - Remove `:rf.http/managed :rf.http/managed-canned-failure` from `:fx-overrides`. Keep `:rf.http/managed-abort -> canned-failure` and the `:rf.http/managed [[:noop]]` body.
  - The expected trace becomes: `:slow/load` run-start, `:slow/abort` run-start, override-applied `{:rf.fx/from :rf.http/managed-abort :rf.fx/to :rf.http/managed-canned-failure}`, then `:slow/load-error` run-start. `:final-app-db` is unchanged.
  - Rewrite the header and the comments at `:37-41`, `:49-50`, `:62-65` and `:84-86` to match, and say plainly that it remains an override example, not a cancellation test.
- FAILING-FIRST. The prose has no executable red. The abort change does, but NOT through `:trace-emissions`: both `check-trace-emissions` and `check-effects-routed` (`conformance_runner.cljc:655-678`) are ORDER-PRESERVING SUBSET matchers ("Extras are tolerated"), so the new, shorter trace expectation also matches the old run.
  - To make the fix discriminate, add an `:effects-routed` expectation. Its first entry is `{:fx-id :rf.http/managed :args {:request {:method :get :url "/slow"} :request-id :slow/load :decode :json :on-failure [:slow/load-error]}}` (the post-override id, read off the `:rf.fx/handled` traces), followed by `{:fx-id :rf.http/managed-canned-failure :args :slow/load}`.
  - It is red with the old `:fx-overrides` (the load routes as canned-failure, so no `:rf.http/managed` entry appears), green with the fix, and red again with the old override restored. Confirm the exact args shape from a run rather than trusting this sketch.
- Gates:
  - the JVM corpus, `cd implementation/core && clojure -M:test -n re-frame.conformance-test`: green, with the corpus fixture count unchanged;
  - `scripts/check_conformance_fixture_edn.py` on the edited fixtures;
  - the CLJS corpus, `npm run test:cljs`, only under a coordinator build-lane grant; otherwise cite CI;
  - `mkdocs build --strict` and `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` for the Checklist and README;
  - the skill guards `scripts/check_skill_implementor_partition_drift.py` and `scripts/check_skill_implementor_order.py`.
  The Python gates print no banner, so plant a fault in a line you are already editing to prove each one read your tree (AGENTS.md §Running Gates).
- Hot zones: none. `spec/Implementor-Checklist.md`, `spec/conformance/README.md`, the fixtures and the skill are not on the list. Do not touch `spec/Spec-Schemas.md`.
- Acceptance: the bead's own clause is kept ("neither Q8 nor any fixture header claims Spec-014 coverage the fixture cannot provide"). In addition, the abort fixture's cancelled reply follows the abort, pinned by the discriminating `:effects-routed` entry, and Q8's obligation text is unchanged.
- After merge, close this bead. rf2-mn2ht.71 depends on it and stays deferred.

PRESERVED ANALYSIS:
- Who is hit: only an alternative port, meaning a human or an AI following `skills/re-frame2-implementor`, whose acceptance gate 2 scores "the full claimed-capability fixture set". Such a port claims Q8, passes 11/11, and is told its managed HTTP conforms whether or not it decodes, retries or aborts. The reference and app developers are unaffected, so P3 is right.
- Same defect class as rf2-k2r1, where the accounting certified a flowless port ("repairing only the skip leaves the accounting certifying a flowless port"). Here the accounting certifies an HTTP-less port.
- Precedent for documenting a limit: `spec/conformance/README.md` §Render-time observables (out of scope), and `skills/re-frame2-implementor/references/phase-2-impl-order.md:93` ("self-reported unless the port tests it").
- What the 11 actually grade duplicates five non-HTTP fixtures that exist at HEAD: `fx-override-by-id`, `dispatch-envelope`, `error-override-fallthrough`, `replay-with-interceptor-override` and `cross-spec-portable-story-fx-override`. The 11 are kept anyway for their readable Spec 014-shaped scenarios, which B reuses.
- What each header claims (in every row, what actually runs is the fixture's own `:dispatch`):
  - `get-success`: GET, JSON decode, `:accept`, envelope synthesis;
  - `post-json`: body encoding and the request envelope;
  - `decode-failure`: decode classification;

title: Machines spawn registered types only: remove inline :definition, resolve :spawn-all join callbacks by reference, keep every runtime-db machine slot EDN (round-trip + SSR leak)
description:
## Bug

Machine durable state holds executable definitions: an inline `:definition` spawn stores the whole authored spec at the actor's `:rf/machine-type`, and a `:spawn-all` join stores the authored spec, callbacks included, in its join state. Two things break as a result:

- **EDN round-trip.** A fn guard, action or `:on-done` inside those copies makes the snapshot and the `:spawned` registry unreadable after `pr-str`. That is the stability invariant SSR hydration and epoch replay rely on.
- **Hydration leak.** A `:sensitive`-declared `:data` default is redacted in the live `:data` but ships raw in its blueprint copy. The SSR projector carries every non-`:data` slot verbatim, so the default reaches every visitor's hydration payload.

## Evidence

- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc:343-356` — `machine-type-ref` returns `(or (:machine-id args) (:definition args))`. `:644` stamps it as `:rf/machine-type`.
- `lifecycle_fx/resolver.cljc:66-85` — `spec-from-snapshot` returns a map type verbatim.
- `spawn.cljc:783` — `prepared-type-ref` can pin a copied registered definition when the registrar changes between preflight and install.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/transition.cljc:2702-2708` — the join state is `{:children … :spec spawn-all-spec …}`, the authored `:spawn-all` map.
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/ssr.cljc:84-102` — only `:data` is projected; "`:rf/machine-type` … ride VERBATIM", and the `:spawned` slot rides unchanged.
- `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/payload_policy.cljc:886-900` — the payload check walks numbers only, so (*inferred*) a fn reaches the wire as `#object[…]`, which the client's EDN reader rejects.

Repro (*probed* at trunk on the JVM, from `implementation/ssr` with the machines artefact):

```clojure
(rf/reg-machine :p/parent
  {:initial :working :data {}
   :states {:working {:spawn {:definition {:initial   :wait
                                           :data      {:token "SECRET-DEFAULT"}
                                           :sensitive [[:data :token]]
                                           :states    {:wait {}}}
                              :id-prefix :p/kid}}}})
(rf/dispatch-sync [:p/parent [:rf.machine/start]])
(pp/project-runtime-db (rf.frame/frame-runtime-db-value :rf/default) :rf/default)
;; :p/kid#1 → {:data {:token :rf/redacted …}
;;             :rf/machine-type {:data {:token "SECRET-DEFAULT"} :sensitive [[:data :token]] …}}
```

- **Inline spawn:** `"SECRET-DEFAULT"` is in the projected payload: `true`.
- **Control:** the same definition registered with `reg-machine` and spawned by `:machine-id` gives `:rf/machine-type :p/kid-type`, and the secret is in the payload: `false`.
- **Inline child with a fn guard** (`:guards {:ok? (fn [_ _] true)}`): `(read-string (pr-str snapshot))` throws "No reader function for tag object".
- **`:spawn-all`** with a registered child carrying a fn `:on-done` and an inline child whose classified default is `"SECRET-JOIN"`:
  - the join state keys are `(:children :done :rf/attempt :cancelled :spec :invoke-id :resolved? :failed)`;
  - `(read-string (pr-str spawned))` throws "No reader function for tag object";
  - `"SECRET-JOIN"` appears under the projected `:spawned` slot, while the child's live `:data :token` is `:rf/redacted`.

Contract:
- Spec 005 stability invariant 1 (`spec/005-StateMachines.md:58`): `(read-string (pr-str snapshot))` returns an `=`-equal value, so that snapshots survive SSR hydration and epoch replay.
- The `:rf/machine-type` row (`:79`) promises that it "Persists across `pr-str` / `read-string` and through SSR hydration / epoch replay".
- Spec 015 §SSR and hydration (`spec/015-Data-Classification.md:403`) requires classified state to be projected before it crosses the hydration wire.

## Expected

Every durable machine slot is EDN facts and references. A classified default exists only in `:data`, where projection reaches it.

## Fix direction

Mike's call between two designs; both reviews prefer references to definitions:

- **A. Spawn registered types only** (the Opus machines review). Remove inline `:definition`, so `:rf/machine-type` is always a keyword. Drop `:spec` from join state and resolve child entries and callbacks from the parent's registered definition at the invoke path. Delete `prepared-type-ref`'s pinning.
  - This is breaking: inline `:definition` spawns appear in 7 machines test files and one epoch test; no example or doc teaches them.
  - It also removes spawn-time definition validation, and lets a spawned actor's handler resolve through its type's registrar entry.
- **B. Scoped references** (the Sol machines review). Keep inline authoring inside a registered parent, but store a reference such as `[parent-type invoke-path]` and resolve the definition and callbacks from the parent's registered definition. A hand-emitted `[:rf.machine/spawn {:definition …}]` from a plain event has no parent to resolve through, and would need registering or refusing.

Not recommended: teaching the SSR projector to scrub blueprint copies. That leaves the round-trip broken and adds a third interpreter.

## Acceptance

- Spawn a child that has fn guards and a per-child fn `:on-done`. No fn reaches runtime-db, and every snapshot and `:spawned` slot satisfies `(= v (read-string (pr-str v)))`. Fails today.
- The inline-definition repro above, adapted to the chosen design, finds no `"SECRET-DEFAULT"` / `"SECRET-JOIN"` anywhere in `project-runtime-db` output. A control check confirms the scan can see a planted secret.
- Existing spawn, join, restore and hydration suites pass, with join callbacks resolving after hot reload.

## Notes

- Origin: Sol review (11 §4 round-trip; 08 §4 hydration echo), read; probed at trunk for this draft.
- Related: rf2-mn2ht.50 (the machine SSR collection-coordinate leak, in a different file). The conformance-security review proposes this exact case as a cross-boundary witness for the security tier.
- Hot-zone files: `spec/005-StateMachines.md` (the `:rf/machine-type` row at `:79`, the `:definition` rows, the spawn-all walkthrough) and `spec/Spec-Schemas.md` (the InvokeSpec `:machine-id` XOR `:definition`) are both hot, so sequence behind any other holder.
- Supporting detail: `ai/findings/advisarial-review/opus/machines.md` §13 and Action 1; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/11-machines.md` §4; `ai/findings/advisarial-review/sol/08-core-privacy-projection.md` §4.
notes:
== RULING (delegated by Mike; decided 2026-10-10 23:52:26 AUSEST at HEAD 200a67df2d) ==

DECISION: Option A. Machines spawn REGISTERED types only. `:definition` is removed from `:spawn`, from `:spawn-all` children and from `:rf.machine/spawn` args, so `:rf/machine-type` is always a keyword. The `:spawn-all` join state drops `:spec`: per-child `:on-done`, `:join` and the resolution events resolve from the parent's CURRENT registered definition at the invoke path, as single `:spawn` already does. Attempt identity stays on the attempt as EDN facts: membership, counts, tombstones, the attempt token, and fixed-vs-generated provenance. `prepared-type-ref`'s definition pin is deleted, and the `:rf/prepared` install scratch carries no executable values. Every machine slot in runtime-db is EDN, at every write.

WHY:
- The defect is that runtime-db holds programs. rf2-xjee ruled that "the registration is a load-time PROGRAM that makes an address creatable; the snapshot is the INSTANCE." Copying the program into the instance inverts that model. Storing references fixes both the round-trip and the SSR leak, and adds no new interpreter.
- A is mostly deletion, and it leaves one way to name a child. The programmer pays one `reg-machine` form per child. In return the child gets a name in Xray, in the registry catalogue and in `machine-transition` tests, and it gains hot reload and real version-drift checks.
- B keeps a convenience that no example app uses. Its price is a second reference shape that the resolver, tooling, Xray and the epoch drift check would all have to learn, plus recursive resolution for nested inline children, plus a refusal path for a hand-emitted `{:definition ...}`. And B loses the hand-emitted form anyway.
- This is not a one-way door. Inline authoring can come back later as a compatible widening (B, below) without disturbing the keyword reference.
- This is a pre-alpha breaking correction of a documented surface, authorized here under Mike's delegation. The docs, the skill, the spec and the schemas all teach inline `:definition` today, and they move in the same PR as the code.
- The join half is barely a choice. Under C or D, a fn-bearing `:spawn-all` stays unserialisable even when every child is registered.

ACCEPTED CONSEQUENCES (state each one in spec prose):
1. Join callbacks and join configuration follow hot reload. This REVERSES Spec 005's sentence "`:spec` is the snapshot of the invoke-all spec at spawn time so resolution is decoupled from later spec edits" (join-state section, 005:3870). Membership and attempt identity do NOT follow hot reload.
2. A registrar change between preflight and install is ordinary hot reload for a prepared child too.
   - Re-registration: the child runs the current definition.
   - Unregistration: the child still installs, because an admitted child always installs. It is then inert and answers `:rf.error/no-such-handler`, exactly like any live actor whose type was unregistered.
   - No closures are kept to rescue a programmer who changes the registrar mid-drain.
3. A runtime-generated definition is still possible: register it under a generated id. That registration must also exist wherever the snapshot is restored (the client, a reloaded page, an imported epoch), because EDN equality does not recreate a program. Trust the programmer.
4. Spawned children follow hot reload, and version-drift checks (`current-definition` in epoch `tool_pair.cljc`) become real for every spawned actor.

REJECTED:
- B. Inline `:definition` kept as sugar inside a registered parent and stored as a scoped reference `{:rf/parent-type ... :rf/invoke-id ... :rf/child-id?}`. It is credible and keeps locality. But every consumer would have to learn a second reference shape, the shape becomes recursive for nested inline grandchildren, and a hand-emitted inline spawn still has to be refused. B is PARKED as the PRE-SETTLED PROMOTION SHAPE, and the documented fallback.
  - Un-park trigger: a real app asks for anonymous children in a declarative `:spawn` / `:spawn-all`.
  - When un-parked, also weigh B's variant: at parent registration, desugar each inline child into a registered type under a derived id. That keeps `:rf/machine-type` a keyword, at the cost of synthetic registrar entries and their cleanup when the parent re-registers without that child.
  - Prefer a map-shaped reference over a positional `[parent path]` vector ("Name over place", spec/Principles.md).
- C. Keep inline children but mark those actors non-durable, so SSR and persistence drop them. This does not contain the problem: the parent's `:rf/spawned` mirror and the `:spawned` slot still name the dropped child, so a hydrated `:spawn-all` waits forever. It also does nothing for fn-bearing joins, and it creates two classes of actor.
- D. Change nothing and document that inline definitions are not serialisable. D would also have to declare any `:spawn-all` with a fn `:on-done` or a fn `:data` unserialisable, and that includes Spec 005's own per-child `:on-done` example and its quorum idiom. The production save loop and SSR would quietly stop working for ordinary apps, and the leak would stay.
- Teaching the SSR projector to scrub the blueprint copies. The round-trip stays broken, and this adds a third interpreter. The bead itself advised against it.
- A content-addressed definition registry, where the snapshot stores a hash. A definition's content includes fns, and a fn has no hash that agrees across processes or between JVM and CLJS. This fixes only the in-process case, which already works.
- Carrying the prepared executable spec in transient control state outside runtime-db as the PRIMARY mechanism. This is allowed only as a fallback (see guidance). The preferred path deletes those values instead of relocating them.

WHERE THE REVIEWS AGREED / DISAGREED:
- Dossier author: A, with the join resolved by reference and the pin deleted.
- Codex: A, the same, plus three refinements. I adopted all three:
  (i) Attempt identity is captured as EDN facts when the join is seeded, never looked up in a parent definition that may have been edited since. Otherwise a reload could change the work identity of work that already happened.
  (ii) `:rf/prepared` carries no executables. Otherwise the bead's literal acceptance, "no fn reaches runtime-db", stays unmet after the settled slots are fixed.
  (iii) The prepared-unregister tests change their expectations to ordinary registrar semantics.
- No mayor or worker recommendation was on the bead. Per the bead, the Opus machines review preferred A and the Sol review preferred B.
- One factual disagreement: the dossier said the malformed-hydration diagnostic fires only in debug builds, and Codex said an always-on record now dispatches. Settled at HEAD in Codex's favour. In `implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/boot.cljc` `read-server-payload`, the `rf.trace/emit-error! :rf.error/malformed-hydration-payload` sits inside `(when rf.interop/debug-enabled? ...)`, but the catch then calls `(dispatch-malformed-hydration-frameless! 'rf.ssr/read-server-payload element-id reason)` unconditionally ("the always-on record is intentionally frameless"). So production SSR does get a diagnostic. The page still falls back to client-only and loses all server state. Persistence's `load!` still swallows the failure silently.
- On refinement (ii), I settled the fact by reading `spawn.cljc` at HEAD; I did not re-probe it. `spawn-all-init-fx` seeds the join with `:rf/prepared` holding `(select-keys % [:spec :snap :type-spec])` per child (`spawn.cljc:2066-2070`). `:spec` is the stamped definition, fns included, and `:type-spec` is the raw definition. Each child install drops its own entry in the same swap that lands its snapshot (`drop-prepared-entry`, :741-755), so the scratch exists only mid-drain. But a frame-state watch sees it (Codex's probe), and it is the one fn left once the settled slots are fixed.

EVIDENCE (HEAD 200a67df2d unless stated):
- `implementation/machines/src/re_frame/machines/lifecycle_fx/spawn.cljc:343-356`: `machine-type-ref` is `(or (:machine-id args) (:definition args))`, stamped as `:rf/machine-type` at :643-644.
- `lifecycle_fx/resolver.cljc:66-85`: `spec-from-snapshot` returns a map type verbatim (`(map? t) t`).
- `spawn.cljc:783-849`: `prepared-type-ref` returns the keyword while the registrar holds exactly the prepared definition, and `type-spec` verbatim otherwise. That verbatim definition is the pin.
- `transition.cljc:2702-2708`: the join seed is `{:children ... :done #{} :failed #{} :resolved? false :spec spawn-all-spec :invoke-id invoke-id}`.
- `lifecycle_fx/join.cljc` reads `:spec` in three places:
  - :170 `join-work-generation`: `(contains? child-spec :fixed-actor-id)` selects the attempt token, otherwise `actor-generation spawned-id`;
  - :575 `child-spec-at`, which supplies the per-child `:on-done`;
  - :836 `intercept-fold`, which receives `(:spec join-state)` and uses it for `:join`, for the resolution events, and for the child count. `join-condition-met?` and `join-unsatisfiable?` count `(:children spec)`.
- The single-`:spawn` contrast: `lifecycle_fx/registration.cljc:710` does `(:on-done (resolver/spawn-spec-at (:machine ctx) invoke-id))`, with the helper at `resolver.cljc:182-208`. A nil lookup (the spawn was removed by a reload) means no fold, and the carrier rides through.
- `machines/ssr.cljc`: every non-`:data` slot, `:rf/machine-type` included, "ride[s] VERBATIM" (:83-86), and `:spawned` rides verbatim (:116-119). The namespace docstring (:36-41) says the sibling slots carry "no user `:data`", which is false today: the join `:spec` holds inline child definitions with their `:data` defaults and fns, plus any child `:data` override map.
- Spec 005:58, invariant 1: "`(read-string (pr-str snapshot))` returns an `=`-equal value." The 005:79 row allows "an inline-`:definition` spec map" and, in the same row, promises it "Persists across `pr-str` / `read-string` and through SSR hydration / epoch replay". The row contradicts itself whenever the map holds a fn.
- `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:2912` requires `[:spec :map]`. Spec 015:403 requires classified state to be projected before it crosses the hydration wire.
- `epoch/tool_pair.cljc:245-272`: `current-definition` reads an inline actor's "current" definition from the very snapshot it is checking, so drift can never fire for inline actors.
- `docs/machines/persist-and-restore.md:12-25`: `save!` `pr-str`s `:rf.runtime/machines`, and `load!` wraps the read in `(catch :default _ nil)`. One fn anywhere means nothing restores, silently.
- The dossier author's JVM probe, run from `implementation/ssr` at trunk around 9f53325507 with `clojure -Sdeps '{:aliases {:probe {:main-opts ["<scratch>/probe.clj"]}}}' -M:test:probe`, exited 0. Verbatim output lines:
  - inline child with a fn guard and a `:sensitive` default:
    `:rf/machine-type keys: (:data :guards :initial :sensitive :states)`
    `snapshot EDN round-trip: THROWS: No reader function for tag object`
    `projected :data :token: :rf/redacted`
    `projected :rf/machine-type :data :token: "SECRET-DEFAULT"`
    `tool/trace egress walker, :rf/machine-type :data :token: :rf/redacted`
    `save!/load! loop reads back: THROWS: No reader function for tag object`
    `after re-registering the parent with a :go2 edge, live inline kid state after [:go2]: :wait` (the inline child ignores hot reload)
  - control, the same child registered: `snapshot EDN round-trip: true` and `SECRET-REG in hydration projection? false`
  - a `:spawn-all` with registered children only and one fn `:on-done`:
    `join-state keys: (:cancelled :children :done :failed :invoke-id :resolved? :rf/attempt :spec)`
    `whole :rf.runtime/machines EDN round-trip: THROWS: No reader function for tag object`
- Codex's probes, run from `implementation/machines` at 9b51da3393 (`clojure -Sdeps ... -M -` via stdin, with the plain-atom reset fixture), both exited 0.

title: [bug] check_doc_slugs.py does not validate markdown links inside fenced code blocks — a link gate that fails OPEN
description:
MEASURED BY rf2-zk1xu's worker on 2026-08-21, as a by-product of its planted-fault proof, and it is a fail-open in a gate this project nominates constantly.

THE FINDING, in the worker's own words: its first planted fault broke a markdown link anchor INSIDE a fenced code block it had just added to spec/Spec-Schemas.md, and scripts/check_doc_slugs.py came back GREEN. A second plant in Spec-Schemas PROSE red at exit 1 naming the planted slug, which both proved the gate read that worktree and pinned the blindness as fence-scoped rather than file-scoped or worktree-scoped.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. This is the same shape as every other fail-open hunted in this repo: a search that returns zero reads identically to a check that passed. A broken link inside a fence is invisible, so an edit confined to a fenced block — and spec/Spec-Schemas.md's *Tags schemas all live inside fences — is UNGATED while the PR body truthfully reports check_doc_slugs.py exit 0. The worker hand-verified its own link because it had caught this; the next author will not know to.

VERIFY THE PREMISE FIRST, at origin/main HEAD, and do it in BOTH directions: plant a broken link target inside a fenced block (expect green, which is the defect) and the same target in prose (expect red, which is the control). A one-direction probe cannot tell blindness from a bad plant.

THE OPEN QUESTION IS WHETHER TO FIX IT OR DOCUMENT IT, and that is a judgement the worker should make and argue rather than assume. Skipping fenced blocks may be DELIBERATE — a fence often carries illustrative or third-party markdown that is not meant to resolve, and validating it would red on examples by design. If that is the reason, the correct deliverable is not a code change: it is one sentence at the top of the checker saying so, plus a line in whatever prose nominates this gate, so the next author knows what the exit 0 does not cover. If there is no such reason, validate inside fences.

DO NOT grow this into a rewrite of the checker. Read what it does, establish which case this is, and land the smaller of the two.

SCOPE: scripts/check_doc_slugs.py and its tests. Do NOT edit spec/ pages to work around it.

FENCE: none known at filing. Re-derive at dispatch.

## The decision in one sentence

Four Xray `rf/reg-view` sites are the only remaining HOST-VISIBLE side effect of loading the Xray preload in a `goog.DEBUG=false` bundle; decide whether to gate them (a one-line `when` per site, my refinement of the bead's A1) or to leave them and rule the four documents true-as-written (B).

## The problem, carefully

**What survives.** A `:require`d namespace's top-level forms run at ns-load, outside that block. rf2-y8doi.16 moved eleven `reg-sub`/`reg-event` writes into `install!` fns (PR #9934) and deliberately left four `rf/reg-view` forms, because the macro's expansion is a `do` that registers AND `def`s the symbol to `(re-frame.core/view id)`, returning the id (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/core_reg_view_macro.cljc:208-214`; `def-form` at :133-135). The four, re-derived at trunk — PR #10031 moved two of them since the bead was written:

| site | id registered (derived by `(keyword (str ns) (str sym))`, macro :92; none carries `^{:rf/id}`) |
| --- | --- |
| `tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/shell.cljs:2561` `event-list` | `:day8.re-frame2-xray.shell/event-list` |

**What a `goog.DEBUG=false` bundle carrying the preload gets from the four, by construction (no build was run — the brief forbids it, and no such build exists in the tree; `tools/xray/README.md:358-362`):**

1. Four `:view`-kind slots in the HOST's process-global registrar. `re-frame.core/reg-view*` (`core.cljc:863-892`) calls `rf.views/reg-view*` (`views.cljs:836-884`), which composes a component head and `rf.registrar/register!`s it at :883. 5. NO DOM, NO listeners, NO behaviour. Mounting lives inside the gated block (`preload.cljs:133`) and in the manual verbs; nothing renders the four. The registrar's trace emit is inert under the same flag (spec/009 §Production builds, `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1082-1094`).

**The four are NOT the only ungated load-time side effects — but they are the only host-visible ones.** A column-0 sweep of `tools/xray/src` for bang-calls and `set!`/`swap!`/`add-watch` forms (two Grep patterns, control: the two gated `(when rf.interop/debug-enabled?` forms at `preload.cljs:94` and `trace_collector.cljs:461` were found by the second) reads nine more: seven `register-first-mount-hook!` forms (`mount.cljs:740-934`) writing a `defonce` private atom (`mount.cljs:457-467`, `:507`), `mount/register-popout-keydown-installer!` (`keybinding.cljs:668` → `reset!` of a private atom, `mount.cljs:126`), `config/register-settings-applier!` (`settings/effects.cljs:812` → `reset!`, `config.cljc:1573`), and an `add-watch` on `config/keybinding-enabled?` (`keybinding.cljs:700`). ## Make it tangible

What the macro turns one site into today (`core_reg_view_macro.cljc:208-214`, simplified):

```clojure
(rf/reg-view edn-inspector "…" [_value & _opts] …)
;; =>
(do
  (binding [rf.source-coords/*pending-coords* (if debug-enabled? <dev-coords> <prod-coords>)]
    (re-frame.core/reg-view* ::edn-inspector {…} (fn edn-inspector [...] …)))   ; UNCONDITIONAL
  (def edn-inspector (re-frame.core/view ::edn-inspector))                        ; head in dev
  ::edn-inspector)
```

The `debug-enabled?` gates inside the expansion cover only the coord literals (:153-164); the registration runs whatever the flag says. And `(rf/view id)` is eager, not lazy: `view-head` returns nil when nothing is registered (`views.cljs:800-816`), which is why the .16 worker could not move the registration into an `install!` — the top-level `def` would bind nil in DEV too.

**Option A1-wrap (mine, a refinement of the bead's A1 — one line per site):**

```clojure
(when ^boolean rf.interop/debug-enabled?
  (rf/reg-view edn-inspector "…" [_value & _opts] …))
```

Dev (`goog.DEBUG` true — every watch build, the node lane and the browser lane): identical expansion, identical head, identical `def`; the injected `dispatch`/`subscribe` that `edn-inspector` relies on (`edn_inspector.cljs:5184`, `:5203-5205`) are untouched. Release (`goog.DEBUG=false`, preload mis-shipped): Closure constant-folds `(if false …)`; no registration, the var is never assigned (`nil?` answers true), and the render body plus everything only it reached becomes unreachable and is stripped — the machines-viz chart included. Nothing in that bundle calls the four (their callers sit behind the gated boot block), so a nil head is never rendered. `.clj-kondo/config.edn:37-45` already switches `:inline-def` OFF because the `reg-view` hook rewrites to `defn`, so the lint stays quiet. No in-tree precedent for a `def` under a `when` (Grep, multiline, 0 hits against a control that found Fresco's gated forms), and CLJS interns a var wherever its `def` sits — the worker compiles ONE site in a dev build and reads the node lane before doing the other three; if the compiler objects, fall to B.

**Option A1b (the bead's literal A1):** replace each site with `(when debug-enabled? (rf/reg-view* ::id {…} (fn …)))` plus `(def sym (rf/view ::id))`. Same release result as A1-wrap, but `reg-view*` is documented as "no auto-def, no auto-inject" (`spec/API.md:102`), so `edn-inspector`'s frame-aware `dispatch`/`subscribe` would have to be hand-built with `capture-frame` — more code for the same outcome. `event-list` already uses `(:dispatch (rf/capture-frame))` and `rf/subscribe` (`shell.cljs:2661-2700`), `Chart` reads nothing (`:453`), so only `edn-inspector` pays, but it pays for nothing A1-wrap does not give.

**Option B (docs):** leave the four; at most one clause each in `Tool-Pair.md:821` and `API.md:19-24` — e.g. after "so Closure DCE strips them from production bundles": "(the boot block only; a required namespace's own top-level `reg-view` forms are not inside it — see 011 §Production posture)". 011 and README need nothing.

**Option B0 (mine, zero edits):** rule that the two summary sentences are true as enumerations and that the normative page (011, to which `Tool-Pair.md:817` defers) already states the exception; close the bead with that as the reason.

What a host sees, per option, in a mis-shipped `goog.DEBUG=false` bundle: today — four `day8.re-frame2-xray.*` rows in its registrar and the four render bodies' bytes; A1-wrap/A1b — zero registrar rows, fewer bytes (the nine private-atom writes and their handlers remain); B/B0 — unchanged, documented.

## Recommendation

**A1-wrap.** It is the cheapest option that leaves nothing overstated: four one-line edits under `tools/xray`, no hot-zone file, no framework change, no dev-mode change, and the hot-zone sentence becomes true without being opened. The thing hosts rely on — "the preload puts nothing of Xray's in my registrar" — is worth keeping literally true when the price is this low, and the nine private-atom writes that remain are Xray's own furniture, which is where "trust the programmer" applies: nobody needs a gate, a census or a diagnostic for those. Skip the optional prod-elision test unless Mike wants the promise pinned; the expansion is read, not measured, and that is proportionate here.

What would change my mind: the compiler or Closure rejecting or warning on a `def` under `when` — then B0, because 011 already says what is true and the summary sentences are true as enumerations, and a hot-zone edit to say it a second time is minutiae. And note the direction of travel makes any of this temporary: `event-list`'s migration to `rf.fresco/defview` is stated as entirely within `shell.cljs` (`:2615-2619`), `Chart` and `edn-inspector` already have `defview` twins (`machine_canvas.cljs:461`, `edn_inspector.cljs:5207`) and keep the `reg-view` heads only for Reagent-tree callers, and `resizable-table`'s head has "NO PRODUCTION CONSUMER" (`resizable_table.cljs:797-801`) — and `defview` gates its registration by construction (`fresco.cljc:279-281`). A1-wrap is a holding pattern that costs nothing to unwind as each site migrates.

title: Incomplete matrix-change guidance: trigger-only changes can activate existing PR checks
description:
Audit of PR #9920 (de3d2c9073a5940ec3b5bf0c3aaa4e1fe40f4c29). The new merge-criterion discharge correctly distinguishes on-block keys from job definitions, but is incomplete as guidance for deciding whether the PR check matrix changed: a new pull_request trigger can activate EXISTING jobs while adding zero jobs. Filtering the trigger match away must not discharge clause 5 as no check-set change.

The PR's own pure-example commit proves the missing case. Parsed .github/workflows/docs.yml at b853f9d57db5^: events [push, workflow_dispatch], existing jobs [build, deploy]. At b853f9d57db5: events [push, pull_request, workflow_dispatch], SAME two jobs, with deploy newly gated to push. The commit's purpose/body explicitly says PRs now build docs before merge. Thus ZERO job definitions added is true but does not establish zero newly scheduled PR checks; build was previously absent from that event and now runs for matching paths. The guidance currently presents this as a pure false-positive/phantom-band example without stating the distinction.

Required correction: retain the structural jobs-versus-on check, and add the complementary rule that trigger/path/branch-filter changes must be evaluated for their effect on which existing jobs participate in PR checks. Correct the example to distinguish job-definition delta from effective check-set delta. Refer back to loops.md clause 5 (check set computed against current workflow matrix). No new CI gate, parser service or exhaustive GitHub-events list is requested.

Acceptance: a trigger-only change cannot be dismissed as no matrix change solely because the added-job-key count is zero; the same b853f9d57db5 before/after YAML is enough to demonstrate why. No runtime test needed for this prose correction. Searched all open Bead descriptions for trigger with band/job-key overlap; no exact open record. Source status must remain unchanged.

description:
HELD FOR MIKE — a product call, not a defect; nothing is built for it. Recorded first on rf2-b7o66 by the research revision, and moved here so the hold survives rf2-b7o66 closing.

OPTIONS:
  A. Keep inheritance, document it. Zero code. Chapter 02 already says CSS is shared; a subject that relies on inherited colour sees Story chrome. Cost: every author meets it once.
  B. Reset colour and font at the cell boundary (the subject gets browser defaults, not Story chrome). Small, contained change in the canvas/cell style. Cost: a subject that intentionally inherits from its app shell sees browser defaults instead, which is also not the real app.
  C. Let the author or a decorator choose the subject ambient (e.g. a background/text preset in the toolbar). Most faithful; most surface; closest to what the research lists under do-not-build until a real CSS-isolation job is named.

MAYOR LEAN, as a claim with its cost: B is the smallest change that stops Story chrome leaking into every subject, and it matches the chapter 02 paragraph; A is what the stance defaults to if nobody is bitten twice. Not dispatched either way.

title: api(testing): drift — hicasso wait-until! over poll-until; stale flush-views! docstrings; slim twin pointer

Three drifts the test-isolation review found beside the sequester finding. None is an API change; the second is a behavioural misstatement, which is why this is P3 and not P4.

## (a) Hicasso's private `wait-until!` re-grew beside the single public poll

`implementation/hicasso/test/re_frame/hicasso/roots_frames_support.cljs:400-418` defines a private `wait-until!` (added `604dffb2b1`, 2026-08-10 — after July deleted the public twin under rf2-7avygn, `88b20f1d22`): real timers, 4 ms tick, 16 ms post-settle delay, resolves `false` on timeout instead of rejecting. Callers: 10 uses across `hooks_island_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, `roots_frames_hydration_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, `roots_frames_shared_frame_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, `tool_views_dom_cljs_test.cljs`, plus `:446` in-file. `re-frame.test-support/poll-until` (`test_support.cljc:1055`, CLJS arity) is the one public poll (naming ledger row 42, rf2-6m4w; Hicasso's mounted door `settle-until!` already composes it).

Action: express `wait-until!` over `poll-until` if `poll-until`'s CLJS arity can run on real timers with a caller-set interval and timeout — `(-> (ts/poll-until pred? {…}) (.then (constantly true)) (.catch (constantly false)))` keeps the boolean contract the `(is (true? ok) "premise…")` rows assert on; keep the 16 ms post-settle delay only if a row measurably needs it (run the four suites). If `poll-until` cannot express the "real timers only" requirement its docstring names, keep the private fn and add one docstring line stating the discriminator against `poll-until`. Either way no public surface changes.

## (b) Two adapter docstrings describe a fallback the shared spine does not have

`implementation/adapters/reagent/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent.cljs:121-130` says "Calls (act (fn [] (reagent.core/flush))) … When act() is unreachable in the current React build it degrades to a plain synchronous flush (still runs `f` and drains the render queue)"; `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/re_frame/adapter/reagent_slim.cljs:58-70` says the same with `(batching/flush!)`. All three adapter vars are `(:flush-views! spine-fns)` → `implementation/core/src/re_frame/substrate/spine.cljs:1908-1917`, which calls `(act f)` with `f` defaulting to `(fn [] nil)` and, when `act` is absent, does NOT run `f` and returns nil (rf2-6r9j.35 retired the React-18 fallback; rf2-b6nm5 converged the three on one Var). The uix docstring (`uix.cljs:173-181`) is correct — use its wording for both. `git grep -n 'degrades to a plain synchronous flush' -- docs spec implementation` to catch any doc copy.

## (c) reagent-slim's second `flush-views!` — write the discriminator on both sides, no rename

`implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/src/reagent2/dom/client.cljs:153-180` is a second `flush-views!`: Promise return, 3-phase microtask/act/microtask drain, `goog.DEBUG`-gated, and it DOES carry the "degrade to a plain synchronous flush" branch the adapter docstrings were describing. It is designed, not residue: `implementation/adapters/reagent-slim/IMPL-SPEC.md:245,282,§4` name it as `r/flush`'s replacement, `reagent_slim.cljs:68-69` points at it for Suspense ordering, and `reagent_slim_flush_views_cljs_test.cljs:15-36` pins the nil-vs-Promise split. Consumers outside its own unit test (`test/reagent2/dom/client_cljs_test.cljs`, 40 mentions): none — bench and the reagent-to-hicasso codemod census mention it in prose only. The pointer runs one way: the client docstring does not name the adapter's converged nil-returning twin. Action: add that reverse cross-pointer to the `client.cljs` docstring ("`re-frame.adapter.reagent-slim/flush-views!` is the converged nil-returning contract (rf2-b6nm5); reach this one only for Promise / Suspense ordering"). The name is reagent-slim's IMPL-SPEC's to rule; do not rename here.

Recorded for another area, NOT actioned here: `spec/008-Testing.md:1013` still teaches `subscribe-once` (extant, `subs.cljc:1817`) as the canonical read-then-discard primitive beside `compute-sub`; wave 1's rf2-ihkk6l ruled it RETAINED, so the sentence is not wrong, but the state-reads area owns its wording.

## Corroboration

One-reviewer; fable flagged all three as "note, not bead" and the coordinator folded them into one drift bead. Codex did not review this slice.

## Deletion list

Possibly the private `wait-until!` body (if expressed over `poll-until`); nothing public.

## Consumers to migrate

None outside the four hicasso DOM suites (which keep calling `wait-until!` under its current name and contract).

## Spec, docs, examples, skills, tests

- No spec change (`spec/008-Testing.md:36-53` already designs per-adapter `flush-views!` as the same spine fn). `spec/API.md` untouched.
- Docs: any copy of the wrong docstring wording in `docs/api/re-frame.adapter.*` (grep above).
- Tests: the four hicasso DOM suites (browser gate, `npm run test:browser` or the per-artefact equivalent — foreground, to completion); `reagent_slim_flush_views_cljs_test` and `client_cljs_test` unchanged and green; `npm run test:cljs`.
- Manifest: no var added or removed; `--check` green.

No hot-zone. Touches `implementation/hicasso/test/`, two adapter `src` files (docstrings only), `reagent2/dom/client.cljs` (docstring only). Independent of @testing.1.

## Risks

Low. (a) is the only behavioural edit and is confined to hicasso test support; if the four suites flake under `poll-until`'s tick, keep the private fn (the second branch of (a)).

title: hic: admit zero-arity rf/capture-frame and rf/current-frame-id inside a Hicasso body (the row-18 seam)
description:

Zero-arity `rf/capture-frame` inside a Hicasso body REFUSES — `:operation :capture-frame`, `:substrate :hicasso`, extent `hicasso/boundary-render` (rf2-lvelh). Re-derived at source by rf2-hic-066 on 2026-08-15 and unchanged.

So the ambient-refusal seam must first admit exactly `:current-frame-id` and `:capture-frame` in-body, resolving to the body's `:extent-frame`, while ambient `rf/subscribe` and `rf/dispatch` stay refused. That is behaviour, not a spelling, which is why it is not rf2-hic-066's.

- 152 `hframe` occurrences across 39 files (measured with rg 14.1.1, repo-wide) stay put until this lands. That is the header rule working as intended, not drift.

- Facade inventory row HS-43 carries `h/hframe`. Per the packet, an inventory row records what is ON the door and does not endorse membership, so HS-43 is not an argument against the retirement.

title: Skill review: skills/re-frame2-pair - completeness, correctness, organisation, skill best practice
description:
Review the `re-frame2-pair` skill: skills/re-frame2-pair/, meaning SKILL.md and every reference and script under it. Do it in four SERIAL passes, finishing each one, and fixing what it finds, before starting the next:

1. COMPLETENESS. Does the skill cover what its description promises, and what an agent invoking it will need? Look for gaps against the current spec/ and implementation/: features, APIs, workflows and failure modes this skill's audience will meet. Also look for references the SKILL.md points at that are missing or empty.
2. CORRECTNESS. Check every claim against spec/ and implementation/ at trunk: API names, signatures, keywords, reserved namespaces, file paths, commands and code examples. Look for names that no longer exist, behaviour that has changed, dead links, and examples that would not compile or run as written.
3. ORGANISATION AND STRUCTURE. SKILL.md should be a concise entry point. References should be split by topic, sit one level deep, and be linked directly from SKILL.md. Nothing should be duplicated across files, terminology should be consistent, and a reader should find what they need in the order they need it.
4. SKILL BEST PRACTICE (Anthropic's Agent Skills authoring guidance).
   - Frontmatter: `name`, and a `description` in the third person that says what the skill does AND when to use it, with specific trigger terms.
   - A lean SKILL.md body (well under ~500 lines) that uses progressive disclosure into reference files.
   - No time-sensitive or history narrative.
   - Concrete examples, and checklists for workflows where order matters.
   - Scripts for deterministic operations rather than prose instructions.

DELIVERABLE: one PR applying the fixes, whose body summarises what each pass found and changed. Report findings outside skills/re-frame2-pair/ (spec/, implementation/, skills/README.md, another skill) rather than editing them. skills/README.md is shared by every skill, so name any change it needs and do not make it.

POSTURE: fix real defects and improve structure where that pays a reader. Do not rewrite for style. Present-tense convention: no bead ids and no history in the skill text.

GATES: `scripts/check_doc_slugs.py` (skills/ is a docs-gate root), and the api-manifest skills check, `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.skills-check` from implementation/scripts/api-manifest (lint.yml's api-manifest job), which fails on a non-manifest API reference. Run `scripts/check_readme_inventories.py` if an inventory is touched. CI covers the rest.

title: Test-suite pruning, fifth pass: implementation/adapters
description:
Child of rf2-nvxtm (test-suite pruning, fifth pass). One worktree, one PR.

SURFACE: implementation/adapters. This is the surface of rf2-txsk5.18 (fourth pass). Read rf2-txsk5.18 first: its description, notes and close reason. Together they give the runners and lanes, the count floors, the surface's cautions, the covers it relied on, and what the fourth pass already pruned. In the fourth pass this surface was split. rf2-txsk5.18 covered only part of it, and rf2-txsk5.43 took the rest. Your scope is exactly the files rf2-txsk5.18 covered (its notes and close reason list them). The rest belongs to sibling children of this epic. Confirm the scope and the runners yourself at tip in step 1, and report the delta.

<DIR> in the prompt below means this surface.

REPO MECHANICS: read rf2-nvxtm's description. Its count-floor, CLJS-lane, test-name, cross-surface-cover, hot-zone, plant and one-PR rules apply in full, and they win over anything in the prompt that seems to conflict.

== THE PROMPT (verbatim from Mike's local prompt file, which is not checked in; also in rf2-nvxtm's description)

Simplify the unit tests under implementation/adapters. Do not change the code under test. LLMs tend to
write too many low-value unit tests, and this suite was largely written by them.

Assume the suite has more tests than it needs, and that many of its tests are longer
than they need to be. Every test costs CI time, reading time and refactoring friction,
and the low-value ones hide the tests that matter. I want a lean suite: each test earns
its place by guarding a behaviour a caller relies on, against a regression that could
plausibly happen and would matter. Each surviving test should be as short as the thing
it proves.

Stay inside implementation/adapters. Do not edit tests elsewhere. If a deletion relies on a test outside
implementation/adapters to keep covering something, name that test in your report.

Work in this order:
1. Run the suite and record the result: tests, assertions, failures, lines. Confirm a
   runner actually executes each file in implementation/adapters; a file nothing runs cannot be pruned on
   evidence, so report it.
2. Read the code under test and list what it promises its callers: normal results, each
   boundary that takes its own path, each promised failure, and any past bug the tests
   refer to.
3. Map every test to the promise it checks. Most of the work shows up in this map:
   promises with five tests, tests with no promise, and tests of something no caller
   relies on.
4. Decide each test: keep, simplify, merge or delete.
5. Run the suite again and prove the pruned suite still guards every promise.

Work in small batches by contract group, and commit as you go. Before each batch,
predict the change in test and assertion counts; after it, confirm the counts moved by
exactly that much. If helper agents are available, use read-only ones for the mapping
step. If implementation/adapters plainly will not finish in about four hours, stop at a group boundary,
ship what is done, and list the files you did not reach.

Decide each test with two questions:
- If this test were deleted, what bug could ship that no remaining test would catch?
  If you cannot name one, delete it.
- If you can name one: is that bug plausible in this code, would a caller notice it,
  and would nothing else surface it at once (a compile or load error, a boot-time
  validation, most of the suite going red)? If the bug is implausible, harmless, or
  loud anyway, delete the test.

Delete:
- A test another test implies. If A cannot pass while B fails, drop B.
- Extra examples of one behaviour that take the same path through the code.
- Existence and smoke checks: a function exists, a var resolves, something "is
  registered", a result is non-nil, a call "does not throw", when another test
  exercises the same call with a real assertion.
- Change detectors: a test that copies a constant, a data table, a default config, a
  roster or a string out of the source and asserts equality. It fails on every intended
  change and catches no bug. The exception is a value callers depend on exactly, such as
  a public id or a documented default, that nothing else pins: keep one test for it.
- Absence checks for things nothing produces, and negative-input tests for inputs no
  caller passes and the contract does not mention.
- Exhaustive enumeration: one row per enum member, keyword or field when they all take
  one path. Keep one representative plus the members that take a different path.
- Tests of the language, a library or the framework: a constructor sets a field, a
  getter returns it, a map holds the key just put in it.
- Tests that pin how the code works instead of what it does: private helpers already
  exercised through the public path, call order, internal data shapes, greps of the
  implementation's own source, and log, trace or error wording that is not part of the
  contract.
- Tests whose expected value is computed by the same logic as the code under test.
- Assertions that a mock returned what it was told to return, and tests whose mock setup
  is most of the test while the assertion checks the mock.
- Separate per-platform test files asserting the same thing about platform-neutral code.
  A single shared test that runs on both platforms is one test, not two: keep it.
- Tests of test helpers and fixtures.
- Tests of code that has no logic in it, and tests whose only subject is production code
  that no production caller uses.

Simplify every test you keep:
- Assert the whole result with one equality instead of one assertion per field. Drop an
  assertion that a later one in the same test implies.
- Cut setup, fixtures and data to what the assertion needs. Remove unused bindings,
  requires, helpers and fixtures.
- Tests that vary one input become one table-driven test. Keep the boundary rows and
  drop the mid-range ones.
- Tests that repeat the same setup for one assertion each become one test.
- Delete comments and docstrings that restate the code or narrate history. Keep a
  one-line why where a test's purpose is not obvious from its name and body.
- Rename a test only when its name no longer says what it asserts, and first check that
  nothing matches on the name, such as a CI filter, a skip list or a doc that cites it.

Keep, however small:
- The only test of a promise a caller relies on: a normal result, a boundary that takes
  a different path (empty, one, many; zero; the limit and one past it), a promised
  failure.
- A regression test for a bug that actually happened, unless a stronger test now covers
  it.
- The last guard of a security, privacy or redaction promise.
- The last test that keeps a gate able to fail, and the last test holding a published
  doc or spec claim to the code.
When a weak test and a strong test overlap, keep the strong one: the one that would fail
on more bugs.

Do not:
- Weaken an assertion, or swap an exact check for a looser one, to make a merge or a
  simplification easier.
- Delete a test because it fails, is slow or is flaky. Report it.
- Leave unused helpers, fixtures or requires behind.
- Add new tests. If you find a promise with no test, report it.
- Change production code. Dead code and stale docs or spec text go in your report as a
  list, not into your change.
If anything pins test counts or names, such as a count floor or a roster, update it in
the same change. Commit one file or module at a time.

Prove it:
- The suite passes before and after. Report both sets of counts.
- For each group of deletions that rests on a surviving cover, break the code in a place
  the deleted tests guarded and confirm a surviving test fails. Then restore the code and
  confirm it matches the committed file. One plant per group sharing a cover is enough.
  If nothing fails, you removed real coverage: put the tests back.
- A cover must actually run. A skipped test, a fixture the runner never loads, or a test
  on a lane nothing executes covers nothing. Confirm the runner executes a cover before
  resting a deletion on it.
- Run each test file you touched on its own at least once. Deleting a file can break a
  sibling that relied on it loading something first; give such a file its own require.
- A deletion made under the second question needs no plant. Give its one-line reason in
  the report instead.
- A simplification must not change what a test can catch. Where you removed an
  assertion, name the assertion that implies it.

Report:
- Before and after: tests, assertions, lines.
- Deleted tests, grouped by reason. For each, the surviving cover, or the one-line
  reason it was not worth keeping.
- Merges and simplifications: what went into what, and the lines each file lost.
- Notable keeps: tests you considered deleting but kept, and why.
- Plants, and which test caught each.
- Tests outside implementation/adapters that your deletions rely on.
- Dead code, stale docs or spec text, and gaps (promises with no test). One line each.

If you are unsure whether a promise a caller relies on is still covered, keep the test
and say so. Losing the only guard of a real promise is still the one mistake that matters
more than leaving an extra test in. But being unsure whether a test is worth keeping is
not a reason to keep it. If you cannot say in one line what plausible regression it
catches that a caller would notice, delete it.
