title: reg-state concerns are unavailable in explicit-image frames because their registrations lack namespace provenance
description:
Audited PR #11585, merge eec225a2e78645756b8c59bb141f27bcfc489907.

Concrete behavior: core_state.cljc:140-147 synthesizes the concern sub and setter through the programmatic reg-sub/reg-event functions without source metadata. Both descriptors consequently have nil namespace provenance. Spec 002 Image resolution and composition (lines 1123-1129) and image.cljc:729-730 select application registrations by source namespace, so a frame with explicit :images cannot resolve either concern registration. The shared :rf.state/clear does resolve through the framework base. The reg-state opts roster only accepts :default, so callers cannot supply the missing ownership through the new public door.

Focused JVM reproduction at the audited core source, using the plain-atom reset fixture, in namespace audit.widget:
- Register (rf/reg-state ::open? {:default false}) and ordinary public reg-sub/reg-event ::control registrations.
- Build an image {:id ::image :select-ns {:include ["audit.widget"]}}.
- An implicit frame reads false and writes true at [:ui ::open? :billing].
- A frame built with :images [image] resolves the control and :rf.state/clear, but resolves neither the concern sub nor setter. Its concern read returns nil and dispatching [::open? :billing true] leaves app-db unchanged, while the control event successfully increments its value.
- Clearing a separately seeded entry works in both frames.

Evidence: ai/pr-audit/probe-pr-audit-sol-oct11-11585-2.clj, .log and .exit; Java exit 0. Source owners were [nil] for both concern registrations, ["audit.widget"] for the control. Exact merge core sources matched the primary checkout before and after the probe. The first probe attempt stopped on a harness inspection of an implicit frame generation; attempt 2 corrected that inspection and completed.

Small correction: give the synthesized concern sub and setter caller namespace provenance through the existing source-coordinate mechanism, retaining the shared clear event in the framework base. Choose the smallest supported way for this registration door to receive/forward that coordinate and document it. Add a regression that reads, writes and clears a concern through an image selecting its owner namespace, beside the implicit-frame control. This is the inherited limitation identified in the PR, now verified as an actionable follow-up.
notes:
== FENCE (mayor), 2026-10-21 11:14:39 AUSEST: OWNED ELSEWHERE. Duplicate of rf2-go1ed (same gap, same fix), which is live in worktree reg-state-provenance, PR #11591 (draft). Routed to that worker with this bead's two extra acceptance items (read/write/clear through an image selecting the owner namespace beside an implicit-frame control; document the mechanism). Do not dispatch separately. CLEARS WHEN PR #11591 merges; close this bead with it.
== WORKER RESULT 2026-10-21 11:36 AUSEST: covered by PR #11591 together with rf2-go1ed (same gap, same fix; see rf2-go1ed's notes for the measurement and gates).
Acceptance item 1: core test an-explicit-image-selecting-the-caller-runs-its-concern-as-an-implicit-frame-does runs one script against a frame made without :images and a frame whose image selects the owning namespace, beside ordinary ::control sub/event registrations: reads the false default, writes true at [:ui ::open? :billing], runs the control, clears the written entry, and clears an entry a separate event seeded. Red at tip, green with the fix.
Acceptance item 2 (mechanism documented): rf/reg-state is a defreg-macro, so *pending-coords* carries the caller's namespace into the sub and setter registrations exactly as for every reg-* macro; :rf.state/clear is registered with *pending-coords* bound to nil and stays in the framework base. Stated in Spec 002 §Per-instance view state and in the re-frame.core / re-frame.core-state docstrings; the CLJS fn alias and the rf.core-state/reg-state fn door record no namespace.
close_reason: Fixed together with rf2-go1ed (this bead was the merged-PR audit's duplicate of it, routed into the same PR). Its extra acceptance is met: the regression reads, writes and clears a concern through an image selecting its owner namespace beside an implicit-frame control and ordinary ::control registrations, and clears a separately seeded entry; the mechanism (the macro door capturing the caller's namespace through *pending-coords*, :rf.state/clear framework-owned) is named in Spec 002 §Per-instance view state and the docstrings. Merged as PR #11591 (rebase, b842e950d2). Reproduced at tip first (JVM, exit 1): a frame whose explicit image selects the reg-state caller's namespace resolved [sub, setter, :rf.state/clear] = [false false true]; a caller namespace registering nothing else made make-frame fail earlier with :rf.error/image-zero-match. title: Resources: attempts live on the entry and mutation instance; the separate work ledger and its index go
description:
## Ruling

Mike approved on 2026-10-21 folding the neutral durable work ledger (`implementation/resources/src/re_frame/resources/work_ledger.cljc`) into the resource entry and the mutation instance, e.g. `:work {:gen :status :owners :reply-targets :page-index :started-at}`.

The fold keeps only the attempt history that Xray's pending/terminal and recent-races views need. It preserves:
- joined read continuations and their transfer to superseding attempts;
- concurrent mutation instances;
- restore dangling;
- exactly-once accepted delivery.

It takes over the ledger's attempt → scoped-key mapping (`ledger-row-for-reply`).

## Problem

Measured at trunk c383c6a92e.

- **A second durable subtree.**
  - `:rf.runtime/work-ledger` holds the attempt rows.
  - `:rf.runtime/work-ledger-by-key` is an inverse index rebuilt after every wholesale install (`work_ledger.cljc:162-212`).
  - Its only writers are in this artefact: `events.cljc` (75 calls) and `mutation_events.cljc` (22).
  - Spec 016 names it neutrally for writers that do not exist (`spec/016-Resources.md:517`, `:538`, `:1975-1977`).
- **Pruning.** A 3-row terminal tail is pruned per key on every settle (`work_ledger.cljc:256-307`), and a drop pass runs when an entry leaves the cache (`:309-325`). Both are in §Ledger row retention and identity (`016:588-602`).
- **The key mapping exists only on the row.** A read reply carries `:work/id`, `:generation` and `:rf.frame/id`, with no key. `events.cljc:1418-1428` finds the key through `ledger-row-for-reply` (`reply_handlers.cljc:26-34`).
- **Read continuations ride the row.** Joins accumulate `:reply-targets` on it (`work_ledger.cljc:123-133`), a superseding read inherits them (`events.cljc:362-399`), and the accepted reply fans them out (`:117-126`).
- **What Xray reads.** Live rows and a dimmed terminal tail (`tools/xray/src/day8/re_frame2_xray/panels/resources_helpers.cljc:942-960`); recent races come from the trace buffer (`panels/resources.cljs:1549`).

## Change

- **The live attempt moves onto its owner,** under `:work` on the entry or instance. The `:current-work`/`:generation` stale gate and "one work id per attempt" are unchanged.
- **Terminal history.** Each entry and instance keeps its last 3 terminal summaries (work id, status, outcome, times) for Xray's tail. Traces can be off, so it stays durable. It leaves with its owner.
- **Key mapping.**
  - A read reply's entry is the one under the work id's resource (`work-id-resource-id`, `work_ledger.cljc:41-48`) whose `:work` carries that id.
  - No correlation token gains the key (rf2-v3ory).
  - Continuations still receive `:resource`, `:params`, `:scope` and `:resource/key`.
  - Add a live-only index only if measured.
- **Joined reads.** `:reply-targets` move to the superseding `:work`. On accept they are delivered once and cleared.
- **Restore.** `dangle-non-terminal-work!` and `dangle-pending-mutations!` (`ssr.cljc:670-737`) walk live `:work`. Hydration still ships no live attempt.
- **Delete:**
  - both ledger subtrees, with their record, index, prune and drop fns;
  - `ledger-row-for-reply`;
  - the ledger key in core's resource-subtree set (`implementation/core/src/re_frame/events.cljc:1175`).
- **Stays:**
  - the host-handle side table (`work_ledger.cljc:326` on);
  - the frame-qualified request id;
  - every trace.
- **Mutation payloads.** Mutation `:reply-to` and `:from-db-scopes` stay on the reply payload (`mutation_events.cljc:906-913`). Its handler finds the instance by `:instance-id` (`:1164`), so the merged `:from-db-scopes` change does not conflict.
- **Size:** M–L.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- **`spec/016-Resources.md`.**
  - These sections go: §Ledger row retention and identity (`:588-602`) and §Work-ledger multi-writer authority (`:1975-1977`).
  - Their identity rules move to §Race and in-flight semantics: one work id, no key on correlation tokens, and the frame-qualified request id.
  - Rewrite §Frame work ledger (`:536-586`), the grading rows (`:514-534`) and §Restore and replay part 2 (`:1778-1789`).
- **Hot zones:**
  - `spec/Conventions.md:117`, `:314-316`, `:590`, `:597`, `:614`;
  - `spec/Spec-Schemas.md:2787`, `:2847-3016`;
  - `spec/002-Frames.md:646`, `:1260`;
  - `spec/009-Instrumentation.md:1023`.
- **Other specs:** `spec/Runtime-Subsystems.md:165-175`, `:323`; `spec/Managed-Effects.md:200`, `:210`; `spec/Derivations.md:766`; `tools/xray/spec/024-Resources-Panel.md:292-310`.
- **Docs:** `docs/api/re-frame.resources.md:119`, `:780-785`, `:938`; `docs/api/re-frame.core.md:537`; `docs/machines/persist-and-restore.md:77`.

## Acceptance

- `resources_work_ledger_cljs_test.cljc` (16 deftests) is rewritten against `:work`. Its join, supersession, reply-resolution, row-gone, two-live-attempts and bounded-failure tests keep their meaning.
- Adjusted and green: the cross-frame-reply, restore, infinite load-more, mutation and SSR suites.
- A joined read's targets transfer to its successor and are delivered once.
- Xray shows live attempts and a dimmed tail. Its `resources_helpers`, `reply_envelope` (`ledger-row-projection`, `live-work-join`) and `resources_shape_parity` tests pass.
- `git grep -F ":rf.runtime/work-ledger" -- implementation tools spec docs ':!spec/findings' ':!docs/EP'` is empty.
- Green: the JVM resources suite, `npm run test:cljs`, the derivation conformance, the Xray suite, `mkdocs build --strict` and `check_doc_slugs.py`.

## Sequencing

This runs after the `:transport`-key deletion bead, because both edit `registry.cljc`, `events.cljc` and Spec 016. It waits for open beads on its hot zones. Related: rf2-v3ory.

1. Mixed-namespace tables need a default namespace plus qualifier resolution, which means moving adapter-aliases into the new namespace.
2. Non-var rows inside Tier tables need skipping: the '— | — | (rf/clear …)' rows, keyword rows and planned-API rows.
3. The 'M/Fn (CLJS)' cell: a macro on the JVM and a fn on CLJS.
4. Seven Status cells carry prose: dispatch, dispatch-sync, subscribe, subscribe-once, reg-sub, register-listener!, unregister-listener!. Move the prose to Notes so the cell is the manifest value.
5. Twelve Spec drifts. Most are a second spec that moves to Notes, per spec/API.md's own Spec-column rule (now at :20). Three need the owner settled: init! (006 against 002), and configure!, current-config and features (— against Conventions). Settle each from spec/Ownership.md; if Ownership.md does not decide it, leave that cell authored and record why.
6. Decide whether api_md_check stops grading generated tables. Its tier and kind checks become redundant there; its qualifier check does not.

title: re-frame.views stays in core: UIx, Fresco and routing use it, and the Conventions park says so
description:
## Ruling

Mike approved on 2026-10-21: measure what the UIx adapter and Fresco use from the Reagent-shaped `re-frame.views`.
- If only the Reagent adapter uses it, move it from core into `day8/re-frame2-reagent` and rewrite the park in `spec/Conventions.md`.
- Otherwise keep it, and record what uses it.

## Problem

Measured at trunk c383c6a92e, by a static require-and-call census.

**What `re-frame.views` is.** It is `implementation/core/src/re_frame/views.cljs`, 1,016 lines, plus `views/`: `frame_boundary.cljs` 428, `provider.cljs` 377, `source_coord_annotation.cljs` 158 and `jvm_source_coord_annotation.clj` 152. That is 2,131 lines in all. None of it requires `reagent.*`; core carries no Reagent dependency (`implementation/core/deps.edn:18-25`). The Reagent shape is duck-typed (`views.cljs:542-683`, `provider.cljs:322`).

**The answer is no: UIx, Fresco, routing and core itself use it, not only the Reagent adapter.**

- **Core's facade (every CLJS app).** `re-frame.core` requires it (`core.cljc:161`).
  - `rf/reg-view*` → `rf.views/reg-view*` (`:809`).
  - `rf/view` → `rf.views/view-head` (`:844`).
  - `rf/frame-provider` and `rf/frame-root` are `rf.views` vars (`:1539`, `:1564`).
- **UIx.**
  - It requires `re-frame.views.frame-boundary` (`implementation/adapters/uix/src/re_frame/adapter/uix.cljs:18`) and calls it at `:91`, `:97` and `:128`.
  - Its `:wrap-view` and `:componentize-view` capabilities exist for `views/reg-view*` to consult (`uix.cljs:264-306`).
  - `($ (rf/view ::row) props)` is taught UIx API (`docs/api/re-frame.adapter.uix.md:249`) and pinned by `uix_reg_view_direct_mount_dom_cljs_test.cljs:82-178`.
- **Fresco.**
  - It requires `re-frame.views.frame-boundary` (`implementation/fresco/src/re_frame/fresco/impl/frame_boundary.cljs:102`, calls at `:181-223`; `substrate.cljs:83`, `:129`).
  - `(rf/view id)` on a Fresco view returns the stored head through `view-head`'s pass-through (`impl/collector.cljs:1274-1279`).
  - Fresco deliberately bypasses `reg-view*` (`:1280-1284`).
- **Routing.** `re-frame.routing` requires `re-frame.views` (`routing.cljc:74`). It registers `:route/link` through `rf.views/reg-view*` (`:404`) and resolves it per render through `view-head` (`:447`).
- **Core subscriptions and the hook spine** consume the late-bind hooks `re-frame.views` publishes (`views.cljs:966`, `:979`, `:997`):
  - `:views/record-view-deref!` (`subs.cljc:1831`);
  - `:views/reading-render-key` (`subs/memo.cljc:320`);
  - `:views/emit-view-unmounted!` (`substrate/spine.cljs:2177`), which the shared React-hook spine fires when a UIx view unmounts.
- **The Reagent adapter** uses `rf.views/build-frame-provider` and `rf.views/current-frame` (`adapter/reagent.cljs:236`, `:238`).

So moving the namespace to `day8/re-frame2-reagent` would take `rf/reg-view*`, `rf/view`, `route-link` and the frame-boundary helpers away from UIx and Fresco apps.

The park, `spec/Conventions.md:1861`, gives the reason as "lives in core because the CLJS reference is Reagent-default". The measured reason is that core's facade, UIx, Fresco and routing all run through it. Its SA-4 trigger (`:1863`), a non-React-family adapter or a measured bundle cost, is unchanged.

## Change

- **Keep `re-frame.views` in core. Nothing moves.**
- **Record the users.** In `Conventions.md:1861`, replace the "Reagent-default" reason with the measured one: the view-registration facade (`rf/reg-view*`, `rf/view`, `frame-provider`, `frame-root`) and `re-frame.views.frame-boundary` serve UIx, Fresco and routing as well as Reagent.
- Leave the SA-4 note as it is.

## Spec and docs that move with it

- `spec/Conventions.md:1861`, one sentence. **Hot zone.**

## Acceptance

- `Conventions.md:1861` names the users above in place of "the CLJS reference is Reagent-default".
- No source file changes.
- `mkdocs build --strict` and `check_doc_slugs.py` are green.

title: Epoch: one :rf.epoch/snapshotted trace per committed epoch carries the outcome; :rf.epoch/outcome retires
description:
## Ruling

Mike approved on 2026-10-21 one epoch trace per committed epoch: `:rf.epoch/outcome` merges into `:rf.epoch/snapshotted`. Both are emitted today by `emit-snapshotted+outcome!` (`implementation/epoch/src/re_frame/epoch/assembly.cljc`). Xray's readers and the Spec 009 rows move with it.

## Problem

title: skill(re-frame-migration): SKILL.md Boot and init requires a duplicate-registration inventory that inventory-and-plan never runs
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 2a6fd908a6.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame-migration/SKILL.md §Boot and init (line 112), and inventory-and-plan.md as a whole (Steps 3 and 5 and the no-M-id reconciliation note at line 138).

## What it says

SKILL.md:112:

> v1 let a later registration of an id replace an earlier one, so an application namespace could override a library's. A single-frame target names no image and resolves the registrar live, which runs neither of two namespaces registering one kind and id: using it raises `:rf.error/ambiguous-registration`. So inventory duplicates before boot: fix an accidental one at its source, and keep an intended override — the definition v1 actually ran, the last one loaded — in a later image.

## What happened (generic)

The Phase 0a leaf never runs that inventory:

- no step covers it;
- Step 3's table has no row for it;
- the Step 5 completeness gate walks only the M-/O- rule index.

So the duplicate census is reconciled nowhere. It is the same no-M-id blind spot that line 138 already flags for the 10x → Xray swap. On a ~170-file app the worker built the census by hand and found 19 duplicate (kind, id) pairs: an accidental duplicate sub registered in two app namespaces, app overrides of library fx ids, and 15 test re-registrations of production ids.

## Evidence

- `grep -c -i -E 'duplicate|ambiguous' skills/re-frame-migration/references/inventory-and-plan.md` gives 0. (Control: `grep -c -i registration` on the same file gives 10.)
- `git grep -n 'ambiguous-registration' origin/main -- skills/re-frame-migration/ migration/` finds only SKILL.md:112, auto-call-site-rewrites.md:193 and orchestrating-a-large-migration.md:77.
- rf2-bmrh9, which introduced the ambiguity error, and rf2-sugyt, its docs follow-up, mention no inventory step: 0 hits for "inventory" in either item.

## Suggested change

- Add a duplicate-registration census to Step 3 as its own row, with no M-id. For every `reg-*` kind, list the (kind, id) pairs registered from more than one namespace across app, test and loaded dependency source. Classify each pair as accidental, an intended override (record which one v1 ran: the last loaded) or a test re-registration, and give each a disposition.
- Add a reconciliation line for it in Step 5, next to the 10x line at 138, so the completeness gate cannot pass without it.
- Optionally name `rf/ambiguous-registrations` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/core.cljc:2067) as the cross-check after boot.

comments.text:
Pass-4 evidence from the same downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626.

## "The last one loaded" has no method

The census this item asks for has to classify each intended override by "which one v1 ran". SKILL.md:112 defines that as "the definition v1 actually ran, the last one loaded". This item's suggested change repeats it ("record which one v1 ran: the last loaded"). Neither the skill nor this item says how to find the load order. The boot unit of the same ~170-file migration raised it again.

That is not obvious. v1's winner is whichever `reg-*` call ran last at runtime. That depends on the build's dependency-sorted namespace order, not on file names or on the order of requires in one ns form.

## State of the related fix at this tip

rf2-9v16x is CLOSED as "Changed in PR #11654", which names the shadow-cljs build report as the loaded-namespace list. But PR #11654 is still OPEN: `gh pr view 11654` gives state OPEN, mergedAt null. And `grep -n build-report skills/re-frame-migration/references/inventory-and-plan.md` finds nothing at 0783705626 (control: `grep -c registration` on the same file gives 10). Even once it lands, the build report lists the namespaces it compiled. It is not presented as a load order.

## Suggested addition to this item's change

Name one method for "which definition did v1 run", with a fallback:

- **Primary.** In a REPL attached to the running, unmodified v1 app, read `(get-in @re-frame.registrar/kind->id->handler [kind id])` (re-frame 1.4.3 registrar.cljc:15) and see which namespace's definition it holds. For `:fx`, `:cofx` and `:sub` it is the registered fn. For `:event` it is the interceptor chain, whose last interceptor wraps the handler.
- **Fallback, without a running app.** Take the build's dependency-sorted source order from the build tool (for shadow-cljs, the compile state's build sources), and pick the registering namespace that comes later.

Record the method beside each override's disposition.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): removing a v1 cofx that read the ROOT db ahead of (rf/path …) and re-reading the value from :db, as the triage and M-72 direct, silently reads the path-focused slice
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626. Priority 2: the rewrite the skill prescribes compiles, boots and silently reads the wrong slice (nil) with no error.

## Skill file and section

- skills/re-frame-migration/references/causal-world-inputs.md §Triage — split an in-handler ambient read by source, the DB-derived bullet (line 19); the Scope note (line 5).
- migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md §M-72 (lines 882-925), item 2 and the mechanical reshape; the M-72 row of skills/re-frame-migration/references/breaking-changes.md (line 89).
- migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md §M-70 (the `[:rf.interceptor/path …]` ref, lines 2890-2970) and the M-73 codemod's path lowering (skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md:572, :593).

## What it says

- causal-world-inputs :19: "The handler already receives app-db as the **`:db` coeffect** … so **read the slice / recompute the derived value from `:db`**. … Do **not** reach for a recordable `reg-cofx` (a value-returning supplier sees only its own arg and **cannot read app-db**)".
- M-72 item 2: "The v1 ctx→ctx shape … is retired. A supplier is now `(fn [] value)` or `(fn [arg] value)` and returns the coeffect value directly."
- auto-call-site-rewrites :593: an inline chain entry other than `(rf/path …)` has "no derivable registered id", so the codemod flags it (an `inject-cofx` entry is resolved by hand through M-72 and the triage above).

Neither the triage nor M-72 says that a read moved out of a coeffect and into a path-focused handler changes WHICH db it reads.

## What happened (generic)

A v1 coeffect handler receives the whole coeffects map, `:db` included (v1 `inject-cofx` runs `(update context :coeffects handler)`), so a v1 app can derive a coeffect from app-db:

```clojure
(rf/reg-cofx :current-user
  (fn [cofx _] (assoc cofx :current-user (get-in (:db cofx) [:auth :user]))))

(rf/reg-event-fx :cart/checkout
  [(rf/inject-cofx :current-user) (rf/path :cart)]
  (fn [{:keys [db current-user]} _] ...))
```

The cofx sits AHEAD of the path interceptor, so its `:before` reads the ROOT db.

In v2 a supplier cannot see `:db`, so the skill routes the read into the handler: delete the cofx, read `(get-in db [:auth :user])`. The M-73 codemod lowers `(rf/path :cart)` to `[:rf.interceptor/path [:cart]]` in the same pass. The handler's `:db` is now the cart slice, so the read returns nil. It compiles, boots and raises nothing.

The route that would read ahead of the focus is closed for events too: the sub-valued source `{:rf/sub query-v :as fact-id}` is machines-only, and on a `reg-event` it is `:rf.error/cofx-request-invalid` with the stated reason "its handler already holds `:db`", which under a path ref it does not.

## Evidence

- implementation/core/src/re_frame/std_interceptors.cljc:74-93 (`standard-path-interceptor`: "2. stages the focused slice as the handler's `:db` coeffect"). The root survives only on the interceptor's own `:rf.interceptor.path/stack` in the context, not in the coeffects (:121-124).
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/cofx.cljc:359-369 and :430-437 (the `:rf/sub` source is machines-only; "a `reg-event` handler declaring one is `:rf.error/cofx-request-invalid` (its handler already holds `:db`)").
- implementation/core/src/re_frame/router.cljc:352-382 (`assemble-initial-ctx`: the coeffects carry `:db` (app-db) and `:rf.db/runtime`, and no other copy of the root app-db).
- re-frame v1 1.4.3 re_frame/cofx.cljc:19-27 (`inject-cofx` hands the cofx handler the whole `:coeffects` map).

title: skill(re-frame-migration): guided-views-m11 omits reaction bodies: Reagent re-runs a watched r/reaction or r/track in its ratom flush, outside any render, so an ambient subscribe inside raises no-frame-context
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626. Priority 2: the hazard passes the first render and the boot smoke, then throws on the first state change.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame-migration/references/guided-views-m11.md §M-11, Identify (lines 13-16) and Decision shape (lines 20-25).

## What it says

Identify 1: "Every bare fully-qualified `rf/dispatch` / `rf/subscribe` … inside an `:on-*` handler or any other callback that runs after the render — a timer, a promise continuation, a lifecycle method".

## What happened (generic)

Reaction bodies are not in the list. A view can create an `r/reaction` or `r/track` whose body calls an ambient `rf/subscribe`. The first computation happens during the render, which resolves the frame from the tree, so it works. But when a source changes, Reagent re-runs a watched reaction from its ratom flush, outside any render and outside any dynamic frame scope, and the ambient `subscribe` raises `:rf.error/no-frame-context`.

Neither the census nor a boot smoke that only renders catches it; it fails on the first change. The guide's own Form-3 recipe already does the right thing, using the captured `subscribe` inside `r/track!` (:145-150), but nothing names the general hazard.

## Evidence

Reagent 2.0.1 `reagent/ratom.cljs`:

- :399-408 `_handle-change`: a non-auto-run reaction sets `dirty?` and calls `rea-enqueue`;
- :419-421 `_queued-run`: re-runs when dirty and watched;
- :511-519 `flush!`: drains the queue.

Observed during a parsed M-11 census on a ~170-file app.

## Suggested change

Add "the body of an `r/reaction` / `r/track` / `reagent.ratom/make-reaction` created in a view" to Identify. Give the remedy: capture at render (the `reg-view`-injected `subscribe`, or `(rf/capture-frame)`), and call the captured `subscribe` inside the reaction body.

The async dispatch path with Reagent's own scheduled flush gave the same. comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
More evidence from the same downstream migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Re-verified at origin/main 0783705626: guided-views-m11.md Identify (lines 13-16) still names no reaction body. `r/track!` appears only inside the Form-3 imperative-subscription recipe (:123-163), and the strings "r/reaction", "reaction bod" and "make-reaction" do not occur in the leaf.

A second, independent unit hit this. Its parsed M-11 census over one feature area (report filters) found 78 deferred sites, and 8 of them were ambient `subscribe` calls inside `r/reaction` bodies created in views. These are the third-largest kind, after `:on-*` handlers (54) and third-party callbacks (12). The unit fixed all 8 by taking `(rf/capture-frame)` at render and calling the captured `subscribe` inside the reaction body, which is the remedy this item suggests.

So the gap is not a one-off. In a filter-heavy v1 codebase, view-local reactions over subscriptions are a common idiom, and every one of them passes the first render and the boot smoke. Adding the Identify row and its remedy would let a census count them up front, instead of discovering them on the first state change.

comments.author: Mike Thompson
comments.text:
More evidence from the same downstream migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Re-verified at origin/main 62a62c7472: guided-views-m11.md is unchanged since 0783705626, and the leaf still names no reaction body.

A third unit hit a variant this item's Identify row would miss, and it adds a guard the remedy needs.

1. **The reaction can belong to a helper.** A view hands a fn to a shared helper, and the helper runs that fn inside an `r/reaction` or `r/track` that the helper itself creates (a common shape for derived-filter or memoising utilities). The view's source contains no `r/reaction`, so a census that looks for reaction forms in views does not count the site. Its ambient `rf/subscribe` still throws `:rf.error/no-frame-context` on the first recompute. Suggested wording for the Identify row: "a fn the view passes to a helper that runs it inside a reaction it creates".
2. **Keep the captured subscribe there; do not switch to subscribe-once.** A subscribe made inside a reaction body is owned by that reaction and released when it disposes. implementation/core/src/re_frame/late_bind/directory.cljc:619 says re-frame.subs "holds ONE reference per (owning reaction, cache slot) and releases it on that owner's dispose", where the owner is the reaction currently capturing derefs. So it is not a leak. `subscribe-once` would be wrong there. It is "Non-reactive. The caller is not registered for re-render or change notification" (spec/006-ReactiveSubstrate.md:1014), and "A balanced read is not an owned read" (:958), so the reaction would stop updating. The remedy should say this explicitly. rf2-jyjyg (filed in this pass) recommends subscribe-once for one-shot reads in callbacks, and that advice must not be applied to reaction bodies.

description:
The corpus README (migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md) carries two of the M-30 gaps the re-frame-migration skill closed in PR #11665. Verified at origin/main 82b8968392.

## 1. v1 flow reads are in no corpus census, and M-23's sub rows have no :flow carve-out

- M-30 "What to look for" (README ~1504-1508) lists producer surfaces only: reg-flow, clear-flow, the :reg-flow / :clear-flow fx entries, a re-frame.flows require.
- v1's re-frame.alpha registers a :flow sub (re-frame v1.4.7 src/re_frame/alpha.cljc:662-664). Its :flow query id routes to the :flow lifecycle (src/re_frame/query/alpha.cljc:24-29), and sub-flow (src/re_frame/subs/alpha.cljc:130-133) returns a reaction over the flow's :path. So views read flows as (sub :flow {:id ...}), [:flow {:id ...}] or {:re-frame/q :flow :id ...}, and handlers read them with get-flow (alpha.cljc:650-654).
- v2 publishes no flow subs (spec/013 §Sub integration), so a read left as it is emits :rf.error/no-such-sub and yields nil (spec/006:1149).
- M-23's table rows (README ~1233-1234), "(sub {:re-frame/q ::id :param 1}) -> (subscribe [::id 1])" and "(sub <vector>) -> (subscribe <vector>) ... just switch the namespace", turn a :flow read into exactly that silent nil. The skill's M-23 row and auto-call-site-rewrites.md already carve :flow out, so the corpus now disagrees with its own skill.

Suggested change: add the read surfaces to M-30's "What to look for". Use :flow as a bare keyword across line breaks, `rg -U ':flow[\s,})\]]'`, plus get-flow; this was controlled against a fixture where it finds all six query spellings, including a line-final :flow. Add the :flow carve-out to M-23's sub rows: read the flow's :output-path through a reg-sub.

## 2. The (reg :flow ...) row's :output rewrite omits 1.4.4+'s extra arguments

- README ~1232 says the :output fn "destructured a resolved-inputs map, so its body must be rewritten to take the inputs positionally".
- In re-frame 1.4.4 and later, :output is called as (output id->in id->old-in old-output): v1.4.7 src/re_frame/flow/alpha.cljc:166, 168 and 170. 1.4.3 calls (output id->in).

title: migration(corpus): M-28 says every reg-machine namespace MUST take the rf.machines alias, but only helper call sites need it; an unused alias trips clj-kondo's unused-namespace warning
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626. Minor.

## Skill file and section

- migration/from-re-frame-v1/README.md §M-28, "What to do" (lines 1463 and 1465).
- skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-cross-cutting.md, the artefact require table, M-28 row (line 387).

## What it says

- README:1463: "Every namespace that calls `rf/reg-machine` (or relies on the `:rf/machine` framework sub registration) MUST `(:require [re-frame.machines :as rf.machines])`".
- README:1465: "Take the alias while you are there. ... it is the spelling the helper call sites below are written against. A bare `(:require [re-frame.machines])` fires the hook registrations but introduces no alias, so those call sites will not resolve."
- auto-cross-cutting.md:387: "`re-frame.machines` — take the alias, `[re-frame.machines :as rf.machines]`".

## What happened (generic)

Most machine namespaces call only `rf/reg-machine` / `rf/defmachine`, which stay on the façade, and no `rf.machines/` helper. Applied as written, M-28 gives each of them an alias that is never used. clj-kondo then warns "namespace re-frame.machines is required but never used" in every such namespace. That breaks a "lint clean" gate, or teaches the migrator to ignore the warning.

The alias is needed only where a helper is called, which :1465 itself implies. The O-16 companion already uses the bare form: async-flow-fx-to-reg-machine.md:95 is `[re-frame.machines]` with the comment ";; per M-28 — require fires the machines artefact's load-time hooks". So the corpus gives two spellings for the same case.

## Evidence

clj-kondo v2025.10.23, default config, three one-namespace files:

- `[re-frame.machines :as rf.machines]` plus a `rf/reg-machine` call: "warning: namespace re-frame.machines is required but never used".
- `[re-frame.machines]` plus the same call: no warning.
- Control, `[re-frame.machines :as rf.machines]` plus a `rf.machines/machine-transition` call: no warning.

The exported config, implementation/core/resources/clj-kondo.exports/day8/re-frame2/config.edn, has no `:unused-namespace` exclusion for `re-frame.machines`.

## Suggested change

Reword README:1463 to require the namespace in either form. Then say:

- take the `rf.machines` alias where the namespace calls a `rf.machines/` helper (`machine-transition`, `reg-machine*`);
- a bare `(:require [re-frame.machines])` is enough, and lint-clean, where it only calls `rf/reg-machine` / `rf/defmachine` or reads `:rf/machine`.

Make auto-cross-cutting.md:387 say the same.

The same "take the alias" wording appears in the M-29 routing row (:388). It has the same effect where a namespace only calls `rf/reg-route`, so check it in the same pass.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): no recipe for host code that swap!s or reset!s app-db inside a function; dispatch-sync is the only synchronous write and is refused anywhere inside a drain, fx bodies included
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626.

## Skill file and section

- skills/re-frame-migration/references/auto-call-site-rewrites.md, the M-1 rewrite table (lines 86-90).
- guided-handlers-state.md §M-15 (line 144).
- breaking-changes.md's M-15 row (line 43).

## What it says

- M-1 :87-90: `@re-frame.db/app-db → (rf/app-db-value :rf/default)` and "`(reset! re-frame.db/app-db v)` → flag (Type B — see M-15) — propose `(rf/dispatch-sync [::reset-app-db v])`".
- M-15 :144: "Identify: top-level `(reset! re-frame.db/app-db ...)` or `(swap! re-frame.db/app-db ...)` calls in namespace bodies (run at load time, not inside a function)."

## What happened (generic)

v1 apps also write app-db from host code inside functions: a JS-library callback, a websocket handler, a dev tool, or a `reg-fx` body doing `(swap! re-frame.db/app-db assoc …)`. These fall between the rules:

title: skill(re-frame-migration): causal-world-inputs calls the event payload 'the simpler route' for a host-held value (:79, :109) but not what the move publishes: every interceptor, sink and epoch history sees it, app-db stores it where the event is queued, and the payload lint skips metadata
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (pass 8). This is a suggestion, not a work order. Verified at origin/main e6cb299c58.

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame-migration/references/causal-world-inputs.md, §"Identify — the up-front grep", the "Then walk the callees" paragraph (:55-79). The same gap sits at §"UUID / random / browser / storage → event payloads or recordable facts" (:109).

## What it says

- :79: "Where the code that owns the editor also dispatches the event, the event payload (below) is the simpler route."
- :109: "Use the **event payload** when the caller owns the value, a **recordable generator** when the fold needs a fresh fact, or a **provided** recordable fact when a boundary owns it."
- :139 gives the exposure warning for one case only. A recorded secret "would *be* the secret, durably embedded in epoch history / replay fixtures". No matching caution covers the payload route.

## What happened (generic)

The callee walk classed a handler as durable. It read and `swap!`ed a host-owned atom (a registry of pending requests), and the claimed request picked the effect. Following :79, the migrator moved the whole request map into the payload of a waiter event. That fixes replay, but the request now reaches three places it never reached before:

1. **Every event observer.** The payload is the event vector, so every interceptor in the chain sees it, along with the trace and epoch history and any `:observability` sink. The request carried the user's free-text prompt. An app-level interceptor that forwards event args to an off-box log would have shipped that prompt. The migrator had to add an app-level elision marker to stop it.
2. **Durable app-db.** The app queues the waiter event in app-db, in a pending-waiters list that is drained when an auth refresh lands. So the payload became durable state. spec/015-Data-Classification.md:446 says "**Classification does not propagate.**", so even a `:sensitive` declaration on the event would not cover the stored copy.
3. **Metadata the lint cannot see.** The request holds a nested callback event vector, and its metadata carries a guard fn. The dev payload lint raised nothing. Its walk, `walk-find-host-handle-bounded` (implementation/core/src/re_frame/reply.cljc:299, cond at :326-331), visits map values and vector and set elements and never reads `meta`. The router calls it through `find-non-serialisable-payload-path` (router/diagnostics.cljc:267) at router.cljc:103-105. `pr-str` omits metadata by default, so a serialised copy of the event also drops the guard.

Observed on a ~170-file app. The migrator found all three by hand, not from the skill.

## Evidence

- The quotes above, at e6cb299c58.
- The framework already has the tools, but :79 and :109 do not link them:
  - spec/015 §Registration-owned transient classification (:88-96): `(rf/reg-event :auth/login {:sensitive [[:password]]} …)`.
  - The commit-plane `:sensitive` effect for durable app-db (spec/015 §Durable app-db, :42).
  - The O-18 logging sweep row in breaking-changes.md:193.
- Related, not a duplicate: rf2-cy26g asks whether event-vector metadata carriage is a contract. This item reports that the payload lint does not walk metadata.

## Suggested change

Add a caution after :79, and link it from :109:

> **A value moved into the payload is published.** The event vector is seen by every interceptor in the chain, by the trace and epoch history, and by any `:observability` sink. Where a handler stores the event (a pending, retry or waiter list in app-db), it is also durable app-db. Before taking this route, check the value's size and sensitivity:
> - Reduce a large value or a live handle to an id or a small EDN projection.
> - Classify sensitive paths with `:sensitive` registration metadata on the `reg-event` (spec 015 §Registration-owned transient classification).
> - Classify them again with the commit-plane `:sensitive` effect wherever a handler stores the event, because classification does not propagate.
> - Add the event to the O-18 logging sweep.
>
> The dev payload lint (`:rf.warning/non-serialisable-event-payload`) walks map values and vector and set elements only. A fn or host object in the payload's metadata draws no warning, and a serialised copy of the event drops it.

Optionally, on the framework side: make the payload lint walk collection metadata too, or document in the lint's reason text that it does not.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): the boot smoke never warns that a dev boot can send real telemetry and that step 7's synthetic window error can reach the app's error tracker; no step blocks third-party intake first
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (a suggestion, not a work order). Verified at re-frame2 origin/main fd1d1565f1. Observed on a ~170-file Reagent app that ships browser telemetry (RUM, session replay, logs) and a chat widget.

- skills/re-frame2-pair has no warning either.

## What it says

- :20: "load the dev build, watch the console ... and reload with an injected `window` `'error'` listener".
- :37, step 7: "raise a `window 'error'`, trigger a JS-lib lifecycle callback — and watch the console for `:rf.error/no-frame-context`".

Neither line, nor anything else in the two skills, mentions that the app under test may report to third-party services.

## What happened (generic)

A dev build commonly initialises the app's real telemetry and error tracking, and a smoke boots it repeatedly. The worker's first boot sent about 2 minutes of real RUM, session-replay and log traffic, and loaded a third-party chat widget. Step 7's synthetic `window` error is exactly the kind of event an app's error hook forwards to its tracker. On this app it went through `log-error!` and was skipped only because a config flag happened to be off. Every later run blocked the intake domains with CDP `Network.setBlockedURLs`. The app's attempts then appeared as `blocked: inspector` in the network log, which is itself useful evidence that the telemetry path still runs after the migration.

- The worker's network log: real intake on the first boot, and `blocked: inspector` on every later run.
- At source: a `git grep` for telemetry, `setBlockedURLs`, "error tracker" and similar terms over skills/ finds only the production observability-sink guidance (error-events.md, production-observability.md), and nothing in the smoke procedure or the pair skill.

Add a precondition to runtime-smoke-test.md, before step 1. A dev boot may send real telemetry, and step 7's synthetic error may reach the app's error tracker. So list the app's third-party intake and widget domains from its config, block them in the smoke browser before the first navigation (CDP `Network.setBlockedURLs`, or the automation tool's request interception), and keep the blocked attempts as evidence that the hook still fires. title: SSR: one path-precise :payload permit, retiring :payload-include-sensitive
description:
## Problem

Measured at trunk 3959d2a5bf.

What reaches the browser in the hydration payload is one decision spelled in two options:

- `:payload` selects app-db keys;
- a classified leaf inside a selected key stays `:rf/redacted` unless a second option, `:payload-include-sensitive`, lists its path (`implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/payload_policy.cljc`).

`restore-permitted` in the same file never pierces a classified ancestor. On a security boundary, every extra spelling is another way to misconfigure it. `:payload-include-sensitive` appears 60 times across 27 files at 3959d2a5bf.

## Change

- `:payload` takes keys or paths, for example `[:articles [:session :csrf]]`.
- A path that names a classified leaf permits exactly that leaf.
- A named ancestor still redacts its classified descendants, so the no-pierce rule survives the merge. Selecting a subtree must not silently authorise its secrets.
- Delete `:payload-include-sensitive`.

Classification still gates the browser payload (EP-0039, rf2-0iyzr), so only the spelling of the permit changes. `:render-state` stays a separate, required policy with no payload-derived default (rf2-9k8kz).

## Spec and docs that move with it

`spec/011-SSR.md` is the one `i/crlf` file in the tree: edit it with the Write/Edit tools or Python bytes, never `sed -i`.

- `spec/011-SSR.md`, payload rules 1–5.
- `spec/015-Data-Classification.md` § SSR.
- `docs/ssr/concepts.md`, the sections "Classified values inside the allowlist" and "Render on Node".
- The `ssr-handler` row in `spec/API.md` with both manifest sidecars. **Hot zone.**

## Acceptance

- Public `:session` data plus a permitted CSRF leaf crosses.
- A classified sibling, and a classified descendant of a named ancestor, stay redacted.
- `:payload-include-sensitive` is refused with a message naming the path form.
- SSR and security-tier suites green.

## Sequencing

Blocked by rf2-o5rtr, whose static-classification slice exercises the same permit.

Breaking. Effort M, risk medium: it is a security boundary, so keep it fail-closed.

close_reason:
Shipped in PR #11717 (branch worker/ssr-payload-permit, head 4724369963, on trunk 5aaf9a8f7e; open and ready at close).

CONTRACT. :payload is an allowlist of keywords and paths (a path is a non-empty vector of map keys), e.g. [:articles :session [:session :csrf]]. A keyword ships that top-level key. A path ships the value it reaches, and permits exactly the classified LEAF it names (a leaf is anything but a map, vector, set or sequence). A named map, by keyword or by path, still redacts its classified descendants; a path naming a classified map leaves it redacted whole. A path never pierces a classified ancestor. A path steps only through maps, so through a vector, a scalar or an absent key it selects and permits nothing. A keyword never permits, and :rf.ssr.payload/whole-app-db permits nothing. :render-state stays a separate required policy; the handler's :payload paths permit inside its own app-db allowlist and select nothing there.

RETIRED, NO ALIAS. :payload-include-sensitive is refused, at handler construction and by the runtime arm (apply-policy, so a Fresco server render, which hands the policy its whole option map, refuses it too). The error is :rf.error/ssr-malformed-payload-allowlist with :opt :payload-include-sensitive and :replacement :payload. The message spells the merged allowlist, e.g. ":payload [:session [:session :csrf]]". The id is reused rather than minted, in the payload family's house style (render-state reuses it with :opt :render-state). scripts/check_retired_spellings.py rule (j) holds the keyword token at zero in source outside implementation/ssr/src/re_frame/ssr/payload_policy.cljc (a closed one-file allowlist). Its self-test is 36/36.

CENSUS. git grep -n -F ':payload-include-sensitive' -- . ':!.beads' read 53 lines in 28 files on trunk b9c9ab1cb7, and 34 lines in 12 files at the branch head. What remains is the refusal code, the docstrings and spec and docs that describe the refusal, the refusal tests, the gate rule, and docs/EP/EP-0039 line 209. That last one is a design-record sentence about the EP's own effect, so it was left alone.

ALSO IN SCOPE, DONE. spec/011 (payload-scope table, runtime-db section), spec/015 (~300: the router stamps :failing-id equal to :event-id at its effect-map site) and spec/002 (~405) no longer name an elision-declaration registry or a classification-effect site. The re-frame.ssr.ring.payload/build-payload and re-frame.ssr/hydration-payload docstrings had the same stale wording, now fixed.

DESIGN CHOICE TO KNOW. A permit is a LEAF. A path naming a classified collection releases nothing, because the projection is a black box from implementation/ssr and cannot lift one declaration while keeping its descendants'. Apps that need a classified map's contents in the browser classify at the leaves.

PLANTS. Each was scoped to re-frame.ssr-payload-path-permit-test (12 tests, 44 assertions) and each restore was verified by blob hash. The control gave 0 failures. Releasing a whole collection gave 2 red rows: a named map still redacts its classified descendants, and a path naming a classified map releases nothing. Piercing a classified ancestor gave 3: the never-pierces row twice and the dead-frame row. Accepting the retired list gave 12, all in the separate-permit-list refusal row.

GATES. Each exit is the runner's own, measured on trunk d64e3695b8. scripts/test-jvm-implementation.sh exited 0 across 18 lanes. The ssr lane ran 318 tests / 1470 assertions against a trunk baseline of 315 / 1443 (predicted +3 / +27). ssr-ring ran 93 / 285 against 92 / 284 (predicted +1 / +1). core ran 1394 / 4252, unchanged as predicted. npm run test:cljs exited 0 (6575 / 19139), with the Fresco refusal row confirmed in the compiled node-test build. npm run test:security exited 0 (31 / 75). mkdocs build --strict exited 0. check_doc_slugs exited 0, and a planted broken anchor turned it red. check_retired_spellings exited 0, self-test 36/36. check_keyword_catalogue_drift exited 0, and a planted uncatalogued id turned it red. The branch was then rebased onto 5aaf9a8f7e (rf2-trcv1, rf2-5zdjy), with PR CI as the final-base gate. No public var changed, so there was no manifest regeneration.

title: senior review: examples: real apps and example scripts
description:
SENIOR-DEVELOPER REVIEW of one slice of the tree. Part of the review sweep rf2-r5cc2, which partitions implementation/, tools/, examples/ and skills/ into slices; this bead owns exactly the slice below, and its siblings own the rest.

SLICE:
- examples/real-apps/**
- examples/scripts/**

FOCUS: The realworld apps as the largest worked examples of re-frame2 (HTTP, resources, SSR, auth, classification), and the scripts that build and check examples.

PERSONA. A senior Clojure/ClojureScript developer who did not write this code, reading it as its next maintainer and as a programmer who has to use it. Judge it against the project stance (CLAUDE.md), quoted verbatim:

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

So record material, actionable insights only: a defect, a simplification that removes real weight, an ergonomic sharp edge a programmer (or the AI they use) will hit, a test that cannot go red, a doc or docstring that misleads. Not style preferences, not nagging diagnostics, not defensive belt-and-braces, not renames for taste.

LENSES, in priority order:
1. Correctness — error paths, concurrency, cleanup, and fail-closed behaviour on any security or privacy boundary.
2. Simplicity and clarity — dead code, duplication (within the slice or with another slice), accidental complexity, an abstraction that earns nothing.
3. Ergonomics — the API or tool as a programmer, or the AI they use, actually meets it.
4. Performance — hot spots on real paths, never at the expense of clarity.
5. Test rigour — a test that cannot fail, a gap on a branch that matters.
6. Comments and docstrings — per CLAUDE.md § Conventions & Patterns: present tense, the reason plus a spec pointer, no provenance, no restated spec.

METHOD. Read the slice's source first, then its tests, against the owning spec sections (spec/Ownership.md maps each surface to its spec). A finding is a CLAIM until checked: confirm each one at source, and confirm a behaviour claim with a quick REPL or test run where that is cheap. This is a read-only review: edit no file, and run only read-only commands and the slice's existing test lanes.

OUTPUT, recorded on THIS bead and never in a separate file: write the section to a file and append it with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes "$(cat <file>)"` (never `--notes`, which replaces). Head it `== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (<datetime with zone>, trunk <short sha>)` and include:
- 0 to 15 numbered findings, most important first. Each gives: `path:line` (plus a short quote so it can be re-found by text), what is wrong, why it matters (the concrete failure or cost), the fix (a sketch is fine), size (S/M/L), confidence (verified / probable), and its lens.
- A short "looked at and sound" list, so the review's coverage is visible.
- Cross-slice findings, whose defect lives in another slice's files, in a separate list naming the owning slice. Do not act on them.

Then add the label `findings-recorded` and leave the bead OPEN: its findings become this slice's fix work, which the coordinator dispatches in clusters. If the slice needs nothing, record zero findings with the coverage list and close the bead with that as the reason.

notes:
== ROUTED FROM rf2-r5cc2.10 (resources review) — a question this slice owns

Does a managed-HTTP abort ALWAYS deliver an aborted reply (the :rf.http/aborted kind) to the issuer? The resources runtime settles an aborted fetch through :rf.resource.internal/failed and garbage-collects the entry only after that reply arrives; if some abort path (a superseded attempt, a frame destroy, a transport that never calls back) delivers no reply, that resource entry is never collected. Check each abort path at source and record a finding with a fix, or record it under looked-at-and-sound.
== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (2026-10-29 13:01:10 AUSEST, trunk 1c19fe04e1)

Slice: implementation/http/** (17 source namespaces, 7.4k lines; 53 test files). Read against Spec 014 (Privacy, Failure mode, Retry and backoff, Request envelope, Middleware, Aborts) and Managed-Effects. Behaviour claims were confirmed with JVM probes against the slice's own test classpath (`clojure -M:test` plus a probe script, exit 0), using stub transports and an in-process HttpServer. The http source is unchanged between the review's start (32572d4fdb) and 1c19fe04e1; only a tracker checkpoint landed in between.

Six findings: 5 S-size verified behaviour or privacy defects, and 1 S doc item.

1. transport.cljc:1220 `decoded' (rf.http.privacy-body/classify-decoded decoded decode)`, used at :1233, :1251 and :1260 (the three `:rf.http/accept-failure` maps).
   What: the trace projection of the decoded body (`:sensitive?` slots become `:rf/redacted`, `:large?` slots become the `:rf.size/large-elided` marker) is put on the failure map that is DELIVERED to the app, not only on the trace row. It is also computed on every 2xx response, outside any `debug-enabled?` gate, although only the accept-failure branches use it.
   Cost: an app's `:on-failure` / `:reply-to` for an accept failure loses data: the slots the `:decode` schema marks arrive as `:rf/redacted` or as an elision marker. The code's own rule (privacy_body.cljc, before `classify-success-value`) says "classification is a trace projection, never a change to application data". On top of that, production walks the schema on every success (and the whole body when it has marks) for a value it throws away. The privacy_body ns docstring ("in production builds ... no body walk runs") is false today.
   Verified: the probe used `:decode [:map [:token {:sensitive? true} :string] [:status :string] [:blob {:large? true} :string]]` with an `:accept` returning `{:failure …}`. The delivered `[:error :decoded]` was `{:token :rf/redacted, :status "rejected", :blob #:rf.size{:large-elided {…}}}`. Control: the same body without the accept failure delivered `:value {:token "SECRET-T" … :blob "BIG"}` raw. No test pins the delivered value: http_privacy_integration_test `accept-failure-emits-category-trace-with-schema-classified-decoded` asserts only on the trace.
   Fix: put the raw `decoded` on the three failure maps. Apply `classify-decoded` to `[:decoded]` at the two trace sites, both already inside `debug-enabled?`: `emit-and-dispatch-failure!` before `prepare-emit-failure`, and the `:error` arm of `emit-reply-trace!`. Add a delivered-reply assertion beside the existing trace test. http_completion_fence_test redefines `classify-decoded` as its throw site, so point it at another pre-commit throw, e.g. `compute-backoff-ms` under a retry policy.
   Size S. Confidence verified. Lens 1 (correctness), also lens 4 (performance).

2. transport_jvm.cljc:141-151, the relative-URL `ex-info` `"... got relative URL " (pr-str url)`, together with privacy.cljc `redact-failure-with-flag` (:371-420), which never touches `:message`.
   What: a `:rf.http/transport` failure's `:message` can quote the request URL, and no redactor reads `:message`. Denylisted query values therefore reach the trace even though `:url` and `[:request :url]` are redacted. Spec 014 §Privacy rule 3's slot list (body / body-text / decoded / detail / cause / returned) also leaves `:message` out, so even a `:sensitive?` request keeps it.
   Cost: this breaks the always-on rule 2 promise ("MUST redact ... query-param values whatever the request's sensitivity") on the category row and on the `:rf.http/replied` row. The likeliest trigger is the commonest JVM mistake: SSR code issuing a relative URL.
   Verified: the probe issued `{:request {:url "/api/items?api_key=SECRET-K&page=2"}}` on the JVM. The `:rf.http/transport` row's `:url` and `[:request :url]` both read `/api/items?api_key=:rf/redacted&page=2`, while its `:message` and the replied row's `[:error :message]` both contained `SECRET-K`. Control: no trace row's `:url` slot contained the secret. Host messages that quote the URL (the JDK's `URI/create` "Illegal character ... : <url>", undici's "Failed to parse URL from <url>") are the same class; that part is probable and was not run.
   Fix: (a) stop quoting the URL in the relative-URL message, since the `:url` slot already names it, redacted. (b) In `redact-failure-with-flag`, give a string `:message` the same treatment as a string `:cause` under `sensitive?`, and on every request replace any occurrence of the raw `:url` inside `:message` with its redacted form. (c) Add `:message` to the slot list of Spec 014 §Privacy rule 3. Pin it with a test modelled on probe P2.
   Size S. Confidence verified. Lens 1 (privacy boundary).

3. encoding.cljc:132, in `normalize-header-pairs`: `(let [name (str k)]`.
   What: a keyword header name goes on the wire as `":x-probe"`, which both host header builders reject, so the header is dropped. Meanwhile `content-type-of` and `redact-headers` already accept keyword names (via `name`), and `prepare-body!` (transport.cljc:1304) sees a keyword `:content-type` and skips the inferred `Content-Type`. The request then goes out with no Content-Type at all.
   Cost: a Clojure programmer's default map style (`{:headers {:authorization "Bearer …"}}`) silently sends an unauthenticated request with no content type. The only signal is `:rf.warning/http-header-invalid`, which is debug-gated, so production gets nothing. Spec 014 §Request envelope types header names as strings, but the slice handles keyword names inconsistently.
   Verified: real JVM transport against an in-process server, with `{:x-probe "v1" :authorization "Bearer T" :content-type "text/csv"}` on a POST with a map body. The server saw none of the three headers and no Content-Type, the reply was `:ok`, and three header-invalid warnings were emitted. Control: the same headers with string names all arrived.
   Fix: in `normalize-header-pairs`, lower the name with `(if (keyword? k) (name k) (str k))`, the rule `content-type-of`, `redact-headers` and `params->query` already use. Alternatively refuse a non-string name at dispatch. Add a test against the real transport, because a stub receives the raw headers map and cannot see this.
   Size S. Confidence verified. Lens 3 (ergonomics), also lens 1.

4. handlers.cljc:62-101, `validate-retry!`.
   What: it validates the `:on` set and that `:max-attempts` is present. It does not check that `:retry` is a map, nor that `:max-attempts` or `:backoff` are numbers. Two consequences: a non-map `:retry` (`:retry 3`) passes and destructures to no policy, and a non-numeric `:backoff` value throws inside `compute-backoff-ms` at the first retry-eligible failure.
   Cost: `:retry 3` silently never retries, the very failure mode the `:on` set check exists to prevent ("would silently disable retry"). A malformed `:backoff` throws inside the completion fence, so the request is retired with NO reply. The only signal is `:rf.error/http-reply-tail-failed`, and its name points at the reply tail rather than the policy. The hosts also diverge: JS coerces `"250"`, so the same request works on CLJS.
   Verified: `:retry 3` against a 503-then-200 stub caused 1 hit and delivered `:status :error` `:rf.http/http-5xx`. Control: the map form caused 2 hits and delivered `:ok`. `:backoff {:base-ms "250"}` against a 503 stub delivered no reply, left 0 records in flight, and produced one error row, `:rf.error/http-reply-tail-failed` (ClassCastException).
   Fix: in `validate-retry!`, refuse a non-map non-nil `:retry`, a `:max-attempts` that is not a positive integer, and `:backoff` `:base-ms` / `:factor` / `:max-ms` values that are not non-negative numbers. Use the existing `:rf.error/http-bad-retry-on` with the offending key in `:extra`. Extend http_retry_on_validation_test.
   Size S. Confidence verified. Lens 3 (ergonomics), also lens 1.

5. transport.cljc:185, `reply-suppressing-abort-reasons #{:request-id-superseded :epoch-restored :frame-destroyed}`, with `:test-reset` absent.
   What: `registry/clear-all-in-flight!` aborts with `:test-reset`, which is not reply-suppressing. It runs from `run-test-resets!`, and `reset-runtime!` (test_support.cljc) empties the frames registry before that call. Each held request's `:status :cancelled` reply therefore runs its captured `:after` chain and is dispatched into a frame that no longer exists.
   Cost: every test that leaves a request held prints a spurious `:rf.error/frame-destroyed` at the next reset and runs app `:after` code mid-reset. That is noise in exactly the suites that use `pending-transport`.
   Verified: the probe replayed the reset order (`reset!` frames, then `clear-all-in-flight!`) with a live listener on one held request. It saw one `:rf.http/aborted` `:reason :test-reset`, one `:rf.http/replied`, and one `:rf.error/frame-destroyed`, which was also printed to the console.
   Fix: add `:test-reset` to `reply-suppressing-abort-reasons`. The target frame is gone for the same reason it is under `:frame-destroyed`.
   Size S. Confidence verified. Lens 1 (cleanup).

6. Stale or misleading commentary. All verified at source.
   (a) Line-number citations that point at the wrong text. transport.cljc:1156 cites "The spec (lines 145, 285, 289)", but Spec 014 :145 is the `:retry` args row and :285 a table header. privacy.cljc:484 cites "Spec 009 line 1176: Consumers treat absent as false", but that phrase appears nowhere in Spec 009 (control: the same search finds the related "treat absent and nil identically" at 009:1608). reply.cljc:278 cites "EP-0011 §Status taxonomy line 763-768", but those lines are an example map. Replace each with a section pointer, per CLAUDE.md § Conventions & Patterns.

title: senior review: security suite
description:
SENIOR-DEVELOPER REVIEW of one slice of the tree. Part of the review sweep rf2-r5cc2, which partitions implementation/, tools/, examples/ and skills/ into slices; this bead owns exactly the slice below, and its siblings own the rest.

SLICE:
- implementation/security/**
- implementation/SECURITY.md

FOCUS: The security regression suite and the threat model it encodes (spec/Security.md).

PERSONA. A senior Clojure/ClojureScript developer who did not write this code, reading it as its next maintainer and as a programmer who has to use it. Judge it against the project stance (CLAUDE.md), quoted verbatim:

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

So record material, actionable insights only: a defect, a simplification that removes real weight, an ergonomic sharp edge a programmer (or the AI they use) will hit, a test that cannot go red, a doc or docstring that misleads. Not style preferences, not nagging diagnostics, not defensive belt-and-braces, not renames for taste.

LENSES, in priority order:
1. Correctness — error paths, concurrency, cleanup, and fail-closed behaviour on any security or privacy boundary.
2. Simplicity and clarity — dead code, duplication (within the slice or with another slice), accidental complexity, an abstraction that earns nothing.
3. Ergonomics — the API or tool as a programmer, or the AI they use, actually meets it.
4. Performance — hot spots on real paths, never at the expense of clarity.
5. Test rigour — a test that cannot fail, a gap on a branch that matters.
6. Comments and docstrings — per CLAUDE.md § Conventions & Patterns: present tense, the reason plus a spec pointer, no provenance, no restated spec.

METHOD. Read the slice's source first, then its tests, against the owning spec sections (spec/Ownership.md maps each surface to its spec). A finding is a CLAIM until checked: confirm each one at source, and confirm a behaviour claim with a quick REPL or test run where that is cheap. This is a read-only review: edit no file, and run only read-only commands and the slice's existing test lanes.

OUTPUT, recorded on THIS bead and never in a separate file: write the section to a file and append it with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes "$(cat <file>)"` (never `--notes`, which replaces). Head it `== SENIOR REVIEW FINDINGS (<datetime with zone>, trunk <short sha>)` and include:
- 0 to 15 numbered findings, most important first. Each gives: `path:line` (plus a short quote so it can be re-found by text), what is wrong, why it matters (the concrete failure or cost), the fix (a sketch is fine), size (S/M/L), confidence (verified / probable), and its lens.
- A short "looked at and sound" list, so the review's coverage is visible.
- Cross-slice findings, whose defect lives in another slice's files, in a separate list naming the owning slice. Do not act on them.

Then add the label `findings-recorded` and leave the bead OPEN: its findings become this slice's fix work, which the coordinator dispatches in clusters. If the slice needs nothing, record zero findings with the coverage list and close the bead with that as the reason.

title: Skills review: every skill under skills/ gets four serial passes (completeness, correctness, organisation, skills best practice) and its own PR
description:
Review every skill under `skills/` and open ONE PR PER SKILL. There are nine, and each one has a child bead: re-frame-migration, re-frame2, re-frame2-implementor, re-frame2-improver, re-frame2-pair, re-frame2-pair-retro, re-frame2-setup, re-frame2-xray, reagent-fresco-migration.

## Scope of one skill

Everything under `skills/<name>/`: `SKILL.md` and its frontmatter, `references/`, `patterns/` and `decision-trees/` where the skill has them, `evals/`, `spec/`, `tests/`, `README.md`, `package.json`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`. Its `docs/skills/` page is in scope only where the skill's purpose, kickoff, or the failures and options a user meets change; `skills/README.md` says a change to a leaf alone never needs a page edit.

## Four passes, in order

Finish each pass before you start the next, because each one changes what the next one reads. The PR body gets one short section per pass: what it found, what changed, and what was noticed but deliberately left alone.

1. **Completeness.** Does the skill cover everything its `description` promises, and everything the current spec and implementation offer for that situation? Look for missing leaves, missing failure modes and missing kickoff steps. Also look for leaves that nothing loads: each `SKILL.md`'s leaf-loading section is the roster, so a leaf it never names is either dead or a gap in the roster.
2. **Correctness.** Check every API name, option, error id, file path and command against the tree as it is now: `spec/API.md` with `spec/api-manifest.edn`, the owning `spec/` sections, and `implementation/`. Run the commands the skill tells people to run, check that its examples are real, and remove retired vocabulary. If the skill is right and the spec or the code is wrong, file a separate bead; don't edit `spec/` in these PRs.
3. **Organisation and structure.** `SKILL.md` should be a router, not an encyclopaedia. Leaves sit one level deep under it, say each thing once, use the same term for the same thing throughout, and come in an order a reader can follow.
4. **Skills best practice.** Read it against Anthropic's Agent Skills authoring guidance:
   - The frontmatter `name` and `description` say, in the third person, what the skill does and when to use it, with concrete triggers, and fit the budget `scripts/check_skill_description_budget.py` enforces.
   - `SKILL.md` stays concise (aim under about 500 lines) and is written for an agent that is already smart: cut what Claude already knows.
   - Detail is disclosed progressively, through references one level deep, and a long reference opens with a list of its contents.
   - A multi-step workflow is a checklist that ends in a validation step.
   - Deterministic work goes in scripts rather than prose.
   - No time-sensitive statements; examples are concrete.
   - The evals reflect how the skill is really used.

## Posture

> Posture is that we are pre-alpha and focused on elegance, power and a masterpiece.
> But we are not over-engineering or gold plating. Also, we trust the programmer.
> We're trying to facilitate high productivity for them (and the AI they use) via a
> library with excellent ergonomics and low friction. We don't need to litigate every
> last fine detail and drown in the minutiae.

Tightening and deleting usually beat adding. A minor item can go in the PR body as noticed-and-left, rather than churning the skill. Prose follows `CLAUDE.md`'s rule: present tense, the reason rather than the history, with no bead ids, PR numbers or dates.

## Gates

- **The fast-PR spine**, run by absolute path: `sh <WORKTREE_ROOT>/scripts/test-fast-pr.sh`. Its skill tier runs the `scripts/check_skill_*.py` gates (description budget, package refs, eval docs and packaging, and the per-skill drift checks) and the doc-link gates. `skills/` is a docs-gate root for `check_doc_slugs.py`. If a skill change has to update that skill's own drift gate, do it in the same PR.
- **API-name drift:** `clojure -M -m re-frame.api-manifest.skills-check`, from `implementation/scripts/api-manifest`. This is the skills-projection step of `lint.yml`'s `api-manifest` job.
- **Fixture projects** (`skills/*/tests/fixture`) are NOT covered by the shadow-cljs lane helper: running one locally needs the coordinator's grant first (`AGENTS.md`). CI builds the re-frame2-pair and reagent-fresco-migration fixtures.

## Sequencing

Each skill is its own directory, so the nine can run in parallel. The exceptions are the shared files: `skills/README.md` (the routing table), `docs/skills/index.md`, `SKILL-REDIRECT.md`, and any `scripts/check_skill_*.py` gate that reads more than one skill. Two PRs touching one of those go one after the other.

title: skill(re-frame-migration): M-30 flow triage has no branch for a parameterized flow that holds state, and the :live? re-home assumes the flipping events can be listed (later v1 passes :db to :live?)
description:
Filed from a downstream v1 -> re-frame2 migration's skills retrospective (suggestion, not a work order). Verified at origin/main 0783705626. Priority 2: the triage routes a real v1 flow shape onto a primitive that silently drops its behaviour. Two downstream reports merged here (same section, same remedy).

## Skill file and section

skills/re-frame-migration/references/breaking-changes.md §M-30 also carries the flow-map conversion:

- the triage (lines 263-268);
- the `:live?` / `:live-inputs` bullet (line 274).

inventory-and-plan.md Step 3's `reg-flow` row (line 81) mirrors the triage.

## What it says

- :266: "Per-instance / parameterized … → a parameterized `reg-sub` with a vector query (`[::the-sub args]`), not a flow."
- :268: "Everything else is a sub (parameterized when it was arg-keyed)."
- :274: "`:live?` / `:live-inputs` — dropped. A gate is data: the events that flipped the predicate write its value into `app-db`, and the flow reads it as one of its `:inputs`. Deciding which events write the gate is intent static analysis can't recover — flag it for human review."

## What happened (generic)

1. **A missing third branch.** A v1 flow can be both arg-keyed and stateful: a vector `:id` per widget instance, plus any of:
   - a `:live?` gate whose `:cleanup` keeps the output while the flow is dead;
   - output that event handlers read;
   - a per-flow `:fx`.

   The triage sends it to a parameterized `reg-sub`. A sub cannot keep a value across a dead period, handlers cannot read it (they read `:db`), and it cannot emit effects. A v2 flow cannot take a non-keyword id (`:rf.error/flow-bad-id`, :266). So neither destination keeps the behaviour, and the `reg-sub` route fails silently.
2. **The `:live?` re-home assumes the flipping events can be listed.** Later v1 1.4.x releases pass the whole db to `:live?`, so a predicate can read any slice and any event can flip it. "The events that flipped the predicate" is then every event, and enumerating them is not a real option.

## Evidence

- re-frame v1 release 1.4.7, `src/re_frame/flow/alpha.cljc`:
  - :162-163 `(live? (assoc id->old-live-in :db old-db))` and `(live? (assoc id->live-in :db db))`;
  - :165-172 the dead/live transitions and `(cleanup db path)`;
  - :174-179 the per-flow `:fx`.
- re-frame 1.4.3 passes only the live inputs to `:live?` and has no per-flow `:fx`, so both points apply to later 1.4.x apps.
- Observed on a ~170-file app's widget-flow design unit.

## Suggested change

1. Add a third triage branch: "Parameterized AND stateful (keeps its output across dead periods, is read by handlers, or emits fx) → per-instance `app-db` state, shown to views through a parameterized sub. The state is written either by an event, or by a frame-level interceptor that evaluates the old and new predicate over the before and after db and writes the state. Type B." Mirror it at inventory-and-plan.md:81.
2. In the `:live?` bullet, say that when the v1 predicate reads `:db`, the gate can flip on any event. Offer the same frame-level before/after-diff interceptor as the route, instead of enumerating the flipping events.

breaking-changes.md §M-30 gains a third triage branch, "Holds state", which wins over the view-only and parameterized branches:
